options.D: 使用请求映射模板选择模拟集成响应。

zh.explanation:
# API Gateway Mock 集成用于后端模拟

## 场景
开发人员需要在 Amazon API Gateway 中的 REST API 集成测试期间模拟不同的后端响应，**无需调用真实的后端服务**，并且具有**最少的操作开销**。

## 正确答案：D — 使用请求映射模板来选择 Mock 集成响应

API Gateway 具有内置的 **Mock 集成**类型，专门用于此目的。使用 Mock 集成，API Gateway 直接返回响应，无需将请求转发到任何后端（无 Lambda、无 HTTP 端点、无 EC2）。使用集成请求映射模板，您可以注入应用逻辑来根据某些条件决定返回哪个 Mock 集成响应。例如，您可以使用传入请求上的 scope 查询参数来确定是返回成功响应还是错误响应，允许内部调用通过，同时使用错误响应拒绝其他类型的调用。

典型的 VTL 请求映射模板根据输入选择响应：

```vtl
{
  #if( $input.params('scope') == "internal" )
    "statusCode": 200
  #else
    "statusCode": 500
  #end
}
```

这完全在 API Gateway 内部管理，无需任何额外的计算资源，满足"最少操作开销"的标准。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

- **A. 带代理集成的 Lambda 函数返回常量响应** — 这在功能上有效，但引入了不必要的计算资源（Lambda 函数），必须编写、部署、维护和监控。它还会产生 Lambda 调用成本。API Gateway 的原生 Mock 集成消除了对任何 Lambda 的需求。第一种方法可以是让 API Gateway 指向一个或多个具有硬编码响应的 Lambda。这不是一个坏办法，但即使它只是一个 Mock，您也将为每次 Lambda 执行付费，如果您有许多端点，设置所有 Mock 可能非常无聊且耗时。您可以使用 MockIntegration 加快流程并节省成本！

- **B. EC2 实例通过 CloudFormation 提供后端** — 这具有**最高**的操作开销：仅为了返回 Mock 响应而配置、修补、扩展和保护 EC2 实例完全与所要求的相反。

- **C. 自定义 API Gateway 阶段以根据请求选择响应类型** — API Gateway 中的阶段表示部署环境（开发、测试、生产）和阶段变量；它们不是根据请求内容选择 Mock 响应的机制。Mock 响应选择在**方法/集成**级别使用映射模板执行，而不是在阶段级别。

## 参考资源
- [API Gateway 中 REST API 的 Mock 集成](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-mock-integration.html)
- [使用 API Gateway 控制台启用 Mock 集成](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-mock-integration-console.html)

en.question: A developer has a legacy application that is hosted on-premises. Other applications hosted on AWS depend on the on-premises application for proper functioning. In case of any application errors, the developer wants to be able to use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor and troubleshoot all applications from one place. How can the developer accomplish this?

options.A: Install an AWS SDK on the on-premises server to automatically send logs to CloudWatch.
options.B: Download the CloudWatch agent to the on-premises server. Configure the agent to use IAM user credentials with permissions for CloudWatch.
options.C: Upload log files from the on-premises server to Amazon S3 and have CloudWatch read the files.
options.D: Upload log files from the on-premises server to an Amazon EC2 instance and have the instance forward the logs to CloudWatch.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

The developer needs centralized monitoring and troubleshooting in **Amazon CloudWatch** for both AWS-hosted applications and a legacy **on-premises** application. The question asks how to get the on-premises server's logs/metrics into CloudWatch so everything can be observed from one place.

## Correct Answer: B

Install the **unified CloudWatch agent** on the on-premises server and configure it with **IAM user credentials** that have permission to publish to CloudWatch.

- AWS provides explicit guidance for installing the CloudWatch agent on on-premises servers. The official documentation explains how to install the CloudWatch agent on an on-premises server.
- Because on-premises servers cannot assume an EC2 instance role natively, you authenticate with an IAM user. If you're going to run the CloudWatch agent on on-premises servers, create an IAM user with the necessary permissions. This scenario requires IAM users with programmatic access and long-term credentials.
- The IAM user is typically attached to the managed policy **CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy**. Choose Attach existing policies directly. In the list of policies, select the check box next to CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy.
- The agent uses these credentials to send metrics and logs to CloudWatch. To enable the CloudWatch agent to send data from an on-premises server, you must specify the access key and secret key of the IAM user that you created earlier. You also must specify the AWS Region to send the metrics to, using the region field.

This satisfies the requirement to monitor and troubleshoot all applications (cloud + on-premises) from one place — the CloudWatch console.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

**A. Install an AWS SDK on the on-premises server to automatically send logs to CloudWatch.**
The AWS SDK does not "automatically" send logs. It only provides API bindings (e.g., `PutLogEvents`, `PutMetricData`); the developer would have to write, deploy, and maintain custom code to read log files and push them. The purpose-built CloudWatch agent already does this out of the box for both EC2 and on-premises hosts.

**C. Upload log files from the on-premises server to Amazon S3 and have CloudWatch read the files.**
CloudWatch Logs does not natively pull/ingest log files from S3. You would need additional plumbing (Lambda, Kinesis Firehose, or custom code) to move S3 objects into CloudWatch Logs. This is unnecessarily complex when the CloudWatch agent supports on-premises servers directly.

**D. Upload log files from the on-premises server to an Amazon EC2 instance and have the instance forward the logs to CloudWatch.**
Adding a relay EC2 instance just to forward logs introduces extra cost, latency, and a single point of failure. The CloudWatch agent on the on-premises server can publish directly to CloudWatch, eliminating the need for the intermediary.

## References
- [Install the CloudWatch agent on on-premises servers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/install-CloudWatch-Agent-on-premise.html)
- [CloudWatch agent prerequisites — IAM users for on-premises](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/prerequisites.html)
- [CloudWatch agent credentials preference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Agent-Credentials-Preference.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员有一个托管在本地的旧版应用程序。其他托管在 AWS 上的应用程序依赖于该本地应用程序才能正常运行。如果应用程序出现任何错误，开发人员希望能够使用 Amazon CloudWatch 从一个位置监控和排查所有应用程序的问题。开发人员该如何实现这一点？

options.A: 在本地服务器上安装 AWS SDK，以自动将日志发送到 CloudWatch。
options.B: 将 CloudWatch 代理下载到本地服务器。配置代理以使用具有 CloudWatch 权限的 IAM 用户凭据。
options.C: 将本地服务器上的日志文件上传到 Amazon S3，并让 CloudWatch 读取这些文件。
options.D: 将本地服务器上的日志文件上传到 Amazon EC2 实例，并让该实例将日志转发到 CloudWatch。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

开发人员需要在 **Amazon CloudWatch** 中为 AWS 托管的应用程序和遗留的**本地**应用程序进行集中监控和故障排除。该问题要求如何将本地服务器的日志/指标导入 CloudWatch，以便从一个地方观察所有内容。

## 正确答案：B

在本地服务器上安装**统一 CloudWatch 代理**，并使用具有发布到 CloudWatch 权限的 **IAM 用户凭证**配置它。

- AWS 提供了在本地服务器上安装 CloudWatch 代理的明确指导。官方文档解释了如何在本地服务器上安装 CloudWatch 代理。
- 由于本地服务器无法原生地假设 EC2 实例角色，你需要使用 IAM 用户进行身份验证。如果你要在本地服务器上运行 CloudWatch 代理，请创建具有必要权限的 IAM 用户。此场景需要具有编程访问权限和长期凭证的 IAM 用户。
- IAM 用户通常附加到托管策略 **CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy**。选择"附加现有策略"。在策略列表中，选中 CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy 旁边的复选框。
- 代理使用这些凭证将指标和日志发送到 CloudWatch。要使 CloudWatch 代理能够从本地服务器发送数据，必须指定之前创建的 IAM 用户的访问密钥和秘密密钥。还必须使用 region 字段指定要将指标发送到的 AWS 区域。

这满足了从一个地方（CloudWatch 控制台）监控和故障排除所有应用程序（云+本地）的要求。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

**A. 在本地服务器上安装 AWS SDK，自动将日志发送到 CloudWatch。**
AWS SDK 不会"自动"发送日志。它仅提供 API 绑定（例如 `PutLogEvents`、`PutMetricData`）；开发人员必须编写、部署和维护自定义代码来读取日志文件并推送它们。用途专用的 CloudWatch 代理已经为 EC2 和本地主机开箱即用地完成了这项工作。

**C. 从本地服务器上载日志文件到 Amazon S3，让 CloudWatch 读取这些文件。**
CloudWatch Logs 不原生支持从 S3 拉取/摄入日志文件。你需要额外的管道（Lambda、Kinesis Firehose 或自定义代码）将 S3 对象移动到 CloudWatch Logs。当 CloudWatch 代理直接支持本地服务器时，这是不必要的复杂化。

**D. 从本地服务器上载日志文件到 Amazon EC2 实例，让该实例将日志转发到 CloudWatch。**
添加中继 EC2 实例只是为了转发日志，这会增加额外的成本、延迟和单点故障。本地服务器上的 CloudWatch 代理可以直接发布到 CloudWatch，从而消除了对中介的需要。

## 参考资源
- [在本地服务器上安装 CloudWatch 代理](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/install-CloudWatch-Agent-on-premise.html)
- [CloudWatch 代理先决条件 — 本地 IAM 用户](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/prerequisites.html)
- [CloudWatch 代理凭证首选项](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Agent-Credentials-Preference.html)

en.question: An Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream is receiving customer data that contains personally identifiable information. A developer needs to remove pattern-based customer identifiers from the data and store the modified data in an Amazon S3 bucket. What should the developer do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Implement Kinesis Data Firehose data transformation as an AWS Lambda function. Configure the function to remove the customer identifiers. Set an Amazon S3 bucket as the destination of the delivery stream.
options.B: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance. Set the EC2 instance as the destination of the delivery stream. Run an application on the EC2 instance to remove the customer identifiers. Store the transformed data in an Amazon S3 bucket.
options.C: Create an Amazon OpenSearch Service instance. Set the OpenSearch Service instance as the destination of the delivery stream. Use search and replace to remove the customer identifiers. Export the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
options.D: Create an AWS Step Functions workflow to remove the customer identifiers. As the last step in the workflow, store the transformed data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Set the workflow as the destination of the delivery stream.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream is ingesting customer data containing PII. The developer must strip pattern‑based identifiers (e.g., SSNs, phone numbers, emails matching regex patterns) from records *before* the data lands in Amazon S3.

## Correct Answer: A

Kinesis Data Firehose has a **built-in data transformation feature** that invokes an AWS Lambda function on buffered batches before delivering records to the destination. With the Firehose data transformation feature, you can specify a Lambda function that performs transformations directly on the stream when you create a delivery stream. Firehose buffers incoming data and invokes the specified Lambda function with each buffered batch, and the transformed data is sent from Lambda to Firehose for buffering and then delivered to the destination.

The Lambda function can apply regex-based logic to detect and remove pattern-based customer identifiers (SSN, phone, email, ZIP, etc.), and Firehose then writes the cleansed records to the configured S3 bucket. This pattern is explicitly documented for PII/PHI scrubbing use cases — Philter can be used with AWS Kinesis Firehose and AWS Lambda to remove sensitive information, such as PII and PHI, from the text as it travels through the firehose.

You can also optionally enable source record backup if you need to retain the originals: you can also choose to enable source record backup, which backs up all untransformed records to your S3 bucket concurrently while delivering transformed records to the destination.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

**B. EC2 instance as the destination** — Firehose does not support EC2 as a delivery destination. Kinesis has multiple destination configuration properties to choose from and each delivery stream only gets one. The options are Elasticsearch, S3, Redshift, Splunk, Kinesis Stream, or a generic HTTP endpoint. Even via an HTTP endpoint, this is operationally heavy (patching, scaling, HA) compared with native Lambda transformation.

**C. OpenSearch as a transformation step** — OpenSearch Service is a search/analytics engine, not a streaming-data transformer. While Firehose *can* deliver to OpenSearch, OpenSearch has no built-in mechanism to mutate Firehose records and then re-export them to S3 as part of the delivery. This adds cost and architectural complexity, and does not perform pre-delivery PII scrubbing.

**D. Step Functions as the destination** — Step Functions is not a supported Firehose destination. Firehose destinations are limited to S3, Redshift, OpenSearch, Splunk, supported third-party HTTP endpoints, and similar. Trying to orchestrate per-record PII removal via Step Functions also does not match Firehose's batch/stream transformation model, which is purpose-built around Lambda processors.

## Reference Links
- [Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose Data Transformation (Developer Guide)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/data-transformation.html)
- [AWS Blog – Amazon Kinesis Firehose Data Transformation with AWS Lambda](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/amazon-kinesis-firehose-data-transformation-with-aws-lambda/)

zh.question: 一个 Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose 数据流正在接收包含个人身份信息的客户数据。开发人员需要从数据中移除基于模式的客户标识符，并将修改后的数据存储在 Amazon S3 存储桶中。开发人员应该如何操作才能满足这些要求？

options.A: 将 Kinesis Data Firehose 数据转换实现为 AWS Lambda 函数。配置该函数以移除客户标识符。将 Amazon S3 存储桶设置为交付流的目标位置。
options.B: 启动一个 Amazon EC2 实例。将该 EC2 实例设置为交付流的目标位置。在该 EC2 实例上运行一个应用程序以移除客户标识符。将转换后的数据存储在 Amazon S3 存储桶中。
options.C: 创建一个 Amazon OpenSearch Service 实例。将该 OpenSearch Service 实例设置为交付流的目标位置。使用查找和替换功能删除客户标识符。将数据导出到 Amazon S3 存储桶。
options.D: 创建一个 AWS Step Functions 工作流来移除客户标识符。作为工作流的最后一步，将转换后的数据存储在 Amazon S3 存储桶中。将该工作流设置为交付流的目标位置。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

Kinesis Data Firehose 传输流正在摄取包含 PII 的客户数据。开发者必须在数据落地到 Amazon S3 *之前*，从记录中去除基于模式的标识符（例如，匹配正则表达式的 SSN、电话号码、电子邮件）。

## 正确答案：A

Kinesis Data Firehose 具有**内置数据转换功能**，在将记录交付到目标之前，对缓冲的批次调用 AWS Lambda 函数。使用 Firehose 数据转换功能，您可以在创建传输流时指定一个 Lambda 函数来执行转换。Firehose 缓冲传入的数据并用每个缓冲的批次调用指定的 Lambda 函数，转换后的数据从 Lambda 发送到 Firehose 进行缓冲，然后交付到目标。

Lambda 函数可以应用基于正则表达式的逻辑来检测和移除基于模式的客户标识符（SSN、电话、电子邮件、ZIP 等），然后 Firehose 将清洁后的记录写入配置的 S3 存储桶。此模式已明确记录用于 PII/PHI 清理用例——Philter 可以与 AWS Kinesis Firehose 和 AWS Lambda 一起使用，以在文本通过 firehose 时从文本中移除敏感信息，例如 PII 和 PHI。

您还可以选择启用源记录备份，如果需要保留原始记录：您还可以选择启用源记录备份，这会在向目标交付转换后的记录时，同时将所有未转换的记录备份到您的 S3 存储桶。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

**B. 以 EC2 实例作为目标** — Firehose 不支持 EC2 作为传输目标。Kinesis 具有多个传输流目标配置属性可供选择，每个传输流只能有一个。选项包括 Elasticsearch、S3、Redshift、Splunk、Kinesis Stream 或通用 HTTP 端点。即使通过 HTTP 端点，与本机 Lambda 转换相比，这在操作上也很繁重（补丁、扩展、高可用性）。

**C. OpenSearch 作为转换步骤** — OpenSearch Service 是一个搜索/分析引擎，而不是流数据转换器。虽然 Firehose *可以*交付到 OpenSearch，但 OpenSearch 没有内置机制来改变 Firehose 记录，然后将其重新导出到 S3 作为传输的一部分。这增加了成本和架构复杂性，并且不执行传输前 PII 清理。

**D. Step Functions 作为目标** — Step Functions 不是受支持的 Firehose 目标。Firehose 目标仅限于 S3、Redshift、OpenSearch、Splunk、受支持的第三方 HTTP 端点等。尝试通过 Step Functions 协调逐条记录的 PII 移除也与 Firehose 的批处理/流转换模型不匹配，该模型是围绕 Lambda 处理器专门设计的。

## 参考链接
- [Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose 数据转换（开发者指南）](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/data-transformation.html)
- [AWS 博客 – 使用 AWS Lambda 的 Amazon Kinesis Firehose 数据转换](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/amazon-kinesis-firehose-data-transformation-with-aws-lambda/)

en.question: A developer is using an AWS Lambda function to generate avatars for profile pictures that are uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket. The Lambda function is automatically invoked for profile pictures that are saved under the /original/ S3 prefix. The developer notices that some pictures cause the Lambda function to time out. The developer wants to implement a fallback mechanism by using another Lambda function that resizes the profile picture. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

options.A: Set the image resize Lambda function as a destination of the avatar generator Lambda function for the events that fail processing.
options.B: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Set the SQS queue as a destination with an on failure condition for the avatar generator Lambda function. Configure the image resize Lambda function to poll from the SQS queue.
options.C: Create an AWS Step Functions state machine that invokes the avatar generator Lambda function and uses the image resize Lambda function as a fallback. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches events from the S3 bucket to invoke the state machine.
options.D: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Set the SNS topic as a destination with an on failure condition for the avatar generator Lambda function. Subscribe the image resize Lambda function to the SNS topic.

en.explanation:
# Lambda Destinations as a Fallback Mechanism

## Scenario
An S3 upload to the `/original/` prefix asynchronously invokes the **avatar generator** Lambda. Some images cause the function to time out. The developer wants a **fallback** — invoke a separate **image resize** Lambda when the first one fails — with the **least development effort**.

Because S3 invokes Lambda **asynchronously**, the avatar generator function qualifies for **AWS Lambda Destinations**, a built‑in feature designed exactly for this kind of success/failure routing without any custom glue code.

## Correct Answer: A
Configure the image resize Lambda function as the **OnFailure destination** of the avatar generator Lambda function.

AWS Lambda Destinations for asynchronous invocations is a feature that provides visibility into Lambda function invocations and routes the execution results to AWS services, simplifying event-driven applications and reducing code complexity.

For each execution status such as Success or Failure you can choose one of four destinations: another Lambda function, SNS, SQS, or EventBridge. Lambda can also be configured to route different execution results to different destinations.

Previously, you needed to write the SQS/SNS/EventBridge handling code within your Lambda function and manage retries and failures yourself. With Destinations, you can route asynchronous function results as an execution record to a destination resource without writing additional code.

Critically for this scenario: When a function invocation fails, such as when retries are exhausted or the event age has been exceeded (hitting its TTL), Destinations routes the record to the destination resource for every failed invocation for further investigation or processing. A timeout counts as a failure, so once retries are exhausted the original event payload is automatically forwarded to the resize Lambda — no code changes, no extra resources to provision.

Example CloudFormation:
```yaml
Resources:
  EventInvokeConfig:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::EventInvokeConfig
    Properties:
      FunctionName: AvatarGenerator
      Qualifier: "$LATEST"
      MaximumRetryAttempts: 0
      DestinationConfig:
        OnFailure:
          Destination: arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:123456789012:function:ImageResize
```

## Why the other options are wrong

**B. SQS queue as the OnFailure destination, polled by the resize Lambda.**
This works, but it requires extra infrastructure — creating an SQS queue, granting permissions, and configuring an event source mapping on the resize Lambda. Since Lambda Destinations natively support **another Lambda function** as a target (Lambda supports the following destinations for asynchronous invocation: Amazon SQS, Amazon SNS, AWS Lambda, Amazon EventBridge), the SQS hop is unnecessary and adds development effort, violating the "LEAST development effort" criterion.

**C. Step Functions state machine + EventBridge rule on S3.**
This requires authoring an ASL state machine with a Catch/Retry fallback branch, creating an EventBridge rule that matches S3 events, enabling EventBridge notifications on the bucket, and changing how the avatar Lambda is invoked. That is significantly more development and configuration than simply attaching an OnFailure destination. Step Functions is better suited for orchestrating multi‑step workflows, not a simple binary fallback.

**D. SNS topic as OnFailure destination with the resize Lambda subscribed.**
Similar problem to B — adds an SNS topic, subscription, and permissions for no functional gain over directly targeting the Lambda. Also, Amazon SNS destinations have a message size limit of 256 KB. If the combined size of the function request and response payload exceeds the limit, Lambda will drop the payload when sending OnFailure event to the destination. Direct Lambda‑to‑Lambda destination is simpler.

## Key takeaway
For asynchronous Lambda invocations (like S3 → Lambda), **Lambda Destinations with OnFailure → another Lambda function** is the lowest‑effort fallback pattern because it is a native, code‑free configuration.

## References
- [Introducing AWS Lambda Destinations (AWS Compute Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/introducing-aws-lambda-destinations/)
- [Implementing AWS Lambda error handling patterns (AWS Compute Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/implementing-aws-lambda-error-handling-patterns/)
- [Asynchronous invocation – Destinations (AWS Lambda Developer Guide)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-async.html#invocation-async-destinations)

zh.question: 一位开发人员使用 AWS Lambda 函数为上传到 Amazon S3 存储桶的个人资料图片生成头像。对于保存在 S3 前缀 `/original/` 下的个人资料图片，Lambda 函数会自动调用。开发人员注意到，某些图片会导致 Lambda 函数超时。开发人员希望实现一个备用机制，即使用另一个 Lambda 函数来调整个人资料图片的大小。哪种解决方案能够以最少的开发工作量满足这些要求？

options.A: 将图像调整大小 Lambda 函数设置为头像生成器 Lambda 函数的目标，用于处理处理失败的事件。
options.B: 创建一个 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列。将该 SQS 队列设置为头像生成器 Lambda 函数的失败条件目标。配置图像调整大小 Lambda 函数，使其从 SQS 队列轮询。
options.C: 创建一个 AWS Step Functions 状态机，该状态机调用头像生成器 Lambda 函数，并使用图像调整大小 Lambda 函数作为备用方案。创建一个 Amazon EventBridge 规则，该规则匹配来自 S3 存储桶的事件以调用该状态机。
options.D: 创建一个 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题。将该 SNS 主题设置为头像生成器 Lambda 函数的失败触发条件。将图像调整大小 Lambda 函数订阅到该 SNS 主题。

zh.explanation:
# Lambda Destinations 作为回退机制

## 场景
S3 上传到 `/original/` 前缀异步调用**头像生成器** Lambda。某些图像导致函数超时。开发者想要一个**回退**——当第一个函数失败时调用单独的**图像调整大小** Lambda——并且**开发工作量最少**。

由于 S3 **异步**调用 Lambda，头像生成器函数符合 **AWS Lambda Destinations** 的条件，这是一个内置功能，专为这种无需任何自定义胶合代码的成功/失败路由而设计。

## 正确答案：A
将图像调整大小 Lambda 函数配置为头像生成器 Lambda 函数的 **OnFailure destination**。

AWS Lambda Destinations for asynchronous invocations 是一项功能，可以提供对 Lambda 函数调用的可见性，并将执行结果路由到 AWS 服务，简化事件驱动型应用程序并降低代码复杂性。

对于每个执行状态（如成功或失败），你可以选择四个目标之一：另一个 Lambda 函数、SNS、SQS 或 EventBridge。Lambda 还可以配置为将不同的执行结果路由到不同的目标。

对于此场景至关重要的是：当函数调用失败时（例如重试用尽或事件年龄已超过 TTL），Destinations 会将记录路由到目标资源以进行进一步调查或处理。超时算作失败，因此一旦重试用尽，原始事件有效负载会自动转发到调整大小 Lambda——无需更改代码，无需配置额外资源。

CloudFormation 示例：
```yaml
Resources:
  EventInvokeConfig:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::EventInvokeConfig
    Properties:
      FunctionName: AvatarGenerator
      Qualifier: "$LATEST"
      MaximumRetryAttempts: 0
      DestinationConfig:
        OnFailure:
          Destination: arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:123456789012:function:ImageResize
```

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

**B. SQS 队列作为 OnFailure destination，由调整大小 Lambda 轮询。**
这有效，但需要额外的基础设施——创建 SQS 队列、授予权限和在调整大小 Lambda 上配置事件源映射。由于 Lambda Destinations 本机支持**另一个 Lambda 函数**作为目标（Lambda 支持以下异步调用目标：Amazon SQS、Amazon SNS、AWS Lambda、Amazon EventBridge），SQS 跳转是不必要的，增加了开发工作量，违反了"开发工作量最少"的标准。

**C. Step Functions 状态机 + S3 上的 EventBridge 规则。**
这需要编写带有 Catch/Retry 回退分支的 ASL 状态机、创建与 S3 事件匹配的 EventBridge 规则、启用存储桶上的 EventBridge 通知，以及更改头像 Lambda 的调用方式。这比仅将 OnFailure destination 附加到函数需要更多的开发和配置。Step Functions 更适合于编排多步工作流，而不是简单的二进制回退。

**D. SNS 主题作为 OnFailure destination，调整大小 Lambda 已订阅。**
与 B 类似的问题——添加 SNS 主题、订阅和权限，与直接针对 Lambda 相比没有功能优势。此外，Amazon SNS destinations 的消息大小限制为 256 KB。如果函数请求和响应有效负载的组合大小超过此限制，Lambda 在向目标发送 OnFailure 事件时将丢弃有效负载。直接 Lambda 到 Lambda destination 更简单。

## 关键要点
对于异步 Lambda 调用（如 S3 → Lambda），**Lambda Destinations with OnFailure → 另一个 Lambda 函数**是最低工作量的回退模式，因为它是原生的、无需代码的配置。

## 参考资料
- [Introducing AWS Lambda Destinations (AWS Compute Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/introducing-aws-lambda-destinations/)
- [Implementing AWS Lambda error handling patterns (AWS Compute Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/implementing-aws-lambda-error-handling-patterns/)
- [Asynchronous invocation – Destinations (AWS Lambda Developer Guide)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-async.html#invocation-async-destinations)

en.question: A developer needs to migrate an online retail application to AWS to handle an anticipated increase in traffic. The application currently runs on two servers: one server for the web application and another server for the database. The web server renders webpages and manages session state in memory. The database server hosts a MySQL database that contains order details. When traffic to the application is heavy, the memory usage for the web server approaches 100% and the application slows down considerably. The developer has found that most of the memory increase and performance decrease is related to the load of managing additional user sessions. For the web server migration, the developer will use Amazon EC2 instances with an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. Which additional set of changes should the developer make to the application to improve the application's performance?

options.A: Use an EC2 instance to host the MySQL database. Store the session data and the application data in the MySQL database.
options.B: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached to store and manage the session data. Use an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance to store the application data.
options.C: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached to store and manage the session data and the application data.
options.D: Use the EC2 instance store to manage the session data. Use an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance to store the application data.

en.explanation:
# Migrating a Stateful Web App to AWS — Externalizing Session State

## Scenario
The retail application has a web tier (rendering pages and storing session state in memory) and a MySQL database tier. Under load, the in-memory session data balloons and the web servers slow down. The team is moving to EC2 + Auto Scaling + ALB. Two architectural problems must be solved:

1. **Session state must move out of the EC2 instance memory.** Otherwise, scaling out is wasteful (each instance keeps its own sessions), Auto Scaling can terminate an instance and lose user sessions, and memory pressure persists.
2. **The MySQL database needs to be a managed, scalable backing store** for the order/application data.

## Correct Answer: B
Use **Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached** as an external in-memory session store, and **Amazon RDS for MySQL** for the relational application/order data.

- ElastiCache for Memcached is explicitly designed as a distributed, in-memory session store. Session stores are easy to create with Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached. Simply use the Memcached hash table, which can be distributed across multiple nodes. It is used for speeding up dynamic web applications with microseconds latency, making it useful as a cache or session store.
- Externalizing sessions to ElastiCache lets the ALB route any user to any EC2 instance (no sticky sessions required) and lets Auto Scaling add/remove instances without losing user sessions.
- RDS for MySQL is the managed equivalent of the existing MySQL database — appropriate for the structured order data and complex relational queries the application already uses.

## Why the other options are wrong

**A. Self-managed MySQL on EC2, with sessions in MySQL.**
- Storing sessions in a relational database adds disk I/O latency and pressure on the same DB that serves orders — the opposite of what the application needs. Querying a database is always slower and more expensive than locating a key in a key-value pair cache.
- Running MySQL on a single EC2 instance reintroduces all the operational/availability problems (no Multi‑AZ failover, no automated backups/patching) that RDS solves.

**C. ElastiCache for Memcached for both sessions and application (order) data.**
- Memcached is a non-durable, non-persistent in-memory cache — node failure or eviction means data loss, which is unacceptable for order records. It also has no relational/SQL features, transactions, joins, or durable storage required for order data.
- ElastiCache is intended as a front end to a database, not a replacement for one. ElastiCache is an ideal front end for data stores like Amazon RDS or DynamoDB, providing a high-performance middle tier for applications with extremely high request rates or low latency requirements.

**D. EC2 instance store for session data + RDS for MySQL.**
- The EC2 **instance store** is ephemeral, local to a single instance. Sessions stored there are not shared across the Auto Scaling fleet, and they are lost when the instance stops, terminates, or fails — exactly the problem to be eliminated. It also doesn't relieve the per-instance memory/disk pressure across the fleet.

## Key takeaway for the exam
For a horizontally scaled web tier behind an ALB + Auto Scaling, **always externalize session state** to a shared, low-latency store (ElastiCache for Memcached/Redis or DynamoDB) and keep relational/transactional data in **Amazon RDS**.

## References
- [Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached – Session Store](https://aws.amazon.com/elasticache/memcached/)
- [What is Memcached?](https://aws.amazon.com/elasticache/what-is-memcached/)
- [Common ElastiCache Use Cases](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/elasticache-use-cases.html)
- [Amazon ElastiCache FAQs](https://aws.amazon.com/elasticache/faqs/)
- [Amazon RDS for MySQL](https://aws.amazon.com/rds/mysql/)

zh.question: 为了应对预期的流量增长，开发人员需要将一个在线零售应用程序迁移到 AWS。该应用程序目前运行在两台服务器上：一台服务器用于 Web 应用程序，另一台服务器用于数据库。Web 服务器负责渲染网页并在内存中管理会话状态。数据库服务器托管一个包含订单详情的 MySQL 数据库。当应用程序流量高峰期，Web 服务器的内存使用率接近 100%，应用程序运行速度显著下降。开发人员发现，内存占用增加和性能下降的主要原因是管理额外用户会话的负载。对于 Web 服务器的迁移，开发人员将使用 Amazon EC2 实例，并在其后部署一个 Auto Scaling 组和一个应用程序负载均衡器。为了提升应用程序的性能，开发人员还需要对应用程序进行哪些更改？

options.A: 使用 EC2 实例托管 MySQL 数据库。将会话数据和应用程序数据存储在 MySQL 数据库中。
options.B: 使用 Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached 来存储和管理会话数据。使用 Amazon RDS for MySQL 数据库实例来存储应用程序数据。
options.C: 使用 Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached 来存储和管理会话数据和应用程序数据。
options.D: 使用 EC2 实例存储来管理会话数据。使用 Amazon RDS for MySQL 数据库实例来存储应用程序数据。

zh.explanation:
# 将有状态的 Web 应用迁移到 AWS — 外部化会话状态

## 场景
零售应用程序具有 Web 层（呈现页面并在内存中存储会话状态）和 MySQL 数据库层。在负载下，内存中的会话数据会膨胀，Web 服务器速度变慢。团队正在迁移到 EC2 + Auto Scaling + ALB。必须解决两个架构问题：

1. **会话状态必须移出 EC2 实例内存。** 否则，横向扩展是浪费的（每个实例保持自己的会话），Auto Scaling 可能终止实例并丢失用户会话，并且内存压力持续存在。
2. **MySQL 数据库需要是托管的、可扩展的后端存储**用于订单/应用程序数据。

## 正确答案：B
使用 **Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached** 作为外部内存中会话存储，以及 **Amazon RDS for MySQL** 用于关系型应用程序/订单数据。

- ElastiCache for Memcached 被明确设计为分布式、内存中会话存储。使用 Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached 可以轻松创建会话存储。只需使用 Memcached 哈希表，该表可以分布在多个节点上。 它用于以微秒级延迟加速动态 Web 应用程序，作为缓存或会话存储非常有用。
- 将会话外部化到 ElastiCache 让 ALB 可以将任何用户路由到任何 EC2 实例（不需要粘性会话），并让 Auto Scaling 添加/删除实例而不丢失用户会话。
- RDS for MySQL 是现有 MySQL 数据库的托管等效项 — 适合于应用程序已经使用的结构化订单数据和复杂关系查询。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

**A. EC2 上自管理的 MySQL，会话存储在 MySQL 中。**
- 在关系数据库中存储会话会增加磁盘 I/O 延迟和与服务订单的同一 DB 的压力 — 与应用程序需要的完全相反。查询数据库总是比在键值对缓存中定位键要慢且更昂贵。
- 在单个 EC2 实例上运行 MySQL 重新引入了 RDS 解决的所有操作/可用性问题（无 Multi-AZ 故障转移、无自动备份/修补）。

**C. 将 ElastiCache for Memcached 用于会话和应用程序（订单）数据。**
- Memcached 是非持久的、非持久化的内存中缓存 — 节点故障或驱逐意味着数据丢失，这对订单记录是不可接受的。它也没有订单数据所需的关系/SQL 功能、事务、联接或持久存储。
- ElastiCache 旨在作为数据库的前端，而不是其替代品。ElastiCache 是 Amazon RDS 或 DynamoDB 等数据存储的理想前端，为具有极高请求率或低延迟要求的应用程序提供高性能中间层。

**D. 用于会话数据的 EC2 实例存储 + RDS for MySQL。**
- EC2 **实例存储**是临时的，位于单个实例的本地。存储在其中的会话不在 Auto Scaling 集群中共享，并且当实例停止、终止或故障时会丢失 — 正是需要消除的问题。它也不能缓解整个集群中每个实例的内存/磁盘压力。

## 考试的关键要点
对于在 ALB + Auto Scaling 后面水平扩展的 Web 层，**始终将会话状态外部化**到共享的、低延迟存储（ElastiCache for Memcached/Redis 或 DynamoDB），并将关系/事务数据保留在 **Amazon RDS** 中。

## 参考资源
- [Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached – 会话存储](https://aws.amazon.com/elasticache/memcached/)
- [什么是 Memcached？](https://aws.amazon.com/elasticache/what-is-memcached/)
- [常见 ElastiCache 使用案例](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/elasticache-use-cases.html)
- [Amazon ElastiCache 常见问题](https://aws.amazon.com/elasticache/faqs/)
- [Amazon RDS for MySQL](https://aws.amazon.com/rds/mysql/)

en.question: An application uses Lambda functions to extract metadata from files uploaded to an S3 bucket; the metadata is stored in Amazon DynamoDB. The application starts behaving unexpectedly, and the developer wants to examine the logs of the Lambda function code for errors. Based on this system configuration, where would the developer find the logs?

options.A: Amazon S3
options.B: AWS CloudTrail
options.C: Amazon CloudWatch
options.D: Amazon DynamoDB

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A serverless application uses an AWS Lambda function (triggered by S3 uploads) to extract metadata and write it to DynamoDB. The application is misbehaving and the developer needs to inspect the **Lambda function's execution logs** to find errors.

## Correct Answer: C — Amazon CloudWatch

AWS Lambda is natively integrated with Amazon CloudWatch Logs. By default, Lambda automatically captures logs for all function invocations and sends them to CloudWatch Logs, provided your function's execution role has the necessary permissions. These logs are, by default, stored in a log group named /aws/lambda/<function-name>.

Lambda automatically streams standard output and standard error messages from a Lambda function to CloudWatch Logs, without requiring logging drivers. Lambda also automatically provisions containers that run your Lambda function and configures them to output log messages in separate log streams.

This means any `print`, `console.log`, `logger.info`, or unhandled exception output from the Lambda code will appear in **CloudWatch Logs** under the log group `/aws/lambda/<function-name>`, where the developer can search for errors and stack traces.

To enable this, the Lambda execution role needs the `logs:CreateLogGroup`, `logs:CreateLogStream`, and `logs:PutLogEvents` permissions (provided by the managed `AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole` policy).

## Why the other options are wrong

- **A. Amazon S3** — S3 is the *event source* that triggers the Lambda function (object upload events). S3 itself does not store Lambda runtime/application logs. S3 can store its own server access logs, but not Lambda function execution output.

- **B. AWS CloudTrail** — CloudTrail records **AWS API calls and management events** (e.g., who invoked `lambda:InvokeFunction`, who modified the function configuration). It does **not** capture the function's runtime stdout/stderr or the application-level errors raised inside the handler code. It cannot show, for example, a `KeyError` thrown when parsing metadata.

- **D. Amazon DynamoDB** — DynamoDB is the destination data store for the metadata. It does not store Lambda function logs. (DynamoDB Streams capture item-level changes, not Lambda code logs.)

## References

- [Sending Lambda function logs to CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/monitoring-cloudwatchlogs.html)
- [Logging and metrics for AWS Lambda — AWS Prescriptive Guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/implementing-logging-monitoring-cloudwatch/lambda-logging-metrics.html)
- [Configuring CloudWatch log groups for Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/monitoring-cloudwatchlogs-loggroups.html)

zh.question: 一个应用程序使用 Lambda 函数从上传到 S3 存储桶的文件中提取元数据；这些元数据存储在 Amazon DynamoDB 中。该应用程序开始出现异常行为，开发人员希望检查 Lambda 函数代码的日志以查找错误。基于此系统配置，开发人员应该在哪里找到这些日志？

options.A: 亚马逊S3
options.B: AWS CloudTrail
options.C: Amazon CloudWatch
options.D: Amazon DynamoDB

zh.explanation:
## 场景

一个无服务器应用程序使用由 S3 上传触发的 AWS Lambda 函数来提取元数据并将其写入 DynamoDB。该应用程序运行异常，开发人员需要检查 **Lambda 函数的执行日志** 来查找错误。

## 正确答案：C — Amazon CloudWatch

AWS Lambda 与 Amazon CloudWatch Logs 原生集成。默认情况下，Lambda 自动捕获所有函数调用的日志，并将其发送到 CloudWatch Logs，前提是您的函数执行角色具有必要的权限。这些日志默认存储在名为 /aws/lambda/<function-name> 的日志组中。

Lambda 自动将 Lambda 函数的标准输出和标准错误消息流式传输到 CloudWatch Logs，无需日志驱动程序。Lambda 还自动为运行 Lambda 函数的容器进行配置，使其能够在单独的日志流中输出日志消息。

这意味着 Lambda 代码中的任何 `print`、`console.log`、`logger.info` 或未处理的异常输出都将显示在 **CloudWatch Logs** 中的日志组 `/aws/lambda/<function-name>` 下，开发人员可以在该处搜索错误和堆栈跟踪。

要启用此功能，Lambda 执行角色需要 `logs:CreateLogGroup`、`logs:CreateLogStream` 和 `logs:PutLogEvents` 权限（由托管策略 `AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole` 提供）。

## 其他选项为什么不正确

- **A. Amazon S3** — S3 是触发 Lambda 函数的事件源（对象上传事件）。S3 本身不存储 Lambda 运行时/应用程序日志。S3 可以存储自己的服务器访问日志，但不能存储 Lambda 函数执行输出。

- **B. AWS CloudTrail** — CloudTrail 记录 **AWS API 调用和管理事件**（例如谁调用了 `lambda:InvokeFunction`，谁修改了函数配置）。它**不**捕获函数的运行时 stdout/stderr 或处理程序代码内引发的应用程序级错误。例如，它无法显示解析元数据时引发的 `KeyError`。

- **D. Amazon DynamoDB** — DynamoDB 是元数据的目标数据存储。它不存储 Lambda 函数日志。（DynamoDB Streams 捕获项目级别的更改，而不是 Lambda 代码日志。）

## 参考资源

- [将 Lambda 函数日志发送到 CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/monitoring-cloudwatchlogs.html)
- [AWS Lambda 的日志和指标 — AWS 规范指南](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/implementing-logging-monitoring-cloudwatch/lambda-logging-metrics.html)
- [为 Lambda 配置 CloudWatch 日志组](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/monitoring-cloudwatchlogs-loggroups.html)

en.question: A company is using an AWS Lambda function to process records from an Amazon Kinesis data stream. The company recently observed slow processing of the records. A developer notices that the iterator age metric for the function is increasing and that the Lambda run duration is constantly above normal. Which actions should the developer take to increase the processing speed? (Choose two.)

options.A: Increase the number of shards of the Kinesis data stream.
options.B: Decrease the timeout of the Lambda function.
options.C: Increase the memory that is allocated to the Lambda function.
options.D: Decrease the number of shards of the Kinesis data stream.
options.E: Increase the timeout of the Lambda function.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A Lambda function consumes records from a Kinesis Data Stream. The team observes:
- **IteratorAge** is increasing → consumer is falling behind the tip of the stream.
- **Lambda Duration** is constantly above normal → the function is slow per invocation.

The question asks which two actions speed up processing.

## Correct Answers: A and C

### A. Increase the number of shards of the Kinesis data stream ✅
A Lambda consumer processes one shard with one concurrent invocation (multiplied by the parallelization factor). A low number of shards in a stream increases a function's iterator age. Increasing the number of shards will directly increase the number of maximum concurrent Lambda function invocations which can increase your Kinesis processing throughput and decrease the Lambda Iterator Age. More shards = more parallel Lambda invocations consuming the stream simultaneously.

### C. Increase the memory allocated to the Lambda function ✅
In Lambda, CPU is allocated proportionally to memory. Allocating more memory therefore increases CPU and reduces the per-invocation duration. A high runtime duration increases a function's iterator age. Decreasing the duration increases a function's throughput, which decreases a function's iterator age. Allocate enough memory that your function will process records quickly enough to drive your IteratorAge back down to acceptable levels.

## Why the other options are wrong

### B. Decrease the Lambda timeout ❌
The timeout is the maximum time a function may run; it does not make code execute faster. Decreasing it would actually cause invocations to be killed before they complete, triggering retries on the same batch (Kinesis processes records sequentially per shard), which makes IteratorAge **worse**, not better.

### D. Decrease the number of shards ❌
This would reduce the maximum number of concurrent Lambda invocations consuming the stream, lowering throughput and *increasing* iterator age — the exact opposite of what is needed.

### E. Increase the Lambda timeout ❌
The problem is not that invocations are timing out; the problem is that runtime duration is consistently elevated and records are accumulating. A longer timeout lets a slow function run even longer per batch, making backlog **worse**. The fix is to make the function faster (more memory/CPU) and to add parallelism (more shards), not to grant it more time per invocation.

## References
- [Decrease your Lambda function's IteratorAge metric (AWS re:Post)](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/lambda-iterator-age)
- [Using AWS Lambda as a consumer for Amazon Kinesis (AWS Compute Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/using-aws-lambda-as-a-consumer-for-amazon-kinesis/)
- [Troubleshoot Kinesis Data Streams consumers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/troubleshooting-consumers.html)

zh.question: 一家公司使用 AWS Lambda 函数处理来自 Amazon Kinesis 数据流的记录。该公司最近发现记录处理速度很慢。一位开发人员注意到该函数的迭代器年龄指标不断增加，并且 Lambda 函数的运行时间也持续高于正常水平。开发人员应该采取哪些措施来提高处理速度？（选择两项。）

options.A: 增加 Kinesis 数据流的分片数量。
options.B: 减少 Lambda 函数的超时时间。
options.C: 增加分配给 Lambda 函数的内存。
options.D: 减少 Kinesis 数据流的分片数量。
options.E: 增加 Lambda 函数的超时时间。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

一个 Lambda 函数从 Kinesis Data Stream 消费记录。团队观察到：
- **IteratorAge** 不断增加 → 消费者落后于流的最新位置。
- **Lambda Duration** 持续高于正常水平 → 每次调用函数都很慢。

问题要求选择两个加速处理的操作。

## 正确答案：A 和 C

### A. 增加 Kinesis 数据流的分片数量 ✅
Lambda 消费者以一个分片配一个并发调用（乘以并行化因子）的方式处理。流中分片数量少会增加函数的迭代器年龄。增加分片数量将直接增加可并发运行的 Lambda 函数调用的最大数量，从而提高 Kinesis 处理吞吐量并降低 Lambda Iterator Age。更多分片 = 更多并行 Lambda 调用同时消费流。

### C. 增加分配给 Lambda 函数的内存 ✅
在 Lambda 中，CPU 与内存成比例分配。分配更多内存因此会增加 CPU 并减少每次调用的持续时间。运行时间长会增加函数的迭代器年龄。降低时间会增加函数的吞吐量，从而降低函数的迭代器年龄。分配足够的内存，使函数能够足够快地处理记录，以将 IteratorAge 恢复到可接受的水平。

## 其他选项为什么错误

### B. 降低 Lambda 超时 ❌
超时是函数可运行的最长时间；它不会让代码执行更快。降低超时实际上会导致调用在完成前被杀死，触发同一批次的重试（Kinesis 按分片顺序处理记录），使 IteratorAge **更差**，而非更好。

### D. 减少分片数量 ❌
这会降低消费流的最大并发 Lambda 调用数，降低吞吐量并*增加*迭代器年龄——这正好与所需的结果相反。

### E. 增加 Lambda 超时 ❌
问题不在于调用超时；问题是运行时间持续升高且记录在堆积。更长的超时会让慢函数每批处理运行更长时间，使积压**更差**。修复方法是让函数运行更快（更多内存/CPU）并增加并行性（更多分片），而不是给它每次调用更多时间。

## 参考资源
- [Decrease your Lambda function's IteratorAge metric (AWS re:Post)](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/lambda-iterator-age)
- [Using AWS Lambda as a consumer for Amazon Kinesis (AWS Compute Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/using-aws-lambda-as-a-consumer-for-amazon-kinesis/)
- [Troubleshoot Kinesis Data Streams consumers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/troubleshooting-consumers.html)

en.question: A company needs to harden its container images before the images are in a running state. The company's application uses Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) as an image registry. Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) for compute, and an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that orchestrates a continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) workflow. Dynamic application security testing occurs in the final stage of the pipeline after a new image is deployed to a development namespace in the EKS cluster. A developer needs to place an analysis stage before this deployment to analyze the container image earlier in the CI/CD pipeline. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

options.A: Build the container image and run the docker scan command locally. Mitigate any findings before pushing changes to the source code repository. Write a pre-commit hook that enforces the use of this workflow before commit.
options.B: Create a new CodePipeline stage that occurs after the container image is built. Configure ECR basic image scanning to scan on image push. Use an AWS Lambda function as the action provider. Configure the Lambda function to check the scan results and to fail the pipeline if there are findings.
options.C: Create a new CodePipeline stage that occurs after source code has been retrieved from its repository. Run a security scanner on the latest revision of the source code. Fail the pipeline if there are findings.
options.D: Add an action to the deployment stage of the pipeline so that the action occurs before the deployment to the EKS cluster. Configure ECR basic image scanning to scan on image push. Use an AWS Lambda function as the action provider. Configure the Lambda function to check the scan results and to fail the pipeline if there are findings.

en.explanation:
# Container Image Hardening in CodePipeline with ECR Scanning

## Scenario
A CI/CD pipeline orchestrated by AWS CodePipeline builds container images, pushes them to Amazon ECR, and deploys them to a development namespace in Amazon EKS. Today, dynamic application security testing (DAST) only happens in the *final* pipeline stage — **after** an image is already running in EKS. The developer wants to shift left: introduce an **analysis stage** that inspects the container image **before** the deployment stage, with the **most operational efficiency** (i.e., least custom infrastructure).

## Correct Answer: **B**

Add a **new CodePipeline stage immediately after the build stage** (when the image lands in ECR). Enable **ECR basic image scanning with scan-on-push**, and use an **AWS Lambda action provider** to read the scan results via `DescribeImageScanFindings` and fail the pipeline when findings exceed the threshold.

Why this is most operationally efficient:
- ECR basic scanning is a **native, no-cost** feature of ECR. With basic scanning, you configure your repositories to scan on push or you can perform manual scans and Amazon ECR provides a list of scan findings.
- Scan-on-push happens automatically every time the build stage pushes a new image, so no extra scan infrastructure (Clair, CodeBuild, third-party scanners) is required. You can either manually trigger the scanning of images that are stored on Amazon ECR or you can configure your container repository to scan images when you push them to the repository, e.g. `aws ecr put-image-scanning-configuration --repository-name name --image-scanning-configuration scanOnPush=true`.
- A Lambda **invoke** action in CodePipeline is the simplest serverless way to consume scan findings and `PutJobSuccessResult` / `PutJobFailureResult` back to the pipeline, blocking promotion to the EKS deployment stage when vulnerabilities are found.
- This places the gate **after build / before deploy**, which is exactly where the question wants the analysis stage.

## Why the other options are wrong

**A. Local `docker scan` + pre-commit hook.**
This relies on developer workstations and client-side hooks. Pre-commit hooks can be bypassed (`git commit --no-verify`), are not centrally enforced, and `docker scan` (Snyk-powered) requires per-developer authentication and licensing. It's neither integrated into the pipeline nor operationally efficient at scale.

**C. Scan source code right after the source stage.**
Source-code SAST is useful but does **not** analyze the *container image*. The question explicitly asks to "analyze the container image earlier in the CI/CD pipeline." OS-level packages, base-image CVEs, and layered dependencies inside the built image won't appear in raw source scans — exactly the class of issues that Amazon ECR uses AWS native technology with the Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) database to scan for operating system vulnerabilities is designed to catch.

**D. Add the scan action inside the deployment stage, before the EKS deploy step.**
Functionally similar to B, but architecturally weaker:
- The requirement explicitly says "*place an analysis **stage** before this deployment*" — that calls for a distinct stage, not an extra action bolted onto the deployment stage. Mixing a security gate into the deployment stage muddies stage semantics, transition approvals, and stage-level metrics/notifications.
- A dedicated stage is the standard CodePipeline pattern for a quality/security gate between build and deploy and aligns with the wording of the question.

For these reasons, **B** is the most operationally efficient and best-aligned answer.

## References
- [Amazon ECR image scanning](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-scanning.html)
- [Basic scanning in Amazon ECR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-scanning-basic.html)
- [Invoke an AWS Lambda function in a pipeline in CodePipeline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/actions-invoke-lambda-function.html)
- [Amazon ECR source action reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/action-reference-ECR.html)

zh.question: 一家公司需要在容器镜像投入运行状态之前对其进行安全加固。该公司的应用程序使用 Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) 作为镜像仓库，Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) 用于计算，并使用 AWS CodePipeline 流水线来编排持续集成和持续交付 (CI/CD) 工作流。动态应用程序安全测试在流水线的最后阶段进行，即在将新镜像部署到 EKS 集群中的开发命名空间之后。开发人员需要在部署之前添加一个分析阶段，以便在 CI/CD 流水线的早期阶段分析容器镜像。哪种解决方案能够以最高的运维效率满足这些要求？

options.A: 构建容器镜像并在本地运行 Docker 扫描命令。在将更改推送到源代码仓库之前，先解决发现的任何问题。编写一个 pre-commit 钩子，强制在提交之前使用此工作流程。
options.B: 创建一个新的 CodePipeline 阶段，该阶段在容器镜像构建完成后执行。配置 ECR 基本镜像扫描，使其在镜像推送时进行扫描。使用 AWS Lambda 函数作为操作提供程序。配置 Lambda 函数以检查扫描结果，并在发现问题时使管道失败。
options.C: 创建一个新的 CodePipeline 阶段，该阶段在从代码库检索源代码后执行。对最新版本的源代码运行安全扫描程序。如果发现任何安全问题，则终止该流程。
options.D: 在流水线的部署阶段添加一个操作，使其在部署到 EKS 集群之前执行。配置 ECR 基本镜像扫描，使其在镜像推送时进行扫描。使用 AWS Lambda 函数作为操作提供程序。配置 Lambda 函数以检查扫描结果，并在发现问题时使流水线失败。

zh.explanation:
# CodePipeline 中的容器镜像强化与 ECR 扫描

## 场景
由 AWS CodePipeline 编排的 CI/CD 管道构建容器镜像，将其推送到 Amazon ECR，然后部署到 Amazon EKS 中的开发命名空间。目前，动态应用安全测试 (DAST) 仅在*最后*的管道阶段进行——**在**镜像已在 EKS 中运行**之后**。开发者希望左移：引入一个**分析阶段**在部署阶段**之前**检查容器镜像，并具有**最高的操作效率**（即需要最少的自定义基础设施）。

## 正确答案：**B**

在构建阶段之后立即添加**新的 CodePipeline 阶段**（当镜像进入 ECR 时）。启用**ECR 基础镜像扫描及推送时扫描**，并使用 **AWS Lambda 操作提供程序**通过 `DescribeImageScanFindings` 读取扫描结果，当发现超过阈值时使管道失败。

为什么这是最具操作效率的方式：
- ECR 基础扫描是 ECR 的**原生、零成本**功能。通过基础扫描，您可以配置存储库在推送时扫描或执行手动扫描，Amazon ECR 将提供扫描发现列表。
- 推送时扫描会在每次构建阶段推送新镜像时自动进行，因此不需要额外的扫描基础设施（Clair、CodeBuild、第三方扫描器）。您可以手动触发存储在 Amazon ECR 中的镜像扫描，或者可以配置容器存储库在将镜像推送到存储库时扫描镜像，例如 `aws ecr put-image-scanning-configuration --repository-name name --image-scanning-configuration scanOnPush=true`。
- CodePipeline 中的 Lambda **invoke** 操作是使用扫描发现并通过 `PutJobSuccessResult` / `PutJobFailureResult` 返回给管道的最简单的无服务器方式，在发现漏洞时阻止升级到 EKS 部署阶段。
- 这将门控放在**构建之后/部署之前**，这正是问题所要求的分析阶段位置。

## 其他选项为何错误

**A. 本地 `docker scan` + 预提交钩子。**
这依赖于开发者工作站和客户端钩子。预提交钩子可以被绕过（`git commit --no-verify`），不是集中强制执行的，而且 `docker scan`（由 Snyk 驱动）需要每个开发者的身份验证和许可证。它既没有集成到管道中，也不能在规模化时实现操作效率。

**C. 在源阶段之后扫描源代码。**
源代码 SAST 很有用，但**不能**分析*容器镜像*。问题明确要求"更早地在 CI/CD 管道中分析容器镜像"。操作系统级包、基础镜像 CVE 和构建镜像内的分层依赖不会出现在原始源代码扫描中——这正是 Amazon ECR 使用 AWS 原生技术与常见漏洞和披露 (CVE) 数据库扫描操作系统漏洞设计用来捕获的问题类别。

**D. 在部署阶段内添加扫描操作，在 EKS 部署步骤之前。**
在功能上与 B 相似，但架构上较弱：
- 要求明确表示"*在此部署**阶段**之前放置一个分析阶段*"——这要求一个独立的阶段，而不是附加到部署阶段的额外操作。将安全门混合到部署阶段会模糊阶段语义、转换批准和阶段级别的指标/通知。
- 独立的阶段是 CodePipeline 中质量/安全门的标准模式，应在构建和部署之间，并与问题的措辞相符。

基于这些原因，**B** 是最具操作效率和最好对齐的答案。

## 参考资源
- [Amazon ECR 镜像扫描](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-scanning.html)
- [Amazon ECR 中的基础扫描](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-scanning-basic.html)
- [在 CodePipeline 中调用 AWS Lambda 函数](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/actions-invoke-lambda-function.html)
- [Amazon ECR 源操作参考](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/action-reference-ECR.html)

en.question: A developer is testing a new file storage application that uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution to serve content from an Amazon S3 bucket. The distribution accesses the S3 bucket by using an origin access identity (OAI). The S3 bucket's permissions explicitly deny access to all other users. The application prompts users to authenticate on a login page and then uses signed cookies to allow users to access their personal storage directories. The developer has configured the distribution to use its default cache behavior with restricted viewer access and has set the origin to point to the S3 bucket. However, when the developer tries to navigate to the login page, the developer receives a 403 Forbidden error. The developer needs to implement a solution to allow unauthenticated access to the login page. The solution also must keep all private content secure. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Add a second cache behavior to the distribution with the same origin as the default cache behavior. Set the path pattern for the second cache behavior to the path of the login page, and make viewer access unrestricted. Keep the default cache behavior's settings unchanged.
options.B: Add a second cache behavior to the distribution with the same origin as the default cache behavior. Set the path pattern for the second cache behavior to *, and make viewer access restricted. Change the default cache behavior's path pattern to the path of the login page, and make viewer access unrestricted.
options.C: Add a second origin as a failover origin to the default cache behavior. Point the failover origin to the S3 bucket. Set the path pattern for the primary origin to *, and make viewer access restricted. Set the path pattern for the failover origin to the path of the login page, and make viewer access unrestricted.
options.D: Add a bucket policy to the S3 bucket to allow read access. Set the resource on the policy to the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the login page object in the S3 bucket. Add a CloudFront function to the default cache behavior to redirect unauthorized requests to the login page's S3 URL.

en.explanation:
# CloudFront Cache Behaviors for Public Login + Private Content

## Scenario
A CloudFront distribution serves an S3 bucket via OAI. The default cache behavior is configured with **Restrict Viewer Access** (signed cookies/URLs required). Because the user has not yet authenticated when visiting the login page, no signed cookie exists, so CloudFront returns **403 Forbidden** for the login page request.

The developer must allow **unauthenticated** access to the login page only, while keeping all other content protected by signed cookies.

## Why A is correct
The proper pattern is to add a **second cache behavior** with a more specific path pattern that matches the login page, point it to the same S3 origin, and set **Restrict Viewer Access = No** for that behavior. The default cache behavior (`*`) keeps Restrict Viewer Access = Yes so that all other content still requires a valid signed cookie.

Key facts that support this:
- Signers are associated with cache behaviors, which allows you to require signed URLs or signed cookies for some files and not for others in the same distribution.
- When CloudFront receives a viewer request, the requested path is compared with path patterns in the order in which cache behaviors are listed in the distribution.
- The path pattern for the default cache behavior is * and cannot be changed. If the request for an object does not match the path pattern for any cache behaviors, CloudFront applies the behavior in the default cache behavior.
- Typically, your CloudFront distribution will have at least two cache behaviors, one that doesn't require authentication and one that does. The error page for the secure portion of the site includes a redirector or a link to a login page.

This is exactly the architecture documented by AWS for signed-cookie-protected sites — add a non-restricted behavior for `/login` (and any assets it needs), and leave the default `*` behavior restricted.

## Why the other options are wrong

**B. Change the default cache behavior's path pattern to the login page path.**
The path pattern for the default cache behavior is `*` and **cannot be changed** — see The path pattern for the default cache behavior is * and cannot be changed. Additionally, making the default behavior unrestricted would expose all private content.

**C. Add a failover origin for the login page.**
Origin failover is triggered only when the **primary origin returns specific failure responses** (e.g., 5xx, 404 from the primary), not based on path. You also cannot assign a path pattern to a failover origin — path patterns belong to cache behaviors, not origins. This does not solve the authentication problem.

**D. Bucket policy allowing public read on the login page object + CloudFront Function redirect.**
This breaks the OAI-only access model. The requirement explicitly states that the S3 bucket denies access to all other principals; opening public read on an object bypasses CloudFront and contradicts the secure-delivery design. The CloudFront Function redirect to the S3 URL would expose the bucket directly, and the original 403 on `/login` through CloudFront would still occur because the default behavior still requires a signed cookie.

## Reference
- [Cache behavior settings - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/DownloadDistValuesCacheBehavior.html)
- [Specify signers that can create signed URLs and signed cookies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-trusted-signers.html)
- [Use signed cookies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-signed-cookies.html)
- [CacheBehavior - CloudFront API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cloudfront/latest/APIReference/API_CacheBehavior.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在测试一款新的文件存储应用程序，该应用程序使用 Amazon CloudFront 分发从 Amazon S3 存储桶提供内容。该分发通过源访问身份 (OAI) 访问 S3 存储桶。S3 存储桶的权限明确拒绝所有其他用户的访问。该应用程序会提示用户在登录页面上进行身份验证，然后使用签名 cookie 允许用户访问其个人存储目录。开发人员已将分发配置为使用其默认缓存行为并限制查看器访问权限，并将源设置为指向 S3 存储桶。但是，当开发人员尝试导航到登录页面时，会收到 403 Forbidden 错误。开发人员需要实现一个解决方案，允许未经身份验证的用户访问登录页面。该解决方案还必须确保所有私有内容的安全。哪个解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 在分发包中添加第二个缓存行为，其源与默认缓存行为相同。将第二个缓存行为的路径模式设置为登录页面的路径，并允许查看者无限制访问。保持默认缓存行为的设置不变。
options.B: 在分发包中添加第二个缓存行为，其源与默认缓存行为相同。将第二个缓存行为的路径模式设置为 *，并限制查看器访问权限。将默认缓存行为的路径模式更改为登录页面的路径，并取消对查看器访问权限的限制。
options.C: 添加第二个源作为默认缓存行为的故障转移源。将故障转移源指向 S3 存储桶。将主源的路径模式设置为 *，并限制查看器访问权限。将故障转移源的路径模式设置为登录页面的路径，并解除对查看器的访问限制。
options.D: 为 S3 存储桶添加存储桶策略，允许读取访问权限。将策略中的资源设置为 S3 存储桶中登录页面对象的 Amazon 资源名称 (ARN)。向默认缓存行为添加 CloudFront 函数，将未经授权的请求重定向到登录页面的 S3 URL。

zh.explanation:
# CloudFront 缓存行为：公开登录页面 + 私有内容

## 场景
CloudFront 分布式网络通过 OAI 向 S3 存储桶提供服务。默认缓存行为配置了**限制查看者访问**（需要签名 Cookie/URL）。由于用户在访问登录页面时尚未进行身份验证，因此不存在签名 Cookie，CloudFront 对登录页面请求返回 **403 Forbidden**。

开发者必须允许**未经身份验证的**访问登录页面，同时保持所有其他内容受签名 Cookie 保护。

## 为什么 A 是正确的
正确的模式是添加**第二个缓存行为**，使用更具体的路径模式来匹配登录页面，将其指向同一个 S3 源，并针对该行为设置**限制查看者访问 = 否**。默认缓存行为 (`*`) 保持"限制查看者访问 = 是"，以便所有其他内容仍然需要有效的签名 Cookie。

支持此方案的关键事实：
- 签名者与缓存行为相关联，这样您可以要求对同一分布式网络中的某些文件使用签名 URL 或签名 Cookie，而对其他文件则不需要。
- 当 CloudFront 收到查看者请求时，请求的路径将与缓存行为中列出的路径模式按顺序进行比较。
- 默认缓存行为的路径模式是 *，无法更改。如果对象请求与任何缓存行为的路径模式不匹配，CloudFront 将应用默认缓存行为中的行为。
- 通常，CloudFront 分布式网络至少有两个缓存行为，一个不需要身份验证，另一个需要。安全部分的错误页面包含重定向器或指向登录页面的链接。

这正是 AWS 为签名 Cookie 保护的站点记录的架构——为 `/login`（及其需要的任何资源）添加非限制行为，而保持默认 `*` 行为受限。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

**B. 将默认缓存行为的路径模式更改为登录页面路径。**
默认缓存行为的路径模式是 `*`，**无法更改**——参见 默认缓存行为的路径模式是 *，无法更改。 此外，使默认行为不受限制会暴露所有私有内容。

**C. 为登录页面添加故障转移源。**
故障转移仅在**主源返回特定失败响应**时触发（例如，来自主源的 5xx、404），而不是基于路径。您也无法为故障转移源分配路径模式——路径模式属于缓存行为，而不是源。这不能解决身份验证问题。

**D. 允许在登录页面对象上公开读取的存储桶策略 + CloudFront 函数重定向。**
这破坏了仅限 OAI 访问的模型。要求明确指出 S3 存储桶拒绝访问所有其他主体；在对象上开放公开读取会绕过 CloudFront，与安全交付设计相矛盾。CloudFront 函数重定向到 S3 URL 会暴露存储桶，而且通过 CloudFront 对 `/login` 的原始 403 仍然会发生，因为默认行为仍然需要签名 Cookie。

## 参考资源
- [缓存行为设置 - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/DownloadDistValuesCacheBehavior.html)

en.question: A developer is using AWS Amplify Hosting to build and deploy an application. The developer is receiving an increased number of bug reports from users. The developer wants to add end-to-end testing to the application to eliminate as many bugs as possible before the bugs reach production. Which solution should the developer implement to meet these requirements?

options.A: Run the amplify add test command in the Amplify CLI.
options.B: Create unit tests in the application. Deploy the unit tests by using the amplify push command in the Amplify CLI.
options.C: Add a test phase to the amplify.yml build settings for the application.
options.D: Add a test phase to the aws-exports.js file for the application.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A developer using **AWS Amplify Hosting** wants to add **end-to-end (E2E) testing** to the CI/CD pipeline so bugs are caught before they reach production.

## Correct Answer: C — Add a test phase to the `amplify.yml` build settings

Amplify Hosting's build specification (`amplify.yml`) supports a dedicated `test` phase. You can run end-to-end (E2E) tests in the test phase of your Amplify app to catch regressions before pushing code to production. The test phase can be configured in the build specification YAML. Currently, you can run only the Cypress testing framework during a build.

You can add Cypress tests to an existing app by updating the app's build settings in the Amplify console. The build specification YAML contains a collection of build commands and related settings that Amplify uses to run your build. Use the test step to run any test commands at build time.

Example structure of the test phase in `amplify.yml`:

```yaml
version: 1
frontend:
  phases:
    preBuild:
      commands:
        - npm ci
    build:
      commands:
        - npm run build
test:
  phases:
    preTest:
      commands:
        - npm ci
        - npm install -g pm2 wait-on
        - npm install mocha mochawesome mochawesome-merge mochawesome-report-generator
        - pm2 start npm -- start
        - wait-on http://localhost:3000
    test:
      commands:
        - 'npx cypress run --reporter mochawesome ...'
    postTest:
      commands:
        - npx mochawesome-merge ...
  artifacts:
    baseDirectory: cypress
    configFilePath: '**/mochawesome.json'
    files:
      - '**/*.png'
      - '**/*.mp4'
```

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A. `amplify add test` CLI command** — This command does not exist in the Amplify CLI. The Amplify CLI uses categories like `add auth`, `add api`, `add storage`, `add hosting`, etc., but there is no `add test` category to wire up E2E testing.

- **B. Create unit tests and deploy with `amplify push`** — Two problems: (1) The question explicitly asks for **end-to-end** tests, not unit tests. (2) `amplify push` is used to provision/update backend resources (Cognito, AppSync, Lambda, DynamoDB, etc.) defined locally — it is not a mechanism for running tests as part of the hosting build pipeline. To run tests during the Amplify Hosting build, you must configure the `test` phase in `amplify.yml`.

- **D. Add a test phase to `aws-exports.js`** — `aws-exports.js` is an auto-generated configuration file containing endpoints, region, pool IDs, etc., that the front-end uses to connect to AWS backend services. It is not a build specification and has no concept of build/test phases.

## References

- [Setting up end-to-end Cypress tests for your Amplify application](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/userguide/running-tests.html)
- [Build specification reference (amplify.yml)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/userguide/yml-specification-syntax.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在使用 AWS Amplify Hosting 构建和部署应用程序。他收到的用户错误报告数量不断增加。为了在错误进入生产环境之前尽可能多地消除错误，开发人员希望为应用程序添加端到端测试。为了满足这些要求，开发人员应该实施哪种解决方案？

options.A: 在 Amplify CLI 中运行 amplify add test 命令。
options.B: 在应用程序中创建单元测试。使用 Amplify CLI 中的 amplify push 命令部署单元测试。
options.C: 在应用程序的 amplify.yml 构建设置中添加测试阶段。
options.D: 为应用程序的 aws-exports.js 文件添加测试阶段。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

一位使用 **AWS Amplify Hosting** 的开发人员想在 CI/CD 管道中添加**端到端 (E2E) 测试**，以便在代码到达生产环境之前捕获缺陷。

## 正确答案: C — 在 `amplify.yml` 构建设置中添加测试阶段

Amplify Hosting 的构建规范 (`amplify.yml`) 支持专门的 `test` 阶段。您可以在 Amplify 应用的测试阶段运行端到端 (E2E) 测试，在将代码推送到生产环境之前捕获回归。测试阶段可以在构建规范 YAML 中配置。目前，您只能在构建过程中运行 Cypress 测试框架。

您可以通过在 Amplify 控制台中更新应用的构建设置，将 Cypress 测试添加到现有应用。构建规范 YAML 包含一组构建命令和相关设置，Amplify 使用它们来运行您的构建。使用测试步骤在构建时运行任何测试命令。

`amplify.yml` 中测试阶段的结构示例：

```yaml
version: 1
frontend:
  phases:
    preBuild:
      commands:
        - npm ci
    build:
      commands:
        - npm run build
test:
  phases:
    preTest:
      commands:
        - npm ci
        - npm install -g pm2 wait-on
        - npm install mocha mochawesome mochawesome-merge mochawesome-report-generator
        - pm2 start npm -- start
        - wait-on http://localhost:3000
    test:
      commands:
        - 'npx cypress run --reporter mochawesome ...'
    postTest:
      commands:
        - npx mochawesome-merge ...
  artifacts:
    baseDirectory: cypress
    configFilePath: '**/mochawesome.json'
    files:
      - '**/*.png'
      - '**/*.mp4'
```

## 其他选项为何错误

- **A. `amplify add test` CLI 命令** — 此命令在 Amplify CLI 中不存在。Amplify CLI 使用诸如 `add auth`、`add api`、`add storage`、`add hosting` 等类别，但没有 `add test` 类别用于连接 E2E 测试。

- **B. 创建单元测试并使用 `amplify push` 部署** — 两个问题：(1) 问题明确要求**端到端**测试，而不是单元测试。(2) `amplify push` 用于配置/更新本地定义的后端资源 (Cognito、AppSync、Lambda、DynamoDB 等) — 它不是在托管构建管道中运行测试的机制。要在 Amplify Hosting 构建期间运行测试，您必须在 `amplify.yml` 中配置 `test` 阶段。

- **D. 在 `aws-exports.js` 中添加测试阶段** — `aws-exports.js` 是自动生成的配置文件，包含端点、区域、池 ID 等，前端使用这些信息连接到 AWS 后端服务。它不是构建规范，也没有构建/测试阶段的概念。

## 参考资源

- [为 Amplify 应用设置端到端 Cypress 测试](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/userguide/running-tests.html)
- [构建规范参考 (amplify.yml)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/userguide/yml-specification-syntax.html)

en.question: An ecommerce company is using an AWS Lambda function behind Amazon API Gateway as its application tier. To process orders during checkout, the application calls a POST API from the frontend. The POST API invokes the Lambda function asynchronously. In rare situations, the application has not processed orders. The Lambda application logs show no errors or failures. What should a developer do to solve this problem?

options.A: Inspect the frontend logs for API failures. Call the POST API manually by using the requests from the log file.
options.B: Create and inspect the Lambda dead-letter queue. Troubleshoot the failed functions. Reprocess the events.
options.C: Inspect the Lambda logs in Amazon CloudWatch for possible errors. Fix the errors.
options.D: Make sure that caching is disabled for the POST API in API Gateway.

en.explanation:
# Lambda Asynchronous Invocation – Missing Orders Troubleshooting

## Scenario
An ecommerce app uses API Gateway → Lambda (asynchronous invocation) for order processing. Occasionally orders are not processed, yet the Lambda CloudWatch logs show no errors or failures. The developer needs to find a way to capture and recover the lost events.

## Correct Answer: B – Create and inspect the Lambda Dead-Letter Queue

When Lambda is invoked asynchronously, the event is placed in an internal queue managed by Lambda. If function execution fails, [Lambda handles errors and retries with asynchronous invocation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-async-error-handling.html) — by default, [Lambda retries a failed asynchronous invocation up to two times](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-retries.html) with delays between attempts. After all retries are exhausted (or for throttling/system errors after up to 6 hours), the event is **discarded**.

Critically, events can also be **dropped silently** without obvious function-level errors:
- Throttling when concurrency is exceeded (the AsyncEventsDropped CloudWatch metric counts these).
- Events expiring in the internal async queue.
- Reserved concurrency set to zero.

According to [AWS – Capturing records of Lambda asynchronous invocations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-async-retain-records.html), a Dead-Letter Queue (SQS or SNS) is used "when an event fails all processing attempts or expires without being processed." The DLQ stores the original event payload along with attributes like RequestID, ErrorCode, and ErrorMessage, allowing the developer to **troubleshoot the root cause and reprocess the lost orders** — exactly what option B describes.

The [AWS announcement for Lambda DLQ support](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2016/12/aws-lambda-supports-dead-letter-queues/) confirms Lambda writes the event object to the DLQ after the standard retry policy is exhausted.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

**A. Inspect frontend logs / replay POST manually** – Asynchronous API Gateway → Lambda integration returns HTTP 202 to the caller as soon as Lambda accepts the event into its internal queue. The frontend would not see any failure indication for events that were accepted but later dropped during async processing. Replaying calls also risks duplicate orders.

**C. Inspect Lambda CloudWatch logs for errors** – The question explicitly states the logs show no errors or failures. Events dropped due to throttling, concurrency exhaustion, or queue expiration may never produce execution log entries (because the function never actually ran for those events). Inspecting logs that contain no errors gives nothing actionable.

**D. Disable API Gateway caching for the POST API** – API Gateway caching applies to GET methods (and method-level cache keys), not POST. POST requests are not cached by default and disabling cache would not affect missing async invocations. This is a distractor.

## Key AWS Reference Points
- [How Lambda handles errors and retries with asynchronous invocation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-async-error-handling.html)
- [Capturing records of Lambda asynchronous invocations (DLQ & Destinations)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-async-retain-records.html)
- [Understanding retry behavior in Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-retries.html)
- [Implementing error handling for Lambda asynchronous invocations](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/implementing-error-handling-for-aws-lambda-asynchronous-invocations/)

## Conclusion
For asynchronous Lambda invocations where events occasionally vanish without log entries, configuring a **Dead-Letter Queue** is the standard AWS-recommended pattern to capture, troubleshoot, and reprocess the lost events. **Answer: B**.

zh.question: 一家电商公司使用位于 Amazon API Gateway 后端的 AWS Lambda 函数作为其应用层。为了在结账过程中处理订单，该应用会从前端调用 POST API。POST API 会异步调用 Lambda 函数。在极少数情况下，应用未能处理订单。Lambda 应用日志中没有显示任何错误或故障。开发人员应该如何解决这个问题？

options.A: 检查前端日志，查找 API 故障。使用日志文件中的请求手动调用 POST API。
options.B: 创建并检查 Lambda 死信队列。排查失败的函数。重新处理事件。
options.C: 检查 Amazon CloudWatch 中的 Lambda 日志，查找可能存在的错误。修复这些错误。
options.D: 确保 API 网关中 POST API 的缓存已禁用。

zh.explanation:
# Lambda 异步调用 – 丢失订单故障排查

## 场景
一个电商应用使用 API Gateway → Lambda（异步调用）处理订单。偶尔订单无法处理，但 Lambda CloudWatch 日志中没有显示任何错误或失败。开发人员需要找到一种方法来捕获和恢复丢失的事件。

## 正确答案：B – 创建并检查 Lambda Dead-Letter Queue

Lambda 异步调用时，事件被放入由 Lambda 管理的内部队列。如果函数执行失败，[Lambda 会处理错误并重试异步调用](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-async-error-handling.html) — 默认情况下，[Lambda 最多重试失败的异步调用两次](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-retries.html)，重试之间有延迟。在所有重试耗尽后（或对于限流/系统错误在最多 6 小时后），事件被**丢弃**。

关键是，事件也可能**无声地丢失**，而没有明显的函数级错误：
- 超过并发时的限流（AsyncEventsDropped CloudWatch 指标计数这些）。
- 事件在内部异步队列中过期。
- 预留并发设置为零。

根据 [AWS – 捕获 Lambda 异步调用记录](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-async-retain-records.html)，Dead-Letter Queue（SQS 或 SNS）用于"在事件失败所有处理尝试或在处理前过期时"。DLQ 存储原始事件有效负载以及 RequestID、ErrorCode 和 ErrorMessage 等属性，允许开发人员**排查根本原因并重新处理丢失的订单** — 完全符合选项 B 的描述。

[Lambda DLQ 支持的 AWS 公告](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2016/12/aws-lambda-supports-dead-letter-queues/)确认 Lambda 在标准重试策略耗尽后将事件对象写入 DLQ。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

**A. 检查前端日志 / 手动重放 POST** – API Gateway → Lambda 异步集成在 Lambda 接受事件进入其内部队列后立即返回 HTTP 202 给调用者。前端不会看到在异步处理期间被接受但后来丢失的事件的任何失败指示。重放调用也会冒订单重复的风险。

**C. 检查 Lambda CloudWatch 日志以查找错误** – 问题明确说明日志没有显示错误或失败。由于限流、并发耗尽或队列过期而丢失的事件可能从不产生执行日志条目（因为函数实际上从未为这些事件运行）。检查不包含错误的日志无法提供任何可操作的信息。

**D. 为 POST API 禁用 API Gateway 缓存** – API Gateway 缓存适用于 GET 方法（和方法级缓存键），不适用于 POST。默认情况下，POST 请求不被缓存，禁用缓存不会影响丢失的异步调用。这是一个干扰项。

## 关键 AWS 参考点
- [Lambda 如何处理异步调用的错误和重试](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-async-error-handling.html)
- [捕获 Lambda 异步调用记录（DLQ 和 Destinations）](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-async-retain-records.html)
- [理解 Lambda 中的重试行为](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-retries.html)
- [为 Lambda 异步调用实现错误处理](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/implementing-error-handling-for-aws-lambda-asynchronous-invocations/)

## 结论
对于事件偶尔消失且无日志条目的 Lambda 异步调用，配置 **Dead-Letter Queue** 是 AWS 推荐的标准模式，用于捕获、排查和重新处理丢失的事件。**答案：B**。

en.question: A company is building a web application on AWS. When a customer sends a request, the application will generate reports and then make the reports available to the customer within one hour. Reports should be accessible to the customer for 8 hours. Some reports are larger than 1 MB. Each report is unique to the customer. The application should delete all reports that are older than 2 days. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Generate the reports and then store the reports as Amazon DynamoDB items that have a specified TTL. Generate a URL that retrieves the reports from DynamoDB. Provide the URL to customers through the web application.
options.B: Generate the reports and then store the reports in an Amazon S3 bucket that uses server-side encryption. Attach the reports to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) message. Subscribe the customer to email notifications from Amazon SNS.
options.C: Generate the reports and then store the reports in an Amazon S3 bucket that uses server-side encryption. Generate a presigned URL that contains an expiration date Provide the URL to customers through the web application. Add S3 Lifecycle configuration rules to the S3 bucket to delete old reports.
options.D: Generate the reports and then store the reports in an Amazon RDS database with a date stamp. Generate an URL that retrieves the reports from the RDS database. Provide the URL to customers through the web application. Schedule an hourly AWS Lambda function to delete database records that have expired date stamps.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A web application generates per-customer reports that:
- Must be available within 1 hour of the request
- Must be accessible to the customer for **8 hours**
- May exceed **1 MB** in size
- Must be deleted automatically after **2 days**

The goal is the solution with the **least operational overhead**.

## Correct Answer: C

Store the reports in an S3 bucket with server-side encryption, hand the customer a **presigned URL** with an expiration time, and use an **S3 Lifecycle rule** to expire (delete) objects after 2 days.

**Why C fits:**

- **S3 handles large objects easily.** S3 supports objects up to 5 TB, so reports >1 MB are no problem.
- **Presigned URLs give time-limited access.** By default, all S3 objects are private. Only the object owner has permission to access them. However, the object owner can optionally share objects with others by creating a pre-signed URL, using their security credentials, to grant time-limited permission to download the objects. Using the SDK/CLI, the expiration time can be set as high as 7 days, which easily covers the 8‑hour requirement.
- **Lifecycle rules automate deletion.** S3 lifecycle expiration policies solve this by automatically deleting objects after a specified number of days. Setting `Expiration: { Days: 2 }` deletes reports after 2 days with no custom code, minimizing operational overhead.
- **Server-side encryption** protects the data at rest with no additional code.

```json
{
  "Rules": [{
    "ID": "expire-reports",
    "Status": "Enabled",
    "Filter": {"Prefix": "reports/"},
    "Expiration": {"Days": 2}
  }]
}
```

## Why the other options are wrong

**A. DynamoDB with TTL** — DynamoDB items have a hard limit of **400 KB** per item, so reports larger than 1 MB cannot be stored as a single item. You would have to chunk reports across items and reassemble them, which is complex and not the intended use of DynamoDB. Additionally, DynamoDB does not natively offer a "URL to retrieve an item" — you would need to build an API/Lambda layer. This adds operational overhead and violates a hard service limit.

**B. S3 + SNS email with attachment** — Amazon SNS does **not support file attachments**. SNS messages are limited to 256 KB of text payload, and email delivery via SNS is plain text only. There is also no mechanism here to delete reports after 2 days, so the lifecycle requirement is unmet.

**D. RDS + hourly Lambda cleanup** — Storing large binary report files in a relational database is inefficient and expensive (BLOB storage in RDS is not cost-effective compared to S3). RDS does not natively produce shareable download URLs, so additional application code is required to stream the report. Writing and operating a scheduled Lambda to delete expired rows is more operational overhead than an S3 Lifecycle rule, which AWS manages for you.

## References

- [Sharing objects with presigned URLs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/ShareObjectPreSignedURL.html)
- [Download and upload objects with presigned URLs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/using-presigned-url.html)
- [Expiring objects (S3 Lifecycle)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/lifecycle-expire-general-considerations.html)
- [DynamoDB service quotas (400 KB item size)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/ServiceQuotas.html)

zh.question: 一家公司正在 AWS 上构建一个 Web 应用程序。当客户发送请求时，该应用程序会生成报告，并在 1 小时内将报告提供给客户。报告应在 8 小时内对客户有效。部分报告大于 1 MB。每份报告都对应一位客户。应用程序应删除所有超过 2 天的报告。哪种解决方案能够以最小的运维开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 生成报告，然后将报告存储为具有指定生存时间 (TTL) 的 Amazon DynamoDB 项。生成一个用于从 DynamoDB 检索报告的 URL。通过 Web 应用程序将此 URL 提供给客户。
options.B: 生成报告，然后将报告存储在使用服务器端加密的 Amazon S3 存储桶中。将报告附加到 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 消息中。让客户订阅来自 Amazon SNS 的电子邮件通知。
options.C: 生成报告，然后将报告存储在启用服务器端加密的 Amazon S3 存储桶中。生成包含过期日期的预签名 URL，并通过 Web 应用程序将此 URL 提供给客户。向 S3 存储桶添加 S3 生命周期配置规则，以删除旧报告。
options.D: 生成报告，然后将报告存储在带有日期戳的 Amazon RDS 数据库中。生成一个 URL，用于从 RDS 数据库检索报告。通过 Web 应用程序将此 URL 提供给客户。安排一个 AWS Lambda 函数每小时运行一次，以删除日期戳已过期的数据库记录。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

Web 应用程序生成每个客户的报告，这些报告需要：
- 在请求后的 **1 小时内**可用
- 客户可访问 **8 小时**
- 可能超过 **1 MB** 的大小
- 在 **2 天后**自动删除

目标是找到**运维开销最少**的解决方案。

## 正确答案：C

将报告存储在 S3 存储桶中，启用服务器端加密，向客户提供带有过期时间的**预签名 URL**，并使用 **S3 生命周期规则**在 2 天后过期（删除）对象。

**为什么 C 符合要求：**

- **S3 轻松处理大型对象。** S3 支持高达 5 TB 的对象，因此超过 1 MB 的报告不成问题。
- **预签名 URL 提供时间限制的访问。** 默认情况下，所有 S3 对象都是私有的。只有对象所有者有权访问它们。但是，对象所有者可以选择通过创建预签名 URL 并使用其安全凭证与他人共享对象，以授予时间限制的下载对象权限。 使用 SDK/CLI，过期时间可以设置为最长 7 天，这完全满足 8 小时的要求。
- **生命周期规则自动删除。** S3 生命周期过期策略通过在指定天数后自动删除对象来解决这个问题。 设置 `Expiration: { Days: 2 }` 可在 2 天后删除报告，无需自定义代码，最大程度地降低运维开销。
- **服务器端加密**无需额外代码即可保护静止数据。

```json
{
  "Rules": [{
    "ID": "expire-reports",
    "Status": "Enabled",
    "Filter": {"Prefix": "reports/"},
    "Expiration": {"Days": 2}
  }]
}
```

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

**A. DynamoDB 加 TTL** — DynamoDB 项目的硬限制为每项 **400 KB**，因此超过 1 MB 的报告无法存储为单个项目。您必须将报告分块存储在多个项目中并重新组装，这很复杂且不是 DynamoDB 的预期用途。此外，DynamoDB 不原生提供"检索项目的 URL"机制——您需要构建 API/Lambda 层。这增加了运维开销并违反了硬性服务限制。

**B. S3 + SNS 电子邮件附件** — Amazon SNS **不支持文件附件**。SNS 消息限制为 256 KB 的文本负载，通过 SNS 的电子邮件传递仅限纯文本。此外，此方案中没有机制在 2 天后删除报告，因此未满足生命周期要求。

**D. RDS + 每小时 Lambda 清理** — 在关系数据库中存储大型二进制报告文件效率低且成本高（RDS 中的 BLOB 存储相比 S3 的成本效益差）。RDS 不原生生成可共享的下载 URL，因此需要额外的应用程序代码来流式传输报告。编写和操作计划的 Lambda 来删除过期行比 AWS 为您管理的 S3 生命周期规则更需要运维开销。

## 参考资源

- [使用预签名 URL 共享对象](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/ShareObjectPreSignedURL.html)
- [使用预签名 URL 下载和上传对象](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/using-presigned-url.html)
- [过期对象（S3 生命周期）](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/lifecycle-expire-general-considerations.html)
- [DynamoDB 服务配额（400 KB 项目大小）](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/ServiceQuotas.html)

en.question: A company has deployed an application on AWS Elastic Beanstalk. The company has configured the Auto Scaling group that is associated with the Elastic Beanstalk environment to have five Amazon EC2 instances. If the capacity is fewer than four EC2 instances during the deployment, application performance degrades. The company is using the all-at-once deployment policy. What is the MOST cost-effective way to solve the deployment issue?

options.A: Change the Auto Scaling group to six desired instances.
options.B: Change the deployment policy to traffic splitting. Specify an evaluation time of 1 hour.
options.C: Change the deployment policy to rolling with additional batch. Specify a batch size of 1.
options.D: Change the deployment policy to rolling. Specify a batch size of 2.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

An Elastic Beanstalk environment runs 5 EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The application degrades if fewer than 4 instances are available during deployment. The current "all-at-once" policy takes all instances out of service simultaneously. We need the **most cost-effective** deployment policy change that keeps at least 4 instances serving traffic.
