A NAT gateway is required to perform source address translation from the private IP to a public IP.

## Reference architecture

```
Lambda (private subnet)  --->  Route table 0.0.0.0/0 -> NAT GW  --->  NAT GW (public subnet)  --->  IGW  --->  Internet
```

## Sources

- [Enable internet access for VPC-connected Lambda functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-vpc-internet.html)
- [Giving Lambda functions access to resources in an Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-vpc.html)
- [Give internet access to a Lambda function in a VPC (AWS re:Post)](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/internet-access-lambda-function)

zh.question: 一位开发人员创建了一个 AWS Lambda 函数，用于从多个公共 API 端点检索和分组数据。该 Lambda 函数已更新并配置为连接到 VPC 的私有子网。VPC 已连接互联网网关。VPC 使用默认的网络 ACL 和安全组配置。开发人员发现 Lambda 函数无法再访问公共 API。开发人员已确保公共 API 可访问，但 Lambda 函数仍然无法连接到该 API。开发人员应该如何解决此连接问题？

options.A: 确保网络 ACL 允许出站流量访问公共互联网。
options.B: 确保安全组允许出站流量访问公共互联网。
options.C: 确保私有子网的出站流量路由到公共 NAT 网关。
options.D: 确保私有子网的出站流量路由到新的互联网网关。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

一个 Lambda 函数之前可以访问公网（非 VPC Lambda 的默认行为）。开发者将该函数附加到 VPC 中的一个**私有子网**。虽然互联网网关已附加到 VPC，但 Lambda 函数现在无法再访问公共 API。

## 问题原因

默认情况下，Lambda 函数可以访问公网。当您将函数附加到 VPC 时，它只能访问该 VPC 内可用的资源。要使函数访问互联网，您还需要配置 VPC 以具有互联网访问权限。

私有子网按照定义没有直接路由到互联网网关。IPv4 互联网流量 (0.0.0.0/0) 必须路由到与公有子网关联的 NAT 网关。这意味着子网是可以通过 NAT 网关访问互联网的私有子网。

## 正确答案：C

私有子网的路由表必须有一条默认路由 (`0.0.0.0/0`) 指向驻留在公有子网中的 **NAT 网关**（该公有子网本身路由到互联网网关）。将函数连接到公有子网不会使其获得互联网访问权限，因此 VPC 附加的 Lambda + 互联网访问的唯一正确架构是私有子网 → NAT 网关 → IGW。

## 其他选项为什么错误

- **A. 网络 ACL 出站规则** — 错误。问题中指出 VPC 使用**默认**网络 ACL。VPC 中的默认网络 ACL 允许所有入站和出站流量。因此网络 ACL 不会阻止流量。

- **B. 安全组出站规则** — 错误。问题中指出默认安全组配置。默认安全组允许所有出站流量，因此这不是失败的原因。

- **D. 路由到新的互联网网关** — 错误。除非每个 Lambda ENI 都有公有 IP（而 Lambda ENI **没有**公有 IP），否则您不能仅通过将其路由表指向 IGW 来使私有子网变为"公有"。VPC 中的 Lambda 函数仅被分配私有 IP，因此 IGW 单独无法提供互联网访问。需要 NAT 网关来执行从私有 IP 到公有 IP 的源地址转换。

## 参考架构

```
Lambda (私有子网)  --->  路由表 0.0.0.0/0 -> NAT GW  --->  NAT GW (公有子网)  --->  IGW  --->  互联网
```

## 参考资源

- [Enable internet access for VPC-connected Lambda functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-vpc-internet.html)
- [Giving Lambda functions access to resources in an Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-vpc.html)
- [Give internet access to a Lambda function in a VPC (AWS re:Post)](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/internet-access-lambda-function)

en.question: A developer needs to store configuration variables for an application. The developer needs to set an expiration date and time for the configuration. The developer wants to receive notifications before the configuration expires. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create a standard parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Set Expiration and ExpirationNotification policy types.
options.B: Create a standard parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Create an AWS Lambda function to expire the configuration and to send Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notifications.
options.C: Create an advanced parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Set Expiration and ExpirationNotification policy types.
options.D: Create an advanced parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Create an Amazon EC2 instance with a cron job to expire the configuration and to send notifications.

en.explanation:
# SSM Parameter Store: Expiration & ExpirationNotification Policies

## Scenario
A developer needs to store configuration variables, set an expiration date/time on the configuration, and receive a notification before it expires — all with the **least operational overhead**.

## Correct Answer: C — Advanced parameter with `Expiration` and `ExpirationNotification` policies

AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store provides built‑in **parameter policies** that satisfy both requirements directly, with no custom code or infrastructure:

- When the expiration time is reached, Parameter Store deletes the parameter. ExpirationNotification: This policy initiates an event in Amazon CloudWatch Events that notifies you about the expiration. By using this policy, you can receive notification before or after the expiration time is reached, in units of days or hours.
- Parameter Store enforces parameter policies by using asynchronous, periodic scans. After you create a policy, you don't need to perform additional actions to enforce the policy. Parameter Store independently performs the action defined by the policy according to the criteria you specified.

This is the lowest-overhead solution because AWS manages the enforcement and notification — no Lambda, EC2, or cron required.

### Why it must be the *Advanced* tier
- Standard parameters have a content size limit of 4 KB and can't be configured to use parameter policies. You can create a maximum of 10,000 standard parameters for each Region in an Amazon Web Services account. Standard parameters are offered at no additional cost. Advanced parameters have a content size limit of 8 KB and can be configured to use parameter policies.
- Parameter policies are available for parameters that use the advanced parameters tier.

### Example policy JSON
```json
[
  {"Type":"Expiration","Version":"1.0","Attributes":{"Timestamp":"2025-12-31T00:00:00.000Z"}},
  {"Type":"ExpirationNotification","Version":"1.0","Attributes":{"Before":"5","Unit":"Days"}}
]
```

## Why the other options are wrong

- **A. Standard parameter with Expiration/ExpirationNotification policies** — Invalid configuration. Standard‑tier parameters do **not** support parameter policies; only advanced‑tier parameters do (Standard parameters have a content size limit of 4 KB and can't be configured to use parameter policies.). The policy assignment would fail or silently force the parameter to advanced tier.

- **B. Standard parameter + custom Lambda for expiration and SNS notification** — Adds significant operational overhead (writing, deploying, scheduling, and maintaining custom Lambda code, plus SNS plumbing) when AWS already provides this functionality natively via parameter policies.

- **D. Advanced parameter + EC2 instance with cron** — Highest overhead of all options. Running and maintaining an EC2 instance (patching, scaling, monitoring, IAM, scheduling) just to fire expiration logic duplicates a feature already provided by Parameter Store policies.

## References
- [Assigning parameter policies in Parameter Store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/parameter-store-policies.html)
- [PutParameter API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/APIReference/API_PutParameter.html)
- [AWS::SSM::Parameter (CloudFormation)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-ssm-parameter.html)

zh.question: 开发人员需要存储应用程序的配置变量。开发人员需要为配置设置过期日期和时间。开发人员希望在配置过期前收到通知。哪种解决方案能够以最小的运维开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 在 AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store 中创建一个标准参数。设置 Expiration 和 ExpirationNotification 策略类型。
options.B: 在 AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store 中创建一个标准参数。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数，使配置过期并发送 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 通知。
options.C: 在 AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store 中创建高级参数。设置 Expiration 和 ExpirationNotification 策略类型。
options.D: 在 AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store 中创建一个高级参数。创建一个 Amazon EC2 实例，并设置一个 cron 作业来使配置过期并发送通知。

zh.explanation:
# SSM Parameter Store：过期和 ExpirationNotification 策略

## 场景
一名开发人员需要存储配置变量，设置配置的过期日期/时间，并在过期前收到通知——同时**操作开销最少**。

## 正确答案：C——带有 `Expiration` 和 `ExpirationNotification` 策略的高级参数

AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store 提供内置的**参数策略**，可直接满足两项要求，无需自定义代码或基础设施：

- 当达到过期时间时，Parameter Store 会删除该参数。ExpirationNotification：此策略在 Amazon CloudWatch Events 中启动事件，通知您参数即将过期。通过使用此策略，您可以在达到过期时间之前或之后接收通知，以天或小时为单位。
- Parameter Store 通过使用异步定期扫描来强制执行参数策略。创建策略后，您无需执行其他操作来强制执行该策略。Parameter Store 会根据您指定的条件独立执行该策略定义的操作。

这是开销最低的解决方案，因为 AWS 管理强制执行和通知——无需 Lambda、EC2 或 cron。

### 为什么必须是*高级*层级
- 标准参数的内容大小限制为 4 KB，不能配置为使用参数策略。对于 AWS 账户中的每个区域，您最多可以创建 10,000 个标准参数。标准参数不收取额外费用。高级参数的内容大小限制为 8 KB，可以配置为使用参数策略。
- 参数策略适用于使用高级参数层级的参数。

### 策略 JSON 示例
```json
[
  {"Type":"Expiration","Version":"1.0","Attributes":{"Timestamp":"2025-12-31T00:00:00.000Z"}},
  {"Type":"ExpirationNotification","Version":"1.0","Attributes":{"Before":"5","Unit":"Days"}}
]
```

## 其他选项为何错误

- **A. 标准参数加 Expiration/ExpirationNotification 策略** — 无效的配置。标准层级参数**不**支持参数策略；只有高级层级参数才支持（标准参数的内容大小限制为 4 KB，不能配置为使用参数策略。）。策略分配会失败或静默地强制将参数升级到高级层级。

- **B. 标准参数加用于过期和 SNS 通知的自定义 Lambda** — 增加了大量操作开销（编写、部署、调度和维护自定义 Lambda 代码，以及 SNS 配置），而 AWS 已通过参数策略原生提供此功能。

- **D. 高级参数加带有 cron 的 EC2 实例** — 所有选项中开销最高。运行和维护 EC2 实例（修补、扩展、监控、IAM、调度）仅用于触发过期逻辑，这复制了 Parameter Store 策略已提供的功能。

## 参考资源
- [在 Parameter Store 中分配参数策略](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/parameter-store-policies.html)
- [PutParameter API 参考](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/APIReference/API_PutParameter.html)
- [AWS::SSM::Parameter (CloudFormation)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-ssm-parameter.html)

en.question: A company is developing a serverless application that consists of various AWS Lambda functions behind Amazon API Gateway APIs. A developer needs to automate the deployment of Lambda function code. The developer will deploy updated Lambda functions with AWS CodeDeploy. The deployment must minimize the exposure of potential errors to end users. When the application is in production, the application cannot experience downtime outside the specified maintenance window. Which deployment configuration will meet these requirements with the LEAST deployment time?

options.A: Use the AWS CodeDeploy in-place deployment configuration for the Lambda functions. Shift all traffic immediately after deployment.
options.B: Use the AWS CodeDeploy linear deployment configuration to shift 10% of the traffic every minute.
options.C: Use the AWS CodeDeploy all-at-once deployment configuration to shift all traffic to the updated versions immediately.
options.D: Use the AWS CodeDeploy predefined canary deployment configuration to shift 10% of the traffic immediately and shift the remaining traffic after 5 minutes.

en.explanation:
# Question Analysis

The scenario involves Lambda functions behind API Gateway, deployed via AWS CodeDeploy. The requirements are:
1. **Minimize exposure of potential errors to end users** (so all-at-once is risky).
2. **No downtime outside maintenance window** (zero downtime — so in-place is not appropriate for Lambda).
3. **LEAST deployment time** (favor canary over slower linear).

## Correct Answer: D — Canary 10% then remaining after 5 minutes

CodeDeploy for Lambda supports three traffic-shifting deployment configurations: Canary (traffic shifted in two increments with predefined options that specify the percentage of traffic shifted in the first increment and the interval before the remaining traffic is shifted), Linear (traffic shifted in equal increments with equal minutes between increments), and All-at-once (all traffic shifted from the original Lambda function to the updated Lambda function version at once).

A canary deployment shifts a small portion of traffic first to validate the new version with limited blast radius, then shifts the remainder after the bake-in interval. For example, route 10% of traffic to the new code first, then route the rest after 5 minutes if CloudWatch alarms are not triggered — this is the classic Canary deployment scenario where traffic is shifted in two increments. This satisfies the "minimize error exposure" requirement while being faster than linear shifts (5 minutes total vs. ~10 minutes for `Linear10PercentEvery1Minute`).

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

**A. In-place deployment, shift all traffic immediately.**
CodeDeploy's *in-place* deployment type does **not** apply to Lambda — it is only available for the EC2/On-Premises compute platform. Gradual traffic shifts using strategies like linear and canary are applicable to AWS Lambda and Amazon ECS, but such approaches do not apply to Amazon EC2 with CodeDeploy, and conversely the in-place model belongs to EC2. Additionally, shifting all traffic immediately does not minimize error exposure.

**B. Linear 10% every minute.**
This is a valid Lambda deployment configuration, but it takes ~10 minutes to complete (10 increments × 1 minute), which is **longer** than the canary option in D (5 minutes). The question explicitly asks for the **LEAST deployment time** while still doing gradual rollout.

**C. All-at-once.**
AllAtOnce: All traffic is shifted from the original Lambda function to the updated Lambda function version at once. This maximizes — rather than minimizes — exposure of potential errors to end users, violating a stated requirement.

## Reference Documentation
- [CodeDeploy Deployment Configurations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployment-configurations.html)
- [Deploying serverless applications gradually with AWS SAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/automating-updates-to-serverless-apps.html)
- [Lambda alias routing (canary deployments)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuring-alias-routing.html)

zh.question: 一家公司正在开发一个无服务器应用程序，该应用程序由多个位于 Amazon API Gateway API 后端的 AWS Lambda 函数组成。开发人员需要自动化部署 Lambda 函数代码。开发人员将使用 AWS CodeDeploy 部署更新后的 Lambda 函数。部署过程必须最大限度地减少潜在错误对最终用户的影响。应用程序在生产环境中运行时，除了指定的维护窗口外，不能出现任何停机时间。哪种部署配置能够以最短的部署时间满足这些要求？

options.A: 对 Lambda 函数使用 AWS CodeDeploy 就地部署配置。部署完成后立即转移所有流量。
options.B: 使用 AWS CodeDeploy 线性部署配置，每分钟转移 10% 的流量。
options.C: 使用 AWS CodeDeploy 一次性部署配置，立即将所有流量转移到更新后的版本。
options.D: 使用 AWS CodeDeploy 预定义的金丝雀部署配置，立即转移 10% 的流量，并在 5 分钟后转移剩余的流量。

zh.explanation:
# 问题分析

该场景涉及 API Gateway 后面的 Lambda 函数，通过 AWS CodeDeploy 部署。要求如下：
1. **最小化向最终用户暴露潜在错误的风险**（因此一次全部部署风险太大）。
2. **维护窗口外无停机时间**（零停机——因此原地部署不适用于 Lambda）。
3. **部署时间最短**（支持金丝雀而非更慢的线性部署）。

## 正确答案：D — Canary 10% 然后 5 分钟后部署剩余流量

CodeDeploy 针对 Lambda 支持三种流量转移部署配置：Canary（分两个增量转移流量，预定义选项指定第一个增量转移的流量百分比和第一次和第二次转移之间的间隔）、Linear（以相等的增量转移流量，增量之间的时间间隔相等）和 All-at-once（一次性将所有流量从原始 Lambda 函数转移到更新的 Lambda 函数版本）。

金丝雀部署首先转移一小部分流量来验证新版本，限制爆炸半径，然后在预留时间间隔后转移剩余流量。例如，首先将 10% 的流量路由到新代码，然后在 5 分钟后如果 CloudWatch 告警未被触发则路由其余流量——这是典型的 Canary 部署场景，流量分两个增量转移。这既满足了"最小化错误暴露"的要求，同时比线性转移更快（总共 5 分钟对比 `Linear10PercentEvery1Minute` 的约 10 分钟）。

## 其他选项为什么错误

**A. 原地部署，一次性转移所有流量。**
CodeDeploy 的*原地*部署类型**不适用**于 Lambda——它仅适用于 EC2/本地计算平台。线性和金丝雀等渐进式流量转移策略适用于 AWS Lambda 和 Amazon ECS，但此类方法不适用于 Amazon EC2 和 CodeDeploy，相反原地模型属于 EC2。此外，一次性转移所有流量并不能最小化错误暴露。

**B. Linear 10% 每分钟。**
这是有效的 Lambda 部署配置，但需要大约 10 分钟才能完成（10 个增量 × 1 分钟），**长于**选项 D 中的金丝雀部署（5 分钟）。问题明确要求在进行渐进式部署的同时**部署时间最短**。

**C. All-at-once。**
AllAtOnce：所有流量一次性从原始 Lambda 函数转移到更新的 Lambda 函数版本。这会最大化——而非最小化——向最终用户暴露潜在错误的风险，违反了所述要求。

## 参考文档
- [CodeDeploy 部署配置](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployment-configurations.html)
- [使用 AWS SAM 逐步部署无服务器应用程序](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/automating-updates-to-serverless-apps.html)
- [Lambda 别名路由（金丝雀部署）](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuring-alias-routing.html)

en.question: A company created four AWS Lambda functions that connect to a relational database server that runs on an Amazon RDS instance. A security team requires the company to automatically change the database password every 30 days. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST securely?

options.A: Store the database credentials in the environment variables of the Lambda function. Deploy the Lambda function with the new credentials every 30 days.
options.B: Store the database credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure a 30-day rotation schedule for the credentials.
options.C: Store the database credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store secure strings. Configure a 30-day schedule for the secure strings.
options.D: Store the database credentials in an Amazon S3 bucket that uses server-side encryption with customer-provided encryption keys (SSE-C). Configure a 30-day key rotation schedule for the customer key.

en.explanation:
# DVA-C02 Question 135: Automatic Database Password Rotation

## Scenario
Four Lambda functions connect to an RDS database. The security team requires the database password to be **automatically changed every 30 days**. We need the **most secure** solution.

## Correct Answer: B — AWS Secrets Manager with 30-day rotation

AWS Secrets Manager is purpose-built for this scenario. Rotation is the process of periodically updating a secret. When you rotate a secret, you update the credentials in both the secret and the database or service. In Secrets Manager, you can set up automatic rotation for your secrets.

Secrets Manager offers built-in integrations for rotating credentials for all Amazon RDS databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, Microsoft SQL Server, MariaDB, and Amazon Aurora.) You can configure a rotation schedule (e.g., 30 days), and Secrets Manager will use a managed rotation or a Lambda rotation function to update the password in both the secret and the database. The Lambda functions retrieve the current credentials at runtime via a `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` call — no redeployment required when the password changes.

Example CLI to enable 30-day rotation:

```bash
aws secretsmanager rotate-secret \
  --secret-id "prod/rds/master" \
  --rotation-lambda-arn "arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:123456789012:function:SecretsManagerRotation" \
  --rotation-rules '{"AutomaticallyAfterDays": 30}'
```

Secrets are encrypted with KMS, transmitted over TLS 1.2, and access can be controlled via fine-grained IAM policies.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

### A. Lambda environment variables, redeploy every 30 days
- Environment variables are visible in the Lambda console to anyone with `lambda:GetFunction` permission and are stored in the function configuration. While they can be encrypted with KMS, storing **database credentials** in env vars is an anti-pattern.
- The "redeploy every 30 days" step is **manual**, not automatic — it directly violates the requirement to *automatically* change the password.
- It also doesn't actually change the password on the RDS instance — only the value Lambda reads.

### C. Systems Manager Parameter Store SecureString with "30-day schedule"
- **Parameter Store does not support automatic rotation of secrets.** There is no native rotation feature for SecureString parameters that updates a database password. Secrets Manager is the AWS service that provides this. (See [Rotate AWS Secrets Manager secrets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotating-secrets.html).)
- The option's premise ("Configure a 30-day schedule for the secure strings") is not a real Parameter Store feature — you'd have to build custom rotation with EventBridge + Lambda yourself, which is less secure and more error-prone than the managed Secrets Manager solution.

### D. S3 bucket with SSE-C and customer key rotation
- SSE-C means **the customer manages and supplies the encryption key on every request** — AWS does not store it. There is no "30-day key rotation schedule" in AWS for SSE-C; rotation would be entirely the customer's responsibility.
- Even if you rotated the encryption key, that **does not rotate the database password** — it only re-encrypts the file holding the password. The actual RDS credential would never change.
- Storing database credentials in an S3 object is not a recommended secrets management pattern.

## Key Takeaway
For automatic, managed rotation of RDS credentials, **AWS Secrets Manager** is the correct service. Secrets Manager offers built-in integrations for MySQL, PostgreSQL, and Amazon Aurora on Amazon RDS, and can rotate credentials for these databases natively.

## References
- [Rotate AWS Secrets Manager secrets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotating-secrets.html)
- [Set up automatic rotation for Amazon RDS secrets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotate-secrets_turn-on-for-db.html)
- [Rotate Amazon RDS database credentials automatically with AWS Secrets Manager](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/rotate-amazon-rds-database-credentials-automatically-with-aws-secrets-manager/)

zh.question: 一家公司创建了四个 AWS Lambda 函数，这些函数连接到运行在 Amazon RDS 实例上的关系数据库服务器。安全团队要求该公司每 30 天自动更改一次数据库密码。哪种解决方案能够最安全地满足这些要求？

options.A: 将数据库凭据存储在 Lambda 函数的环境变量中。每 30 天使用新凭据部署 Lambda 函数。
options.B: 将数据库凭证存储在 AWS Secrets Manager 中。配置凭证的 30 天轮换计划。
options.C: 将数据库凭证存储在 AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store 的安全字符串中。为安全字符串配置 30 天的更新周期。
options.D: 将数据库凭证存储在采用服务器端加密和客户提供的加密密钥（SSE-C）的 Amazon S3 存储桶中。为客户密钥配置 30 天的密钥轮换计划。

zh.explanation:
# DVA-C02 Question 135：自动数据库密码轮换

## 场景
四个 Lambda 函数连接到一个 RDS 数据库。安全团队要求数据库密码**每 30 天自动更改一次**。我们需要**最安全的**解决方案。

## 正确答案：B — AWS Secrets Manager，进行 30 天轮换

AWS Secrets Manager 是专为此场景而构建的。轮换是定期更新密钥的过程。轮换密钥时，你会同时更新密钥和数据库或服务中的凭证。在 Secrets Manager 中，你可以为密钥设置自动轮换。

Secrets Manager 为所有 Amazon RDS 数据库（MySQL、PostgreSQL、Oracle、Microsoft SQL Server、MariaDB 和 Amazon Aurora）提供内置的凭证轮换集成。你可以配置轮换时间表（例如 30 天），Secrets Manager 将使用托管轮换或 Lambda 轮换函数来更新密钥和数据库中的密码。Lambda 函数在运行时通过 `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` 调用检索当前凭证 — 密码更改时无需重新部署。

启用 30 天轮换的 CLI 示例：

```bash
aws secretsmanager rotate-secret \
  --secret-id "prod/rds/master" \
  --rotation-lambda-arn "arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:123456789012:function:SecretsManagerRotation" \
  --rotation-rules '{"AutomaticallyAfterDays": 30}'
```

密钥通过 KMS 加密、通过 TLS 1.2 传输，并且可以通过细粒度的 IAM 策略控制访问权限。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

### A. Lambda 环境变量，每 30 天重新部署一次
- 环境变量在 Lambda 控制台对任何拥有 `lambda:GetFunction` 权限的用户可见，并存储在函数配置中。虽然可以使用 KMS 加密，但在环境变量中存储**数据库凭证**是反模式。
- "每 30 天重新部署一次"步骤是**手动的**，而不是自动的 — 它直接违反了*自动*更改密码的要求。
- 它也不会实际更改 RDS 实例上的密码 — 仅更改 Lambda 读取的值。

### C. Systems Manager Parameter Store SecureString，配置"30 天时间表"
- **Parameter Store 不支持密钥的自动轮换。** SecureString 参数没有本机轮换功能来更新数据库密码。Secrets Manager 是提供此功能的 AWS 服务。（参见[轮换 AWS Secrets Manager 密钥](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotating-secrets.html)。）
- 该选项的前提（"为安全字符串配置 30 天时间表"）不是真实的 Parameter Store 功能 — 你必须使用 EventBridge + Lambda 自己构建自定义轮换，这不如托管 Secrets Manager 解决方案安全且容易出错。

### D. S3 存储桶，使用 SSE-C 和客户密钥轮换
- SSE-C 意味着**客户管理并在每个请求上提供加密密钥** — AWS 不存储它。AWS 没有针对 SSE-C 的"30 天密钥轮换时间表"；轮换将完全由客户负责。
- 即使轮换加密密钥，也**不会轮换数据库密码** — 它仅重新加密保存密码的文件。实际的 RDS 凭证永远不会更改。
- 在 S3 对象中存储数据库凭证不是推荐的密钥管理模式。

## 关键要点
对于 RDS 凭证的自动、托管轮换，**AWS Secrets Manager** 是正确的服务。Secrets Manager 为 Amazon RDS 上的 MySQL、PostgreSQL 和 Amazon Aurora 提供内置集成，并可以本机轮换这些数据库的凭证。

## 参考资源
- [轮换 AWS Secrets Manager 密钥](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotating-secrets.html)
- [为 Amazon RDS 密钥设置自动轮换](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotate-secrets_turn-on-for-db.html)
- [使用 AWS Secrets Manager 自动轮换 Amazon RDS 数据库凭证](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/rotate-amazon-rds-database-credentials-automatically-with-aws-secrets-manager/)

en.question: A developer is setting up a deployment pipeline. The pipeline includes an AWS CodeBuild build stage that requires access to a database to run integration tests. The developer is using a buildspec.yml file to configure the database connection. Company policy requires automatic rotation of all database credentials. Which solution will handle the database credentials MOST securely?

options.A: Retrieve the credentials from variables that are hardcoded in the buildspec.yml file. Configure an AWS Lambda function to rotate the credentials.
options.B: Retrieve the credentials from an environment variable that is linked to a SecureString parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Configure Parameter Store for automatic rotation.
options.C: Retrieve the credentials from an environment variable that is linked to an AWS Secrets Manager secret. Configure Secrets Manager for automatic rotation.
options.D: Retrieve the credentials from an environment variable that contains the connection string in plaintext. Configure an Amazon EventBridge event to rotate the credentials.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A developer needs to securely supply database credentials to an AWS CodeBuild integration test stage via `buildspec.yml`. Company policy requires **automatic rotation** of database credentials. The question asks for the MOST secure solution.

## Correct Answer: C

Retrieve the credentials from a CodeBuild environment variable that is linked to an **AWS Secrets Manager** secret, and configure Secrets Manager for automatic rotation.

### Why C is correct

1. **Native CodeBuild integration with Secrets Manager.** CodeBuild's buildspec supports a dedicated `env/secrets-manager` mapping that pulls secret values into environment variables at build time. Per the AWS docs, this section is "Required if you want to retrieve custom environment variables stored in AWS Secrets Manager" using the pattern `<key>: <secret-id>:<json-key>:<version-stage>:<version-id>` ([Build specification reference for CodeBuild](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/build-spec-ref.html)). Example:

   ```yaml
   version: 0.2
   env:
     secrets-manager:
       DB_PASSWORD: my-database-secret:password
   phases:
     build:
       commands:
         - run-integration-tests --password "$DB_PASSWORD"
   ```

2. **Built-in automatic rotation.** AWS Secrets Manager natively supports scheduled, Lambda-driven rotation for RDS, DocumentDB, Redshift, and custom databases. See [Rotate AWS Secrets Manager secrets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotate-secrets_managed.html). The credential value is updated centrally; CodeBuild always retrieves the latest version at build time, so no pipeline change is required when the password rotates.

3. **No plaintext exposure.** AWS explicitly recommends against storing sensitive values in PLAINTEXT environment variables and instead "recommend that you use parameter-store or secrets-manager mapping" for sensitive values ([CodeBuild buildspec reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/build-spec-ref.html)).

### Why the other options are wrong

- **A. Hardcoded credentials in buildspec.yml + custom Lambda rotation.** Hardcoding credentials in a buildspec file commits them to source control and exposes them to anyone with repository access. Even if a Lambda rotates the value in some store, the buildspec still contains a literal value that becomes stale or leaked. This violates AWS's explicit guidance against placing sensitive data in plaintext build configuration.

- **B. SecureString SSM Parameter Store with automatic rotation.** SSM Parameter Store SecureString parameters are encrypted, but **Parameter Store does not natively support automatic credential rotation**. Rotation is a feature of AWS Secrets Manager (Parameter Store can *reference* a Secrets Manager secret via the `secretsmanager` prefix, but the Parameter Store service itself doesn't rotate values). See [What is AWS Secrets Manager / Compare to Parameter Store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html). Therefore the "Configure Parameter Store for automatic rotation" step is not a real feature.

- **D. Plaintext connection string + EventBridge rotation.** Storing the connection string in a plaintext environment variable directly contradicts AWS's guidance: PLAINTEXT environment variables can be displayed by the CodeBuild console and CLI, so they must not be used for secrets ([EnvironmentVariable API reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/APIReference/API_EnvironmentVariable.html)). EventBridge alone does not rotate database credentials; it is only an event scheduler/router.

## Key Takeaway

When you see "secure storage" + "automatic rotation" + "database credentials" on the DVA-C02 exam, the answer is almost always **AWS Secrets Manager**, and CodeBuild has first-class support for it via the `env/secrets-manager` block in buildspec.yml.

zh.question: 开发人员正在设置部署流水线。该流水线包含一个 AWS CodeBuild 构建阶段，该阶段需要访问数据库才能运行集成测试。开发人员使用 buildspec.yml 文件来配置数据库连接。公司策略要求自动轮换所有数据库凭证。哪种解决方案能够最安全地处理数据库凭证？

options.A: 从buildspec.yml 文件中硬编码的变量中检索凭证。配置 AWS Lambda 函数来轮换凭证。
options.B: 从与 AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store 中的 SecureString 参数关联的环境变量中检索凭证。配置 Parameter Store 以实现自动轮换。
options.C: 从与 AWS Secrets Manager 密钥关联的环境变量中检索凭证。配置 Secrets Manager 以实现自动轮换。
options.D: 从包含明文连接字符串的环境变量中检索凭证。配置 Amazon EventBridge 事件以轮换凭证。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

一位开发人员需要通过 `buildspec.yml` 安全地向 AWS CodeBuild 集成测试阶段提供数据库凭证。公司政策要求**自动轮换**数据库凭证。题目要求找到最安全的解决方案。

## 正确答案：C

从链接到 **AWS Secrets Manager** 密钥的 CodeBuild 环境变量中检索凭证，并配置 Secrets Manager 进行自动轮换。

### 为什么 C 是正确的

1. **CodeBuild 与 Secrets Manager 的原生集成。** CodeBuild 的 buildspec 支持专用的 `env/secrets-manager` 映射，在构建时将密钥值拉入环境变量。根据 AWS 文档，此部分是"如果要检索存储在 AWS Secrets Manager 中的自定义环境变量，则必须使用"，格式为 `<key>: <secret-id>:<json-key>:<version-stage>:<version-id>`（[CodeBuild 构建规范参考](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/build-spec-ref.html)）。示例：

   ```yaml
   version: 0.2
   env:
     secrets-manager:
       DB_PASSWORD: my-database-secret:password
   phases:
     build:
       commands:
         - run-integration-tests --password "$DB_PASSWORD"
   ```

2. **内置自动轮换。** AWS Secrets Manager 原生支持针对 RDS、DocumentDB、Redshift 和自定义数据库的计划型、Lambda 驱动的轮换。参见[轮换 AWS Secrets Manager 密钥](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotate-secrets_managed.html)。凭证值在中央更新；CodeBuild 在构建时总是检索最新版本，因此密码轮换时无需更改管道。

3. **无明文泄露。** AWS 明确建议不要在纯文本环境变量中存储敏感值，而是"建议使用 parameter-store 或 secrets-manager 映射"处理敏感值（[CodeBuild buildspec 参考](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/build-spec-ref.html)）。

### 为什么其他选项是错误的

- **A. 在 buildspec.yml 中硬编码凭证 + 自定义 Lambda 轮换。** 在 buildspec 文件中硬编码凭证会将其提交到源代码控制，并将其暴露给任何有仓库访问权限的人。即使 Lambda 在某个存储库中轮换该值，buildspec 仍然包含一个过期或泄露的字面值。这违反了 AWS 关于不在纯文本构建配置中放置敏感数据的明确指导。

- **B. SecureString SSM Parameter Store 加自动轮换。** SSM Parameter Store SecureString 参数是加密的，但 **Parameter Store 不原生支持自动凭证轮换**。轮换是 AWS Secrets Manager 的功能（Parameter Store 可以通过 `secretsmanager` 前缀引用 Secrets Manager 密钥，但 Parameter Store 服务本身不轮换值）。参见[什么是 AWS Secrets Manager / 与 Parameter Store 比较](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html)。因此"配置 Parameter Store 进行自动轮换"这一步不是真实功能。

- **D. 纯文本连接字符串 + EventBridge 轮换。** 在纯文本环境变量中存储连接字符串直接违反了 AWS 的指导：纯文本环境变量可以由 CodeBuild 控制台和 CLI 显示，因此不能用于密钥（[EnvironmentVariable API 参考](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/APIReference/API_EnvironmentVariable.html)）。EventBridge 本身不轮换数据库凭证；它仅是事件调度/路由器。

## 核心要点

当您在 DVA-C02 考试中看到"安全存储" + "自动轮换" + "数据库凭证"时，答案几乎总是 **AWS Secrets Manager**，而 CodeBuild 通过 buildspec.yml 中的 `env/secrets-manager` 块为其提供一流支持。

en.question: A company is developing a serverless multi-tier application on AWS. The company will build the serverless logic tier by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. While the company builds the logic tier, a developer who works on the frontend of the application must develop integration tests. The tests must cover both positive and negative scenarios, depending on success and error HTTP status codes. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST effort?

options.A: Set up a mock integration for API methods in API Gateway. In the integration request from Method Execution, add simple logic to return either a success or error based on HTTP status code. In the integration response, add messages that correspond to the HTTP status codes.
options.B: Create two mock integration resources for API methods in API Gateway. In the integration request, return a success HTTP status code for one resource and an error HTTP status code for the other resource. In the integration response, add messages that correspond to the HTTP status codes.
options.C: Create Lambda functions to perform tests. Add simple logic to return either success or error, based on the HTTP status codes. Build an API Gateway Lambda integration. Select appropriate Lambda functions that correspond to the HTTP status codes.
options.D: Create a Lambda function to perform tests. Add simple logic to return either success or error-based HTTP status codes. Create a mock integration in API Gateway. Select the Lambda function that corresponds to the HTTP status codes.

en.explanation:
# API Gateway Mock Integration for Frontend Integration Testing

## Scenario
A serverless application is being built with API Gateway and Lambda. The backend logic tier is still under development, but a frontend developer needs to write integration tests **now** that exercise both success (positive) and error (negative) HTTP status code paths. The question asks for the solution requiring the **LEAST effort**.

## Correct Answer: A

API Gateway provides a built-in **Mock integration** type specifically designed for this use case—returning canned responses without invoking any real backend. You configure the method's integration request and integration response to associate a response with a given status code. For a method with the mock integration to return a 200 response, configure the integration request body mapping template to return the appropriate value.

A single API method with a mock integration can return both success and error responses by adding simple conditional logic in the integration request mapping template. The AWS docs show exactly this pattern:

```vtl
{
  #if( $input.params('scope') == "internal" )
    "statusCode": 200
  #else
    "statusCode": 500
  #end
}
```

This way, the method of the mock integration lets internal calls to go through while rejecting other types of calls with an error response. The integration responses then map each status code (e.g., 200, 5xx) to corresponding response messages. This is the lowest-effort approach because it requires **no Lambda code, no IAM roles, no deployment packages**—only API Gateway configuration.

Mock integrations are explicitly purposed for this kind of work: the Mock Integration is excellent for prototyping APIs in a fast and efficient manner. It could also be used to unblock teams that depend on the API before the development is complete.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

**B. Two mock integration resources (one per status code)** — Creating two separate resources doubles the configuration work and, more importantly, breaks the test model. Integration tests must hit the **same endpoint** and observe both positive and negative responses based on input. Splitting success and error onto two different resources means you are no longer testing one endpoint's behavior—you're testing two different URLs. It is also more effort than option A, which uses a single mock integration with conditional logic.

**C. Lambda functions behind a Lambda integration** — This requires writing, packaging, deploying, and maintaining Lambda code (plus IAM execution roles) just to return canned status codes. You will pay for every Lambda execution, even though it is just a mock, and if you have many endpoints it could be very time-consuming to set up all the mocks. You can speed up the process, and save money, using MockIntegration. You can configure a specific Resource, or Method, or the entire API with few lines of code and no Lambda at all. This is strictly more effort than a mock integration.

**D. Lambda function combined with a mock integration** — This option is technically incoherent: a *mock* integration in API Gateway does not invoke a Lambda function. Mock integrations terminate at API Gateway and return responses generated from mapping templates. You cannot "select a Lambda function" for a mock integration—that would be a Lambda integration. The option mixes two mutually exclusive integration types.

## Key AWS Documentation
- [Mock integrations for REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-mock-integration.html)
- [Enable mock integration using the API Gateway console](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-mock-integration-console.html)

zh.question: 一家公司正在 AWS 上开发一个无服务器多层应用程序。该公司将使用 Amazon API Gateway 和 AWS Lambda 构建无服务器逻辑层。在构建逻辑层的同时，负责应用程序前端开发的开发人员需要编写集成测试。这些测试必须涵盖正反两种场景，并根据 HTTP 状态码的成功和错误情况进行测试。哪种解决方案能够以最少的投入满足这些要求？

options.A: 在 API 网关中为 API 方法设置模拟集成。在方法执行的集成请求中，添加简单的逻辑，根据 HTTP 状态码返回成功或错误。在集成响应中，添加与 HTTP 状态码对应的消息。
options.B: 为 API 网关中的 API 方法创建两个模拟集成资源。在集成请求中，一个资源返回成功 HTTP 状态码，另一个资源返回错误 HTTP 状态码。在集成响应中，添加与 HTTP 状态码对应的消息。
options.C: 创建 Lambda 函数来执行测试。添加简单的逻辑，根据 HTTP 状态码返回成功或错误。构建 API 网关 Lambda 集成。选择与 HTTP 状态码对应的 Lambda 函数。
options.D: 创建一个 Lambda 函数来执行测试。添加简单的逻辑，使其返回基于成功或错误的 HTTP 状态码。在 API Gateway 中创建一个模拟集成。选择与 HTTP 状态码对应的 Lambda 函数。

zh.explanation:
# API Gateway Mock Integration 用于前端集成测试

## 场景
正在使用 API Gateway 和 Lambda 构建无服务器应用程序。后端逻辑层仍在开发中，但前端开发人员需要**现在就**编写集成测试，以同时测试成功（正向）和错误（负向）HTTP 状态码路径。问题要求找到**工作量最少**的解决方案。

## 正确答案：A

API Gateway 提供了内置的 **Mock integration** 类型，专门为此用例设计——在不调用任何真实后端的情况下返回预设响应。配置方法的集成请求和集成响应，将响应与给定的状态码关联。对于使用 mock integration 的方法要返回 200 响应，配置集成请求正文映射模板以返回适当的值。

单个 API 方法配合 mock integration 可以通过在集成请求映射模板中添加简单的条件逻辑来返回成功和错误响应。AWS 文档展示了这个精确的模式：

```vtl
{
  #if( $input.params('scope') == "internal" )
    "statusCode": 200
  #else
    "statusCode": 500
  #end
}
```

这样，mock integration 方法允许内部调用通过，同时拒绝其他类型的调用并返回错误响应。集成响应随后将每个状态码（例如 200、5xx）映射到相应的响应消息。这是工作量最少的方法，因为它**不需要 Lambda 代码、不需要 IAM 角色、不需要部署包**——仅需 API Gateway 配置。

Mock integration 明确用于此类工作：Mock Integration 非常适合以快速有效的方式原型化 API。它也可以用于在开发完成前解锁依赖该 API 的团队。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

**B. 两个 mock integration 资源（每个状态码一个）** —— 创建两个单独的资源使配置工作量翻倍，更重要的是，这破坏了测试模型。集成测试必须点击**同一个端点**，并根据输入观察正向和负向响应。将成功和错误分割到两个不同的资源意味着你不再测试一个端点的行为——而是在测试两个不同的 URL。与选项 A 相比工作量也更多，选项 A 使用单个 mock integration 配合条件逻辑。

**C. Lambda integration 后面的 Lambda 函数** —— 这需要编写、打包、部署和维护 Lambda 代码（加上 IAM 执行角色），仅仅是为了返回预设状态码。你需要为每次 Lambda 执行付费，即使它只是一个 mock，如果有许多端点，设置所有 mock 可能非常耗时。你可以使用 MockIntegration 加快流程并节省成本。你可以用几行代码配置特定资源、方法或整个 API，根本不需要 Lambda。这严格上比 mock integration 工作量多。

**D. Lambda 函数与 mock integration 结合** —— 此选项在技术上是不连贯的：API Gateway 中的 *mock* integration 不调用 Lambda 函数。Mock integration 在 API Gateway 处终止，并返回从映射模板生成的响应。你不能为 mock integration "选择 Lambda 函数"——那将是 Lambda integration。该选项混淆了两种互斥的集成类型。

## 关键 AWS 文档
- [API Gateway 中 REST API 的 Mock integration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-mock-integration.html)
- [使用 API Gateway 控制台启用 mock integration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-mock-integration-console.html)

en.question: Users are reporting errors in an application. The application consists of several microservices that are deployed on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate. Which combination of steps should a developer take to fix the errors? (Choose two.)

options.A: Deploy AWS X-Ray as a sidecar container to the microservices. Update the task role policy to allow access to the X-Ray API.
options.B: Deploy AWS X-Ray as a daemonset to the Fargate cluster. Update the service role policy to allow access to the X-Ray API.
options.C: Instrument the application by using the AWS X-Ray SDK. Update the application to use the PutXrayTrace API call to communicate with the X-Ray API.
options.D: Instrument the application by using the AWS X-Ray SDK. Update the application to communicate with the X-Ray daemon.
options.E: Instrument the ECS task to send the stdout and stderr output to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Update the task role policy to allow the cloudwatch:PullLogs action.

en.explanation:
# ECS/Fargate Microservices Troubleshooting with X-Ray

## Scenario
A microservices application running on **Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate** is experiencing errors. The developer needs to identify and fix these errors. To diagnose distributed microservices, **AWS X-Ray** is the right tool — it provides distributed tracing across services, exposing latency hotspots, faults, and errors. The question asks for the two steps that correctly enable X-Ray tracing on a Fargate-backed ECS application.

## Correct Answers: A and D

### A. Deploy AWS X-Ray as a sidecar container; update the task role to allow X-Ray API access ✅
On Fargate, you cannot install software on the underlying host because AWS manages the data plane. Since Fargate doesn't yet have support for daemonsets, you have to deploy X-Ray as a sidecar container — a container that runs alongside another container in the same Fargate task. The X-Ray daemon container needs permission to upload trace segments. Add managed policies to your task role to grant the daemon permission to upload trace data to X-Ray. The standard managed policy is `AWSXRayDaemonWriteAccess` attached to the **task role** (not the execution role), because the daemon container itself, running inside the task, makes the X-Ray API calls.

### D. Instrument the application with the X-Ray SDK; communicate with the X-Ray daemon ✅
The application must be instrumented to generate trace segments. To integrate application tracing with your applications, use the X-Ray SDK for one of the supported programming languages. The SDK does **not** call the X-Ray API directly — it sends segments via UDP to the local X-Ray daemon, which batches and forwards them. By default, the X-Ray SDK expects the daemon to be available on 127.0.0.1:2000. Since we're running X-Ray as a sidecar container, no changes are necessary.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

### B. Deploy X-Ray as a daemonset; update the service role ❌
"DaemonSet" is a **Kubernetes (EKS) concept**, not Fargate/ECS. In Christoph Kassen's blog post, he describes how to deploy the X-Ray pod as a Kubernetes daemonset. A daemonset is a special type of deployment strategy that places one instance of a pod onto each instance in the cluster. It will also deploy an instance of that pod onto Kubernetes workers as they're added to the cluster. Since Fargate doesn't yet have support for daemonsets, you have to deploy X-Ray as a sidecar container. Also, the **service role** is not the correct role to grant X-Ray write permissions; the **task role** is what containers in the task assume.

### C. Instrument with X-Ray SDK; use `PutXrayTrace` API directly ❌
There is no `PutXrayTrace` API call (the actual API is `PutTraceSegments`), and more importantly the X-Ray SDK is **not designed to call the X-Ray API directly from the application**. The way that AWS solves this problem is by introducing a notion of an X-Ray Daemon. X-Ray Daemon is a process that runs along side your service. The job of X-Ray Daemon is to collect the traces and send them to the API in a performant manner. Instead of sending an http request to an X-Ray API in a service, the instrumentation will report tracing info to the daemon using a lighter protocol (UDP) and that daemon in turn handles reporting to X-Ray API in an optimal manner. Bypassing the daemon adds unnecessary latency and load.

### E. Send stdout/stderr to CloudWatch Logs; allow `cloudwatch:PullLogs` ❌
There is **no `cloudwatch:PullLogs` IAM action** — this is a fabricated permission. The correct logs API actions are `logs:CreateLogGroup`, `logs:CreateLogStream`, and `logs:PutLogEvents` (granted via the **task execution role**, typically through `AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy`). Even if logs were sent to CloudWatch, raw application logs alone don't trace requests across microservices the way X-Ray does, so this isn't the right combination for diagnosing distributed errors.

## References
- [Running the X-Ray daemon on Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-daemon-ecs.html)
- [aws-samples/aws-xray-fargate (sidecar pattern)](https://github.com/aws-samples/aws-xray-fargate)
- [Deploying the CloudWatch agent and X-Ray daemon on Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/deploy_servicelens_CloudWatch_agent_deploy_ECS.html)
- [Giving the daemon permission to send data to X-Ray](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-daemon-permissions.html)

zh.explanation:
# ECS/Fargate 微服务 X-Ray 故障排除

## 场景
在 **Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate** 上运行的微服务应用程序正在出现错误。开发人员需要识别并修复这些错误。要诊断分布式微服务，**AWS X-Ray** 是正确的工具 — 它提供跨服务的分布式追踪，暴露延迟瓶颈、故障和错误。问题要求两个步骤来正确启用 Fargate 支持的 ECS 应用程序上的 X-Ray 追踪。

## 正确答案：A 和 D

### A. 将 AWS X-Ray 部署为 sidecar 容器；更新任务角色以允许 X-Ray API 访问 ✅
在 Fargate 上，您无法在底层主机上安装软件，因为 AWS 管理数据平面。由于 Fargate 还不支持 daemonset，您必须将 X-Ray 部署为 sidecar 容器 — 一个与同一 Fargate 任务中的另一个容器一起运行的容器。X-Ray daemon 容器需要权限来上传追踪段。将托管策略添加到您的任务角色以授予 daemon 权限来将追踪数据上传到 X-Ray。标准托管策略是 `AWSXRayDaemonWriteAccess`，附加到**任务角色**（而非执行角色），因为 daemon 容器本身在任务内运行，会进行 X-Ray API 调用。

### D. 使用 X-Ray SDK 对应用程序进行检测；与 X-Ray daemon 通信 ✅
应用程序必须经过检测才能生成追踪段。要将应用程序追踪与应用程序集成，请使用支持的编程语言之一的 X-Ray SDK。SDK **不会**直接调用 X-Ray API — 它通过 UDP 将段发送到本地 X-Ray daemon，后者对它们进行批处理并转发。默认情况下，X-Ray SDK 期望 daemon 可在 127.0.0.1:2000 上使用。由于我们将 X-Ray 作为 sidecar 容器运行，无需进行任何更改。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

### B. 将 X-Ray 部署为 daemonset；更新服务角色 ❌
"DaemonSet" 是一个 **Kubernetes (EKS) 概念**，而不是 Fargate/ECS。在 Christoph Kassen 的博文中，他描述了如何将 X-Ray pod 部署为 Kubernetes daemonset。Daemonset 是一种特殊的部署策略，在集群中的每个实例上放置一个 pod 实例。它还会在 Kubernetes 工作者添加到集群时在其上部署该 pod 的实例。由于 Fargate 还不支持 daemonset，您必须将 X-Ray 部署为 sidecar 容器。此外，**服务角色**不是授予 X-Ray 写入权限的正确角色；**任务角色**是任务中的容器假设的角色。

### C. 使用 X-Ray SDK 进行检测；直接使用 `PutXrayTrace` API ❌
不存在 `PutXrayTrace` API 调用（实际 API 是 `PutTraceSegments`），更重要的是，X-Ray SDK **不是设计用来从应用程序直接调用 X-Ray API 的**。AWS 解决这个问题的方式是引入 X-Ray Daemon 的概念。X-Ray Daemon 是与您的服务一起运行的进程。X-Ray Daemon 的工作是收集追踪信息并以高效的方式将其发送到 API。与其向服务中的 X-Ray API 发送 http 请求，检测会使用更轻的协议 (UDP) 向 daemon 报告追踪信息，而该 daemon 反过来以最优方式处理向 X-Ray API 的报告。绕过 daemon 会增加不必要的延迟和负载。

### E. 将 stdout/stderr 发送到 CloudWatch Logs；允许 `cloudwatch:PullLogs` ❌
**不存在 `cloudwatch:PullLogs` IAM 操作** — 这是一个虚构的权限。正确的日志 API 操作是 `logs:CreateLogGroup`、`logs:CreateLogStream` 和 `logs:PutLogEvents`（通过**任务执行角色**授予，通常通过 `AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy`）。即使日志被发送到 CloudWatch，原始应用程序日志本身也不会像 X-Ray 那样跨微服务追踪请求，所以这不是诊断分布式错误的正确组合。

## 参考资源
- [Running the X-Ray daemon on Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-daemon-ecs.html)
- [aws-samples/aws-xray-fargate (sidecar pattern)](https://github.com/aws-samples/aws-xray-fargate)
- [Deploying the CloudWatch agent and X-Ray daemon on Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/deploy_servicelens_CloudWatch_agent_deploy_ECS.html)
- [Giving the daemon permission to send data to X-Ray](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-daemon-permissions.html)

en.question: A developer is creating an application for a company. The application needs to read the file doc.txt that is placed in the root folder of an Amazon S3 bucket that is named DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET. The company’s security team requires the principle of least privilege to be applied to the application’s IAM policy. Which IAM policy statement will meet these security requirements?
en.explanation:
## Scenario

The application needs to read **only one specific object** (`doc.txt`) from the root of the S3 bucket `DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET`. The security team requires the **principle of least privilege**, meaning the IAM policy must grant the minimum permissions necessary — only the `s3:GetObject` action on only that single object.

## Correct Answer: A

```json
{
    "Action": ["s3:GetObject"],
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET/doc.txt"
}
```

This is the most restrictive policy that still satisfies the requirement:
- **Action** is limited to `s3:GetObject`, the only action needed to read an object.
- **Resource** is scoped to the exact object ARN (`arn:aws:s3:::DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET/doc.txt`), not the entire bucket.

AWS recommends specifying resources by their exact ARN whenever possible to apply least privilege ([How Amazon S3 works with IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/security_iam_service-with-iam.html)). The AWS Security Blog on [Techniques for writing least privilege IAM policies](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/techniques-for-writing-least-privilege-iam-policies/) explicitly demonstrates narrowing `s3:GetObject` to a specific bucket/object ARN.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **B.** `"Action": "s3:*"` on `"Resource": "*"` grants every S3 API action (read, write, delete, modify ACLs, etc.) on **every** bucket and object in the account. This is the opposite of least privilege.

- **C.** `"Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET/*"` allows `s3:GetObject` on **every** object in the bucket, not just `doc.txt`. The wildcard `/*` matches all object keys, which is broader than required.

- **D.** Although the resource is correctly scoped to `doc.txt`, `"Action": "s3:*"` allows **all** S3 actions on that object, including `s3:DeleteObject`, `s3:PutObject`, `s3:PutObjectAcl`, etc. The application only needs to *read* the file, so this violates least privilege.

## Key Takeaway

Least privilege requires narrowing **both** the action list **and** the resource ARN to the minimum needed. Only Option A does both: a single read action (`s3:GetObject`) on a single object ARN.

## References

- [How Amazon S3 works with IAM – AWS docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/security_iam_service-with-iam.html)
- [Techniques for writing least privilege IAM policies – AWS Security Blog](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/techniques-for-writing-least-privilege-iam-policies/)
- [Identity-based policy examples for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/example-policies-s3.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在为一家公司开发一个应用程序。该应用程序需要读取位于名为 DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET 的 Amazon S3 存储桶根文件夹中的 doc.txt 文件。该公司的安全团队要求该应用程序的 IAM 策略必须遵循最小权限原则。以下哪个 IAM 策略语句能够满足这些安全要求？
zh.explanation:
## 场景

应用程序需要**仅读取一个特定的对象**（`doc.txt`）从 S3 存储桶 `DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET` 的根目录。安全团队要求遵循**最小权限原则**，这意味着 IAM 策略必须授予最少必要的权限 — 仅在该单个对象上的 `s3:GetObject` 操作。

## 正确答案：A

```json
{
    "Action": ["s3:GetObject"],
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET/doc.txt"
}
```

这是仍然满足要求的最具限制性的策略：
- **Action** 限制为 `s3:GetObject`，这是读取对象所需的唯一操作。
- **Resource** 限定于确切的对象 ARN（`arn:aws:s3:::DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET/doc.txt`），而不是整个存储桶。

AWS 建议尽可能按照确切的 ARN 指定资源以应用最小权限原则（[Amazon S3 如何与 IAM 协作](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/security_iam_service-with-iam.html)）。AWS 安全博客上关于[编写最小权限 IAM 策略的技术](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/techniques-for-writing-least-privilege-iam-policies/)明确演示了如何将 `s3:GetObject` 限定于特定的存储桶/对象 ARN。

## 其他选项为何错误

- **B.** `"Action": "s3:*"` 作用于 `"Resource": "*"` 授予了**每一个** S3 API 操作（读取、写入、删除、修改 ACL 等）在账户中**每一个**存储桶和对象上的权限。这与最小权限原则相反。

- **C.** `"Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET/*"` 允许对**存储桶中的每一个**对象执行 `s3:GetObject`，而不仅仅是 `doc.txt`。通配符 `/*` 匹配所有对象键，这超出了所需范围。

- **D.** 虽然资源正确地限定于 `doc.txt`，但 `"Action": "s3:*"` 允许在该对象上执行**所有** S3 操作，包括 `s3:DeleteObject`、`s3:PutObject`、`s3:PutObjectAcl` 等。应用程序仅需要*读取*该文件，因此这违反了最小权限原则。

## 关键要点

最小权限原则要求同时缩小**操作列表**和**资源 ARN** 到最少必要范围。只有选项 A 同时做到了这两点：单个读取操作（`s3:GetObject`）作用于单个对象 ARN。

## 参考资源

- [Amazon S3 如何与 IAM 协作 – AWS 文档](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/security_iam_service-with-iam.html)
- [编写最小权限 IAM 策略的技术 – AWS 安全博客](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/techniques-for-writing-least-privilege-iam-policies/)
- [Amazon S3 基于身份的策略示例](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/example-policies-s3.html)

en.question: A company has an application that uses AWS CodePipeline to automate its continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) workflow. The application uses AWS CodeCommit for version control. A developer who was working on one of the tasks did not pull the most recent changes from the main branch. A week later, the developer noticed merge conflicts. How can the developer resolve the merge conflicts in the developer's branch with the LEAST development effort?

options.A: Clone the repository. Create a new branch. Update the branch with the changes.
options.B: Create a new branch. Apply the changes from the previous branch.
options.C: Use the Commit Visualizer view to compare the commits when a feature was added. Fix the merge conflicts.
options.D: Stop the pull from the main branch to the feature branch. Rebase the feature branch from the main branch.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A developer's feature branch has diverged from `main` over the course of a week, and now there are merge conflicts. The question asks for the way to resolve these conflicts with the **least development effort**.

## Correct Answer: D — Rebase the feature branch from the main branch

Rebasing the feature branch onto `main` replays the developer's commits on top of the latest tip of `main`, which is the standard, lowest-effort way to bring a stale feature branch up to date and resolve divergence. The phrase "Stop the pull from the main branch to the feature branch" reflects the idea of not continuously merging `main` into the feature branch (which produces noisy merge commits) and instead doing a single rebase to linearize history.

CodeCommit is a standard Git service, so all normal Git workflows apply. AWS guidance and Git best practice show that when a feature branch has diverged from `main`, you can either merge `main` into it or rebase onto it; rebasing produces a cleaner result and conflicts are resolved as a normal part of the rebase. After rebasing locally, the developer pushes the updated feature branch back to CodeCommit, where the pull request will return to a "Mergable" state ([Using CodeCommit Pull Requests](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/devops/using-aws-codecommit-pull-requests-to-request-code-reviews-and-discuss-code/), [Compare and merge branches in CodeCommit](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-compare-branches.html)).

## Why the other options are wrong

- **A. Clone the repository, create a new branch, update the branch with the changes.** Cloning a fresh copy and creating yet another branch does not resolve the existing conflicts — the same conflicts will reappear when the new branch is merged into `main`. It also adds extra steps (re-cloning, re-applying work) which is *more* development effort, not less.

- **B. Create a new branch and apply the changes from the previous branch.** Manually re-applying changes (cherry-picking or copying files) into a new branch is essentially doing the merge by hand. It is more labor-intensive than a rebase and does not leverage Git's built-in conflict resolution machinery.

- **C. Use the Commit Visualizer view to compare commits when a feature was added. Fix the merge conflicts.** The [Commit Visualizer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-view-commit-details.html#how-to-view-commit-details-console-visualizer) is a read-only DAG visualization tool — it helps you *understand* commit history but provides no mechanism to *resolve* conflicts. You would still need to perform a merge or rebase afterwards, so it adds an extra investigation step rather than reducing effort. CodeCommit's actual conflict resolution happens via the pull-request "Resolve conflicts" editor or local Git merge/rebase, not in the visualizer ([Resolve conflicts in a pull request](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-resolve-conflict-pull-request.html)).

## Key takeaways

- Treat CodeCommit like any Git remote — `git rebase main` on the feature branch is the canonical, lowest-effort way to reconcile a stale branch.
- The Commit Visualizer is a viewing aid, not a conflict-resolution tool.
- Creating a brand-new branch does not eliminate conflicts; the divergent changes still must be reconciled.

zh.question: 一家公司使用 AWS CodePipeline 来自动化其持续集成和持续交付 (CI/CD) 工作流程，并使用 AWS CodeCommit 进行版本控制。一位正在处理某个任务的开发人员没有从主分支拉取最新更改。一周后，该开发人员发现合并冲突。如何以最小的开发工作量解决开发人员分支中的合并冲突？

options.A: 克隆代码仓库。创建一个新分支。将更改更新到该分支。
options.B: 创建一个新分支。应用来自前一个分支的更改。
options.C: 使用提交可视化工具视图比较添加功能时的提交记录，并修复合并冲突。
options.D: 停止从主分支拉取代码到特性分支。从主分支变基特性分支。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

一名开发者的功能分支在一周内已经与 `main` 分支产生分歧，现在出现了合并冲突。问题要求以**最少开发工作量**的方式解决这些冲突。

## 正确答案：D — 将功能分支从 main 分支进行变基

将功能分支变基到 `main` 会将开发者的提交重新应用到 `main` 的最新顶端，这是使陈旧功能分支保持最新状态并解决分歧的标准且工作量最少的方法。短语"停止从 main 分支拉取到功能分支"反映了不持续地合并 `main` 到功能分支的理念（这会产生冗余合并提交），而是执行单次变基以线性化历史。

CodeCommit 是标准的 Git 服务，因此所有常规 Git 工作流都适用。AWS 指南和 Git 最佳实践表明，当功能分支与 `main` 产生分歧时，你可以选择将 `main` 合并到它或变基到它；变基会产生更清洁的结果，冲突作为变基的一个正常部分被解决。在本地变基后，开发者将更新后的功能分支推送回 CodeCommit，此时拉取请求将恢复到"可合并"状态（[Using CodeCommit Pull Requests](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/devops/using-aws-codecommit-pull-requests-to-request-code-reviews-and-discuss-code/)、[Compare and merge branches in CodeCommit](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-compare-branches.html)）。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

- **A. 克隆仓库、创建新分支、使用更改更新该分支。** 克隆一份新副本并创建另一个分支无法解决现有冲突 — 当新分支合并到 `main` 时，相同的冲突会再次出现。这还增加了额外步骤（重新克隆、重新应用工作），这是*更多*开发工作量而非更少。

- **B. 创建新分支并应用之前分支的更改。** 手动重新应用更改（cherry-pick 或复制文件）到新分支本质上是手工执行合并。这比变基更加费力，且没有利用 Git 的内置冲突解决机制。

- **C. 使用提交可视化器视图来比较添加功能时的提交。修复合并冲突。** [提交可视化器](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-view-commit-details.html#how-to-view-commit-details-console-visualizer)是一个只读 DAG 可视化工具 — 它可以帮助你*理解*提交历史，但无法*解决*冲突。你仍然需要之后执行合并或变基，因此它增加了额外的调查步骤而非减少工作量。CodeCommit 的实际冲突解决发生在拉取请求的"解决冲突"编辑器或本地 Git 合并/变基中，而非在可视化器中（[Resolve conflicts in a pull request](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-resolve-conflict-pull-request.html)）。

## 关键要点

- 将 CodeCommit 视为任何 Git 远程仓库 — 在功能分支上执行 `git rebase main` 是协调陈旧分支的规范且工作量最少的方法。
- 提交可视化器是一个查看辅助工具，而非冲突解决工具。
- 创建全新分支无法消除冲突；分歧的更改仍然必须被协调。

en.question: A developer wants to add request validation to a production environment Amazon API Gateway API. The developer needs to test the changes before the API is deployed to the production environment. For the test, the developer will send test requests to the API through a testing tool. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Export the existing API to an OpenAPI file. Create a new API. Import the OpenAPI file. Modify the new API to add request validation. Perform the tests. Modify the existing API to add request validation. Deploy the existing API to production.
options.B: Modify the existing API to add request validation. Deploy the updated API to a new API Gateway stage. Perform the tests. Deploy the updated API to the API Gateway production stage.
options.C: Create a new API. Add the necessary resources and methods, including new request validation. Perform the tests. Modify the existing API to add request validation. Deploy the existing API to production
options.D: Clone the existing API. Modify the new API to add request validation. Perform the tests. Modify the existing API to add request validation. Deploy the existing API to production.

en.explanation:
# API Gateway: Testing Request Validation Changes Before Production

## Scenario
A developer needs to add request validation to a production API Gateway API. They want to test the validation changes via a testing tool before exposing them to production traffic, with the **least operational overhead**.

## Why B is Correct

API Gateway uses **stages** as named references to deployments (snapshots) of an API. An API stage is a logical reference to a lifecycle state of your API (for example, dev, prod, beta, or v2). API stages are identified by their API ID and stage name, and they're included in the URL you use to invoke the API. Each stage is a named reference to a deployment of the API and is made available for client applications to call.

The simplest approach is to:
1. Modify the existing API to add request validation.
2. Deploy that updated configuration to a **new (non-production) stage** (e.g., `test`).
3. Send test requests through the testing tool to the new stage's invoke URL.
4. Once validated, deploy the same API to the existing **production stage**.

This works because when making changes to the REST API definitions, you can first deploy it to the Test stage, test the changes first, and push it to the Prod stage when ready. Each stage gets its own unique invoke URL, so production traffic is unaffected while you test.

This is the least-overhead solution because there is **only one API resource** to maintain — no exporting/importing, no cloning, and no duplicating resources/methods. You also avoid the risk of configuration drift between two separate APIs.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

### A. Export to OpenAPI, create a new API, import, modify, test, then modify the existing API again
- Requires creating and managing a **second API** plus an OpenAPI export/import cycle.
- Request validation changes must be made **twice** (once on the imported API, again on the production API), introducing overhead and risk of mismatch.
- See [Working with API Gateway extensions to OpenAPI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-swagger-extensions.html).

### C. Create a brand-new API from scratch with new resources/methods
- Highest overhead — you have to **rebuild all resources, methods, integrations, and authorizers** from scratch just to test validation.
- Validation logic must again be duplicated onto the production API afterward.

### D. Clone the existing API, modify, test, then modify the existing API
- API Gateway's "clone" produces a **second independent API** that must be maintained separately. Validation work has to be done **twice** (once on the clone for testing, again on the production API). 
- Stages on the existing API already provide the same isolation without the duplication. See [Set up a stage for a REST API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/set-up-stages.html).

## Key AWS Docs
- [Stages for REST APIs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/set-up-stages.html)
- [Stages for HTTP APIs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/http-api-stages.html)
- [Request validation in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-method-request-validation.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员希望在生产环境中的 Amazon API Gateway API 中添加请求验证功能。在将 API 部署到生产环境之前，开发人员需要测试这些更改。测试时，开发人员将通过测试工具向 API 发送测试请求。哪种解决方案能够以最小的运维开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 将现有 API 导出为 OpenAPI 文件。创建一个新的 API。导入 OpenAPI 文件。修改新 API 以添加请求验证。执行测试。修改现有 API 以添加请求验证。将现有 API 部署到生产环境。
options.B: 修改现有 API 以添加请求验证。将更新后的 API 部署到新的 API 网关阶段。执行测试。将更新后的 API 部署到 API 网关生产阶段。
options.C: 创建新的 API。添加必要的资源和方法，包括新的请求验证。执行测试。修改现有 API 以添加请求验证。将现有 API 部署到生产环境。
options.D: 克隆现有 API。修改新 API 以添加请求验证。执行测试。修改现有 API 以添加请求验证。将现有 API 部署到生产环境。

zh.explanation:
# API Gateway：在生产环境前测试请求验证更改

## 场景
开发人员需要向生产 API Gateway API 添加请求验证。他们想通过测试工具测试验证更改，然后再将其暴露给生产流量，**运营开销最少**。

## 为什么 B 是正确的

API Gateway 使用**阶段** (stage) 作为 API 部署（快照）的命名引用。API 阶段是对 API 生命周期状态的逻辑引用（例如 dev、prod、beta 或 v2）。API 阶段由其 API ID 和阶段名称标识，并包含在用于调用 API 的 URL 中。每个阶段是 API 部署的命名引用，供客户端应用程序调用。

最简单的方法是：
1. 修改现有 API 以添加请求验证。
2. 将更新后的配置部署到**新的（非生产）阶段**（例如 `test`）。
3. 通过测试工具向新阶段的调用 URL 发送测试请求。
4. 验证完成后，将相同的 API 部署到现有的**生产阶段**。

这行得通是因为当对 REST API 定义进行更改时，可以先将其部署到 Test 阶段，先测试更改，然后在准备好时推送到 Prod 阶段。每个阶段都有自己唯一的调用 URL，因此生产流量不受影响，同时您可以进行测试。

这是开销最少的解决方案，因为**只需维护一个 API 资源**——无需导出/导入、无需克隆，也无需复制资源/方法。您还可以避免两个独立 API 之间配置漂移的风险。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

### A. 导出为 OpenAPI、创建新 API、导入、修改、测试，然后再次修改现有 API
- 需要创建和管理**第二个 API** 以及 OpenAPI 导出/导入周期。
- 请求验证更改必须进行**两次**（一次在导入的 API 上，再次在生产 API 上），引入开销和不匹配风险。
- 参阅[在 OpenAPI 中使用 API Gateway 扩展](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-swagger-extensions.html)。

### C. 从头创建全新 API，使用新资源/方法
- 开销最高——您必须从头**重新构建所有资源、方法、集成和授权方**，仅仅为了测试验证。
- 验证逻辑之后必须再次复制到生产 API。

### D. 克隆现有 API、修改、测试，然后修改现有 API
- API Gateway 的"克隆"会生成**第二个独立 API**，必须单独维护。验证工作必须进行**两次**（一次在克隆上进行测试，再次在生产 API 上）。
- 现有 API 上的阶段已经提供相同的隔离，无需重复。参阅[为 REST API 设置阶段](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/set-up-stages.html)。

## 关键 AWS 文档
- [REST API 的阶段](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/set-up-stages.html)
- [HTTP API 的阶段](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/http-api-stages.html)
- [API Gateway 中的请求验证](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-method-request-validation.html)

en.question: An online food company provides an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API to receive orders for partners. The API is integrated with an AWS Lambda function. The Lambda function stores the orders in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company expects to onboard additional partners. Some of the partners require additional Lambda functions to receive orders. The company has created an Amazon S3 bucket. The company needs to store all orders and updates in the S3 bucket for future analysis. How can the developer ensure that all orders and updates are stored to Amazon S3 with the LEAST development effort?

options.A: Create a new Lambda function and a new API Gateway API endpoint. Configure the new Lambda function to write to the S3 bucket. Modify the original Lambda function to post updates to the new API endpoint.
options.B: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to create a new data stream. Modify the Lambda function to publish orders to the data stream. Configure the data stream to write to the S3 bucket.
options.C: Enable DynamoDB Streams on the DynamoDB table. Create a new Lambda function. Associate the stream’s Amazon Resource Name (ARN) with the Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to write to the S3 bucket as records appear in the table's stream.
options.D: Modify the Lambda function to publish to a new Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as the Lambda function receives orders. Subscribe a new Lambda function to the topic. Configure the new Lambda function to write to the S3 bucket as updates come through the topic.

en.explanation:
# Capturing All DynamoDB Orders & Updates to S3 with Least Effort

## Scenario
An online food ordering platform receives orders via API Gateway HTTP API → Lambda → DynamoDB. Additional partners may onboard with their own dedicated Lambda functions writing to the same DynamoDB table. The company needs **all** orders and updates persisted into a single S3 bucket for analysis, with **least development effort**.

The key insight: regardless of how many different Lambda functions are added in the future, every order and update ultimately lands in the **DynamoDB table**. So the most efficient capture point is the table itself, not the upstream Lambdas.

## Correct Answer: C — Enable DynamoDB Streams + a single Lambda → S3

If you enable DynamoDB Streams on a table, you can associate the stream Amazon Resource Name (ARN) with an AWS Lambda function that you write. All mutation actions to that DynamoDB table can then be captured as an item on the stream. For example, you can set a trigger so that when an item in a table is modified a new record immediately appears in that table's stream.

This means **a single new Lambda triggered by the DynamoDB Stream** will see every INSERT/MODIFY/REMOVE produced by *any* of the partner Lambdas — without modifying any existing code paths. You can write a Lambda function to simply copy each stream record to persistent storage, such as Amazon S3, and create a permanent audit trail of write activity in your table.

This is exactly the canonical AWS pattern (also used by AWS's own [archive-to-S3 prescriptive guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/patterns/automatically-archive-items-to-amazon-s3-using-dynamodb-ttl.html)) and requires:
1. Toggle DynamoDB Streams ON (one click / one CFN property).
2. Create one new Lambda with `s3:PutObject` permission.
3. Add the stream ARN as an event source mapping. To enable a trigger, you associate its ARN with an existing Lambda function and specify the trigger options. This is done by creating an Event Source Mapping that links your DynamoDB Stream with your function.

No existing Lambda code is touched — crucial because new partner Lambdas are expected to be added.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

### A. New Lambda + new API Gateway endpoint, original Lambda POSTs updates
- Requires modifying the **existing** Lambda (and every future partner Lambda) to POST to a second API endpoint. As partners are added, every new Lambda must implement and maintain this dual-write logic.
- Introduces extra network hops, IAM/SigV4 considerations, retry/error handling, and double-billing for API Gateway requests.
- Risk of inconsistency: an order may succeed in DynamoDB but fail to reach the second API.

### B. Kinesis Data Streams → S3
- KDS does **not** natively deliver to S3. You would need **Amazon Data Firehose** (or a consumer Lambda) in between — the option's claim that the data stream itself "writes to the S3 bucket" is technically incorrect.
- Still requires modifying every existing and future partner Lambda to publish to the stream — same maintenance burden as A.
- More moving parts (shards, capacity mode, consumers) than a Streams + Lambda trigger.

### D. SNS topic fan-out to a logging Lambda
- Again requires editing the existing Lambda (and every future partner Lambda) to `Publish` to SNS on every order/update — high coupling and maintenance.
- SNS delivery is best-effort and asynchronous; if the publish call is omitted in any new partner's Lambda, those orders will never reach S3. DynamoDB Streams, by contrast, captures *every* table mutation automatically.

## Key AWS Documentation
- [DynamoDB Streams and AWS Lambda triggers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Streams.Lambda.html)
- [Using AWS Lambda with Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-ddb.html)
- [Automatically archive items to S3 using DynamoDB TTL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/patterns/automatically-archive-items-to-amazon-s3-using-dynamodb-ttl.html)

**Answer: C**

zh.question: 一家在线食品公司提供 Amazon API Gateway HTTP API 来接收合作伙伴的订单。该 API 与 AWS Lambda 函数集成。Lambda 函数将订单存储在 Amazon DynamoDB 表中。该公司计划引入更多合作伙伴。部分合作伙伴需要额外的 Lambda 函数来接收订单。该公司已创建 Amazon S3 存储桶。为了便于后续分析，该公司需要将所有订单和更新存储在 S3 存储桶中。开发人员如何才能以最小的开发工作量确保所有订单和更新都存储到 Amazon S3 中？

options.A: 创建一个新的 Lambda 函数和一个新的 API 网关 API 端点。配置新的 Lambda 函数以写入 S3 存储桶。修改原始 Lambda 函数，使其将更新发布到新的 API 端点。
options.B: 使用 Amazon Kinesis Data Streams 创建一个新的数据流。修改 Lambda 函数，将订单发布到该数据流。配置该数据流以写入 S3 存储桶。
options.C: 在 DynamoDB 表上启用 DynamoDB Streams。创建一个新的 Lambda 函数。将流的 Amazon 资源名称 (ARN) 与 Lambda 函数关联。配置 Lambda 函数，使其在表流中出现记录时写入 S3 存储桶。
options.D: 修改 Lambda 函数，使其在收到订单时发布到新的 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题。将新的 Lambda 函数订阅到该主题。配置新的 Lambda 函数，使其在主题更新时写入 S3 存储桶。

zh.explanation:
# 使用最少努力将所有 DynamoDB 订单和更新捕获到 S3

## 场景
一个在线美食订单平台通过 API Gateway HTTP API → Lambda → DynamoDB 接收订单。其他合作伙伴可能会加入，使用自己的专用 Lambda 函数向同一个 DynamoDB 表写入数据。公司需要将**所有**订单和更新持久化到单个 S3 存储桶中用于分析，**开发工作量最少**。

关键洞察：无论未来添加多少个不同的 Lambda 函数，每个订单和更新最终都会进入 **DynamoDB 表**。因此，最高效的捕获点是表本身，而不是上游的 Lambda。

## 正确答案：C — 启用 DynamoDB Streams + 单个 Lambda → S3

如果在表上启用 DynamoDB Streams，可以将流的 Amazon Resource Name (ARN) 与编写的 AWS Lambda 函数关联。对该 DynamoDB 表的所有变更操作都可以作为流上的项进行捕获。例如，可以设置触发器，使得当表中的项被修改时，新记录立即出现在该表的流中。

这意味着**由 DynamoDB Stream 触发的单个新 Lambda** 将看到*任何*合作伙伴 Lambda 生成的每个 INSERT/MODIFY/REMOVE——而无需修改任何现有代码路径。可以编写一个 Lambda 函数，简单地将每个流记录复制到持久存储（如 Amazon S3），并为表中的写入活动创建永久审计日志。

这正是规范的 AWS 模式（也被 AWS 自己的[归档到 S3 的最佳实践指南](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/patterns/automatically-archive-items-to-amazon-s3-using-dynamodb-ttl.html)所使用），需要：
1. 启用 DynamoDB Streams（一次点击/一个 CFN 属性）。
2. 创建一个具有 `s3:PutObject` 权限的新 Lambda。
3. 将流 ARN 添加为事件源映射。要启用触发器，需要将其 ARN 与现有 Lambda 函数关联，并指定触发器选项。这是通过创建事件源映射来完成的，该映射将 DynamoDB Stream 与函数链接起来。

不涉及现有 Lambda 代码——这很关键，因为预计会添加新的合作伙伴 Lambda。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

### A. 新 Lambda + 新 API Gateway 端点，原始 Lambda POST 更新
- 需要修改**现有** Lambda（以及每个未来的合作伙伴 Lambda）以 POST 到第二个 API 端点。随着合作伙伴的增加，每个新 Lambda 都必须实现并维护这种双写逻辑。
- 引入额外的网络跳转、IAM/SigV4 考虑、重试/错误处理和 API Gateway 请求的双倍计费。
- 一致性风险：订单可能在 DynamoDB 中成功，但无法到达第二个 API。

### B. Kinesis Data Streams → S3
- KDS **不**原生交付到 S3。你需要在中间添加 **Amazon Data Firehose**（或消费者 Lambda）——该选项声称数据流本身"写入 S3 存储桶"在技术上是不正确的。
- 仍然需要修改每个现有和未来的合作伙伴 Lambda 以发布到流——与 A 相同的维护负担。
- 比 Streams + Lambda 触发器有更多活动部件（分片、容量模式、消费者）。

### D. SNS 主题扇出到日志记录 Lambda
- 再次需要编辑现有 Lambda（以及每个未来的合作伙伴 Lambda）在每个订单/更新时 `Publish` 到 SNS——高耦合性和维护成本。
- SNS 交付是尽力而为的异步方式；如果任何新合作伙伴的 Lambda 中遗漏发布调用，这些订单将永远无法到达 S3。相比之下，DynamoDB Streams 自动捕获*每个*表的变更。

## 关键 AWS 文档
- [DynamoDB Streams 和 AWS Lambda 触发器](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Streams.Lambda.html)
- [将 AWS Lambda 与 Amazon DynamoDB 结合使用](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-ddb.html)
- [使用 DynamoDB TTL 自动将项归档到 S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/patterns/automatically-archive-items-to-amazon-s3-using-dynamodb-ttl.html)

**答案：C**

en.question: A company’s website runs on an Amazon EC2 instance and uses Auto Scaling to scale the environment during peak times. Website users across the world are experiencing high latency due to static content on the EC2 instance, even during non-peak hours. Which combination of steps will resolve the latency issue? (Choose two.)

options.A: Double the Auto Scaling group’s maximum number of servers.
options.B: Host the application code on AWS Lambda.
options.C: Scale vertically by resizing the EC2 instances.
options.D: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to cache the static content.
options.E: Store the application’s static content in Amazon S3.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A website runs on EC2 with Auto Scaling. Global users experience high latency due to **static content** served from the EC2 instance — even during non-peak hours. This means the issue is **not capacity-related** (Auto Scaling already handles peak load), but rather a **content delivery / geographic distribution** problem.

The fix needs to (1) move static content off EC2 to a purpose-built object store, and (2) deliver it from edge locations close to users.

## Correct Answers: D and E

**E. Store the application's static content in Amazon S3** — Offloading static assets (HTML, CSS, JS, images, videos) from the EC2 instance to S3 is the standard AWS pattern. Amazon S3 is a cloud object storage suitable for hosting static websites, while Amazon CloudFront is a CDN designed to work with Amazon S3 origins to decrease latency and improve user experience. S3 alone, however, still serves from a single region.

**D. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to cache the static content** — CloudFront caches the S3-hosted assets at edge locations worldwide. Amazon CloudFront is a CDN that uses a global network of edge locations for content delivery. It can distribute content with low latency and high data transfer rates. No matter where a visitor lives in the world, there is an Amazon CloudFront edge location that is relatively close (from an Internet latency perspective). The edge locations cache content from an origin server and deliver that cached content to the user.

The combined S3 + CloudFront pattern is the AWS-recommended architecture. When creating an Amazon CloudFront distribution, specify your Amazon S3 bucket as the origin server.

## Why the other options are wrong

- **A. Double the Auto Scaling group's maximum number of servers.** Auto Scaling addresses **compute capacity** during traffic spikes. The problem occurs *even during non-peak hours*, so the bottleneck is not capacity. Adding more EC2 instances in a single region will not reduce the geographic latency for global users.

- **B. Host the application code on AWS Lambda.** Lambda changes the compute model but does not address content delivery latency. Lambda functions still execute in a single AWS region (unless using Lambda@Edge specifically configured for that), so global users would still experience the same geographic latency for static assets. It also requires re-architecting the entire application unnecessarily.

- **C. Scale vertically by resizing the EC2 instances.** A larger instance provides more CPU/RAM/network throughput at the origin, but does nothing to shorten the physical distance between the EC2 instance and far-away users. Latency for global users is dominated by network round-trip time, not server compute speed.

## Reference Architecture

```
User (global) → CloudFront edge location (cache HIT) → response
                       ↓ (cache MISS)
                  S3 bucket (static content origin)
                  EC2/ASG (dynamic content origin)
```

## AWS Documentation

- [Speeding up your Amazon S3-based website using Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/build-static-websites-aws/speeding-up-your-amazon-s3-based-website-using-amazon-cloudfront.html)
- [Amazon CloudFront — Content Delivery Network](https://aws.amazon.com/cloudfront/)
- [Hosting a static website using Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/WebsiteHosting.html)

zh.question: 一家公司的网站运行在 Amazon EC2 实例上，并使用自动扩展功能在高峰时段扩展环境。由于 EC2 实例上的内容是静态的，即使在非高峰时段，全球各地的网站用户也都会遇到高延迟问题。以下哪两项措施可以解决延迟问题？

options.A: 将自动扩展组的最大服务器数量加倍。
options.B: 将应用程序代码托管在 AWS Lambda 上。
options.C: 通过调整 EC2 实例的大小进行垂直扩展。
options.D: 创建 Amazon CloudFront 分发以缓存静态内容。
options.E: 将应用程序的静态内容存储在 Amazon S3 中。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

一个网站运行在具有自动扩展的 EC2 上。全球用户经历高延迟，因为**静态内容**从 EC2 实例提供——即使在非峰值时段也是如此。这意味着问题**不是容量相关的**（Auto Scaling 已经处理峰值负载），而是**内容交付 / 地理分布**问题。

该解决方案需要（1）将静态内容从 EC2 迁出到专用对象存储，以及（2）从靠近用户的边缘位置交付。

## 正确答案：D 和 E

**E. 在 Amazon S3 中存储应用程序的静态内容** — 将静态资产（HTML、CSS、JS、图像、视频）从 EC2 实例卸载到 S3 是标准的 AWS 模式。Amazon S3 是一个适合托管静态网站的云对象存储，而 Amazon CloudFront 是一个 CDN，设计用于与 Amazon S3 源配合以降低延迟并改善用户体验。但是，S3 单独仍然从单个区域提供。

**D. 创建 Amazon CloudFront 分布以缓存静态内容** — CloudFront 在全球边缘位置缓存 S3 托管的资产。Amazon CloudFront 是一个 CDN，使用全球边缘位置网络进行内容交付。它可以以低延迟和高数据传输速率分配内容。无论访问者住在世界何处，都有一个 Amazon CloudFront 边缘位置相对较近（从互联网延迟角度来看）。边缘位置从源服务器缓存内容并向用户交付该缓存内容。

S3 + CloudFront 的组合模式是 AWS 推荐的架构。创建 Amazon CloudFront 分布时，指定 Amazon S3 存储桶作为源服务器。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

- **A. 将自动扩展组的最大服务器数翻倍。** Auto Scaling 解决流量峰值期间的**计算容量**问题。问题发生*即使在非峰值时段*，所以瓶颈不是容量。在单个区域中添加更多 EC2 实例不会减少全球用户的地理延迟。

- **B. 在 AWS Lambda 上托管应用程序代码。** Lambda 改变了计算模型但不解决内容交付延迟问题。Lambda 函数仍然在单个 AWS 区域中执行（除非特别配置使用 Lambda@Edge），所以全球用户仍然会经历相同的地理延迟来获取静态资产。它还需要不必要地重新架构整个应用程序。

- **C. 通过调整 EC2 实例大小垂直扩展。** 较大的实例在源处提供更多 CPU/RAM/网络吞吐量，但对缩短 EC2 实例和远方用户之间的物理距离没有任何帮助。全球用户的延迟主要受网络往返时间支配，而不是服务器计算速度。

## 参考架构

```
用户（全球）→ CloudFront 边缘位置（缓存命中）→ 响应
                       ↓ (缓存未命中)
                  S3 存储桶（静态内容源）
                  EC2/ASG（动态内容源）
```

## AWS 文档

- [使用 Amazon CloudFront 加快基于 Amazon S3 的网站速度](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/build-static-websites-aws/speeding-up-your-amazon-s3-based-website-using-amazon-cloudfront.html)
- [Amazon CloudFront — 内容分发网络](https://aws.amazon.com/cloudfront/)
- [使用 Amazon S3 托管静态网站](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/WebsiteHosting.html)

en.question: A company has an Amazon S3 bucket containing premier content that it intends to make available to only paid subscribers of its website. The S3 bucket currently has default permissions of all objects being private to prevent inadvertent exposure of the premier content to non-paying website visitors. How can the company limit the ability to download a premier content file in the S3 bucket to paid subscribers only?

options.A: Apply a bucket policy that allows anonymous users to download the content from the S3 bucket.
options.B: Generate a pre-signed object URL for the premier content file when a paid subscriber requests a download.
options.C: Add a bucket policy that requires multi-factor authentication for requests to access the S3 bucket objects.
options.D: Enable server-side encryption on the S3 bucket for data protection against the non-paying website visitors.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A company stores premier (paid) content in a private S3 bucket and wants to allow only paying subscribers to download specific files, while keeping the bucket and its objects private to the public.

## Correct Answer: B — Generate a pre-signed object URL on demand
