Lambda has no built-in self-scheduler driven by an env var; an external event source is always required to invoke the function.

- **D. SNS topic with a "600-second timer"** — Amazon SNS does **not** have any built-in periodic timer or scheduling feature. SNS is a pub/sub messaging service: it only delivers a message to subscribers when something publishes to the topic. There is no native mechanism in SNS to publish messages on a recurring interval.

## References
- [Tutorial: Schedule a Lambda function (EventBridge)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-run-lambda-schedule.html)
- [Creating a scheduled rule in Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-create-rule-schedule.html)
- [Invoke a Lambda function on a schedule (EventBridge Scheduler)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-eventbridge-scheduler.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在编写一个无服务器应用程序，该应用程序需要每 10 分钟调用一次 AWS Lambda 函数。有没有一种自动化且无服务器的方式来调用该函数？

options.A: 部署一个基于 Linux 的 Amazon EC2 实例，并通过添加定期调用 Lambda 函数的命令来编辑其 /etc/crontab 文件。
options.B: 为 Lambda 函数配置一个名为 PERIOD 的环境变量，并将其值设置为 600。
options.C: 创建一个 Amazon EventBridge 规则，按计划定期运行以调用 Lambda 函数。
options.D: 创建一个 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题，该主题订阅 Lambda 函数，并设置 600 秒的定时器。

zh.explanation:
# 每 10 分钟触发一次 Lambda 函数

## 场景
开发者需要使用完全**自动化**和**无服务器**的方法在固定时间表（每 10 分钟）上调用 Lambda 函数——无需管理服务器，无需手动触发。

## 正确答案：C — Amazon EventBridge 定时规则

Amazon EventBridge（原称 CloudWatch Events）支持在 `rate(...)` 或 `cron(...)` 表达式上触发的定时规则，并将事件传递给 AWS Lambda 函数等目标。在 EventBridge 中，可以创建定时规则以定期运行；要指定速率，可定义速率表达式；要指定时间和日期，可定义 cron 表达式。 选择按固定速率运行的时间表（例如每 10 分钟），并指定值和单位字段以定义速率。

对于"每 10 分钟"，您将使用：

```text
rate(10 minutes)
```

此解决方案完全无服务器：AWS EventBridge 是一个完全托管的无服务器事件总线，可让您创建自定义事件（如 cron 表达式）或从 AWS 服务和外部应用程序捕获事件。 通过控制台配置时，EventBridge 必须有权调用 Lambda 函数，如果使用 EventBridge 控制台创建规则，控制台会自动将所需权限添加到函数的基于资源的策略。

（注：AWS 现在还推荐 EventBridge Scheduler 作为替代方案——AWS 建议改用 Amazon EventBridge Scheduler，因为它提供更好的可扩展性、更广泛的目标 API 操作集、灵活的时间窗口以及内置的重试和死信队列支持。 EventBridge 定时规则和 EventBridge Scheduler 都满足选项 C。）

## 为什么其他选项错误

- **A. EC2 + `/etc/crontab` 中的 cron** — 这**不是无服务器**的。您必须配置、修补、监控并为持续运行的 EC2 实例付费，仅仅是为了运行一个 cron 作业。这也引入了单点故障和操作开销，与无服务器需求相反。

- **B. Lambda 环境变量 `PERIOD=600`** — 环境变量只是在运行时传递给函数的键值配置数据。它们不会触发或安排调用。Lambda 没有由环境变量驱动的内置自我调度程序；始终需要外部事件源来调用函数。

- **D. 带有"600 秒计时器"的 SNS 主题** — Amazon SNS **没有**任何内置的定期计时器或调度功能。SNS 是一项发布/订阅消息传递服务：仅当有内容发布到主题时，它才会向订阅者传递消息。SNS 中没有本机机制来按定期间隔发布消息。

## 参考资源
- [教程：安排 Lambda 函数（EventBridge）](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-run-lambda-schedule.html)
- [在 Amazon EventBridge 中创建定时规则](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-create-rule-schedule.html)
- [按时间表调用 Lambda 函数（EventBridge Scheduler）](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-eventbridge-scheduler.html)

en.question: A company is using Amazon OpenSearch Service to implement an audit monitoring system. A developer needs to create an AWS CloudFormation custom resource that is associated with an AWS Lambda function to configure the OpenSearch Service domain. The Lambda function must access the OpenSearch Service domain by using OpenSearch Service internal master user credentials. What is the MOST secure way to pass these credentials to the Lambda function?

options.A: Use a CloudFormation parameter to pass the master user credentials at deployment to the OpenSearch Service domain’s MasterUserOptions and the Lambda function’s environment variable. Set the NoEcho attribute to true.
options.B: Use a CloudFormation parameter to pass the master user credentials at deployment to the OpenSearch Service domain’s MasterUserOptions and to create a parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Set the NoEcho attribute to true. Create an IAM role that has the ssm:GetParameter permission. Assign the role to the Lambda function. Store the parameter name as the Lambda function’s environment variable. Resolve the parameter’s value at runtime.
options.C: Use a CloudFormation parameter to pass the master user credentials at deployment to the OpenSearch Service domain’s MasterUserOptions and the Lambda function’s environment variable. Encrypt the parameter’s value by using the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encrypt command.
options.D: Use CloudFormation to create an AWS Secrets Manager secret. Use a CloudFormation dynamic reference to retrieve the secret’s value for the OpenSearch Service domain’s MasterUserOptions. Create an IAM role that has the secretsmanager:GetSecretValue permission. Assign the role to the Lambda function. Store the secret’s name as the Lambda function’s environment variable. Resolve the secret’s value at runtime.

en.explanation:
# Securely Passing OpenSearch Master Credentials to a Lambda Function

## Scenario
A CloudFormation custom resource backed by a Lambda function needs to configure an OpenSearch Service domain using the **internal master user credentials**. Both the OpenSearch domain (via `MasterUserOptions`) and the Lambda function need access to those credentials. The question asks for the **MOST secure** way to pass these credentials.

## Correct Answer: D

Option D uses **AWS Secrets Manager** as the source of truth for the credentials, then:
1. Lets CloudFormation fetch the value for `MasterUserOptions` via a **dynamic reference** (`{{resolve:secretsmanager:...}}`).
2. Grants the Lambda execution role `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` permission.
3. Stores only the **secret name** (not the secret value) in the Lambda environment variable.
4. The Lambda calls Secrets Manager at runtime to retrieve the credential.

This is the AWS-recommended pattern. For sensitive data, always use secure string parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store or secrets in AWS Secrets Manager to ensure your data is encrypted at rest. Restrict access to only authorized principals and roles. Regularly rotate your sensitive data, and leverage the automatic rotation features of Secrets Manager.

The OpenSearch `MasterUserOptions.MasterUserPassword` property explicitly supports this pattern: Password for the master user. Only specify if InternalUserDatabaseEnabled is true in AdvancedSecurityOptionsInput. If you don't want to specify this value directly within the template, you can use a dynamic reference instead.

The dynamic reference pattern is `{{resolve:secretsmanager:secret-id:SecretString:json-key}}`, e.g.:

```yaml
MasterUserOptions:
  MasterUserName: !Sub '{{resolve:secretsmanager:${MySecret}:SecretString:username}}'
  MasterUserPassword: !Sub '{{resolve:secretsmanager:${MySecret}:SecretString:password}}'
```

Using the secretsmanager dynamic reference indicates that neither Secrets Manager nor CloudFormation logs should persist any resolved secret value. However, the secret value may show up in the service whose resource it's being used in. The Lambda holds only the secret **name** in its environment variable and resolves the value at runtime via the IAM role — so the plaintext password never lives in the template, the stack outputs, or the Lambda configuration.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

### A. CloudFormation parameter → Lambda environment variable (with `NoEcho: true`)
- `NoEcho` only masks the value in the CloudFormation console/API output. The credential is still placed **in plaintext into the Lambda environment variable**, where anyone with `lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration` can read it.
- No rotation, no central secret management, no encryption-at-rest with a customer-managed KMS key by default.
- Violates AWS guidance to keep sensitive data out of environment variables.

### B. CloudFormation parameter → SSM Parameter Store (standard parameter) with `NoEcho`
- This stores credentials in Parameter Store as a **standard (plaintext) parameter** — the option does not specify `SecureString`. For sensitive data, always use secure string parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store or secrets in AWS Secrets Manager to ensure your data is encrypted at rest.
- Even with SecureString, Parameter Store lacks Secrets Manager's built-in **automatic rotation** for credentials, which is the gold standard for master credentials.
- Less secure than D, which uses the purpose-built secrets service.

### C. CloudFormation parameter → encrypt with KMS encrypt CLI → Lambda env var
- Storing a KMS-encrypted blob in a Lambda environment variable is brittle and error-prone. The developer manually performs the encrypt step out-of-band, which is not reproducible from the template alone.
- It bypasses managed services (Secrets Manager) that already provide envelope encryption, IAM-based access control, audit logging via CloudTrail, and rotation.
- The plaintext still passes through CloudFormation parameters at deploy time and could end up in CloudTrail/stack events.

## Key References
- [AWS::OpenSearchService::Domain MasterUserOptions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-properties-opensearchservice-domain-masteruseroptions.html)
- [Get a secret from Secrets Manager (CloudFormation dynamic reference)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/dynamic-references-secretsmanager.html)
- [Dynamic references in CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/dynamic-references.html)
- [Reference a Secrets Manager secret in a CloudFormation resource](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/cfn-example_reference-secret.html)

zh.question: 一家公司正在使用 Amazon OpenSearch Service 来实现审计监控系统。开发人员需要创建一个与 AWS Lambda 函数关联的 AWS CloudFormation 自定义资源，以配置 OpenSearch Service 域。Lambda 函数必须使用 OpenSearch Service 内部主用户凭证访问 OpenSearch Service 域。将这些凭证传递给 Lambda 函数的最安全方法是什么？

options.A: 使用 CloudFormation 参数在部署时将主用户凭据传递给 OpenSearch Service 域的 MasterUserOptions 和 Lambda 函数的环境变量。将 NoEcho 属性设置为 true。
options.B: 使用 CloudFormation 参数在部署时将主用户凭证传递给 OpenSearch Service 域的 MasterUserOptions，并在 AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store 中创建一个参数。将 NoEcho 属性设置为 true。创建一个具有 ssm:GetParameter 权限的 IAM 角色。将该角色分配给 Lambda 函数。将参数名称存储为 Lambda 函数的环境变量。在运行时解析参数值。
options.C: 使用 CloudFormation 参数在部署时将主用户凭证传递给 OpenSearch Service 域的 MasterUserOptions 和 Lambda 函数的环境变量。使用 AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) 的 encrypt 命令加密参数值。
options.D: 使用 CloudFormation 创建一个 AWS Secrets Manager 密钥。使用 CloudFormation 动态引用检索 OpenSearch Service 域的 MasterUserOptions 中该密钥的值。创建一个具有 secretsmanager:GetSecretValue 权限的 IAM 角色。将该角色分配给 Lambda 函数。将密钥名称存储为 Lambda 函数的环境变量。在运行时解析该密钥的值。

zh.explanation:
# 安全地将 OpenSearch 主凭证传递给 Lambda 函数

## 场景
由 Lambda 函数支持的 CloudFormation 自定义资源需要使用**内部主用户凭证**来配置 OpenSearch Service 域。OpenSearch 域（通过 `MasterUserOptions`）和 Lambda 函数都需要访问这些凭证。问题要求找到传递这些凭证的**最安全**方式。

## 正确答案：D

选项 D 使用 **AWS Secrets Manager** 作为凭证的真实来源，然后：
1. 让 CloudFormation 通过**动态参考** (`{{resolve:secretsmanager:...}}`) 获取 `MasterUserOptions` 的值。
2. 向 Lambda 执行角色授予 `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` 权限。
3. 仅在 Lambda 环境变量中存储**密钥名称**（而非密钥值）。
4. Lambda 在运行时调用 Secrets Manager 来检索凭证。

这是 AWS 推荐的模式。对于敏感数据，始终在 AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store 中使用安全字符串参数或在 AWS Secrets Manager 中使用密钥，以确保数据在静止时加密。限制访问权限仅授予授权的主体和角色。定期轮换敏感数据，并利用 Secrets Manager 的自动轮换功能。

OpenSearch `MasterUserOptions.MasterUserPassword` 属性明确支持此模式：主用户的密码。仅在 AdvancedSecurityOptionsInput 中 InternalUserDatabaseEnabled 为 true 时指定。如果不想在模板中直接指定此值，可以改用动态参考。

动态参考模式为 `{{resolve:secretsmanager:secret-id:SecretString:json-key}}`，例如：

```yaml
MasterUserOptions:
  MasterUserName: !Sub '{{resolve:secretsmanager:${MySecret}:SecretString:username}}'
  MasterUserPassword: !Sub '{{resolve:secretsmanager:${MySecret}:SecretString:password}}'
```

使用 secretsmanager 动态参考表示 Secrets Manager 和 CloudFormation 日志都不应保留任何已解析的密钥值。但是，密钥值可能会出现在使用它的资源的服务中。Lambda 仅在其环境变量中持有密钥**名称**，并通过 IAM 角色在运行时解析该值 — 因此纯文本密码永远不会存留在模板、堆栈输出或 Lambda 配置中。

## 其他选项为何错误

### A. CloudFormation 参数 → Lambda 环境变量（带 `NoEcho: true`）
- `NoEcho` 仅掩盖 CloudFormation 控制台/API 输出中的值。凭证仍然以**纯文本形式被放入 Lambda 环境变量**中，任何拥有 `lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration` 的人都可以读取它。
- 没有轮换，没有中央密钥管理，默认情况下没有使用客户托管 KMS 密钥的静止加密。
- 违反了 AWS 关于将敏感数据保留在环境变量之外的指导。

### B. CloudFormation 参数 → SSM Parameter Store（标准参数）带 `NoEcho`
- 这会将凭证存储在 Parameter Store 中作为**标准（纯文本）参数** — 该选项未指定 `SecureString`。对于敏感数据，始终在 AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store 中使用安全字符串参数或在 AWS Secrets Manager 中使用密钥，以确保数据在静止时加密。
- 即使使用 SecureString，Parameter Store 也缺少 Secrets Manager 为凭证提供的内置**自动轮换**功能，这是主凭证的黄金标准。
- 不如 D 安全，后者使用专用的密钥服务。

### C. CloudFormation 参数 → 使用 KMS encrypt CLI 加密 → Lambda 环境变量
- 在 Lambda 环境变量中存储 KMS 加密的 blob 很脆弱且容易出错。开发人员在带外手动执行加密步骤，这不能从模板单独重现。
- 它绕过了已提供信封加密、基于 IAM 的访问控制、通过 CloudTrail 的审计日志和轮换的托管服务（Secrets Manager）。
- 纯文本仍会通过部署时的 CloudFormation 参数传递，可能出现在 CloudTrail/堆栈事件中。

## 关键参考
- [AWS::OpenSearchService::Domain MasterUserOptions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-properties-opensearchservice-domain-masteruseroptions.html)
- [从 Secrets Manager 获取密钥（CloudFormation 动态参考）](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/dynamic-references-secretsmanager.html)
- [CloudFormation 中的动态参考](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/dynamic-references.html)
- [在 CloudFormation 资源中引用 Secrets Manager 密钥](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/cfn-example_reference-secret.html)

en.question: An application runs on multiple EC2 instances behind an ELB. Where is the session data best written so that it can be served reliably across multiple requests?

options.A: Write data to Amazon ElastiCache.
options.B: Write data to Amazon Elastic Block Store.
options.C: Write data to Amazon EC2 Instance Store.
options.D: Write data to the root filesystem.

en.explanation:
# Session Storage for EC2 Behind ELB

## Scenario
An application runs on multiple EC2 instances behind an Elastic Load Balancer. Because the ELB can route any given user's request to **any** healthy instance in the fleet, session data stored locally on a single instance would not be available when subsequent requests are routed to a different instance. The question asks where session data should be written so it can be served reliably across requests.

## Correct Answer: A — Write data to Amazon ElastiCache

ElastiCache provides a fast, managed, in-memory data store (Redis/Valkey/Memcached) that is **external** to the EC2 instances. All instances in the fleet can read/write the same session keys, so a session is preserved no matter which instance the ELB selects.

Storing sessions on individual application servers is fine until you have more than one server. The moment you scale horizontally — multiple EC2 instances behind a load balancer, containers in ECS, or functions in Lambda — you need a centralized session store. ElastiCache Redis is one of the best options for this because it's fast, supports TTL-based expiration natively, and can handle thousands of session operations per second.

This is also the AWS-recommended pattern to avoid relying on ELB sticky sessions: "You can use ElastiCache to share ASP.NET session information with multiple web servers and eliminate the dependency on ELB stick sessions."

References:
- [ElastiCache as an ASP.NET Session Store (AWS Developer Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/developer/elasticache-as-an-asp-net-session-store/)
- [Build a multi-Region session store with Amazon ElastiCache (AWS Database Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/build-a-multi-region-session-store-with-amazon-elasticache-for-valkey-global-datastore/)

## Why the other options are wrong

- **B. Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS).** An EBS volume can be attached to **only one EC2 instance at a time** (with the exception of io1/io2 Multi-Attach in a small set of scenarios, which still does not provide cross-instance session sharing semantics). Sessions written to an EBS volume by Instance A are invisible to Instance B, so the ELB routing requests to a different instance would fail to find the session. EBS is block storage for a single instance, not a shared session store. See [Amazon EBS volumes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-volumes.html).

- **C. Amazon EC2 Instance Store.** Instance store is **ephemeral, host-local** storage. Data is lost when the instance stops, hibernates, or is terminated, and it is **not shared** across instances. Any session data on instance store would disappear during scale-in events or instance failure, the exact failure mode the ELB+ASG pattern is supposed to tolerate. See [Amazon EC2 instance store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/InstanceStorage.html).

- **D. Root filesystem.** The root filesystem is local to a single EC2 instance (typically an EBS root volume). Sessions written to `/` on Instance A cannot be read by Instance B, so a request load-balanced to a different instance would not find the session. It also disappears if the instance is replaced by Auto Scaling.

Only **ElastiCache (A)** provides a shared, low-latency, durable-enough session tier accessible from every instance behind the ELB.

zh.question: 一个应用程序运行在 ELB 后端的多个 EC2 实例上。为了确保会话数据能够可靠地在多个请求中提供服务，应该将会话数据写入哪里？

options.A: 将数据写入 Amazon ElastiCache。
options.B: 将数据写入 Amazon Elastic Block Store。
options.C: 将数据写入 Amazon EC2 实例存储。
options.D: 将数据写入根文件系统。

zh.explanation:
# EC2 后面 ELB 的会话存储

## 场景
应用程序在 Elastic Load Balancer 后面的多个 EC2 实例上运行。由于 ELB 可以将任何给定用户的请求路由到舰队中的**任何**健康实例，存储在单个实例上的本地会话数据在后续请求被路由到不同实例时将不可用。该问题询问应在何处写入会话数据，以便能够跨请求可靠地提供服务。

## 正确答案：A — 将数据写入 Amazon ElastiCache

ElastiCache 提供快速、托管的内存数据存储（Redis/Valkey/Memcached），**独立于** EC2 实例之外。舰队中的所有实例都可以读写相同的会话密钥，因此无论 ELB 选择哪个实例，会话都会被保留。

在单个应用服务器上存储会话很好，直到你有不止一个服务器。一旦你开始水平扩展——在负载均衡器后面有多个 EC2 实例、ECS 中的容器或 Lambda 中的函数——你需要一个集中式会话存储。ElastiCache Redis 是最佳选择之一，因为它速度快、原生支持基于 TTL 的过期，并且可以处理每秒数千次会话操作。

这也是 AWS 推荐的模式，以避免依赖 ELB 粘性会话："你可以使用 ElastiCache 与多个 Web 服务器共享 ASP.NET 会话信息，并消除对 ELB 粘性会话的依赖。"

参考资源：
- [ElastiCache 作为 ASP.NET 会话存储 (AWS 开发者博客)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/developer/elasticache-as-an-asp-net-session-store/)
- [使用 Amazon ElastiCache 构建多区域会话存储 (AWS 数据库博客)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/build-a-multi-region-session-store-with-amazon-elasticache-for-valkey-global-datastore/)

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

- **B. Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS)。** EBS 卷**只能同时连接到一个 EC2 实例**（除了 io1/io2 Multi-Attach 在少数情况下的例外，这仍然不提供跨实例会话共享语义）。由实例 A 写入 EBS 卷的会话对实例 B 不可见，因此 ELB 路由请求到不同实例时会找不到会话。EBS 是单个实例的块存储，而不是共享会话存储。见 [Amazon EBS 卷](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-volumes.html)。

- **C. Amazon EC2 实例存储。** 实例存储是**临时的、主机本地**存储。当实例停止、休眠或终止时数据会丢失，并且**不在实例之间共享**。实例存储上的任何会话数据在缩减事件或实例故障期间会消失，这正是 ELB + ASG 模式应该容许的故障模式。见 [Amazon EC2 实例存储](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/InstanceStorage.html)。

- **D. 根文件系统。** 根文件系统是本地的单个 EC2 实例（通常是 EBS 根卷）。写入实例 A 上 `/` 的会话无法被实例 B 读取，因此负载均衡到不同实例的请求会找不到会话。如果实例被 Auto Scaling 替换，它也会消失。

只有 **ElastiCache (A)** 提供可从 ELB 后面每个实例访问的共享、低延迟、足够耐用的会话层。

en.question: An ecommerce application is running behind an Application Load Balancer. A developer observes some unexpected load on the application during non-peak hours. The developer wants to analyze patterns for the client IP addresses that use the application. Which HTTP header should the developer use for this analysis?

options.A: The X-Forwarded-Proto header
options.B: The X-Forwarded-Host header
options.C: The X-Forwarded-For header
options.D: The X-Forwarded-Port header

en.explanation:
## Scenario

An ecommerce app sits behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The developer wants to analyze **client IP address patterns** to investigate unexpected load during off-peak hours. Because the ALB terminates the TCP connection from the client and opens a new TCP connection to the target, the source IP that the backend sees in the TCP packet is the ALB's IP, not the original client. To recover the client IP, the developer must inspect the appropriate HTTP header that ALB injects.

## Correct answer: C — `X-Forwarded-For`

The X-Forwarded-For request header helps you identify the IP address of a client when you use an HTTP or HTTPS load balancer. Because load balancers intercept traffic between clients and servers, your server access logs only contain the IP address of the load balancer. By default, the Application Load Balancer stores the IP address of the client in the X-Forwarded-For request header and passes the header to your server.

This is precisely what the developer needs to analyze client IP patterns.

## Why the other options are wrong

- **A. `X-Forwarded-Proto`** — This header identifies the protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) the client used to reach the load balancer, not the client IP. Useful for redirect logic, not IP analysis.

- **B. `X-Forwarded-Host`** — This (non‑standard) header conveys the original `Host` header value the client requested (i.e., the hostname/domain), not the source IP address.

- **D. `X-Forwarded-Port`** — The X-Forwarded-Port request header helps you identify the destination port that the client used to connect to the load balancer. It captures the port, not the client IP.

## Reference

- [HTTP headers and Application Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/x-forwarded-headers.html)
- [How the client IP address is preserved – AWS Global Accelerator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/preserve-client-ip-address.headers.html)

zh.question: 一个电商应用运行在应用负载均衡器之后。开发人员发现该应用在非高峰时段出现了一些意外负载。开发人员想要分析使用该应用的客户端 IP 地址的模式。开发人员应该使用哪个 HTTP 标头来进行此分析？

options.A: X-Forwarded-Proto 标头
options.B: X-Forwarded-Host 标头
options.C: X-Forwarded-For 标头
options.D: X转发端口报头

zh.explanation:
## 场景

一个电商应用位于应用负载均衡器 (ALB) 后面。开发人员想要分析**客户端 IP 地址模式**来调查非高峰时段的意外负载。由于 ALB 终止来自客户端的 TCP 连接，并向目标打开新的 TCP 连接，后端在 TCP 数据包中看到的源 IP 是 ALB 的 IP，而不是原始客户端。要恢复客户端 IP，开发人员必须检查 ALB 注入的相应 HTTP 标头。

## 正确答案：C — `X-Forwarded-For`

X-Forwarded-For 请求标头帮助您在使用 HTTP 或 HTTPS 负载均衡器时识别客户端的 IP 地址。由于负载均衡器拦截客户端和服务器之间的流量，您的服务器访问日志仅包含负载均衡器的 IP 地址。默认情况下，Application Load Balancer 将客户端的 IP 地址存储在 X-Forwarded-For 请求标头中，并将标头传递给您的服务器。

这正是开发人员分析客户端 IP 模式所需的。

## 为什么其他选项错误

- **A. `X-Forwarded-Proto`** — 此标头标识客户端用来到达负载均衡器的协议（HTTP 或 HTTPS），而不是客户端 IP。适用于重定向逻辑，不适用于 IP 分析。

- **B. `X-Forwarded-Host`** — 这个（非标准）标头传达客户端请求的原始 `Host` 标头值（即主机名/域名），而不是源 IP 地址。

- **D. `X-Forwarded-Port`** — X-Forwarded-Port 请求标头帮助您识别客户端用来连接到负载均衡器的目标端口。它捕获端口，而不是客户端 IP。

## 参考

- [HTTP 标头和 Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/x-forwarded-headers.html)
- [如何保留客户端 IP 地址 – AWS Global Accelerator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/preserve-client-ip-address.headers.html)

en.question: A developer migrated a legacy application to an AWS Lambda function. The function uses a third-party service to pull data with a series of API calls at the end of each month. The function then processes the data to generate the monthly reports. The function has been working with no issues so far. The third-party service recently issued a restriction to allow a fixed number of API calls each minute and each day. If the API calls exceed the limit for each minute or each day, then the service will produce errors. The API also provides the minute limit and daily limit in the response header. This restriction might extend the overall process to multiple days because the process is consuming more API calls than the available limit. What is the MOST operationally efficient way to refactor the serverless application to accommodate this change?

options.A: Use an AWS Step Functions state machine to monitor API failures. Use the Wait state to delay calling the Lambda function.
options.B: Use an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to hold the API calls. Configure the Lambda function to poll the queue within the API threshold limits.
options.C: Use an Amazon CloudWatch Logs metric to count the number of API calls. Configure an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that stops the currently running instance of the Lambda function when the metric exceeds the API threshold limits.
options.D: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to batch the API calls and deliver them to an Amazon S3 bucket with an event notification to invoke the Lambda function.

en.explanation:
# Refactoring Lambda for Third-Party API Rate Limits

## Scenario Analysis

A Lambda function pulls monthly data from a third-party API. The API now enforces both **per-minute** and **per-day** rate limits, returning these limits in response headers. Exceeding the limits causes errors. Because the workload may consume more API calls than the daily limit allows, the overall job may need to span **multiple days**. The question asks for the MOST operationally efficient refactor.

Key constraints:
- Need to throttle outbound calls based on dynamic limits returned in headers
- Process must be able to **pause and resume across multiple days**
- Lambda alone has a 15-minute max execution timeout — it cannot natively wait hours/days

## Correct Answer: A — Step Functions State Machine with Wait state

AWS Step Functions is purpose-built to orchestrate Lambda invocations across long-running, stateful workflows. The Lambda function can read the API response headers (minute/day limit, remaining quota) and return that to the state machine. A **Choice** state can then route to a **Wait** state that delays the next invocation by the appropriate number of seconds, minutes, or even until a future timestamp the next day.

- [Wait workflow state](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/state-wait.html) lets the state machine pause for a specified time before continuing.
- Step Functions Standard workflows can run for **up to 1 year**, easily covering the multi-day case.
- [Step Functions error handling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/concepts-error-handling.html) provides Retry/Catch on Task states, allowing the state machine to react to API failures (e.g., 429 Too Many Requests) and trigger a Wait before retrying.
- Wait states are a recognized pattern for **rate limiting** by spacing API requests, particularly when limits change dynamically based on response data.

This solution is fully serverless, requires no custom polling/queue management code, and natively supports multi-day pause/resume behavior.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

### B. SQS queue with Lambda polling within thresholds
- **Maximum SQS message delay (delay queue / per-message DelaySeconds) is 15 minutes.** This cannot defer work to the next day when a daily limit is exhausted. See [Amazon SQS delay queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-delay-queues.html).
- SQS event source mapping for Lambda will **continuously poll**; you cannot natively configure Lambda to "poll within threshold limits" — you'd need custom logic (concurrency throttles, manual pausing) which is operationally complex.
- SQS is for decoupling/buffering; it does not orchestrate timing or scheduled resumption.

### C. CloudWatch Logs metric + alarm to stop the running Lambda
- CloudWatch alarms cannot **stop** a running Lambda function — Lambda has no "stop instance" API. Alarms can trigger SNS/EventBridge/Lambda but not abort an in-flight invocation.
- This approach is reactive, not preventive: it would only react after errors are already logged. It also doesn't solve resumption after the daily reset.
- Operationally fragile and doesn't address the multi-day scheduling requirement.

### D. Kinesis Data Firehose batching to S3 → S3 event triggers Lambda
- Firehose is for **ingesting and delivering streaming data to destinations** (S3/Redshift/OpenSearch). It does not throttle outbound API calls.
- S3 event notifications fire immediately on object creation, so this provides no rate-limiting mechanism.
- Adds Firehose + S3 to the architecture without addressing the actual problem (pacing outbound API calls across minutes and days).

## Conclusion

**Option A** is the most operationally efficient: Step Functions natively orchestrates the Lambda, uses Wait states to honor minute/day limits returned in API headers, retries on errors, and supports multi-day execution windows — all without custom queue/poller infrastructure.

zh.question: 一位开发人员将一个旧版应用程序迁移到了 AWS Lambda 函数。该函数使用第三方服务，在每个月底通过一系列 API 调用来获取数据。然后，该函数处理这些数据以生成月度报告。到目前为止，该函数一直运行良好。但最近，该第三方服务发布了一项限制，规定每分钟和每天的 API 调用次数都有限制。如果 API 调用次数超过每分钟或每天的限制，则该服务会报错。API 还在响应头中提供了分钟限制和每日限制。由于该过程消耗的 API 调用次数超过了可用限制，因此这项限制可能会导致整个流程延长至数天。为了适应这一变化，如何以最高效的方式重构这个无服务器应用程序？

options.A: 使用 AWS Step Functions 状态机监控 API 故障。使用等待状态延迟调用 Lambda 函数。
options.B: 使用 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列来保存 API 调用。配置 Lambda 函数，使其在 API 调用阈值限制内轮询该队列。
options.C: 使用 Amazon CloudWatch Logs 指标来统计 API 调用次数。配置 Amazon CloudWatch 警报，当该指标超过 API 调用阈值限制时，停止当前正在运行的 Lambda 函数实例。
options.D: 使用 Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose 将 API 调用批量处理，并通过事件通知将其发送到 Amazon S3 存储桶，以调用 Lambda 函数。

zh.explanation:
# Lambda 第三方 API 速率限制重构

## 场景分析

一个 Lambda 函数从第三方 API 拉取每月数据。该 API 现在强制实施**每分钟**和**每天**速率限制，并在响应标头中返回这些限制。超过限制会导致错误。因为工作负载可能消耗超过每日限制允许的 API 调用，整个作业可能需要跨**多天**执行。问题要求最在运维效率方面最优的重构。

关键约束：
- 需要根据标头中返回的动态限制来限制出站调用
- 流程必须能够在**跨多天暂停和恢复**
- Lambda 单独有 15 分钟最大执行超时——它无法原生等待数小时/数天

## 正确答案：A — Step Functions 状态机与 Wait 状态

AWS Step Functions 专为跨长运行、有状态工作流编排 Lambda 调用而构建。Lambda 函数可以读取 API 响应标头（分钟/天限制、剩余配额），然后将其返回给状态机。一个 **Choice** 状态随后可以路由到 **Wait** 状态，该状态会延迟下一次调用相应的秒数、分钟数，甚至延迟到次日的特定时间戳。

- [Wait 工作流状态](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/state-wait.html)让状态机在继续前暂停指定的时间。
- Step Functions Standard 工作流可以运行**长达 1 年**，轻松覆盖多天用例。
- [Step Functions 错误处理](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/concepts-error-handling.html)在 Task 状态上提供 Retry/Catch，允许状态机对 API 故障（如 429 Too Many Requests）做出反应，并在重试前触发 Wait。
- Wait 状态是通过间隔 API 请求来**速率限制**的公认模式，特别是当限制根据响应数据动态变化时。

此解决方案完全无服务器，无需自定义轮询/队列管理代码，并原生支持多天暂停/恢复行为。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

### B. SQS 队列与在阈值内轮询的 Lambda
- **SQS 消息最大延迟（延迟队列 / 每消息 DelaySeconds）为 15 分钟**。当每日限制用尽时，这无法将工作推迟到次日。请参见 [Amazon SQS 延迟队列](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-delay-queues.html)。
- SQS 事件源映射用于 Lambda 时会**持续轮询**；您无法原生配置 Lambda 为"在阈值限制内轮询"——您需要自定义逻辑（并发节流、手动暂停），这在运维上很复杂。
- SQS 用于解耦/缓冲；它不编排计时或计划恢复。

### C. CloudWatch Logs 指标 + 告警以停止运行的 Lambda
- CloudWatch 告警无法**停止**正在运行的 Lambda 函数——Lambda 没有"停止实例"API。告警可以触发 SNS/EventBridge/Lambda，但不能中止正在进行的调用。
- 这种方法是被动的，而不是预防性的：它只会在错误已被日志记录后做出反应。它也不能解决每日重置后的恢复问题。
- 在运维上脆弱，无法满足多天调度需求。

### D. Kinesis Data Firehose 批处理到 S3 → S3 事件触发 Lambda
- Firehose 用于**摄取流数据并将其传输到目标**（S3/Redshift/OpenSearch）。它不限制出站 API 调用。
- S3 事件通知在对象创建时立即触发，因此无法提供速率限制机制。
- 在不解决实际问题（跨分钟和天数调整出站 API 调用步伐）的情况下，向架构中添加 Firehose + S3。

## 结论

**选项 A** 在运维效率上最优：Step Functions 原生编排 Lambda，使用 Wait 状态来遵守 API 标头中返回的分钟/天限制，对错误进行重试，并支持多天执行窗口——所有这些都无需自定义队列/轮询基础设施。

en.question: A developer must analyze performance issues with production-distributed applications written as AWS Lambda functions. These distributed Lambda applications invoke other components that make up the applications. How should the developer identify and troubleshoot the root cause of the performance issues in production?

options.A: Add logging statements to the Lambda functions, then use Amazon CloudWatch to view the logs.
options.B: Use AWS CloudTrail and then examine the logs.
options.C: Use AWS X-Ray, then examine the segments and errors.
options.D: Run Amazon Inspector agents and then analyze performance.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A developer needs to identify and troubleshoot the **root cause of performance issues** in **production-distributed Lambda applications** that invoke other components. The key requirements are: distributed tracing, performance bottleneck detection, and visibility into downstream calls.

## Correct Answer: C — Use AWS X-Ray, then examine the segments and errors

AWS X-Ray is purpose-built for this exact use case. AWS X-Ray helps developers analyze and debug production, distributed applications, such as those built using a microservices architecture. With X-Ray, you can understand how your application and its underlying services are performing to identify and troubleshoot the root cause of performance issues and errors. It allows you to view, filter, and gain insights to identify issues and opportunities for optimization.

For Lambda specifically, you can use AWS X-Ray to visualize the components of your application, identify performance bottlenecks, and troubleshoot requests that resulted in an error. X-Ray records **segments** (units of work) and **subsegments** for downstream calls, exposing latencies and errors at each hop. In X-Ray, a trace records information about a request that is processed by one or more services. Lambda records 2 segments per trace, which creates two nodes on the service graph.

When active tracing is enabled on Lambda, X-Ray automatically traces requests as they flow into Lambda and to downstream AWS services, producing a **service map** and detailed segment timing that pinpoints the slow component.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A. CloudWatch Logs with logging statements** — Logs alone do not provide a correlated, end-to-end view across distributed components. You'd have to manually stitch together log entries across multiple Lambda functions and downstream services, which does not visualize latency hotspots or dependencies. This is precisely the limitation X-Ray was created to solve — previously, Lambda customers who wanted to understand their application's latency breakdown, diagnose slowdowns, or troubleshoot timeouts had to rely on custom logging and analysis.

- **B. AWS CloudTrail** — CloudTrail records **AWS API management/data events for auditing and governance** (who did what, when, from where). It is not a performance tracing or latency analysis tool and contains no segment/subsegment timing data for application requests.

- **D. Amazon Inspector** — Inspector is an **automated vulnerability and security assessment** service for EC2, ECR container images, and Lambda functions. It identifies CVEs and security issues, not application performance bottlenecks. It does not trace request flow across distributed components.

## Key AWS Documentation

- [Visualize Lambda function invocations using AWS X-Ray](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-xray.html)
- [AWS X-Ray — Analyzing Performance for Lambda Apps](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/analyzing-performance-for-amazon-rekognition-apps-written-on-aws-lambda-using-aws-x-ray/)
- [AWS X-Ray Lambda Integration GA Announcement](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/aws-x-ray-update-general-availability-including-lambda-integration/)

zh.question: 开发人员需要分析以 AWS Lambda 函数编写的生产环境分布式应用程序的性能问题。这些分布式 Lambda 应用程序会调用构成应用程序的其他组件。开发人员应该如何识别和排查生产环境中性能问题的根本原因？

options.A: 向 Lambda 函数添加日志记录语句，然后使用 Amazon CloudWatch 查看日志。
options.B: 使用 AWS CloudTrail，然后检查日志。
options.C: 使用 AWS X-Ray，然后检查段和错误。
options.D: 运行 Amazon Inspector 代理，然后分析性能。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

开发人员需要识别和排查**生产分布式 Lambda 应用程序中的性能问题根本原因**，这些应用程序会调用其他组件。关键需求是：分布式追踪、性能瓶颈检测和下游调用的可视化。

## 正确答案：C — 使用 AWS X-Ray，然后检查分段和错误

AWS X-Ray 专为此用例而设计。AWS X-Ray 帮助开发人员分析和调试生产环境中的分布式应用程序，例如使用微服务架构构建的应用程序。通过 X-Ray，您可以了解应用程序及其底层服务的性能，以识别和排查性能问题和错误的根本原因。它允许您查看、过滤和获得洞察，以识别问题和优化机会。

对于 Lambda 特别地，您可以使用 AWS X-Ray 来可视化应用程序的组件、识别性能瓶颈，以及排查导致错误的请求。X-Ray 记录**分段**（工作单元）和下游调用的**子分段**，暴露每一跳中的延迟和错误。在 X-Ray 中，追踪记录由一个或多个服务处理的请求的信息。Lambda 每个追踪记录 2 个分段，在服务图上创建两个节点。

在 Lambda 上启用主动追踪时，X-Ray 会自动追踪流入 Lambda 和下游 AWS 服务的请求，生成**服务地图**和详细的分段计时信息，精确定位缓慢的组件。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

- **A. CloudWatch Logs 和日志语句** — 仅靠日志无法跨分布式组件提供相关的端到端视图。您必须手动将多个 Lambda 函数和下游服务的日志条目拼接在一起，这无法可视化延迟热点或依赖关系。这正是 X-Ray 被创建来解决的限制 — 以前，想要理解应用程序延迟分解、诊断速度下降或排查超时的 Lambda 客户必须依赖自定义日志记录和分析。

- **B. AWS CloudTrail** — CloudTrail 记录**用于审计和治理的 AWS API 管理/数据事件**（谁做了什么、何时、从哪里）。它不是性能追踪或延迟分析工具，不包含应用程序请求的分段/子分段计时数据。

- **D. Amazon Inspector** — Inspector 是一个**自动化的漏洞和安全评估**服务，用于 EC2、ECR 容器镜像和 Lambda 函数。它识别 CVE 和安全问题，而非应用程序性能瓶颈。它无法追踪跨分布式组件的请求流。

## 关键 AWS 文档

- [Visualize Lambda function invocations using AWS X-Ray](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-xray.html)
- [AWS X-Ray — Analyzing Performance for Lambda Apps](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/analyzing-performance-for-amazon-rekognition-apps-written-on-aws-lambda-using-aws-x-ray/)
- [AWS X-Ray Lambda Integration GA Announcement](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/aws-x-ray-update-general-availability-including-lambda-integration/)

en.question: A developer wants to deploy a new version of an AWS Elastic Beanstalk application. During deployment, the application must maintain full capacity and avoid service interruption. Additionally, the developer must minimize the cost of additional resources that support the deployment. Which deployment method should the developer use to meet these requirements?

options.A: All at once
options.B: Rolling with additional batch
options.C: Blue/green
options.D: Immutable

en.explanation:
## Scenario

The developer needs to deploy a new version of an Elastic Beanstalk app with three constraints:
1. **Maintain full capacity** during deployment
2. **Avoid service interruption** (no downtime)
3. **Minimize the cost of additional resources**

## Correct Answer: B – Rolling with additional batch

RollingWithAdditionalBatch launches an extra batch of instances, before starting the deployment, to maintain full capacity. Then it performs a normal rolling update on the existing instances batch by batch, and when the deployment completes, Elastic Beanstalk terminates the additional batch of instances.

This satisfies all three requirements:
- **Full capacity** is preserved because the extra batch compensates for the instances taken out of service during each rolling step. Rolling with additional batch deployments address the chief shortcoming of rolling deployments — one batch is out of service, reducing overall capacity. This variation creates an extra batch and maintains full capacity throughout the update.
- **No service interruption** – instances are updated in batches while the rest continue serving traffic.
- **Minimized additional cost** – only **one extra batch** of instances is launched, not a full duplicate environment. There's a small additional cost for the extra batch during deployment.

## Why the other options are wrong

**A. All at once** – This is the quickest and least expensive deployment method, but also the only one that incurs downtime. All of your instances will go out of service for a short time. This violates the "no service interruption" and "maintain full capacity" requirements.

**C. Blue/green** – Requires running an entire **second environment** in parallel (double the resources) plus a CNAME swap. This is the most expensive in terms of additional resources, directly conflicting with the "minimize cost of additional resources" requirement. It also requires manual setup outside of a single deployment policy.

**D. Immutable** – Although it maintains full capacity and avoids downtime, it launches a **complete new set of instances** in a separate Auto Scaling group equal in size to the existing fleet. Immutable updates take the longest amount of time and are the most expensive, as you are temporarily doubling your instances. Therefore it does NOT minimize additional resource cost compared to "Rolling with additional batch," which only adds **one batch** of extra instances.

## Key differentiator

The phrase **"minimize the cost of additional resources"** is the decisive constraint. Rolling with additional batch adds only one batch of extra instances, while Immutable and Blue/Green both temporarily double the fleet size.

## References
- [Elastic Beanstalk deployment policies and settings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.rolling-version-deploy.html)
- [Seamless Production Deployment with Elastic Beanstalk (AWS Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/dotnet/seamless-production-deployment-with-elastic-beanstalk/)

zh.question: 一位开发人员想要部署新版本的 AWS Elastic Beanstalk 应用程序。部署期间，应用程序必须保持满负荷运行，避免服务中断。此外，开发人员还必须尽可能降低支持部署所需的额外资源成本。开发人员应该使用哪种部署方法才能满足这些要求？

options.A: 一次性
options.B: 滚动并添加批次
options.C: 蓝/绿色
options.D: 不可改变的

zh.explanation:
## 场景

开发人员需要部署新版本的 Elastic Beanstalk 应用，有三个约束条件：
1. **部署期间保持满容量**
2. **避免服务中断**（零停机）
3. **最小化额外资源成本**

## 正确答案：B – Rolling with additional batch

Rolling with additional batch 在开始部署前启动一个额外的实例批次，以保持满容量。然后它在现有实例上逐批执行正常的滚动更新，部署完成时，Elastic Beanstalk 会终止额外的实例批次。

这满足了所有三个要求：
- **保持满容量** – 额外批次补偿了滚动过程中每个步骤中被取出服务的实例。Rolling with additional batch 部署解决了滚动部署的主要缺点——一个批次处于离线状态，降低整体容量。这种变体创建额外的批次，在整个更新过程中保持满容量。
- **无服务中断** – 实例分批更新，其余实例继续处理流量。
- **最小化额外成本** – 仅启动**一个额外批次**的实例，不是完整的重复环境。部署期间额外批次产生少量额外成本。

## 其他选项错误的原因

**A. All at once** – 这是最快且成本最低的部署方法，但也是唯一会导致停机的方法。您的所有实例将在短时间内离线。这违反了"无服务中断"和"保持满容量"的要求。

**C. Blue/green** – 需要并行运行整个**第二个环境**（资源加倍）加上 CNAME 交换。这在额外资源方面成本最高，直接与"最小化额外资源成本"的要求冲突。它还需要在单个部署策略之外进行手动设置。

**D. Immutable** – 虽然保持了满容量并避免了停机，但它在单独的 Auto Scaling 组中启动**完整的新实例集**，大小与现有集群相同。Immutable 更新花费时间最长，成本最高，因为您暂时增加了实例数量。因此与仅添加**一个批次**额外实例的 "Rolling with additional batch" 相比，它**不能**最小化额外资源成本。

## 关键区别

短语**"最小化额外资源成本"**是决定性的约束条件。Rolling with additional batch 仅添加一个批次的额外实例，而 Immutable 和 Blue/green 都临时增加了整个集群的大小。

## 参考资源
- [Elastic Beanstalk 部署策略和设置](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.rolling-version-deploy.html)
- [使用 Elastic Beanstalk 实现无缝生产部署（AWS 博客）](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/dotnet/seamless-production-deployment-with-elastic-beanstalk/)

en.question: A developer has observed an increase in bugs in the AWS Lambda functions that a development team has deployed in its Node.js application. To minimize these bugs, the developer wants to implement automated testing of Lambda functions in an environment that closely simulates the Lambda environment. The developer needs to give other developers the ability to run the tests locally. The developer also needs to integrate the tests into the team’s continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline before the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) deployment. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create sample events based on the Lambda documentation. Create automated test scripts that use the cdk local invoke command to invoke the Lambda functions. Check the response. Document the test scripts for the other developers on the team. Update the CI/CD pipeline to run the test scripts.
options.B: Install a unit testing framework that reproduces the Lambda execution environment. Create sample events based on the Lambda documentation. Invoke the handler function by using a unit testing framework. Check the response. Document how to run the unit testing framework for the other developers on the team. Update the CI/CD pipeline to run the unit testing framework.
options.C: Install the AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM) CLI tool. Use the sam local generate- event command to generate sample events for the automated tests. Create automated test scripts that use the sam local invoke command to invoke the Lambda functions. Check the response. Document the test scripts for the other developers on the team. Update the CI/CD pipeline to run the test scripts.
options.D: Create sample events based on the Lambda documentation. Create a Docker container from the Node.js base image to invoke the Lambda functions. Check the response. Document how to run the Docker container for the other developers on the team. Update the CI/CD pipeline to run the Docker container.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

The team has a Node.js Lambda application deployed via AWS CDK and wants to:

1. Run **automated tests** of Lambda functions in an environment that **closely simulates the Lambda runtime**.
2. Allow developers to **run tests locally**.
3. **Integrate the tests into a CI/CD pipeline before** the CDK deployment.

## Correct Answer: C

The **AWS SAM CLI** is purpose-built for local Lambda testing. The AWS SAM CLI sam local invoke subcommand initiates a one-time invocation of an AWS Lambda function locally. Internally, SAM uses Docker images that mirror the actual Lambda runtime, providing a high-fidelity simulation of the Lambda environment.

The two relevant subcommands fit the requirements directly:

- `sam local generate-event` – Generates sample event payloads for various AWS services, providing realistic test data for your functions.
- `sam local invoke` – Perfect for testing individual Lambda functions. This command lets you execute a single function, passing custom event payloads and environment variables to mimic specific scenarios.

Example workflow:

```bash
# Generate a sample S3 event
sam local generate-event s3 put > events/s3.json

# Invoke the Lambda locally with that event
sam local invoke MyFunction --event events/s3.json
```

These commands run in Docker containers that emulate the Lambda runtime, can be scripted, executed by every developer locally, and easily wired into a CI/CD job that runs **before** the `cdk deploy` step. Note that AWS SAM CLI also supports CDK projects through `sam local invoke` against a synthesized CloudFormation template, so it works with CDK-based applications.

References:
- [Introduction to testing with sam local invoke](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/using-sam-cli-local-invoke.html)
- [sam local invoke command reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/sam-cli-command-reference-sam-local-invoke.html)
- [sam local generate-event](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/using-sam-cli-local-generate-event.html)

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

**A. `cdk local invoke`** – This command **does not exist**. The AWS CDK CLI has no `local invoke` subcommand for running Lambda functions locally. CDK is an infrastructure-as-code synthesis tool; local Lambda emulation is provided by the SAM CLI (which can consume CDK-synthesized templates), not CDK itself. This option is fabricated.

**B. Unit testing framework that "reproduces the Lambda execution environment"** – Standard unit testing frameworks (Jest, Mocha) only execute the handler in the local Node.js process. They do **not** reproduce the actual Lambda execution environment (Amazon Linux 2 container, /var/task layout, Lambda runtime API, init/extension lifecycle, memory/CPU limits, etc.). The requirement explicitly asks for an environment that *closely simulates the Lambda environment*, which unit-testing frameworks alone cannot provide.

**D. Custom Docker container from a Node.js base image** – A plain `node:` base image is not the Lambda runtime. The Lambda execution environment uses specific AWS Lambda runtime images (e.g., `public.ecr.aws/lambda/nodejs`) that include the Runtime Interface Client, init process, and bootstrapping. Building a custom container from the Node.js base image would not faithfully reproduce Lambda's behavior and reinvents what the SAM CLI already provides out of the box (which itself uses official Lambda runtime images per public.ecr.aws/lambda/python:3.9-rapid-style images). It is the wrong-tool/undifferentiated-heavy-lifting answer.

## Conclusion

**C** is correct. The AWS SAM CLI's `sam local generate-event` and `sam local invoke` provide the closest fidelity to the Lambda runtime, are runnable locally by every developer, and slot cleanly into a CI/CD pipeline ahead of the CDK deployment step.

zh.question: 一位开发人员发现，其开发团队部署在 Node.js 应用程序中的 AWS Lambda 函数的 bug 数量有所增加。为了最大限度地减少这些 bug，该开发人员希望在一个能够高度模拟 Lambda 环境的环境中实现 Lambda 函数的自动化测试。此外，该开发人员还需要允许其他开发人员在本地运行这些测试。同时，在部署 AWS 云开发工具包 (AWS CDK) 之前，该开发人员还需要将这些测试集成到团队的持续集成和持续交付 (CI/CD) 流水线中。哪种解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 根据 Lambda 文档创建示例事件。创建使用 cdk local invoke 命令调用 Lambda 函数的自动化测试脚本。检查响应。为团队中的其他开发人员编写测试脚本文档。更新 CI/CD 流水线以运行测试脚本。
options.B: 安装一个能够复现 Lambda 执行环境的单元测试框架。根据 Lambda 文档创建示例事件。使用单元测试框架调用处理函数。检查响应。编写文档，向团队其他开发人员说明如何运行该单元测试框架。更新 CI/CD 流水线以运行该单元测试框架。
options.C: 安装 AWS 无服务器应用程序模型 (AWS SAM) CLI 工具。使用 `sam local generate-event` 命令生成用于自动化测试的示例事件。创建自动化测试脚本，使用 `sam local invoke` 命令调用 Lambda 函数。检查响应。为团队中的其他开发人员编写测试脚本文档。更新 CI/CD 流水线以运行测试脚本。
options.D: 根据 Lambda 文档创建示例事件。使用 Node.js 基础镜像创建 Docker 容器来调用 Lambda 函数。检查响应。编写文档，说明如何运行 Docker 容器，供团队其他开发人员参考。更新 CI/CD 流水线以运行 Docker 容器。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

团队有一个通过 AWS CDK 部署的 Node.js Lambda 应用程序，希望：

1. 在**紧密模拟 Lambda 运行时**的环境中运行 Lambda 函数的**自动化测试**。
2. 允许开发人员**在本地运行测试**。
3. 在 CDK 部署**之前**将测试**集成到 CI/CD 管道**中。

## 正确答案：C

**AWS SAM CLI** 是为本地 Lambda 测试而专门构建的。AWS SAM CLI 的 sam local invoke 子命令在本地启动 AWS Lambda 函数的一次性调用。在内部，SAM 使用的 Docker 映像与实际的 Lambda 运行时相同，提供对 Lambda 环境的高保真模拟。

这两个相关的子命令直接满足需求：

- `sam local generate-event` – 为各种 AWS 服务生成样本事件有效负载，为函数提供逼真的测试数据。
- `sam local invoke` – 非常适合测试单个 Lambda 函数。此命令允许执行单个函数，传递自定义事件有效负载和环境变量来模拟特定场景。

示例工作流：

```bash
# 生成样本 S3 事件
sam local generate-event s3 put > events/s3.json

# 使用该事件在本地调用 Lambda
sam local invoke MyFunction --event events/s3.json
```

这些命令在模拟 Lambda 运行时的 Docker 容器中运行，可以编写脚本、由每个开发人员在本地执行，并可轻松集成到在 `cdk deploy` 步骤**之前**运行的 CI/CD 作业中。请注意，AWS SAM CLI 也通过针对合成的 CloudFormation 模板的 `sam local invoke` 支持 CDK 项目，因此它适用于基于 CDK 的应用程序。

参考资源：
- [Introduction to testing with sam local invoke](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/using-sam-cli-local-invoke.html)
- [sam local invoke command reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/sam-cli-command-reference-sam-local-invoke.html)
- [sam local generate-event](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/using-sam-cli-local-generate-event.html)

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

**A. `cdk local invoke`** – 此命令**不存在**。AWS CDK CLI 没有 `local invoke` 子命令来在本地运行 Lambda 函数。CDK 是一个基础设施即代码合成工具；本地 Lambda 模拟由 SAM CLI（可以使用 CDK 合成的模板）提供，而不是 CDK 本身。此选项是虚构的。

**B. "再现 Lambda 执行环境"的单元测试框架** – 标准单元测试框架（Jest、Mocha）仅在本地 Node.js 进程中执行处理程序。它们**不会**再现实际的 Lambda 执行环境（Amazon Linux 2 容器、/var/task 布局、Lambda 运行时 API、初始化/扩展生命周期、内存/CPU 限制等）。需求明确要求一个**紧密模拟 Lambda 环境**的环境，仅凭单元测试框架无法提供。

**D. 来自 Node.js 基础映像的自定义 Docker 容器** – 普通 `node:` 基础映像不是 Lambda 运行时。Lambda 执行环境使用特定的 AWS Lambda 运行时映像（例如 `public.ecr.aws/lambda/nodejs`），其中包括运行时接口客户端、初始化进程和引导程序。从 Node.js 基础映像构建自定义容器无法忠实再现 Lambda 的行为，并重新发明了 SAM CLI 已经开箱即用的功能（SAM CLI 本身使用官方 Lambda 运行时映像，如 public.ecr.aws/lambda/python:3.9-rapid 风格的映像）。这是错误工具/未区分的重型任务答案。

## 结论

**C** 是正确的。AWS SAM CLI 的 `sam local generate-event` 和 `sam local invoke` 提供了与 Lambda 运行时最接近的保真度，可由每个开发人员在本地运行，并在 CDK 部署步骤之前整洁地融入 CI/CD 管道。

en.question:
A developer is troubleshooting an application that uses Amazon DynamoDB in the us-west-2 Region. The application is deployed to an Amazon EC2 instance. The application requires read-only permissions to a table that is named Cars. The EC2 instance has an attached IAM role that contains the following IAM policy:
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "ReadOnlyAPIActions",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "dynamodb:GetItem",
        "dynamodb:BatchGetItem",
        "dynamodb:Scan",
        "dynamodb:Query",
        "dynamodb:ConditionCheckItem"
      ],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:dynamodb:us-west-2:account-id:table/Cars"
    }
  ]
}
```
 When the application tries to read from the Cars table, an Access Denied error occurs. How can the developer resolve this error?

options.A: Modify the IAM policy resource to be “arn:aws:dynamodb:us-west-2:account-id:table/*”.
options.B: Modify the IAM policy to include the dynamodb:* action.
options.C: Create a trust policy that specifies the EC2 service principal. Associate the role with the policy.
options.D: Create a trust relationship between the role and dynamodb.amazonaws.com.

en.explanation:
# Analysis

## Scenario
An EC2 instance has an IAM role attached that contains a permissions policy granting read-only DynamoDB actions (e.g., `GetItem`, `BatchGetItem`, `Scan`, `Query`, `ConditionCheckItem`) on the `Cars` table in `us-west-2`. The application gets an **Access Denied** error when reading from the table.

The question is asking why an IAM role attached to an EC2 instance would not work even though the permissions policy looks correct.

## Why C is correct
For an EC2 instance to actually be able to use ("assume") an IAM role via its instance profile, the role must have a **trust policy** that lets the EC2 service principal (`ec2.amazonaws.com`) call `sts:AssumeRole`. Without that trust relationship, the EC2 instance cannot obtain temporary credentials from the instance metadata service, so every API call to DynamoDB will fail with Access Denied — regardless of how permissive the permissions policy is.

The role attached to an EC2 instance must trust the Amazon EC2 service to assume the role, which requires a trust policy whose Principal is the service `ec2.amazonaws.com` with action `sts:AssumeRole`.

The required trust policy looks like:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": { "Service": "ec2.amazonaws.com" },
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
    }
  ]
}
```

A role attached to an EC2 instance includes a trust policy that allows the Amazon EC2 instance to assume the role and retrieve the temporary credentials.

The wording of option C ("Create a trust policy that specifies the EC2 service principal. Associate the role with the policy.") is awkward, but it is the only option describing the actual fix: setting up a trust policy with the EC2 service principal so the instance can assume the role.

## Why the other options are wrong

**A. Change the resource ARN to `arn:aws:dynamodb:us-west-2:account-id:table/*`** — This widens permissions to every table in the region, violating least privilege. The given policy already lists the `Cars` table by ARN; the read-only actions specified (`GetItem`, `BatchGetItem`, `Scan`, `Query`, `ConditionCheckItem`) operate on the table resource, not on indexes (LSIs share the table ARN, and there's no indication a GSI is used). The Access Denied isn't caused by ARN scope — it's caused by the role not being assumable. A typical least-privilege read-only policy lists actions like GetItem, BatchGetItem, Scan, Query, and ConditionCheckItem with the specific table ARN as the Resource.

**B. Use `dynamodb:*`** — Grants full DynamoDB access (write/delete/admin), violating least privilege. The application only needs read access, and granting `*` does not address the actual problem (missing trust relationship).

**D. Create a trust relationship between the role and `dynamodb.amazonaws.com`** — This is the most common distractor. The trust policy must trust the service that *consumes* (assumes) the role — EC2 — not the service the application *calls* (DynamoDB). In an EC2 role's trust policy, the administrator specifies that only Amazon EC2 instances can assume the role. Trusting `dynamodb.amazonaws.com` would let the DynamoDB service assume the role, which is not what's needed.

## Correct Answer: **C**

## References
- [Use an IAM role to grant permissions to applications running on Amazon EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_use_switch-role-ec2.html)
- [Identity and access management in Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/authentication-and-access-control.html)
- [How to use trust policies with IAM roles (AWS Security Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/how-to-use-trust-policies-with-iam-roles/)

zh.question:
一位开发人员正在排查一个使用 Amazon DynamoDB 的应用程序的问题，该应用程序部署在 us-west-2 区域。该应用程序需要对名为 Cars 的表拥有只读权限。该 EC2 实例附加了一个 IAM 角色，其中包含以下 IAM 策略：
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "ReadOnlyAPIActions",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "dynamodb:GetItem",
        "dynamodb:BatchGetItem",
        "dynamodb:Scan",
        "dynamodb:Query",
        "dynamodb:ConditionCheckItem"
      ],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:dynamodb:us-west-2:account-id:table/Cars"
    }
  ]
}
```
当应用程序尝试从 Cars 表读取数据时，出现“访问被拒绝”错误。开发人员该如何解决此错误？

options.A: 将 IAM 策略资源修改为“arn:aws:dynamodb:us-west-2:account-id:table/*”。
options.B: 修改 IAM 策略，使其包含 dynamodb:* 操作。
options.C: 创建指定 EC2 服务主体的信任策略。将角色与该策略关联。
options.D: 在角色和 dynamodb.amazonaws.com 之间建立信任关系。

zh.explanation:
# 分析

## 场景
一个 EC2 实例附加了一个 IAM 角色，该角色包含授予对 `us-west-2` 中 `Cars` 表的 DynamoDB 只读操作权限（例如 `GetItem`、`BatchGetItem`、`Scan`、`Query`、`ConditionCheckItem`）的权限策略。应用程序在读取表时收到 **Access Denied** 错误。

问题询问的是，为什么即使权限策略看起来正确，附加到 EC2 实例的 IAM 角色也无法工作。

## 为什么 C 是正确答案
要让 EC2 实例能够通过其实例配置文件实际使用（"假设"）IAM 角色，该角色必须拥有一个**信任策略**，允许 EC2 服务主体（`ec2.amazonaws.com`）调用 `sts:AssumeRole`。没有这种信任关系，EC2 实例无法从实例元数据服务获取临时凭证，因此对 DynamoDB 的所有 API 调用都将失败并返回 Access Denied —— 无论权限策略有多宽泛。

附加到 EC2 实例的角色必须信任 Amazon EC2 服务来假设该角色，这需要一个信任策略，其 Principal 是服务 `ec2.amazonaws.com`，操作为 `sts:AssumeRole`。

所需的信任策略如下所示：

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": { "Service": "ec2.amazonaws.com" },
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
    }
  ]
}
```

附加到 EC2 实例的角色包含一个信任策略，允许 Amazon EC2 实例假设该角色并检索临时凭证。

选项 C 的措辞（"创建一个指定 EC2 服务主体的信任策略。将角色与策略相关联。"）有些尴尬，但它是唯一描述实际修复的选项：设置一个包含 EC2 服务主体的信任策略，以便实例可以假设该角色。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

**A. 将资源 ARN 更改为 `arn:aws:dynamodb:us-west-2:account-id:table/*`** —— 这会将权限扩大到区域中的每个表，违反最小权限原则。给定的策略已经按 ARN 列出了 `Cars` 表；指定的只读操作（`GetItem`、`BatchGetItem`、`Scan`、`Query`、`ConditionCheckItem`）对表资源进行操作，而不是对索引进行操作（LSI 共享表 ARN，没有迹象表明使用了 GSI）。Access Denied 不是由 ARN 范围引起的 —— 它是由角色无法被假设引起的。典型的最小权限只读策略使用特定的表 ARN 作为 Resource，列出 GetItem、BatchGetItem、Scan、Query 和 ConditionCheckItem 等操作。

**B. 使用 `dynamodb:*`** —— 授予完整的 DynamoDB 访问权限（写入/删除/管理），违反最小权限原则。应用程序仅需要读取访问权限，而授予 `*` 不会解决实际问题（缺失信任关系）。

**D. 在角色和 `dynamodb.amazonaws.com` 之间创建信任关系** —— 这是最常见的干扰项。信任策略必须信任*消费*（假设）角色的服务 —— EC2 —— 而不是应用程序*调用*的服务（DynamoDB）。在 EC2 角色的信任策略中，管理员指定只有 Amazon EC2 实例可以假设该角色。信任 `dynamodb.amazonaws.com` 会让 DynamoDB 服务假设该角色，但这不是所需要的。

## 正确答案：**C**

## 参考资源
- [使用 IAM 角色为在 Amazon EC2 实例上运行的应用程序授予权限](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_use_switch-role-ec2.html)
- [Amazon DynamoDB 中的身份和访问管理](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/authentication-and-access-control.html)
- [如何在 IAM 角色中使用信任策略（AWS 安全博客）](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/how-to-use-trust-policies-with-iam-roles/)

en.question: When using the AWS Encryption SDK, how does the developer keep track of the data encryption keys used to encrypt data?

options.A: The developer must manually keep track of the data encryption keys used for each data object.
options.B: The SDK encrypts the data encryption key and stores it (encrypted) as part of the returned ciphertext.
options.C: The SDK stores the data encryption keys automatically in Amazon S3.
options.D: The data encryption key is stored in the Userdata for the EC2 instance.

en.explanation:
# AWS Encryption SDK – Tracking Data Encryption Keys

## Scenario
The question asks how a developer keeps track of data encryption keys (DEKs) when using the AWS Encryption SDK. This is a fundamental concept of **envelope encryption** as implemented by the SDK.

## Correct Answer: B
The AWS Encryption SDK uses envelope encryption. The AWS Encryption SDK uses envelope encryption to protect your data. Each message is encrypted under a unique data key. Then the data key is encrypted by the wrapping keys you specify.

The encrypted DEK is then bundled together with the ciphertext into a single encrypted message. The AWS Encryption SDK stores the encrypted data and encrypted data key together in an encrypted message that uses a defined data format. This means you don't need to keep track of or protect the data keys that encrypt your data because the AWS Encryption SDK does it for you.

When multiple wrapping keys are used, the encrypted data keys (one per wrapping key) are stored with the encrypted data in the encrypted message that the AWS Encryption SDK returns. To decrypt the data, the AWS Encryption SDK must first use one of your wrapping keys to decrypt an encrypted data key.

The encryption method output structure: The encryption method returns an encrypted message that contains the encrypted data, the encrypted data keys, and other metadata, including the encryption context, if you used one.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A. The developer must manually keep track of the data encryption keys** – Incorrect. The whole point of the Encryption SDK is to eliminate this burden; the SDK packages the encrypted DEK inside the returned ciphertext message, so the developer doesn't need to track keys per object.

- **C. The SDK stores the data encryption keys automatically in Amazon S3** – Incorrect. The SDK does not use S3 as a key store. The encrypted DEK is embedded in the encrypted message format itself (header section), not stored in any external AWS service automatically.

- **D. The data encryption key is stored in the Userdata for the EC2 instance** – Incorrect. EC2 user data is plaintext metadata used for instance bootstrapping; storing a DEK there would be insecure and is unrelated to how the Encryption SDK operates. The SDK is platform-agnostic and works in any compute environment.

## References
- [What is the AWS Encryption SDK?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/encryption-sdk/latest/developer-guide/introduction.html)
- [How the AWS Encryption SDK works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/encryption-sdk/latest/developer-guide/how-it-works.html)
- [Configuring the AWS Encryption SDK](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/encryption-sdk/latest/developer-guide/configure.html)
- [AWS Encryption SDK message format reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/encryption-sdk/latest/developer-guide/message-format.html)

zh.question: 使用 AWS 加密 SDK 时，开发人员如何跟踪用于加密数据的数据加密密钥？

options.A: 开发人员必须手动跟踪每个数据对象使用的数据加密密钥。
options.B: SDK 对数据加密密钥进行加密，并将其（加密后）作为返回的密文的一部分存储。
options.C: SDK 会自动将数据加密密钥存储在 Amazon S3 中。
options.D: 数据加密密钥存储在 EC2 实例的用户数据中。

zh.explanation:
# AWS 加密 SDK – 跟踪数据加密密钥

## 场景
该问题询问开发人员在使用 AWS Encryption SDK 时如何跟踪数据加密密钥 (DEK)。这是 SDK 实现的**信封加密**的一个基本概念。

## 正确答案：B
AWS Encryption SDK 使用信封加密。AWS Encryption SDK 使用信封加密来保护您的数据。每条消息都使用唯一的数据密钥进行加密。然后数据密钥由您指定的包装密钥加密。

然后，加密的 DEK 与密文一起打包到单个加密消息中。AWS Encryption SDK 将加密数据和加密数据密钥存储在一起，放入使用定义的数据格式的加密消息中。这意味着您不需要跟踪或保护用于加密数据的数据密钥，因为 AWS Encryption SDK 会为您完成此操作。

当使用多个包装密钥时，加密的数据密钥（每个包装密钥一个）与加密数据一起存储在 AWS Encryption SDK 返回的加密消息中。要解密数据，AWS Encryption SDK 必须首先使用您的某个包装密钥来解密加密的数据密钥。

加密方法输出结构：加密方法返回一个加密消息，该消息包含加密数据、加密数据密钥和其他元数据（包括加密上下文，如果您使用了的话）。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

- **A. 开发人员必须手动跟踪数据加密密钥** – 错误。Encryption SDK 的全部目的是消除这种负担；SDK 将加密的 DEK 打包在返回的密文消息中，因此开发人员不需要跟踪每个对象的密钥。

- **C. SDK 自动将数据加密密钥存储在 Amazon S3 中** – 错误。SDK 不使用 S3 作为密钥存储。加密的 DEK 嵌入在加密消息格式本身（标头部分）中，而不是自动存储在任何外部 AWS 服务中。

- **D. 数据加密密钥存储在 EC2 实例的用户数据中** – 错误。EC2 用户数据是用于实例引导的纯文本元数据；将 DEK 存储在那里会不安全，且与 Encryption SDK 的运作方式无关。SDK 是平台无关的，在任何计算环境中都可以工作。

## 参考资源
- [什么是 AWS Encryption SDK？](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/encryption-sdk/latest/developer-guide/introduction.html)
- [AWS Encryption SDK 的工作原理](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/encryption-sdk/latest/developer-guide/how-it-works.html)
- [配置 AWS Encryption SDK](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/encryption-sdk/latest/developer-guide/configure.html)
- [AWS Encryption SDK 消息格式参考](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/encryption-sdk/latest/developer-guide/message-format.html)

en.question: An application that runs on AWS Lambda requires access to specific highly confidential objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. In accordance with the principle of least privilege, a company grants access to the S3 bucket by using only temporary credentials. How can a developer configure access to the S3 bucket in the MOST secure way?

options.A: Hardcode the credentials that are required to access the S3 objects in the application code. Use the credentials to access the required S3 objects.
options.B: Create a secret access key and access key ID with permission to access the S3 bucket. Store the key and key ID in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure the application to retrieve the Secrets Manager secret and use the credentials to access the S3 objects.
options.C: Create a Lambda function execution role. Attach a policy to the role that grants access to specific objects in the S3 bucket.
options.D: Create a secret access key and access key ID with permission to access the S3 bucket. Store the key and key ID as environment variables in Lambda. Use the environment variables to access the required S3 objects.

en.explanation:
# Lambda Access to S3 with Least Privilege - Temporary Credentials

## Scenario
A Lambda function needs access to **specific** highly confidential S3 objects. The company requires:
1. **Principle of least privilege** (only the specific objects needed)
2. **Only temporary credentials** (no long-lived access keys)

## Correct Answer: C

Create a Lambda function execution role and attach a policy granting access to the specific S3 objects.

When Lambda invokes a function, Lambda automatically provides your function with temporary credentials by assuming this role. You don't have to call sts:AssumeRole in your function code. These credentials are made available as environment variables during a function's invocation, are short-lived, and rotate automatically — fulfilling the "temporary credentials" requirement.

By scoping the policy to specific object ARNs (e.g., `arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name/path/to/object`), the role satisfies the least privilege principle. AWS guidance reinforces this: Scope resources tightly. Use specific ARNs rather than wildcards. Instead of "Resource": "*", specify the exact S3 bucket, DynamoDB table, or SQS queue.

Example policy:
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Action": "s3:GetObject",
    "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::confidential-bucket/specific-prefix/*"
  }]
}
```

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

**A. Hardcode credentials in application code** — This is the worst possible practice. Credentials are long-lived (not temporary), exposed in source control, cannot be rotated easily, and violate every AWS security best practice. Fails both the "temporary credentials" and "most secure" requirements.

**B. Store IAM user access keys in Secrets Manager** — While Secrets Manager protects secrets at rest, this approach **uses long-term IAM user credentials**, not temporary credentials. The question explicitly mandates temporary credentials. It also requires creating an IAM user (an anti-pattern when an AWS service like Lambda can use a role) and adds unnecessary cost/complexity. IAM roles eliminate standard long-term credentials and provide temporary security credentials when being used. Roles are the AWS-recommended mechanism — not stored access keys.

**D. Store access key/secret as Lambda environment variables** — This stores **long-lived static credentials** in plaintext environment variables (visible to anyone with `lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration`). It violates the temporary-credentials requirement and is explicitly discouraged. The execution role already injects temporary credentials automatically — there's no need (or justification) to add static keys.

## Key Takeaway
For any AWS-native compute service (Lambda, EC2, ECS, etc.) accessing other AWS resources, always use an **IAM role** with a tightly scoped resource policy. A Lambda function that needs to read from S3 does not store AWS credentials. Instead, it assumes an execution role, and AWS provides temporary credentials valid for the function's execution. If those credentials leak, they expire within hours rather than being permanently valid.

## References
- [Defining Lambda function permissions with an execution role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-intro-execution-role.html)
- [Managing permissions in AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-permissions.html)
- [Operator Guide: Apply least privilege](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/operatorguide/least-privilege.html)

zh.question: 运行在 AWS Lambda 上的应用程序需要访问 Amazon S3 存储桶中的特定高度机密对象。根据最小权限原则，公司仅使用临时凭证授予对 S3 存储桶的访问权限。开发人员如何以最安全的方式配置对 S3 存储桶的访问权限？

options.A: 将访问 S3 对象所需的凭据硬编码到应用程序代码中。使用这些凭据访问所需的 S3 对象。
options.B: 创建一个具有访问 S3 存储桶权限的秘密访问密钥和访问密钥 ID。将密钥和密钥 ID 存储在 AWS Secrets Manager 中。配置应用程序以检索 Secrets Manager 密钥，并使用该凭证访问 S3 对象。
options.C: 创建一个 Lambda 函数执行角色。将策略附加到该角色，以授予其对 S3 存储桶中特定对象的访问权限。
options.D: 创建一个具有访问 S3 存储桶权限的秘密访问密钥和访问密钥 ID。将密钥和密钥 ID 作为环境变量存储在 Lambda 函数中。使用这些环境变量访问所需的 S3 对象。

zh.explanation:
# Lambda 通过最小权限原则访问 S3 - 临时凭证

## 场景
Lambda 函数需要访问**特定的**高度机密 S3 对象。公司要求：
1. **最小权限原则**（仅访问所需的特定对象）
2. **仅使用临时凭证**（无长期访问密钥）

## 正确答案：C

创建 Lambda 函数执行角色，并附加授予特定 S3 对象访问权限的策略。

当 Lambda 调用函数时，Lambda 会自动通过担任此角色为函数提供临时凭证。您不必在函数代码中调用 sts:AssumeRole。这些凭证是在函数调用期间作为环境变量提供的，具有短期有效期，并自动轮换 — 满足"临时凭证"要求。

通过将策略范围限定为特定对象 ARN（例如 `arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name/path/to/object`），该角色满足最小权限原则。AWS 指南强化了这一点：严格限定资源范围。使用特定的 ARN 而不是通配符。应使用具体的 S3 存储桶、DynamoDB 表或 SQS 队列，而不是 "Resource": "*"。

示例策略：
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Action": "s3:GetObject",
    "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::confidential-bucket/specific-prefix/*"
  }]
}
```

## 其他选项为什么错误

**A. 在应用程序代码中硬编码凭证** — 这是最糟糕的做法。凭证具有长期有效期（非临时），暴露在源代码控制中，无法轻松轮换，违反所有 AWS 安全最佳实践。不满足"临时凭证"和"最安全"的要求。

**B. 将 IAM 用户访问密钥存储在 Secrets Manager 中** — 尽管 Secrets Manager 保护静态密钥的安全，但此方法**使用长期 IAM 用户凭证**，不是临时凭证。问题明确要求临时凭证。它还需要创建 IAM 用户（当 Lambda 等 AWS 服务可以使用角色时，这是反模式），增加了不必要的成本和复杂性。IAM 角色消除了标准长期凭证，并在使用时提供临时安全凭证。角色是 AWS 推荐的机制 — 而不是存储访问密钥。

**D. 将访问密钥/密钥存储为 Lambda 环境变量** — 这会在纯文本环境变量中存储**长期静态凭证**（对拥有 `lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration` 权限的任何人都可见）。违反了临时凭证要求，明确不被推荐。执行角色已自动注入临时凭证 — 没有必要（或理由）添加静态密钥。

## 关键要点
对于任何需要访问其他 AWS 资源的 AWS 原生计算服务（Lambda、EC2、ECS 等），始终使用**IAM 角色**，并配置严格限定范围的资源策略。需要从 S3 读取的 Lambda 函数不存储 AWS 凭证。相反，它担任执行角色，AWS 提供函数执行期间有效的临时凭证。如果这些凭证泄露，它们会在几小时内过期，而不是永久有效。

## 参考资源
- [使用执行角色定义 Lambda 函数权限](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-intro-execution-role.html)
- [在 AWS Lambda 中管理权限](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-permissions.html)
- [操作指南：应用最小权限原则](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/operatorguide/least-privilege.html)

en.question: A developer has code that is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The code must be deployed as an AWS Lambda function across multiple accounts in the same AWS Region as the S3 bucket. An AWS CloudFormation template that runs for each account will deploy the Lambda function. What is the MOST secure way to allow CloudFormation to access the Lambda code in the S3 bucket?

options.A: Grant the CloudFormation service role the S3 ListBucket and GetObject permissions. Add a bucket policy to Amazon S3 with the principal of “AWS”: [account numbers].
options.B: Grant the CloudFormation service role the S3 GetObject permission. Add a bucket policy to Amazon S3 with the principal of “*”.
options.C: Use a service-based link to grant the Lambda function the S3 ListBucket and GetObject permissions by explicitly adding the S3 bucket’s account number in the resource.
options.D: Use a service-based link to grant the Lambda function the S3 GetObject permission. Add a resource of “*” to allow access to the S3 bucket.

en.explanation:
# Cross-Account CloudFormation Lambda Deployment from S3

## Scenario
Lambda code is stored in a **single S3 bucket** (in one account/region). A CloudFormation template is executed in **multiple AWS accounts** (in the same region) to deploy a Lambda function whose code package lives in that S3 bucket. Each account's CloudFormation stack must be able to read the Lambda zip from the central S3 bucket. The question asks for the **most secure** approach.

## Why A is Correct
For cross-account S3 access you need **both**:
1. An **identity-based policy** on the CloudFormation service role (in each consumer account) that allows `s3:GetObject` (and optionally `s3:ListBucket`) on the bucket holding the Lambda code.
2. A **resource-based policy** (S3 bucket policy) on the central bucket that explicitly trusts the **specific account principals** (`"Principal": { "AWS": ["arn:aws:iam::<account-id>:root", ...] }`).

This dual-permission model is the standard AWS cross-account access pattern. As shown in AWS documentation and guides, the bucket policy must list the trusted accounts as principals while granting `s3:GetObject` and `s3:ListBucket`, restricting access to **only** the specified accounts — adhering to least privilege at the account boundary. See [AWS CloudFormation: Specify a Bucket from Another AWS Account for Lambda Code](https://saturncloud.io/blog/aws-cloudformation-how-to-specify-a-bucket-from-another-aws-account-for-lambda-code/) and the AWS re:Post pattern using `"Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_B:root"}` with `s3:GetObject` and `s3:ListBucket`.

`ListBucket` is commonly included so CloudFormation can verify the object exists and avoid generic "AccessDenied" responses; while strictly only `GetObject` is required if the exact key is known, including `ListBucket` is still a valid least-privilege configuration scoped to the specific bucket and accounts. Among the four options, A is the only one that scopes both the IAM permissions and the bucket policy to the precise needed actions and to specific trusted accounts.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

### B. Bucket policy with `Principal: "*"`
A wildcard principal makes the bucket effectively **public** for `s3:GetObject` to anyone on the internet (any AWS account, anonymous if combined with public access). This violates least privilege and is explicitly the opposite of "most secure." Per [AWS S3 BucketPolicy reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-s3-bucketpolicy.html), a `"Principal": "*"` policy without strong conditions exposes objects publicly. Even if Block Public Access blocks it, relying on that is far less secure than explicitly listing trusted account principals.

### C. "Service-based link" granting Lambda S3 ListBucket and GetObject
There is no such concept as a "service-based link" — the term confuses **service-linked roles** with something that does not exist for this scenario. Lambda does not need to read its own code from S3 at runtime; **CloudFormation** (not Lambda) is what fetches the deployment package during `CreateFunction`. The Lambda execution role is irrelevant for retrieving the deployment ZIP. See [AWS::Lambda::Function Code property](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-lambda-function-code.html) — CloudFormation/Lambda service uses the caller's credentials to access the S3 bucket.

### D. "Service-based link" with Resource `"*"`
Same conceptual error as C (service-linked roles do not apply here), and granting `s3:GetObject` on `Resource: "*"` violates least privilege by allowing access to **every** S3 object the principal can reach. Best practice is to scope resources to `arn:aws:s3:::bucket` and `arn:aws:s3:::bucket/*`.

## Correct Bucket Policy Pattern (Option A)
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Principal": { "AWS": [
        "arn:aws:iam::111111111111:root",
        "arn:aws:iam::222222222222:root"
    ]},
    "Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:ListBucket"],
    "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:s3:::lambda-code-bucket",
        "arn:aws:s3:::lambda-code-bucket/*"
    ]
  }]
}
```
Combined with an IAM policy on each account's CloudFormation service role granting the same `s3:GetObject` (and optionally `s3:ListBucket`) on the same resources.

## References
- [Bucket policies for cross-account access (AWS S3 User Guide)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/example-bucket-policies.html)
- [AWS::S3::BucketPolicy CloudFormation reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-s3-bucketpolicy.html)
- [Specifying a bucket from another AWS account for Lambda code (Saturn Cloud)](https://saturncloud.io/blog/aws-cloudformation-how-to-specify-a-bucket-from-another-aws-account-for-lambda-code/)
- [S3 bucket permissions for CloudFormation across accounts (AWS re:Post)](https://repost.aws/questions/QUNhxgNM19TiCvvvCxEI50Ew/s3-bucket-permissions-to-run-cloudformation-from-different-accounts-and-create-lambda-funtions)

**Answer: A**

zh.question: 开发人员的代码存储在 Amazon S3 存储桶中。该代码必须以 AWS Lambda 函数的形式部署到与 S3 存储桶位于同一 AWS 区域的多个账户中。每个账户都会运行一个 AWS CloudFormation 模板来部署 Lambda 函数。如何以最安全的方式允许 CloudFormation 访问 S3 存储桶中的 Lambda 代码？

options.A: 授予 CloudFormation 服务角色 S3 ListBucket 和 GetObject 权限。向 Amazon S3 添加一个存储桶策略，其主体为“AWS”: [账号]。
options.B: 授予 CloudFormation 服务角色 S3 GetObject 权限。向 Amazon S3 添加一个主体为“*”的存储桶策略。
options.C: 使用基于服务的链接，通过在资源中显式添加 S3 存储桶的账号，授予 Lambda 函数 S3 ListBucket 和 GetObject 权限。
options.D: 使用基于服务的链接授予 Lambda 函数 S3 GetObject 权限。添加资源“*”以允许访问 S3 存储桶。

zh.explanation:
# 跨账户 CloudFormation Lambda 从 S3 部署

## 场景
Lambda 代码存储在**单个 S3 bucket**（在一个账户/区域中）。CloudFormation 模板在**多个 AWS 账户**（同一区域）中执行，以部署 Lambda 函数，其代码包位于该 S3 bucket 中。每个账户的 CloudFormation 堆栈必须能够从中央 S3 bucket 读取 Lambda zip。该问题要求最**安全**的方法。

## 为什么 A 是正确的
对于跨账户 S3 访问，您需要**两者**：
1. **基于身份的策略**，在 CloudFormation 服务角色（在每个消费账户中）上允许 `s3:GetObject`（以及可选的 `s3:ListBucket`）访问保存 Lambda 代码的 bucket。
2. **基于资源的策略**（S3 bucket 策略），在中央 bucket 上明确信任**特定账户主体**（`"Principal": { "AWS": ["arn:aws:iam::<account-id>:root", ...] }`）。

这种双权限模型是标准的 AWS 跨账户访问模式。如 AWS 文档和指南所示，bucket 策略必须列出信任的账户作为主体，同时授予 `s3:GetObject` 和 `s3:ListBucket`，将访问限制为**仅**指定的账户——在账户边界处遵守最小权限原则。参见 [AWS CloudFormation: 为 Lambda 代码指定来自另一个 AWS 账户的 Bucket](https://saturncloud.io/blog/aws-cloudformation-how-to-specify-a-bucket-from-another-aws-account-for-lambda-code/) 和使用 `"Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_B:root"}` 与 `s3:GetObject` 和 `s3:ListBucket` 的 AWS re:Post 模式。

通常包括 `ListBucket`，以便 CloudFormation 可以验证对象存在并避免通用"AccessDenied"响应；虽然严格来说，如果已知确切的密钥，仅需要 `GetObject`，但包括 `ListBucket` 仍然是有效的最小权限配置，其作用范围限于特定的 bucket 和账户。在四个选项中，A 是唯一一个将 IAM 权限和 bucket 策略范围都限定为精确所需操作和特定信任账户的选项。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

### B. 带有 `Principal: "*"` 的 Bucket 策略
通配符主体使 bucket 对互联网上任何人（任何 AWS 账户、如果与公共访问结合则为匿名用户）的 `s3:GetObject` 实际上**公开**。这违反了最小权限原则，与"最安全"明确相反。根据 [AWS S3 BucketPolicy 参考](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-s3-bucketpolicy.html)，没有强条件的 `"Principal": "*"` 策略会公开对象。即使"阻止公共访问"阻止了它，依赖这种方式也远不如明确列出信任的账户主体安全。

### C. "基于服务的链接"授予 Lambda S3 ListBucket 和 GetObject
不存在"基于服务的链接"这样的概念——该术语将**服务相关角色**与此场景中不存在的某种东西混淆了。Lambda 不需要在运行时从 S3 读取自己的代码；**CloudFormation**（不是 Lambda）在 `CreateFunction` 期间获取部署包。Lambda 执行角色与检索部署 ZIP 无关。参见 [AWS::Lambda::Function Code 属性](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-lambda-function-code.html)——CloudFormation/Lambda 服务使用调用者的凭证访问 S3 bucket。

### D. "基于服务的链接"，资源为 `"*"`
与 C 相同的概念错误（服务相关角色在此不适用），并且授予 `s3:GetObject` on `Resource: "*"` 违反最小权限，允许访问主体可以到达的**每个** S3 对象。最佳实践是将资源范围限制为 `arn:aws:s3:::bucket` 和 `arn:aws:s3:::bucket/*`。

## 正确的 Bucket 策略模式（选项 A）
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Principal": { "AWS": [
        "arn:aws:iam::111111111111:root",
        "arn:aws:iam::222222222222:root"
    ]},
    "Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:ListBucket"],
    "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:s3:::lambda-code-bucket",
        "arn:aws:s3:::lambda-code-bucket/*"
    ]
  }]
}
```
结合每个账户的 CloudFormation 服务角色上的 IAM 策略，授予相同资源上的相同 `s3:GetObject`（以及可选的 `s3:ListBucket`）。

## 参考资源
- [用于跨账户访问的 Bucket 策略（AWS S3 用户指南）](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/example-bucket-policies.html)
- [AWS::S3::BucketPolicy CloudFormation 参考](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-s3-bucketpolicy.html)
- [为 Lambda 代码指定来自另一个 AWS 账户的 Bucket（Saturn Cloud）](https://saturncloud.io/blog/aws-cloudformation-how-to-specify-a-bucket-from-another-aws-account-for-lambda-code/)
- [跨账户 CloudFormation 的 S3 bucket 权限（AWS re:Post）](https://repost.aws/questions/QUNhxgNM19TiCvvvCxEI50Ew/s3-bucket-permissions-to-run-cloudformation-from-different-accounts-and-create-lambda-funtions)

**答案：A**

en.question: A developer at a company needs to create a small application that makes the same API call once each day at a designated time.
