The company does not have infrastructure in the AWS Cloud yet, but the company wants to implement this functionality on AWS. Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient manner?

options.A: Use a Kubernetes cron job that runs on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS).
options.B: Use an Amazon Linux crontab scheduled job that runs on Amazon EC2.
options.C: Use an AWS Lambda function that is invoked by an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event.
options.D: Use an AWS Batch job that is submitted to an AWS Batch job queue.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

The company has **no existing AWS infrastructure** and needs to make the **same API call once a day** at a designated time. The goal is to choose the **most operationally efficient** solution — meaning minimal infrastructure to provision, manage, patch, or scale.

## Correct Answer: C — Lambda + EventBridge scheduled event

A serverless combination of AWS Lambda (to execute the API call) triggered by an Amazon EventBridge schedule (cron/rate expression) is the canonical pattern for this use case. There are no servers, clusters, or job queues to manage; the developer only writes the function code and defines a schedule expression.

Amazon EventBridge scheduled events can invoke an AWS Lambda function using a cron expression to schedule when the Lambda function is invoked. With EventBridge Scheduler, you can create schedules using cron and rate expressions for recurring patterns, set up flexible time windows, define retry limits, and set retention time for failed invocations.

This is fully managed and serverless — perfect when the company has no existing AWS infrastructure to leverage.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A. Kubernetes cron job on Amazon EKS** — EKS requires provisioning and managing a Kubernetes control plane (with hourly cluster cost) and worker nodes (EC2 or Fargate). Operating a cluster just to run one API call per day is dramatically over-engineered and incurs significant operational overhead (node patching, cluster upgrades, IAM/RBAC, networking).

- **B. Amazon Linux crontab on EC2** — Requires launching, patching, monitoring, and paying for an EC2 instance running 24/7 just to fire one cron job per day. The developer is responsible for OS maintenance, availability, and recovery if the instance fails. Far less operationally efficient than a serverless function.

- **D. AWS Batch job submitted to a Batch job queue** — AWS Batch is designed for **batch computing workloads** (large-scale parallel/HPC jobs running on managed EC2 or Fargate compute environments). It also doesn't provide native time-based scheduling on its own — you'd still need EventBridge to submit the job. This adds unnecessary components (compute environment, job queue, job definition) for a single daily API call.

## Reference Documentation

- [Use scheduled events to invoke a Lambda function (EventBridge)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/example_cross_LambdaScheduledEvents_section.html)
- [Schedule a Lambda function – EventBridge tutorial](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-run-lambda-schedule.html)
- [Invoke a Lambda function on a schedule (EventBridge Scheduler)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-eventbridge-scheduler.html)

zh.question: 某公司的开发人员需要创建一个小型应用程序，该应用程序每天在指定时间调用相同的 API 一次。该公司目前在 AWS 云上还没有基础设施，但希望在 AWS 上实现此功能。哪种解决方案能够以最高效的方式满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用在 Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) 上运行的 Kubernetes cron 作业。
options.B: 使用在 Amazon EC2 上运行的 Amazon Linux crontab 定时任务。
options.C: 使用由 Amazon EventBridge 计划事件调用的 AWS Lambda 函数。
options.D: 使用提交到 AWS Batch 作业队列的 AWS Batch 作业。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

该公司**没有现有的 AWS 基础设施**，需要**每天在指定时间执行一次相同的 API 调用**。目标是选择**最具操作效率**的解决方案——意味着需要配置、管理、修补或扩展的基础设施最少。

## 正确答案：C — Lambda + EventBridge 计划事件

无服务器组合，使用 AWS Lambda（执行 API 调用）由 Amazon EventBridge 计划事件（cron/rate 表达式）触发，是此用例的标准模式。没有服务器、集群或作业队列需要管理；开发人员只需编写函数代码并定义计划表达式。

Amazon EventBridge 计划事件可以使用 cron 表达式调用 AWS Lambda 函数，以计划 Lambda 函数的调用时间。 使用 EventBridge Scheduler，您可以使用 cron 和 rate 表达式创建循环模式的计划，设置灵活的时间窗口，定义重试限制，并为失败的调用设置保留时间。

这是完全托管和无服务器的——非常适合公司没有现有 AWS 基础设施可利用的情况。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

- **A. Amazon EKS 上的 Kubernetes cron 作业** — EKS 需要配置和管理 Kubernetes 控制平面（需要按小时支付集群费用）和工作节点（EC2 或 Fargate）。为了运行每天一次的 API 调用而操作集群是过度设计，会产生巨大的操作开销（节点修补、集群升级、IAM/RBAC、网络）。

- **B. Amazon Linux EC2 上的 crontab** — 需要启动、修补、监控并为 24/7 运行的 EC2 实例付费，仅为了触发每天一次的 cron 作业。开发人员需要负责操作系统维护、可用性以及实例故障时的恢复。远不如无服务器函数高效。

- **D. 提交到 AWS Batch 作业队列的 AWS Batch 作业** — AWS Batch 针对**批计算工作负载**（在托管 EC2 或 Fargate 计算环境上运行的大规模并行/HPC 作业）设计。它本身也不提供基于时间的原生计划——您仍需要 EventBridge 来提交作业。这会为单个每日 API 调用添加不必要的组件（计算环境、作业队列、作业定义）。

## 参考文档

- [使用计划事件调用 Lambda 函数 (EventBridge)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/example_cross_LambdaScheduledEvents_section.html)
- [按计划调用 Lambda 函数——EventBridge 教程](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-run-lambda-schedule.html)
- [按计划调用 Lambda 函数 (EventBridge Scheduler)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-eventbridge-scheduler.html)

en.question: A developer is building a serverless application that is based on AWS Lambda. The developer initializes the AWS software development kit (SDK) outside of the Lambda handler function. What is the PRIMARY benefit of this action?

options.A: Improves legibility and stylistic convention
options.B: Takes advantage of runtime environment reuse
options.C: Provides better error handling
options.D: Creates a new SDK instance for each invocation

en.explanation:
# AWS Lambda – Initializing the SDK Outside the Handler

## Scenario
A developer building a serverless application with AWS Lambda chooses to instantiate the AWS SDK client **outside** of the handler function (i.e., at module/global scope). The question asks for the PRIMARY benefit of this design pattern.

## Correct Answer: B — Takes advantage of runtime environment reuse

When Lambda invokes a function, it provisions an **execution environment** (also called the runtime/execution context). Code placed outside the handler runs only during the cold-start initialization phase. After the handler returns, Lambda freezes the environment and can reuse it for subsequent invocations — this is known as a "warm start."

According to the official AWS Lambda best practices: "Take advantage of execution environment reuse to improve the performance of your function. Initialize SDK clients and database connections outside of the function handler, and cache static assets locally in the /tmp directory. Subsequent invocations processed by the same instance of your function can reuse these resources. This saves cost by reducing function run time."

The Lambda execution environment lifecycle documentation confirms this behavior: "When the function is invoked again, Lambda thaws the environment for reuse. Reusing the execution environment has the following implications: Objects declared outside of the function's handler method remain initialized, providing additional optimization when the function is invoked again. For example, if your Lambda function establishes a database connection, instead of reestablishing the connection, the original connection is used in subsequent invocations."

This means the SDK client (with its TCP connections, credential providers, and configuration) is initialized **once per execution environment** and reused across many invocations, dramatically reducing per-invocation latency and cost.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A. Improves legibility and stylistic convention** — While code organization may be a minor side effect, AWS does not recommend this pattern for stylistic reasons. The recommendation is explicitly grounded in **performance** (execution environment reuse), not aesthetics.

- **C. Provides better error handling** — Initialization code that lives outside the handler actually runs during the INIT phase. If it throws, it can cause an init failure that's harder to catch in handler-level try/catch blocks. There is no error-handling benefit; if anything, errors thrown outside the handler are reported differently and can affect cold starts.

- **D. Creates a new SDK instance for each invocation** — This is the **opposite** of what happens. Initializing outside the handler creates the SDK client **once** per execution environment and reuses it. Putting initialization inside the handler is what would create a new instance every invocation, which is the anti-pattern AWS warns against.

## Key Takeaway
Place `const s3Client = new S3Client(...)` (or equivalent SDK client construction) at the module's top level so Lambda runs it during the INIT phase. The frozen-and-thawed execution environment then reuses that client across warm invocations, lowering latency and cost.

## References
- [Best practices for working with AWS Lambda functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/best-practices.html)
- [Define Lambda function handler in Node.js](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/nodejs-handler.html)
- [Understanding the Lambda execution environment lifecycle](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-runtime-environment.html)
- [Define Lambda function handler in Python](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/python-handler.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在构建一个基于 AWS Lambda 的无服务器应用程序。该开发人员在 Lambda 处理函数之外初始化了 AWS 软件开发工具包 (SDK)。此操作的主要好处是什么？

options.A: 提高易读性和风格规范
options.B: 利用运行时环境重用
options.C: 提供更好的错误处理
options.D: 为每次调用创建一个新的 SDK 实例

zh.explanation:
# AWS Lambda — 在处理程序外初始化 SDK

## 场景
使用 AWS Lambda 构建无服务器应用程序的开发者选择在处理程序函数**外部**（即在模块/全局作用域）实例化 AWS SDK 客户端。问题要求找出这种设计模式的**主要**优势。

## 正确答案：B — 利用运行时环境重用

当 Lambda 调用一个函数时，它会配置一个**执行环境**（也称为运行时/执行上下文）。位于处理程序外的代码仅在冷启动初始化阶段运行一次。处理程序返回后，Lambda 会冻结该环境，并可以将其重用于后续调用 — 这被称为"热启动"。

根据官方 AWS Lambda 最佳实践："利用执行环境重用来改善函数的性能。在函数处理程序外初始化 SDK 客户端和数据库连接，并将静态资产缓存到 /tmp 目录中。由同一函数实例处理的后续调用可以重用这些资源。这通过减少函数运行时间来节省成本。"

Lambda 执行环境生命周期文档证实了这一行为："当函数再次被调用时，Lambda 会解冻该环境以供重用。重用执行环境具有以下含义：在函数处理程序方法外声明的对象保持初始化状态，在再次调用函数时提供额外的优化。例如，如果您的 Lambda 函数建立了数据库连接，无需重新建立连接，原始连接将在后续调用中被使用。"

这意味着 SDK 客户端（及其 TCP 连接、凭证提供程序和配置）**每个执行环境初始化一次**，并在许多调用中被重用，大大降低了每次调用的延迟和成本。

## 为什么其他选项错误

- **A. 改善可读性和风格约定** — 虽然代码组织可能是一个次要的副作用，但 AWS 不会因为风格原因推荐此模式。该建议明确基于**性能**（执行环境重用），而非美观性。

- **C. 提供更好的错误处理** — 位于处理程序外的初始化代码实际上在 INIT 阶段运行。如果抛出异常，它会导致初始化失败，这很难被处理程序级别的 try/catch 块捕获。没有错误处理优势；反而，在处理程序外抛出的错误被报告方式不同，并且可能会影响冷启动。

- **D. 为每次调用创建一个新的 SDK 实例** — 这与实际情况**相反**。在处理程序外初始化会**每个执行环境创建一次** SDK 客户端并重用它。将初始化放在处理程序内是导致每次调用创建新实例的做法，这正是 AWS 警告的反模式。

## 关键要点
将 `const s3Client = new S3Client(...)` （或等效的 SDK 客户端构造）放在模块的顶层，以便 Lambda 在 INIT 阶段运行它。被冻结和解冻的执行环境随后会在热启动调用中重用该客户端，降低延迟和成本。

## 参考资源

- [在 Node.js 中定义 Lambda 函数处理程序](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/nodejs-handler.html)
- [了解 Lambda 执行环境生命周期](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-runtime-environment.html)
- [在 Python 中定义 Lambda 函数处理程序](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/python-handler.html)

en.question: A company is using Amazon RDS as the backend database for its application. After a recent marketing campaign, a surge of read requests to the database increased the latency of data retrieval from the database. The company has decided to implement a caching layer in front of the database. The cached content must be encrypted and must be highly available. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Amazon CloudFront
options.B: Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached
options.C: Amazon ElastiCache for Redis in cluster mode
options.D: Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)

en.explanation:
## Scenario Analysis

The company's RDS database is suffering high read latency after a marketing campaign caused a surge in read traffic. They want to add a caching layer with two key requirements:
1. **Cached content must be encrypted** (at rest and in transit)
2. **Must be highly available**

## Correct Answer: C — Amazon ElastiCache for Redis in cluster mode

ElastiCache for Redis is purpose-built as a cache in front of databases like RDS and meets both requirements:

- **Encryption**: It offers encryption in transit, at rest (including customer managed CMK stored in AWS KMS), and Redis AUTH for internode communications.
- **High Availability**: Amazon ElastiCache for Redis supports both Redis cluster and non-cluster modes and provides high availability via support for automatic failover by detecting primary node failures and promoting a replica to be primary with minimal impact. It allows for read availability for your application by supporting read replicas (across availability zones), to enable the reads to be served when the primary is busy with the increased workload.
- **Cluster mode scalability**: Amazon ElastiCache (Redis OSS) supports three cluster configurations (Redis (single node), Redis (cluster mode disabled), and Redis (cluster mode enabled)), depending on your reliability, availability, and scaling requirements. With Cluster Mode enabled, your Redis cluster can now scale horizontally (in or out) in addition to scaling vertically (up and down).

This makes Redis (cluster mode) ideal for offloading read traffic from RDS while satisfying encryption and HA requirements.

## Why the other options are wrong

### A. Amazon CloudFront ❌
CloudFront is a **content delivery network (CDN)** designed to cache static and dynamic web content (HTML, images, video, API responses) at edge locations close to end users. It is **not designed as a database query cache** in front of RDS. CloudFront cannot cache RDS query results directly — applications query RDS via SQL connections, not HTTP requests that CloudFront can intercept.

### B. Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached ❌
Memcached does **not support encryption at rest** and historically had limited in-transit encryption support compared to Redis. It also lacks built-in replication and automatic failover, so it does **not provide high availability** — if a node fails, the cached data on that node is lost. This fails both stated requirements (encryption + HA). See [ElastiCache: Comparing Memcached and Redis](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/mem-ug/SelectEngine.html).

### D. Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) ❌
DAX is an in-memory cache **exclusively for Amazon DynamoDB**, not RDS. It uses the DynamoDB API and cannot cache relational SQL queries from RDS. See [DAX overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html).

## Reference Documentation
- [Amazon ElastiCache for Redis – Encryption at Rest](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/at-rest-encryption.html)
- [Amazon ElastiCache for Redis – Encryption in Transit](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/in-transit-encryption.html)
- [High availability using replication groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/Replication.html)
- [Database Caching Strategies Using Redis (AWS Whitepaper)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/database-caching-strategies-using-redis/redis-cluster-modes-enabled-and-disabled.html)

zh.question: 一家公司使用 Amazon RDS 作为其应用程序的后端数据库。最近一次市场营销活动后，数据库读取请求激增，导致数据检索延迟增加。该公司决定在数据库前端部署一个缓存层。缓存内容必须加密且具有高可用性。哪种解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 亚马逊云前沿
options.B: Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached
options.C: 集群模式下的 Amazon ElastiCache for Redis
options.D: Amazon DynamoDB 加速器 (DAX)

zh.explanation:
## 场景分析

公司的 RDS 数据库在营销活动导致读流量激增后出现高读延迟。他们想添加一个缓存层，有两个关键要求：
1. **缓存内容必须加密**（静态和传输中）
2. **必须高度可用**

## 正确答案：C — Amazon ElastiCache for Redis（集群模式）

ElastiCache for Redis 是专为在 RDS 等数据库前面作为缓存而设计的，满足两个要求：

- **加密**：它提供传输中加密、静态加密（包括存储在 AWS KMS 中的客户托管 CMK）和用于节点间通信的 Redis AUTH。
- **高可用性**：Amazon ElastiCache for Redis 支持 Redis 集群和非集群模式，并通过检测主节点故障并将副本提升为主节点来提供高可用性，影响最小。它通过支持读副本（跨可用区）为应用程序提供读可用性，以便在主节点忙于处理增加的工作负载时为读取请求提供服务。
- **集群模式可扩展性**：Amazon ElastiCache (Redis OSS) 支持三种集群配置（Redis（单节点）、Redis（集群模式禁用）和 Redis（集群模式启用））根据你的可靠性、可用性和扩展需求而定。启用集群模式后，你的 Redis 集群现在可以在水平方向（进出）缩放，除了垂直方向（上下）缩放。

这使得 Redis（集群模式）成为从 RDS 卸载读流量同时满足加密和高可用性要求的理想选择。

## 其他选项为什么错误

### A. Amazon CloudFront ❌
CloudFront 是一个**内容分发网络（CDN）**，专为在靠近最终用户的边缘位置缓存静态和动态网络内容（HTML、图像、视频、API 响应）而设计。它**不是设计用来作为 RDS 前面的数据库查询缓存**的。CloudFront 无法直接缓存 RDS 查询结果——应用程序通过 SQL 连接查询 RDS，而不是 CloudFront 可以拦截的 HTTP 请求。

### B. Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached ❌
Memcached **不支持静态加密**，与 Redis 相比在传输中加密的支持有限。它还缺乏内置复制和自动故障转移，因此**不提供高可用性**——如果节点失败，该节点上的缓存数据会丢失。这违反了两个既定要求（加密 + 高可用性）。见 [ElastiCache：Memcached 和 Redis 比较](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/mem-ug/SelectEngine.html)。

### D. Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) ❌
DAX 是一个内存缓存，**仅专用于 Amazon DynamoDB**，不是 RDS。它使用 DynamoDB API，无法缓存来自 RDS 的关系型 SQL 查询。见 [DAX 概览](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html)。

## 参考文档
- [Amazon ElastiCache for Redis – 静态加密](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/at-rest-encryption.html)
- [Amazon ElastiCache for Redis – 传输中加密](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/in-transit-encryption.html)
- [使用复制组实现高可用性](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/Replication.html)
- [使用 Redis 的数据库缓存策略（AWS 白皮书）](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/database-caching-strategies-using-redis/redis-cluster-modes-enabled-and-disabled.html)

en.question: A developer at a company recently created a serverless application to process and show data from business reports. The application’s user interface (UI) allows users to select and start processing the files. The UI displays a message when the result is available to view. The application uses AWS Step Functions with AWS Lambda functions to process the files. The developer used Amazon API Gateway and Lambda functions to create an API to support the UI. The company’s UI team reports that the request to process a file is often returning timeout errors because of the size or complexity of the files. The UI team wants the API to provide an immediate response so that the UI can display a message while the files are being processed. The backend process that is invoked by the API needs to send an email message when the report processing is complete. What should the developer do to configure the API to meet these requirements?

options.A: Change the API Gateway route to add an X-Amz-Invocation-Type header with a static value of ‘Event’ in the integration request. Deploy the API Gateway stage to apply the changes.
options.B: Change the configuration of the Lambda function that implements the request to process a file. Configure the maximum age of the event so that the Lambda function will run asynchronously.
options.C: Change the API Gateway timeout value to match the Lambda function timeout value. Deploy the API Gateway stage to apply the changes.
options.D: Change the API Gateway route to add an X-Amz-Target header with a static value of ‘Async’ in the integration request. Deploy the API Gateway stage to apply the changes.

en.explanation:
# API Gateway Asynchronous Lambda Invocation

## Scenario
The UI calls an API Gateway endpoint that triggers a Lambda function which starts a Step Functions workflow to process large/complex files. Because processing takes a long time, the synchronous API call frequently exceeds the API Gateway integration timeout (max 29 seconds for REST APIs). The UI needs an immediate response (so it can show "processing" message) and the backend will email the user via SES when finished.

The fix is to make the Lambda invocation **asynchronous** at the API Gateway integration layer so API Gateway returns immediately (HTTP 202) without waiting for Lambda to complete.

## Correct Answer: A
Add an `X-Amz-Invocation-Type` header with a static value of `'Event'` in the Integration Request, then redeploy the stage.

You can configure the Lambda function for a Lambda non-proxy integration to be invoked asynchronously by specifying 'Event' as the Lambda invocation type. This is done by adding an X-Amz-Invocation-Type header with a static value of 'Event' in Integration request.

When the invocation type is `Event`, asynchronous lambda invocation allows for a quick response back (e.g. 202 Accepted) while allowing the lambda to continue running. This is desired if you wish to kick off a lambda that runs longer than the API GW 30 second timeout.

Example OpenAPI snippet:
```json
"x-amazon-apigateway-integration": {
  "type": "aws",
  "httpMethod": "POST",
  "uri": "arn:aws:apigateway:us-east-2:lambda:path/2015-03-31/functions/arn:aws:lambda:us-east-2:123456789012:function:my-function/invocations",
  "requestParameters": {
    "integration.request.header.X-Amz-Invocation-Type": "'Event'"
  }
}
```

The Lambda function then starts the Step Functions execution, and when processing completes, an SES email is sent to the user.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **B. Configure Lambda's maximum event age** – Maximum event age is a property of Lambda's asynchronous invocation queue (how long an already-async event can stay in the queue before being discarded). It does **not** change a synchronous API Gateway → Lambda call into an asynchronous one. The synchronous timeout problem would persist.

- **C. Match API Gateway timeout to Lambda timeout** – API Gateway REST API integration timeout is capped at 29 seconds (and 30 seconds for HTTP APIs by default), while Lambda can run up to 15 minutes. You cannot raise API Gateway's integration timeout to match Lambda's, and even if you could, the UI still wouldn't get an immediate response.

- **D. `X-Amz-Target` header with value `'Async'`** – This header/value combination does **not exist** for the Lambda Invoke API. The Lambda Invoke API uses `X-Amz-Invocation-Type` with values `Event` (async), `RequestResponse` (sync), or `DryRun`. `X-Amz-Target` is used by other AWS service JSON RPC APIs but not to switch Lambda to asynchronous mode. This option is fabricated.

## References
- [Set up asynchronous invocation of the backend Lambda function](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/set-up-lambda-integration-async.html)
- [Invoke a Lambda function asynchronously from API Gateway (re:Post)](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/api-gateway-invoke-lambda)
- [Lambda Invoke API – InvocationType](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/API_Invoke.html)

zh.question: 某公司的一位开发人员最近创建了一个无服务器应用程序，用于处理和显示业务报告中的数据。该应用程序的用户界面 (UI) 允许用户选择并开始处理文件。当处理结果可用时，UI 会显示一条消息。该应用程序使用 AWS Step Functions 和 AWS Lambda 函数来处理文件。开发人员使用 Amazon API Gateway 和 Lambda 函数创建了一个 API 来支持 UI。公司的 UI 团队报告称，由于文件的大小或复杂性，处理文件的请求经常返回超时错误。UI 团队希望 API 能够立即响应，以便 UI 能够在文件处理过程中显示消息。API 调用的后端进程需要在报告处理完成后发送电子邮件。开发人员应该如何配置 API 以满足这些要求？

options.A: 修改 API 网关路由，在集成请求中添加一个 X-Amz-Invocation-Type 标头，其静态值为“Event”。部署 API 网关阶段以应用更改。
options.B: 更改实现文件处理请求的 Lambda 函数的配置。配置事件的最大期限，以便 Lambda 函数异步运行。
options.C: 将 API 网关超时值更改为与 Lambda 函数超时值一致。部署 API 网关阶段以应用更改。
options.D: 修改 API 网关路由，在集成请求中添加一个 X-Amz-Target 标头，其静态值为“Async”。部署 API 网关阶段以应用更改。

zh.explanation:
# API Gateway 异步 Lambda 调用

## 场景
UI 调用 API Gateway 端点，触发 Lambda 函数启动 Step Functions 工作流来处理大型/复杂文件。由于处理需要很长时间，同步 API 调用经常超过 API Gateway 集成超时（REST API 最大 29 秒）。UI 需要立即获得响应（以便显示"处理中"消息），后端将在完成后通过 SES 向用户发送电子邮件。

修复方案是在 API Gateway 集成层使 Lambda 调用**异步化**，以便 API Gateway 立即返回（HTTP 202），而不必等待 Lambda 完成。

## 正确答案：A
在集成请求中添加 `X-Amz-Invocation-Type` 标头，其静态值为 `'Event'`，然后重新部署阶段。

您可以通过指定 `'Event'` 作为 Lambda 调用类型，将 Lambda 函数配置为 Lambda 非代理集成异步调用。这是通过在集成请求中添加值为 `'Event'` 的 X-Amz-Invocation-Type 标头来完成的。

当调用类型为 `Event` 时，异步 Lambda 调用允许快速响应返回（例如 202 Accepted），同时允许 Lambda 继续运行。如果您希望启动一个运行时间超过 API GW 30 秒超时的 Lambda，这是理想的选择。

OpenAPI 片段示例：
```json
"x-amazon-apigateway-integration": {
  "type": "aws",
  "httpMethod": "POST",
  "uri": "arn:aws:apigateway:us-east-2:lambda:path/2015-03-31/functions/arn:aws:lambda:us-east-2:123456789012:function:my-function/invocations",
  "requestParameters": {
    "integration.request.header.X-Amz-Invocation-Type": "'Event'"
  }
}
```

Lambda 函数随后启动 Step Functions 执行，当处理完成时，向用户发送 SES 电子邮件。

## 为什么其他选项错误

- **B. 配置 Lambda 的最大事件年龄** – 最大事件年龄是 Lambda 异步调用队列的属性（已异步事件在被丢弃之前可在队列中保留多长时间）。它**不会**将同步 API Gateway → Lambda 调用变为异步调用。同步超时问题将继续存在。

- **C. 匹配 API Gateway 超时和 Lambda 超时** – API Gateway REST API 集成超时上限为 29 秒（HTTP API 默认为 30 秒），而 Lambda 可以运行最长 15 分钟。您无法将 API Gateway 的集成超时提高到与 Lambda 匹配，即使可以，UI 仍然无法获得立即响应。

- **D. `X-Amz-Target` 标头值为 `'Async'`** – 此标头/值组合**不存在**于 Lambda Invoke API 中。Lambda Invoke API 使用 `X-Amz-Invocation-Type`，其值为 `Event`（异步）、`RequestResponse`（同步）或 `DryRun`。`X-Amz-Target` 由其他 AWS 服务 JSON RPC API 使用，但不用于将 Lambda 切换为异步模式。此选项是虚构的。

## 参考资源
- [设置后端 Lambda 函数的异步调用](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/set-up-lambda-integration-async.html)
- [从 API Gateway 异步调用 Lambda 函数 (re:Post)](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/api-gateway-invoke-lambda)
- [Lambda Invoke API – InvocationType](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/API_Invoke.html)

en.question: A developer has an application that is composed of many different AWS Lambda functions. The Lambda functions all use some of the same dependencies. To avoid security issues, the developer is constantly updating the dependencies of all of the Lambda functions. The result is duplicated effort for each function. How can the developer keep the dependencies of the Lambda functions up to date with the LEAST additional complexity?

options.A: Define a maintenance window for the Lambda functions to ensure that the functions get updated copies of the dependencies.
options.B: Upgrade the Lambda functions to the most recent runtime version.
options.C: Define a Lambda layer that contains all of the shared dependencies.
options.D: Use an AWS CodeCommit repository to host the dependencies in a centralized location.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

The developer manages many Lambda functions that share common dependencies (e.g., libraries). To address security issues, those dependencies must be updated frequently. Currently, each function has its own copy of the dependencies, requiring duplicated update effort across all functions. The goal is to keep dependencies updated with the **least additional complexity**.

## Correct Answer: C — Define a Lambda layer that contains all of the shared dependencies

A Lambda **layer** is a `.zip` archive that holds libraries, custom runtimes, or other dependencies. To share dependencies across multiple functions, after you create a layer, you can apply it to any number of functions in your account. Without layers, you need to include the same dependencies in each individual deployment package.

When dependencies need a security update, the developer simply publishes a new version of the layer and points the functions at the new version, instead of rebuilding and redeploying every function's package. Layers are versioned. The content of each layer version is immutable. The owner of a layer can release new layer versions to provide updated content. You can use the console to update the layer version attached to your functions.

This perfectly matches "share common dependencies across multiple Lambda functions" with minimal extra complexity. See [Managing Lambda dependencies with layers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/chapter-layers.html).

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A. Define a maintenance window for the Lambda functions** — Lambda is fully managed and serverless; it has **no concept of a "maintenance window"** that the developer can configure to refresh function dependencies. Maintenance windows exist for services like RDS or Systems Manager, not for Lambda function code/dependency updates. This option does not exist as an AWS feature for this purpose.

- **B. Upgrade the Lambda functions to the most recent runtime version** — Updating the Lambda *runtime* (e.g., Node.js 18 → 20, Python 3.11 → 3.12) only updates the language runtime/standard library managed by AWS. It does **not** update the third-party application dependencies that the developer bundles in their deployment package. This wouldn't solve the duplicated-dependency-update problem.

- **D. Use an AWS CodeCommit repository to host the dependencies in a centralized location** — While CodeCommit can store source code centrally, Lambda does **not** load dependencies at runtime from a Git repository. The developer would still need to rebuild and redeploy each function's deployment package whenever the repo changes, so the duplicated effort and complexity remain. This is more complex than using a native Lambda layer (which is purpose-built for this exact use case). Lambda layers allow you to extract code from a Lambda function that can then be re-used across several Lambda functions. Building only Lambda layers can benefit you in a few ways. It can help you reduce the size of your deployment packages, separate core function logic from dependencies, and allow you to share dependencies across multiple functions.

## Reference

- [Managing Lambda dependencies with layers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/chapter-layers.html)
- [Adding layers to functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/adding-layers.html)
- [Packaging your layer content](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/packaging-layers.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员的应用程序由许多不同的 AWS Lambda 函数组成。这些 Lambda 函数都使用一些相同的依赖项。为了避免安全问题，开发人员需要不断更新所有 Lambda 函数的依赖项。这导致每个函数都需要重复工作。开发人员如何才能以最小的额外复杂性来保持 Lambda 函数依赖项的最新状态？

options.A: 为 Lambda 函数定义维护窗口，以确保函数获得依赖项的更新副本。
options.B: 将 Lambda 函数升级到最新运行时版本。
options.C: 定义一个包含所有共享依赖项的 Lambda 层。
options.D: 使用 AWS CodeCommit 存储库将依赖项托管在集中位置。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

开发人员管理许多共享共同依赖项（例如库）的 Lambda 函数。为了解决安全问题，这些依赖项必须经常更新。目前，每个函数都有自己的依赖项副本，需要在所有函数中进行重复的更新工作。目标是以**最小的额外复杂性**保持依赖项更新。

## 正确答案：C — 定义包含所有共享依赖项的 Lambda 层

Lambda **层**是一个包含库、自定义运行时或其他依赖项的 `.zip` 存档。要在多个函数之间共享依赖项，创建层后，可以将其应用于帐户中的任意数量的函数。如果不使用层，需要在每个部署包中包含相同的依赖项。

当依赖项需要安全更新时，开发人员只需发布层的新版本，并将函数指向新版本，而不是重新构建和重新部署每个函数的包。层是有版本的。每个层版本的内容是不可变的。层的所有者可以发布新的层版本以提供更新的内容。您可以使用控制台更新附加到函数的层版本。

这完美地匹配了"在多个 Lambda 函数之间共享共同依赖项"且复杂性最小。请参阅 [Managing Lambda dependencies with layers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/chapter-layers.html)。

## 其他选项为什么错误

- **A. 为 Lambda 函数定义维护窗口** — Lambda 是完全托管的无服务器服务，**没有开发人员可以配置的"维护窗口"**的概念来刷新函数依赖项。维护窗口存在于 RDS 或 Systems Manager 等服务，而不是 Lambda 函数代码/依赖项更新。此选项不作为 AWS 功能存在以实现此目的。

- **B. 将 Lambda 函数升级到最新的运行时版本** — 更新 Lambda *运行时*（例如 Node.js 18 → 20、Python 3.11 → 3.12）仅更新由 AWS 管理的语言运行时/标准库。它**不会**更新开发人员在其部署包中捆绑的第三方应用程序依赖项。这无法解决重复的依赖项更新问题。

- **D. 使用 AWS CodeCommit 存储库在中央位置托管依赖项** — 虽然 CodeCommit 可以集中存储源代码，但 Lambda **不会**在运行时从 Git 存储库加载依赖项。开发人员仍然需要在存储库更改时重新构建和重新部署每个函数的部署包，因此重复的工作和复杂性仍然存在。这比使用为此用例设计的本地 Lambda 层更复杂。Lambda 层允许您从 Lambda 函数中提取可跨多个 Lambda 函数重用的代码。仅构建 Lambda 层可以通过多种方式使您受益。它可以帮助您减少部署包的大小、将核心函数逻辑与依赖项分离，并允许您在多个函数之间共享依赖项。

## 参考

- [Managing Lambda dependencies with layers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/chapter-layers.html)
- [Adding layers to functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/adding-layers.html)
- [Packaging your layer content](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/packaging-layers.html)

en.question: A mobile app stores blog posts in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Millions of posts are added every day, and each post represents a single item in the table. The mobile app requires only recent posts. Any post that is older than 48 hours can be removed. What is the MOST cost-effective way to delete posts that are older than 48 hours?

options.A: For each item, add a new attribute of type String that has a timestamp that is set to the blog post creation time. Create a script to find old posts with a table scan and remove posts that are older than 48 hours by using the BatchWriteItem API operation. Schedule a cron job on an Amazon EC2 instance once an hour to start the script.
options.B: For each item, add a new attribute of type String that has a timestamp that is set to the blog post creation time. Create a script to find old posts with a table scan and remove posts that are older than 48 hours by using the BatchWriteItem API operation. Place the script in a container image. Schedule an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task on AWS Fargate that invokes the container every 5 minutes.
options.C: For each item, add a new attribute of type Date that has a timestamp that is set to 48 hours after the blog post creation time. Create a global secondary index (GSI) that uses the new attribute as a sort key. Create an AWS Lambda function that references the GSI and removes expired items by using the BatchWriteItem API operation. Schedule the function with an Amazon CloudWatch event every minute.
options.D: For each item, add a new attribute of type Number that has a timestamp that is set to 48 hours after the blog post creation time. Configure the DynamoDB table with a TTL that references the new attribute.

en.explanation:
# Cost-Effective Deletion of Old DynamoDB Items

## Scenario
A mobile app stores millions of blog posts per day in DynamoDB. Posts older than 48 hours can be deleted. The question asks for the **MOST cost-effective** way to delete these old items.

## Correct Answer: D

Use DynamoDB's built-in **Time to Live (TTL)** feature. Add a Number attribute to each item containing the expiration time (creation time + 48 hours) as a Unix epoch timestamp in seconds, then enable TTL on the table referencing that attribute.

Key reasons this is most cost-effective:
- DynamoDB automatically deletes expired items within a few days of their expiration time, without consuming write throughput.
- TTL doesn't incur any additional costs.
- To use TTL, first enable it on a table and then define a specific attribute to store the TTL expiration timestamp. The timestamp must be stored as a Number data type in Unix epoch format (seconds).
- No custom code, scheduled jobs, scans, GSIs, or extra compute resources are needed.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

### Option A — EC2 cron + Scan + BatchWriteItem
- A full table **Scan** on a table receiving millions of new items per day is extremely expensive in **read capacity units** (Scan reads every item).
- **BatchWriteItem** deletes consume **write capacity units** for every deletion, unlike TTL which is free.
- An always-on EC2 instance adds compute cost just to run a cron job.
- Far more expensive and operationally complex than TTL.

### Option B — ECS Fargate task every 5 minutes + Scan + BatchWriteItem
- Same Scan + BatchWriteItem cost problems as A (RCU/WCU consumption on a huge table).
- Running a Fargate task every 5 minutes adds continuous compute charges.
- Still requires custom code and container management — not cost-effective compared to the free, native TTL feature.

### Option C — GSI + Lambda every minute + BatchWriteItem
- Adding a **Global Secondary Index** duplicates data and consumes additional **storage and write capacity** for every item written to the base table — very costly at millions of items/day.
- BatchWriteItem deletions still consume WCU on both the base table and the GSI.
- Lambda invocations every minute add compute cost.
- Also, the TTL attribute itself does not need to be a "Date" type — TTL attribute value must be of DynamoDB Number data type.
- Strictly more expensive than D, which achieves the same outcome with zero added infrastructure.

## Implementation Sketch for D

```python
import time, boto3
dynamodb = boto3.client('dynamodb')

# Enable TTL once on the table
dynamodb.update_time_to_live(
    TableName='BlogPosts',
    TimeToLiveSpecification={'Enabled': True, 'AttributeName': 'expireAt'}
)

# When inserting a post:
expire_at = int(time.time()) + 48 * 3600  # 48 hours from now, epoch seconds
```

## References
- [Using time to live (TTL) in DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/TTL.html)
- [Enable time to live (TTL) in DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/time-to-live-ttl-how-to.html)
- [Troubleshoot expired TTL not deleted](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/dynamodb-expired-ttl-not-deleted)

zh.question: 一款移动应用将博客文章存储在 Amazon DynamoDB 表中。每天都会添加数百万篇帖子，每篇帖子在表中对应一个条目。该移动应用只需要最新的帖子。任何超过 48 小时的帖子都将被删除。删除超过 48 小时的帖子最经济高效的方法是什么？

options.A: 为每个条目添加一个字符串类型的新属性，该属性的时间戳设置为博文的创建时间。创建一个脚本，通过表扫描查找旧博文，并使用 BatchWriteItem API 操作删除超过 48 小时的博文。在 Amazon EC2 实例上设置一个定时任务，每小时运行一次该脚本。
options.B: 为每个条目添加一个字符串类型的新属性，该属性的时间戳设置为博文的创建时间。创建一个脚本，通过表扫描查找旧博文，并使用 BatchWriteItem API 操作删除超过 48 小时的博文。将该脚本放置在容器镜像中。在 AWS Fargate 上安排一个 Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) 任务，每 5 分钟调用一次该容器。
options.C: 对于每个条目，添加一个日期类型的新属性，该属性的时间戳设置为博文创建时间后 48 小时。创建一个全局二级索引 (GSI)，并将该新属性用作排序键。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数，该函数引用 GSI 并使用 BatchWriteItem API 操作删除过期条目。将该函数设置为每分钟通过 Amazon CloudWatch 事件进行调度。
options.D: 对于每个条目，添加一个类型为“数字”的新属性，该属性的时间戳设置为博文创建时间后 48 小时。配置 DynamoDB 表，使其 TTL 值引用该新属性。

zh.explanation:
# DynamoDB 旧项目的成本效益删除

## 场景
一个移动应用每天在 DynamoDB 中存储数百万篇博文。超过 48 小时的帖子可以被删除。该问题要求找到**最具成本效益**的方式来删除这些旧项目。

## 正确答案：D

使用 DynamoDB 内置的 **Time to Live (TTL)** 功能。为每个项目添加一个 Number 属性，包含过期时间（创建时间 + 48 小时）作为 Unix 时间戳（秒），然后在表上启用 TTL 并引用该属性。

这是最具成本效益的关键原因：
- DynamoDB 会在项目过期后的几天内自动删除过期项目，不消耗写吞吐量。
- TTL 不产生任何额外成本。
- 要使用 TTL，首先在表上启用它，然后定义一个特定属性来存储 TTL 过期时间戳。时间戳必须存储为 Number 数据类型，格式为 Unix 时间戳（秒）。
- 不需要自定义代码、计划作业、扫描、GSI 或额外的计算资源。

## 其他选项为何错误

### 选项 A — EC2 cron + Scan + BatchWriteItem
- 在每天接收数百万个新项目的表上进行完整的 **Scan** 在**读容量单位** (RCU) 上成本极高（Scan 读取每个项目）。
- **BatchWriteItem** 删除会为每次删除消耗**写容量单位**，不像 TTL 是免费的。
- 始终运行的 EC2 实例仅为了运行 cron 作业就增加了计算成本。
- 比 TTL 的成本高得多，在运维上也更复杂。

### 选项 B — ECS Fargate 任务每 5 分钟运行一次 + Scan + BatchWriteItem
- 与 A 相同的 Scan + BatchWriteItem 成本问题（在大型表上消耗 RCU/WCU）。
- 每 5 分钟运行一次 Fargate 任务会产生持续的计算费用。
- 仍然需要自定义代码和容器管理——与免费的原生 TTL 功能相比成本效益不佳。

### 选项 C — GSI + Lambda 每分钟运行一次 + BatchWriteItem
- 添加**全局二级索引**会复制数据，并为写入基础表的每个项目消耗额外的**存储和写容量**——在每天数百万项目的情况下成本非常高。
- BatchWriteItem 删除仍然会在基础表和 GSI 上消耗 WCU。
- 每分钟调用 Lambda 会增加计算成本。
- 另外，TTL 属性本身不需要是"Date"类型——TTL 属性值必须是 DynamoDB Number 数据类型。
- 严格来说比 D 更昂贵，而 D 用零额外基础设施实现了相同的结果。

## 选项 D 的实现示例

```python
import time, boto3
dynamodb = boto3.client('dynamodb')

# 在表上启用一次 TTL
dynamodb.update_time_to_live(
    TableName='BlogPosts',
    TimeToLiveSpecification={'Enabled': True, 'AttributeName': 'expireAt'}
)

# 插入帖子时：
expire_at = int(time.time()) + 48 * 3600  # 从现在起 48 小时，时间戳秒数
```

## 参考资源
- [Using time to live (TTL) in DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/TTL.html)
- [Enable time to live (TTL) in DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/time-to-live-ttl-how-to.html)
- [Troubleshoot expired TTL not deleted](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/dynamodb-expired-ttl-not-deleted)

en.question: A developer is modifying an existing AWS Lambda function. While checking the code, the developer notices hardcoded parameter values for an Amazon RDS for SQL Server user name, password, database, host, and port. There are also hardcoded parameter values for an Amazon DynamoDB table, an Amazon S3 bucket, and an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. The developer wants to securely store the parameter values outside the code in an encrypted format and wants to turn on rotation for the credentials. The developer also wants to be able to reuse the parameter values from other applications and to update the parameter values without modifying code. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create an RDS database secret in AWS Secrets Manager. Set the user name, password, database, host, and port. Turn on secret rotation. Create encrypted Lambda environment variables for the DynamoDB table, S3 bucket, and SNS topic.
options.B: Create an RDS database secret in AWS Secrets Manager. Set the user name, password, database, host, and port. Turn on secret rotation. Create SecureString parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store for the DynamoDB table, S3 bucket, and SNS topic.
options.C: Create RDS database parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store for the user name, password, database, host, and port. Create encrypted Lambda environment variables for the DynamoDB table, S3 bucket, and SNS topic. Create a Lambda function and set the logic for the credentials rotation task. Schedule the credentials rotation task in Amazon EventBridge.
options.D: Create RDS database parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store for the user name, password, database, host, and port. Store the DynamoDB table, S3 bucket, and SNS topic in Amazon S3. Create a Lambda function and set the logic for the credentials rotation. Invoke the Lambda function on a schedule.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A Lambda function has hardcoded values for:
- **RDS for SQL Server credentials** (username, password, database, host, port) — these are sensitive and need **rotation**.
- **Non-secret configuration values** — DynamoDB table name, S3 bucket name, SNS topic ARN.

The developer wants:
1. Values stored **outside the code**, **encrypted**.
2. **Credential rotation** enabled.
3. **Reusability** by other applications.
4. Ability to **update without modifying code**.
5. **Least operational overhead**.

## Correct Answer: B

**AWS Secrets Manager** is purpose-built for database credentials. Secrets Manager was designed specifically for sensitive credentials such as database passwords and can be used to replicate secrets to other AWS Regions and rotate passwords automatically based on a configurable schedule. It has a native RDS secret type that captures username, password, engine, host, port, and dbname in one secret, and provides built-in (managed) rotation Lambdas — no custom rotation code to maintain. The service includes built-in rotation capabilities for common databases like RDS, DocumentDB, and Redshift. You can also implement custom rotation logic using Lambda functions. Secrets Manager handles the complexity of updating credentials without causing application downtime.

For the non-secret config (DynamoDB table, S3 bucket, SNS topic), **Systems Manager Parameter Store SecureString** parameters are ideal: encrypted with KMS, centrally accessible, reusable across applications, updatable without code changes, and lower cost than Secrets Manager. You can use the SecureString parameter type for textual data that you want to encrypt, such as passwords, application secrets, confidential configuration data, or any other types of data that you want to protect. SecureString data is encrypted and decrypted using an AWS KMS key. Feature flags, app config, non-rotating bootstrap values, and anything read thousands of times per second at container start belong in Parameter Store SecureString.

This combination meets every requirement with minimal operational overhead because rotation is managed by AWS, and parameters are centrally stored, encrypted, and reusable across applications.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A. Lambda environment variables for DynamoDB/S3/SNS values.** Environment variables are scoped to a single Lambda function — they **cannot be reused by other applications** without duplication, violating the reusability requirement. Updating them also requires modifying the Lambda configuration per function.

- **C. Parameter Store for RDS credentials + custom rotation Lambda + EventBridge schedule.** This puts a high operational burden on the developer: you must write, test, and maintain the entire 4-step rotation logic yourself. To implement password rotation lifecycles, use AWS Secrets Manager. You can rotate, manage, and retrieve database credentials, API keys, and other secrets throughout their lifecycle using Secrets Manager. Parameter Store has no native rotation, and Lambda env variables again break reusability.

- **D. Storing the DynamoDB table, S3 bucket, and SNS topic "in Amazon S3"** is nonsensical for configuration values — S3 is not a configuration store, has no encrypted parameter API, and offers no clean integration pattern. The custom rotation Lambda also adds unnecessary overhead compared with Secrets Manager managed rotation.

## References
- [AWS Secrets Manager – Rotate secrets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotating-secrets.html)
- [AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.html)
- [Choosing between Secrets Manager and Parameter Store](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/how-to-choose-the-right-aws-service-for-managing-secrets-and-configurations/)

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在修改现有的 AWS Lambda 函数。在检查代码时，他发现 Amazon RDS for SQL Server 的用户名、密码、数据库、主机和端口等参数值是硬编码的。此外，Amazon DynamoDB 表、Amazon S3 存储桶和 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题的参数值也是硬编码的。开发人员希望将这些参数值以加密格式安全地存储在代码外部，并启用凭证轮换。他还希望能够从其他应用程序重用这些参数值，并且无需修改代码即可更新这些参数值。哪种解决方案能够以最小的运维开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 在 AWS Secrets Manager 中创建 RDS 数据库密钥。设置用户名、密码、数据库、主机和端口。启用密钥轮换。为 DynamoDB 表、S3 存储桶和 SNS 主题创建加密的 Lambda 环境变量。
options.B: 在 AWS Secrets Manager 中创建 RDS 数据库密钥。设置用户名、密码、数据库、主机和端口。启用密钥轮换。在 AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store 中为 DynamoDB 表、S3 存储桶和 SNS 主题创建 SecureString 参数。
options.C: 在 AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store 中创建 RDS 数据库参数，包括用户名、密码、数据库、主机和端口。为 DynamoDB 表、S3 存储桶和 SNS 主题创建加密的 Lambda 环境变量。创建 Lambda 函数并设置凭证轮换任务的逻辑。在 Amazon EventBridge 中调度凭证轮换任务。
options.D: 在 AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store 中创建 RDS 数据库参数，包括用户名、密码、数据库、主机和端口。将 DynamoDB 表、S3 存储桶和 SNS 主题存储在 Amazon S3 中。创建一个 Lambda 函数并设置凭证轮换逻辑。按计划调用该 Lambda 函数。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

一个 Lambda 函数对以下内容进行了硬编码：
- **RDS for SQL Server 凭证**（用户名、密码、数据库、主机、端口）— 这些是敏感信息，需要**轮换**。
- **非机密配置值** — DynamoDB 表名、S3 存储桶名、SNS 主题 ARN。

开发者需要：
1. 值存储在**代码之外**，**加密**。
2. **启用凭证轮换**。
3. **可由其他应用程序重复使用**。
4. 能够**无需修改代码即可更新**。
5. **最少的运维开销**。

## 正确答案：B

**AWS Secrets Manager** 是专为数据库凭证设计的。Secrets Manager 是专门为数据库密码等敏感凭证而设计的，可用于将机密复制到其他 AWS 区域，并根据可配置的计划自动轮换密码。它拥有本机 RDS 机密类型，可在一个机密中捕获用户名、密码、引擎、主机、端口和数据库名，并提供内置（托管）轮换 Lambda — 无需维护自定义轮换代码。该服务包括对 RDS、DocumentDB 和 Redshift 等常见数据库的内置轮换功能。您还可以使用 Lambda 函数实现自定义轮换逻辑。Secrets Manager 处理更新凭证而不会导致应用程序停机的复杂性。

对于非机密配置（DynamoDB 表、S3 存储桶、SNS 主题），**Systems Manager Parameter Store SecureString** 参数是理想选择：使用 KMS 加密、集中式可访问、可在应用程序间重复使用、无需代码更改即可更新，且成本低于 Secrets Manager。您可以使用 SecureString 参数类型来处理想要加密的文本数据，例如密码、应用程序机密、机密配置数据或任何其他想要保护的数据类型。SecureString 数据使用 AWS KMS 密钥进行加密和解密。功能标志、应用配置、非轮换引导值以及在容器启动时每秒读取数千次的任何内容都应位于 Parameter Store SecureString 中。

这种组合满足所有要求，运维开销最少，因为轮换由 AWS 管理，参数集中存储、加密，并可在应用程序间重复使用。

## 其他选项为何不正确

- **A. Lambda 环境变量用于 DynamoDB/S3/SNS 值。** 环境变量的作用域限于单个 Lambda 函数 — 它们**无法由其他应用程序重复使用**而不会造成重复，违反了可重复使用的要求。更新它们还需要按函数修改 Lambda 配置。

- **C. Parameter Store 用于 RDS 凭证 + 自定义轮换 Lambda + EventBridge 计划。** 这给开发者带来了很高的运维负担：您必须自己编写、测试和维护整个 4 步轮换逻辑。要实现密码轮换生命周期，请使用 AWS Secrets Manager。您可以使用 Secrets Manager 在整个生命周期中轮换、管理和检索数据库凭证、API 密钥和其他机密。Parameter Store 没有本机轮换功能，而 Lambda 环境变量再次破坏了可重复使用性。

- **D. 将 DynamoDB 表、S3 存储桶和 SNS 主题"存储在 Amazon S3 中"** 对于配置值没有意义 — S3 不是配置存储，没有加密参数 API，也不提供干净的集成模式。自定义轮换 Lambda 相比 Secrets Manager 托管轮换也增加了不必要的开销。

## 参考资源
- [AWS Secrets Manager – 轮换机密](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotating-secrets.html)
- [AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.html)
- [在 Secrets Manager 和 Parameter Store 之间进行选择](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/how-to-choose-the-right-aws-service-for-managing-secrets-and-configurations/)

en.question: A developer accesses AWS CodeCommit over SSH. The SSH keys configured to access AWS CodeCommit are tied to a user with the following permissions: The developer needs to create/delete branches. Which specific IAM permissions need to be added, based on the principle of least privilege?

options.A: "codecommit:CreateBranch" "codecommit:DeleteBranch"
options.B: "codecommit:Put*"
options.C: "codecommit:Update*"
options.D: "codecommit:*"

en.explanation:
# CodeCommit IAM Permissions for Branch Create/Delete

## Scenario
A developer accesses CodeCommit over SSH and needs the ability to **create** and **delete branches**. The question asks which IAM permissions to add following the **principle of least privilege**.

## Correct Answer: A — `codecommit:CreateBranch` and `codecommit:DeleteBranch`

CodeCommit defines specific, granular IAM actions that map 1:1 to API operations. For branch management, the dedicated actions are `CreateBranch` and `DeleteBranch`. The DeleteBranch permission applies to actions performed with the console, the AWS CLI, the SDKs, and the API, but not the Git protocol.

These permissions appear in the AWS-published example policies as the canonical actions used to allow/deny branch creation and deletion (see the customer managed policy examples that explicitly list `codecommit:CreateBranch` and `codecommit:DeleteBranch`). Granting only these two satisfies the **least-privilege** requirement.

Example IAM statement:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "codecommit:CreateBranch",
        "codecommit:DeleteBranch"
      ],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:codecommit:us-east-1:111122223333:MyDemoRepo"
    }
  ]
}
```

> Note: Because the developer is using SSH (Git protocol), they would also need `codecommit:GitPush` to actually push the new/deleted branch reference to the remote, but among the four answer options provided, only A names the specific branch‑management API permissions required, and it is the only least-privilege choice.

## Why the other options are wrong

- **B. `codecommit:Put*`** — The `Put*` wildcard covers actions like `PutFile`, `PutCommentReaction`, `PutRepositoryTriggers`, etc. It does **not** match `CreateBranch` or `DeleteBranch` (those start with `Create`/`Delete`, not `Put`). It grants the wrong permissions and still misses what is needed.

- **C. `codecommit:Update*`** — Update actions cover things like `UpdateDefaultBranch`, `UpdatePullRequestTitle`, `UpdateRepositoryDescription`, etc. Neither `CreateBranch` nor `DeleteBranch` begins with `Update`, so this wildcard does not authorize the required operations.

- **D. `codecommit:*`** — Grants every CodeCommit action, including destructive ones like `DeleteRepository`. You can attach the AWSCodeCommitFullAccess policy to your IAM identities. This policy grants full access to CodeCommit. Apply this policy only to administrative-level users to whom you want to grant full control over CodeCommit repositories and related resources in your Amazon Web Services account, including the ability to delete repositories. This clearly violates the **principle of least privilege**.

## References
- [CodeCommit permissions reference – Permissions for actions on branches](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/auth-and-access-control-permissions-reference.html)
- [Customer managed policy examples for CodeCommit](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/customer-managed-policies.html)
- [AWS managed policies for CodeCommit](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/security-iam-awsmanpol.html)

zh.question: 开发人员通过 SSH 访问 AWS CodeCommit。用于访问 AWS CodeCommit 的 SSH 密钥已配置给一个具有以下权限的用户：开发人员需要创建/删除分支。根据最小权限原则，需要添加哪些特定的 IAM 权限？

options.A: “codecommit:CreateBranch” “codecommit:DeleteBranch”
options.B: “codecommit:Put*”
options.C: “codecommit:Update*”
options.D: “codecommit:*”

zh.explanation:
# CodeCommit IAM 权限用于分支创建/删除

## 场景
开发人员通过 SSH 访问 CodeCommit，需要能够**创建**和**删除分支**。问题要求根据**最小权限原则**添加哪些 IAM 权限。

## 正确答案：A — `codecommit:CreateBranch` 和 `codecommit:DeleteBranch`

CodeCommit 定义了特定的粒度级 IAM 操作，与 API 操作一一对应。对于分支管理，专用操作是 `CreateBranch` 和 `DeleteBranch`。DeleteBranch 权限适用于使用控制台、AWS CLI、SDK 和 API 执行的操作，但不适用于 Git 协议。

这些权限出现在 AWS 发布的示例策略中，作为允许/拒绝分支创建和删除的规范操作（参见明确列出 `codecommit:CreateBranch` 和 `codecommit:DeleteBranch` 的客户托管策略示例）。仅授予这两个权限满足**最小权限**要求。

IAM 语句示例：

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "codecommit:CreateBranch",
        "codecommit:DeleteBranch"
      ],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:codecommit:us-east-1:111122223333:MyDemoRepo"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 注意：因为开发人员使用 SSH（Git 协议），他们还需要 `codecommit:GitPush` 才能将新建/删除的分支引用推送到远程，但在提供的四个答案选项中，只有 A 列出了所需的特定分支管理 API 权限，这是唯一满足最小权限的选择。

## 其他选项为什么错误

- **B. `codecommit:Put*`** — `Put*` 通配符覆盖 `PutFile`、`PutCommentReaction`、`PutRepositoryTriggers` 等操作。它**不**匹配 `CreateBranch` 或 `DeleteBranch`（这些操作以 `Create`/`Delete` 开头，而不是 `Put`）。它授予错误的权限，仍然缺少所需的权限。

- **C. `codecommit:Update*`** — Update 操作涵盖 `UpdateDefaultBranch`、`UpdatePullRequestTitle`、`UpdateRepositoryDescription` 等。`CreateBranch` 和 `DeleteBranch` 都不以 `Update` 开头，因此此通配符不授予所需的操作权限。

- **D. `codecommit:*`** — 授予所有 CodeCommit 操作权限，包括 `DeleteRepository` 等破坏性操作。您可以将 AWSCodeCommitFullAccess 策略附加到您的 IAM 身份。此策略授予对 CodeCommit 的完全访问权限。仅将此策略应用于要授予其对 Amazon Web Services 账户中的 CodeCommit 存储库和相关资源的完全控制权的管理级别用户，包括删除存储库的权限。 这清楚地违反了**最小权限原则**。

## 参考资源
- [CodeCommit 权限参考 – 分支操作权限](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/auth-and-access-control-permissions-reference.html)
- [CodeCommit 的客户托管策略示例](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/customer-managed-policies.html)
- [CodeCommit 的 AWS 托管策略](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/security-iam-awsmanpol.html)

en.question: An application that is deployed to Amazon EC2 is using Amazon DynamoDB. The application calls the DynamoDB REST API. Periodically, the application receives a ProvisionedThroughputExceededException error when the application writes to a DynamoDB table. Which solutions will mitigate this error MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)

options.A: Modify the application code to perform exponential backoff when the error is received.
options.B: Modify the application to use the AWS SDKs for DynamoDB.
options.C: Increase the read and write throughput of the DynamoDB table.
options.D: Create a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster for the DynamoDB table.
options.E: Create a second DynamoDB table. Distribute the reads and writes between the two tables.

en.explanation:
# DynamoDB ProvisionedThroughputExceededException — Cost-Effective Mitigation

## Scenario
An EC2-hosted application calls the **DynamoDB REST API directly** and periodically receives `ProvisionedThroughputExceededException` on writes. The question asks for the **two most cost-effective** mitigations.

The key clues are:
- The error is **periodic** (occasional spikes), not constant — so the table capacity is generally adequate.
- The application uses **raw REST API** calls instead of an AWS SDK.
- The solution must be **cost-effective** (avoid simply paying for more capacity).

## Correct Answers: A and B

### A. Implement exponential backoff
When DynamoDB throttles a read or write, it returns a ProvisionedThroughputExceededException to the caller. The application can then take appropriate action, such as waiting for a short interval before retrying the request. Each AWS SDK implements an exponential backoff algorithm for better flow control. The concept behind exponential backoff is to use progressively longer waits between retries for consecutive error responses. For example, up to 50 milliseconds before the first retry, up to 100 milliseconds before the second, up to 200 milliseconds before third, and so on. This smooths out periodic spikes without provisioning extra (paid) capacity — making it the most cost-effective fix.

### B. Use the AWS SDKs for DynamoDB
The AWS SDKs implement automatic retry logic and exponential backoff. The Amazon Web Services SDKs for DynamoDB automatically retry requests that receive this exception. Your request is eventually successful, unless your retry queue is too large to finish. Reduce the frequency of requests and use exponential backoff. Because the application is calling the raw REST API today, simply switching to an AWS SDK gives you the built-in retry/backoff behavior for free — at no additional AWS cost.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

### C. Increase read/write throughput on the table — INCORRECT
While this would mitigate the exception, it is **explicitly not cost-effective**: you pay continuously for higher provisioned RCU/WCU even though throttling only happens "periodically." "just increase the provisioned capacity" isn't always the right answer - sometimes the problem is deeper than that. The question asks for the *most cost-effective* approach, which is to handle the transient throttling via retries first.

### D. Create a DAX cluster — INCORRECT
DAX is an **in-memory read cache**. It does not help with **write** throttling (writes still pass through to the underlying table and consume WCU). The question explicitly states the throttling occurs on writes. DAX also adds significant cost (per-node hourly billing), violating the cost-effectiveness requirement. See [DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html).

### E. Create a second table and split traffic — INCORRECT
This doubles operational complexity, breaks data consistency/queries, and doubles base provisioned capacity costs. The proper way to distribute load within DynamoDB is to design a good partition key — not to manually shard across two tables. It is neither simple nor cost-effective.

## Reference Pattern (Python boto3)
```python
import boto3
from botocore.config import Config

config = Config(
    retries={
        'max_attempts': 10,
        'mode': 'adaptive'   # built-in exponential backoff + adaptive throttling
    }
)
dynamodb = boto3.resource('dynamodb', config=config)
```

## Documentation
- [Error handling with DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Programming.Errors.html)
- [Error retries and exponential backoff in AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/api-retries.html)
- [DynamoDB throttling – AWS re:Post](https://repost.aws/questions/QUXmOaxmt3SEiRsHrAbqvgVQ/dynamodb-throttling)

**Final Answer: A and B**

zh.question: 部署在 Amazon EC2 上的应用程序正在使用 Amazon DynamoDB。该应用程序调用 DynamoDB REST API。当应用程序写入 DynamoDB 表时，会周期性地收到 ProvisionedThroughputExceededException 错误。哪些解决方案能够以最具成本效益的方式缓解此错误？（选择两项。）

options.A: 修改应用程序代码，以便在收到错误时执行指数退避。
options.B: 修改应用程序以使用适用于 DynamoDB 的 AWS SDK。
options.C: 提高 DynamoDB 表的读取和写入吞吐量。
options.D: 为 DynamoDB 表创建 DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) 集群。
options.E: 创建第二个 DynamoDB 表。将读写操作分配到这两个表中。

zh.explanation:
# DynamoDB ProvisionedThroughputExceededException — 成本有效的缓解方案

## 场景
EC2 托管的应用程序直接调用 **DynamoDB REST API**，周期性地在写入操作中收到 `ProvisionedThroughputExceededException`。问题要求找到**两个最具成本效益**的缓解措施。

关键提示包括：
- 错误是**周期性的**（偶发尖峰），而非持续发生 — 因此表容量通常是充足的。
- 应用程序使用**原始 REST API** 调用，而不是 AWS SDK。
- 解决方案必须**具有成本效益**（避免单纯地为更多容量付费）。

## 正确答案：A 和 B

### A. 实现指数退避
当 DynamoDB 对读取或写入进行限流时，它会向调用方返回 ProvisionedThroughputExceededException。应用程序随后可以采取适当措施，例如在重试请求之前等待短时间间隔。 每个 AWS SDK 都实现了指数退避算法以实现更好的流量控制。指数退避的原理是在连续错误响应的重试之间使用逐步增长的等待时间。例如，第一次重试前最多等待 50 毫秒，第二次前 100 毫秒，第三次前 200 毫秒，以此类推。这种方法可以平滑周期性尖峰，无需配置额外的（付费）容量 — 因此是最具成本效益的解决方案。

### B. 使用 AWS DynamoDB SDK
AWS SDK 实现了自动重试逻辑和指数退避。 Amazon Web Services DynamoDB SDK 会自动重试收到此异常的请求。您的请求最终会成功，除非重试队列太大而无法完成。降低请求频率并使用指数退避。由于应用程序目前调用原始 REST API，只需切换到 AWS SDK 即可免费获得内置的重试/退避行为 — 无需支付额外的 AWS 费用。

## 为什么其他选项错误

### C. 增加表的读/写吞吐量 — 错误
虽然这会缓解异常，但**明确不具成本效益**：即使限流仅"周期性地"发生，您也会持续为更高的配置 RCU/WCU 付费。"只是增加配置容量"并非总是正确答案 - 有时问题比这更深层。问题要求*最具成本效益*的方法，即先通过重试处理暂时性限流。

### D. 创建 DAX 集群 — 错误
DAX 是一个**内存读取缓存**。它对**写入**限流没有帮助（写入仍然传递到底层表并消耗 WCU）。问题明确指出限流发生在写入操作上。DAX 还会增加显著成本（按节点按小时计费），违反成本效益要求。参见 [DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html)。

### E. 创建第二个表并分流 — 错误
这会加倍操作复杂性，破坏数据一致性/查询，并将基本配置容量成本翻倍。在 DynamoDB 中分散负载的正确方法是设计良好的分区键 — 而不是手动跨两个表分片。这既不简单也不具成本效益。

## 参考模式（Python boto3）
```python
import boto3
from botocore.config import Config

config = Config(
    retries={
        'max_attempts': 10,
        'mode': 'adaptive'   # 内置指数退避 + 自适应限流
    }
)
dynamodb = boto3.resource('dynamodb', config=config)
```

## 文档
- [使用 DynamoDB 处理错误](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Programming.Errors.html)
- [AWS 中的错误重试和指数退避](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/api-retries.html)
- [DynamoDB 限流 – AWS re:Post](https://repost.aws/questions/QUXmOaxmt3SEiRsHrAbqvgVQ/dynamodb-throttling)

**最终答案：A 和 B**

en.question: When a developer tries to run an AWS CodeBuild project, it raises an error because the length of all environment variables exceeds the limit for the combined maximum of characters. What is the recommended solution?

options.A: Add the export LC_ALL="en_US.utf8" command to the pre_build section to ensure POSIX localization.
options.B: Use Amazon Cognito to store key-value pairs for large numbers of environment variables.
options.C: Update the settings for the build project to use an Amazon S3 bucket for large numbers of environment variables.
options.D: Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to store large numbers of environment variables.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A developer's AWS CodeBuild project fails to start because the combined length of all environment variables exceeds the allowed character limit. The question asks for the AWS-recommended way to handle a large number of (or large-sized) environment variables in CodeBuild.

## Correct Answer: D — Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store

CodeBuild natively integrates with AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Instead of defining many/long values directly as PLAINTEXT environment variables on the build project (which is subject to character limits and a validation error), you store the values in Parameter Store and reference them in the buildspec or in the project's environment variable configuration with type `PARAMETER_STORE`. PARAMETER_STORE is an environment variable stored in Systems Manager Parameter Store. For environment variables of this type, specify the name of the parameter as the value of the EnvironmentVariable. The parameter value will be substituted for the name at runtime.

The official AWS CodeBuild troubleshooting guidance for "the length of all environment variables exceeds the limit for the combined maximum of characters" recommends using Parameter Store (or Secrets Manager) to off‑load the values. We strongly discourage the use of environment variables to store sensitive values, especially AWS access key IDs. Environment variables can be displayed in plain text using tools such as the CodeBuild console and the AWS CLI. We recommend you store sensitive values in the Amazon EC2 Systems Manager Parameter Store and then retrieve them from your buildspec.

Example buildspec snippet:

```yaml
version: 0.2
env:
  parameter-store:
    DB_PASSWORD: "/myapp/prod/db_password"
    API_KEY: "/myapp/prod/api_key"
phases:
  build:
    commands:
      - echo "Using $DB_PASSWORD"
```

## Why the other options are wrong

- **A. `export LC_ALL="en_US.utf8"` in pre_build** — This sets POSIX locale for character encoding inside the running build container. It has nothing to do with the CodeBuild project's environment-variable character limit, which is enforced by the CodeBuild API/configuration before the container even starts.

- **B. Use Amazon Cognito to store key-value pairs** — Cognito is an identity and user authentication service (user pools / identity pools). It is not a configuration or parameter storage service and CodeBuild has no native integration to load environment variables from Cognito.

- **C. Use an Amazon S3 bucket for environment variables** — CodeBuild does not support an "S3 environment variables" setting on a build project. The valid environment variable types are `PLAINTEXT`, `PARAMETER_STORE`, and `SECRETS_MANAGER` only. A list of maps, that contain the keys 'name', 'value', and 'type' to be used as additional environment variables for the build. Valid types are 'PLAINTEXT', 'PARAMETER_STORE', or 'SECRETS_MANAGER' While you could manually download a config file from S3 in the buildspec, AWS does not offer this as the documented/recommended fix for the environment-variable length error.

## References

- [AWS CodeBuild Troubleshooting](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/troubleshooting.html)
- [Environment variables in build environments (CodeBuild)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/build-env-ref-env-vars.html)
- [CodeBuild API – EnvironmentVariable](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/APIReference/API_EnvironmentVariable.html)
- [AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.html)

zh.question: 当开发人员尝试运行 AWS CodeBuild 项目时，由于所有环境变量的长度超过了字符总数的限制，因此会引发错误。建议的解决方案是什么？

options.A: 在 pre_build 部分添加 export LC_ALL="en_US.utf8" 命令，以确保 POSIX 本地化。
options.B: 使用 Amazon Cognito 存储大量环境变量的键值对。
options.C: 更新构建项目的设置，使其使用 Amazon S3 存储桶来存储大量环境变量。
options.D: 使用 AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store 存储大量环境变量。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

开发人员的 AWS CodeBuild 项目启动失败，因为所有环境变量的总长度超过了允许的字符限制。问题询问在 CodeBuild 中处理大量（或大型）环境变量的 AWS 推荐方式。

## 正确答案：D — 使用 AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store

CodeBuild 原生集成 AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store。与其直接在构建项目上定义许多/长值作为 PLAINTEXT 环境变量（受字符限制和验证错误限制），你可以将值存储在 Parameter Store 中，并在 buildspec 或项目的环境变量配置中以 `PARAMETER_STORE` 类型引用它们。PARAMETER_STORE 是存储在 Systems Manager Parameter Store 中的环境变量。对于此类型的环境变量，指定参数的名称作为 EnvironmentVariable 的值。参数值将在运行时替换该名称。

官方 AWS CodeBuild 故障排除指南对"所有环境变量的长度超过组合字符最大限制"的问题建议使用 Parameter Store（或 Secrets Manager）来卸载这些值。我们强烈不建议使用环境变量存储敏感值，尤其是 AWS 访问密钥 ID。环境变量可以使用 CodeBuild 控制台和 AWS CLI 等工具以纯文本形式显示。我们建议你将敏感值存储在 Amazon EC2 Systems Manager Parameter Store 中，然后从你的 buildspec 中检索它们。

示例 buildspec 片段：

```yaml
version: 0.2
env:
  parameter-store:
    DB_PASSWORD: "/myapp/prod/db_password"
    API_KEY: "/myapp/prod/api_key"
phases:
  build:
    commands:
      - echo "Using $DB_PASSWORD"
```

## 其他选项为什么错误

- **A. 在 pre_build 中执行 `export LC_ALL="en_US.utf8"`** — 这在运行的构建容器内设置 POSIX 区域设置以处理字符编码。它与 CodeBuild 项目的环境变量字符限制无关，该限制由 CodeBuild API/配置在容器启动之前就已强制执行。

- **B. 使用 Amazon Cognito 存储键值对** — Cognito 是身份和用户身份验证服务（用户池/身份池）。它不是配置或参数存储服务，CodeBuild 没有原生集成从 Cognito 加载环境变量。

- **C. 使用 Amazon S3 桶存储环境变量** — CodeBuild 不支持构建项目上的"S3 环境变量"设置。有效的环境变量类型仅为 `PLAINTEXT`、`PARAMETER_STORE` 和 `SECRETS_MANAGER`。包含键"name"、"value"和"type"的映射列表，用作构建的其他环境变量。有效类型为"PLAINTEXT"、"PARAMETER_STORE"或"SECRETS_MANAGER"虽然你可以在 buildspec 中手动从 S3 下载配置文件，但 AWS 未将此作为环境变量长度错误的文档化/推荐修复方案。

## 参考资料

- [AWS CodeBuild 故障排除](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/troubleshooting.html)
- [构建环境中的环境变量 (CodeBuild)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/build-env-ref-env-vars.html)
- [CodeBuild API – EnvironmentVariable](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/APIReference/API_EnvironmentVariable.html)
- [AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.html)

en.question: A company is expanding the compatibility of its photo-sharing mobile app to hundreds of additional devices with unique screen dimensions and resolutions. Photos are stored in Amazon S3 in their original format and resolution. The company uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution to serve the photos. The app includes the dimension and resolution of the display as GET parameters with every request. A developer needs to implement a solution that optimizes the photos that are served to each device to reduce load time and increase photo quality. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Use S3 Batch Operations to invoke an AWS Lambda function to create new variants of the photos with the required dimensions and resolutions. Create a dynamic CloudFront origin that automatically maps the request of each device to the corresponding photo variant.
options.B: Use S3 Batch Operations to invoke an AWS Lambda function to create new variants of the photos with the required dimensions and resolutions. Create a Lambda@Edge function to route requests to the corresponding photo variant by using request headers.
options.C: Create a Lambda@Edge function that optimizes the photos upon request and returns the photos as a response. Change the CloudFront TTL cache policy to the maximum value possible.
options.D: Create a Lambda@Edge function that optimizes the photos upon request and returns the photos as a response. In the same function, store a copy of the processed photos on Amazon S3 for subsequent requests.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A photo-sharing app must serve images optimized for hundreds of unique device dimensions/resolutions. The app supplies the desired dimension and resolution as GET (query) parameters on each request. Photos are stored in S3 in original format and served via CloudFront. The developer needs the MOST cost-effective approach to optimize photos per device.

## Correct Answer: D

Use a **Lambda@Edge** function that, on demand, optimizes (resizes/transcodes) the photo for the requested dimensions and returns it. The same function stores the processed photo back to S3, so subsequent requests for the same variant skip the Lambda transformation and are served directly from S3 (and cached at CloudFront edges).

This is the canonical AWS reference architecture documented in the AWS blog [Resizing Images with Amazon CloudFront & Lambda@Edge](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/resizing-images-with-amazon-cloudfront-lambdaedge-aws-cdn-blog/), which describes exactly this flow: if the resized object exists, proceed with the CloudFront response cycle; if it doesn't exist on S3, fetch the source image, apply the resize transformation, store the resized image back into the S3 bucket with the correct prefix and metadata, and return a binary response using the resized image.

This is cost-effective because:
- Only photos that are actually requested get processed (no wasted compute on unviewed photos).
- Each variant is generated **once**; subsequent requests are served from S3/CloudFront cache. If a resized image is accessed frequently, calculating it once and saving it is cheaper, and is usually the preferred option also from a latency point of view.
- CloudFront also caches the response at edge locations for additional savings.

## Why the other options are wrong

**A. S3 Batch Operations + Lambda to pre-generate every variant + "dynamic CloudFront origin".**
Pre-generating variants for hundreds of device dimensions × every photo wastes Lambda compute and S3 storage on photos that may never be viewed. Additionally, there is no native CloudFront feature called a "dynamic origin that automatically maps requests to photo variants" — that mapping must be implemented with Lambda@Edge or CloudFront Functions, so the described mechanism is fictional/incorrect.

**B. S3 Batch Operations to pre-generate variants + Lambda@Edge to route by request headers.**
Same pre-generation cost problem as A — you generate every variant up front, including ones that will never be accessed, multiplying storage and compute charges. Additionally, the dimension/resolution arrives as **GET (query) parameters**, not request headers, so routing by headers does not match the described request format.

**C. Lambda@Edge optimizes on every request; rely solely on CloudFront max TTL.**
CloudFront caches per edge location, so a cache miss at any of hundreds of edges re-invokes Lambda@Edge to re-process the same image, repeatedly paying compute cost. Cache entries can also be evicted before TTL expires, and CloudFront caches at the edge are not globally shared. If you trigger a Lambda@Edge function from an OriginRequest or OriginResponse, the result can be cached, but only in the nearest Regional Edge Cache, meaning other edges still trigger reprocessing. Storing the processed object back to S3 (option D) avoids re-running the transformation across all edges and over time.

## Reference Architecture Flow

1. Viewer request hits CloudFront with `?w=300&h=400` style parameters.
2. CloudFront cache miss → Lambda@Edge runs.
3. Lambda@Edge checks S3 for an existing variant key; if present, returns it.
4. If absent, Lambda fetches the original from S3, resizes via Sharp/ImageMagick, **PUTs the variant back to S3**, and returns it to the viewer.
5. CloudFront caches the response for subsequent edge-local requests.

## Sources

- [Resizing Images with Amazon CloudFront & Lambda@Edge — AWS Networking & Content Delivery Blog](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/resizing-images-with-amazon-cloudfront-lambdaedge-aws-cdn-blog/)
- [Image Optimization using Amazon CloudFront and AWS Lambda — AWS Blog](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/image-optimization-using-amazon-cloudfront-and-aws-lambda/)
- [AWS re:Post — Cost comparison: pre-resize to S3 vs Lambda@Edge per request](https://repost.aws/questions/QUcLWr0gc9SXC0uhydpd3T4w/)

zh.question: 一家公司正在扩展其照片分享移动应用的兼容性，使其能够适配数百种屏幕尺寸和分辨率各异的设备。照片以原始格式和分辨率存储在 Amazon S3 中。该公司使用 Amazon CloudFront 分发来提供照片服务。该应用会在每个请求中将屏幕尺寸和分辨率作为 GET 参数包含在内。开发人员需要实现一个解决方案，以优化提供给每台设备的照片，从而缩短加载时间并提高照片质量。哪种解决方案能够以最具成本效益的方式满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 S3 批量操作调用 AWS Lambda 函数，创建具有所需尺寸和分辨率的照片新版本。创建一个动态 CloudFront 源，自动将每个设备的请求映射到相应的照片版本。
options.B: 使用 S3 批量操作调用 AWS Lambda 函数，创建具有所需尺寸和分辨率的照片新版本。创建一个 Lambda@Edge 函数，通过请求头将请求路由到相应的照片版本。
options.C: 创建一个 Lambda@Edge 函数，用于在请求时优化照片并将优化后的照片作为响应返回。将 CloudFront TTL 缓存策略更改为尽可能大的最大值。
options.D: 创建一个 Lambda@Edge 函数，该函数在收到请求时优化照片，并将优化后的照片作为响应返回。在同一函数中，将处理后的照片副本存储在 Amazon S3 上，以供后续请求使用。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

一个照片分享应用需要为数百种独特的设备尺寸/分辨率提供优化的图像。该应用在每个请求中通过 GET（查询）参数提供所需的尺寸和分辨率。照片以原始格式存储在 S3 中，并通过 CloudFront 提供。开发人员需要最具成本效益的方法来针对每个设备优化照片。

## 正确答案：D

使用 **Lambda@Edge** 函数，该函数按需针对请求的尺寸优化（调整大小/转码）照片并返回。同一函数将处理后的照片存储回 S3，因此后续对同一变体的请求会跳过 Lambda 转换，直接从 S3 提供（并在 CloudFront 边缘缓存）。

这是 AWS 博客 [Resizing Images with Amazon CloudFront & Lambda@Edge](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/resizing-images-with-amazon-cloudfront-lambdaedge-aws-cdn-blog/) 中记录的规范 AWS 参考架构，该博客描述了完全相同的流程：如果调整大小的对象存在，继续进行 CloudFront 响应周期；如果它不存在于 S3 中，获取源图像，应用调整大小转换，使用正确的前缀和元数据将调整大小的图像存储回 S3 存储桶，并使用调整大小的图像返回二进制响应。

这具有成本效益，因为：
- 只有实际请求的照片才会被处理（不浪费计算在未查看的照片上）。
- 每个变体仅生成**一次**；后续请求从 S3/CloudFront 缓存提供。如果经常访问调整大小的图像，计算一次并保存它更便宜，通常从延迟角度来看也是首选选项。
- CloudFront 还在边缘位置缓存响应，以实现额外的节省。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

**A. S3 批量操作 + Lambda 预生成每个变体 + "动态 CloudFront 源"。**
为数百个设备尺寸 × 每张照片预生成变体会浪费 Lambda 计算和 S3 存储在可能永远不会被查看的照片上。此外，不存在称为"自动将请求映射到照片变体的动态源"的本地 CloudFront 功能——该映射必须使用 Lambda@Edge 或 CloudFront Functions 实现，因此所描述的机制是虚构/不正确的。

**B. S3 批量操作预生成变体 + Lambda@Edge 按请求头路由。**
与 A 相同的预生成成本问题——您预先生成每个变体，包括永远不会被访问的变体，从而增加存储和计算费用。此外，尺寸/分辨率以 **GET（查询）参数**而非请求头的形式到达，因此按头路由不符合所描述的请求格式。

**C. Lambda@Edge 在每个请求上优化；仅依赖 CloudFront 最大 TTL。**
CloudFront 在每个边缘位置进行缓存，因此数百个边缘中任何一个处的缓存未命中都会重新调用 Lambda@Edge 以重新处理同一图像，反复支付计算成本。缓存条目也可能在 TTL 过期之前被逐出，CloudFront 边缘缓存不是全局共享的。如果从 OriginRequest 或 OriginResponse 触发 Lambda@Edge 函数，结果可以被缓存，但仅在最近的区域边缘缓存中，意味着其他边缘仍会触发重新处理。将处理后的对象存储回 S3（选项 D）避免了在所有边缘和长期内重新运行转换。

## 参考架构流程

1. 查看器请求通过 `?w=300&h=400` 风格的参数命中 CloudFront。
2. CloudFront 缓存未命中 → Lambda@Edge 运行。
3. Lambda@Edge 检查 S3 中是否存在现有的变体键；如果存在，返回它。
4. 如果不存在，Lambda 从 S3 获取原始图像，通过 Sharp/ImageMagick 调整大小，**将变体 PUT 回 S3**，并将其返回给查看器。
5. CloudFront 为后续边缘本地请求缓存响应。

## 来源

- [Resizing Images with Amazon CloudFront & Lambda@Edge — AWS Networking & Content Delivery Blog](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/resizing-images-with-amazon-cloudfront-lambdaedge-aws-cdn-blog/)
- [Image Optimization using Amazon CloudFront and AWS Lambda — AWS Blog](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/image-optimization-using-amazon-cloudfront-and-aws-lambda/)
- [AWS re:Post — Cost comparison: pre-resize to S3 vs Lambda@Edge per request](https://repost.aws/questions/QUcLWr0gc9SXC0uhydpd3T4w/)

en.question: A company is building an application for stock trading. The application needs sub-millisecond latency for processing trade requests. The company uses Amazon DynamoDB to store all the trading data that is used to process each trading request. A development team performs load testing on the application and finds that the data retrieval time is higher than expected. The development team needs a solution that reduces the data retrieval time with the least possible effort. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Add local secondary indexes (LSIs) for the trading data.
options.B: Store the trading data in Amazon S3, and use S3 Transfer Acceleration.
options.C: Add retries with exponential backoff for DynamoDB queries.
options.D: Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) to cache the trading data.

en.explanation:
# Stock Trading Application Requiring Sub-millisecond DynamoDB Reads

## Scenario
A stock trading application stores all data in Amazon DynamoDB and requires **sub-millisecond latency** for trade processing. Load testing shows data retrieval times higher than expected. The team needs a solution with the **least effort** to reduce read latency.

## Correct Answer: D — Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) to cache the trading data

DAX is purpose-built for exactly this scenario. For use cases that require response times in microseconds, DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) delivers fast response times for accessing eventually consistent data. DAX is a DynamoDB-compatible caching service that enables you to benefit from fast in-memory performance for demanding applications.

Trading applications are explicitly called out as an ideal DAX workload: DAX is ideal for applications that require the fastest possible response time for reads. Some examples include real-time bidding, social gaming, and trading applications. DAX delivers fast, in-memory read performance for these use cases.

DAX requires minimal effort to adopt — it is API-compatible with DynamoDB. DAX is tightly integrated with DynamoDB—you simply provision a DAX cluster, use the DAX client SDK to point your existing DynamoDB API calls at the DAX cluster, and let DAX handle the rest. Because DAX is API-compatible with DynamoDB, you don't have to make any functional application code changes.

DAX achieves the latency target the question requires: DAX is a fully managed, highly available, in-memory cache for DynamoDB that delivers requests in as low as sub-millisecond latencies, even at millions of requests per second.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A. Add local secondary indexes (LSIs).** LSIs allow you to query on alternate sort keys, but they do **not** reduce base read latency below DynamoDB's standard single-digit millisecond service-side latency. They also can only be defined at table creation time, so adding them to an existing table is not a "least effort" change — it requires recreating the table. LSIs solve query *flexibility*, not latency.

- **B. Store the trading data in Amazon S3 with S3 Transfer Acceleration.** S3 is object storage with latencies measured in tens to hundreds of milliseconds — much slower than DynamoDB, let alone sub-millisecond. S3 Transfer Acceleration optimizes long-distance uploads/downloads via CloudFront edge locations; it does not provide low-latency key/value lookups suitable for trade processing. It would also require a major rewrite of the data access layer.

- **C. Add retries with exponential backoff for DynamoDB queries.** Retries with backoff are a resilience pattern for handling throttling/transient errors (`ProvisionedThroughputExceededException`). They actually *increase* end-to-end response time when triggered and do nothing to lower base read latency.

## References
- [In-memory acceleration with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html)
- [Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) product page](https://aws.amazon.com/dynamodbaccelerator/)
- [Understanding Amazon DynamoDB latency (AWS Database Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/understanding-amazon-dynamodb-latency/)

zh.question: 一家公司正在开发一款股票交易应用程序。该应用程序需要亚毫秒级的延迟来处理交易请求。该公司使用 Amazon DynamoDB 来存储所有用于处理每个交易请求的交易数据。开发团队对应用程序进行负载测试后发现，数据检索时间高于预期。开发团队需要一个能够以尽可能小的代价来缩短数据检索时间的解决方案。哪个解决方案符合这些要求？

options.A: 添加本地二级指数（LSI）用于交易数据。
options.B: 将交易数据存储在 Amazon S3 中，并使用 S3 传输加速。
options.C: 为 DynamoDB 查询添加指数退避重试机制。
