SNS supports email, SMS, mobile push (APNs/FCM/etc.), HTTP(S) endpoints, SQS, and Lambda — none of which deliver real-time messages to an open web page session. To actually update a browser you would still need a WebSocket-style channel, so this answer conflates services. It also adds DynamoDB and SNS to a flow where they are not needed.

## Key takeaway for the exam

For "push real-time updates to a web dashboard from a serverless backend," the canonical AWS pattern is **API Gateway WebSocket API + Lambda + connectionId mapping**, with messages sent back via the API Gateway Management API. Choose this over EC2-managed WebSocket servers, email notifications, or SNS-to-browser designs.

## References
- [API Gateway WebSocket APIs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-websocket-api.html)
- [Manage connected users: $connect / $disconnect routes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-websocket-api-route-keys-connect-disconnect.html)
- [Use @connections commands in your backend service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-how-to-call-websocket-api-connections.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员创建了一个数据采集应用程序，该应用程序使用了 Amazon API Gateway、AWS Lambda 和 Amazon S3。应用程序的用户定期上传数据文件，并等待处理仪表板上显示验证状态。对于大型文件，验证过程既复杂又耗时。一些用户上传了数十个大型文件，不得不等待并刷新处理仪表板才能查看文件是否已验证。开发人员必须重构应用程序，使其能够在不重新加载整个仪表板的情况下，立即在用户的仪表板上更新验证结果。满足这些要求的最高效解决方案是什么？

options.A: 将客户端与 API 网关 WebSocket API 集成。将用户上传的文件与 WebSocket 连接 ID 一起保存。处理完成后，将验证状态推送至该连接 ID，以启动用户界面更新。
options.B: 启动一个 Amazon EC2 微型实例，并设置一个 WebSocket 服务器。用户上传文件后，将用户上传的文件和用户详细信息发送到该 EC2 实例。文件处理完毕后，使用该 WebSocket 服务器向用户界面发送更新信息。
options.C: 将用户的电子邮件地址与用户上传的文件一起保存。验证过程完成后，通过 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 向上传文件的用户发送电子邮件通知。
options.D: 将用户上传的文件和用户详细信息保存到 Amazon DynamoDB。使用 Amazon DynamoDB Streams 和 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 推送通知向浏览器发送更新，以更新用户界面。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

一个无服务器数据收集应用程序（API Gateway + Lambda + S3）允许用户上传文件。大文件的验证速度很慢，用户目前必须刷新仪表板才能看到结果。需求是**推送**验证状态到仪表板实时显示，**无需完整页面重新加载**，使用**运营效率最高**的方法。

## 正确答案：A — API Gateway WebSocket API

WebSocket 提供了一个持久的双向通道，允许服务器向客户端推送数据，而无需轮询。API Gateway WebSocket API 是双向的。客户端可以向服务发送消息，服务也可以独立地向客户端发送消息。这种双向行为能够实现更丰富的客户端/服务交互，因为服务可以向客户端推送数据，而无需客户端发出显式请求。

标准模式完全符合此场景：

1. 浏览器打开与 API Gateway 的 WebSocket 连接。当客户端连接到 API Gateway WebSocket 端点时，API Gateway 会分配一个唯一的 connectionId——一个在全局范围内标识此套接字的字符串。
2. 在 `$connect` 上，Lambda 将 `connectionId`（通常与用户身份一起）存储在数据库中，上传元数据也被标记此连接 ID。您希望后端向客户端发送回复消息。您希望将每个连接 ID 和其他信息存储到数据库中（例如 Amazon DynamoDB）。
3. 当验证 Lambda 完成时，它调用 API Gateway Management API（`@connections/{connectionId}`）将状态推送到用户的浏览器。您的后端服务可以使用 WebSocket 连接 HTTP 请求向连接的客户端发送回调消息、获取连接信息或断开客户端连接。这些请求使用 IAM 授权，因此您必须使用签名版本 4 (SigV4) 对其进行签名。为此，您可以使用 API Gateway Management API。

这是完全无服务器的，无需服务器修补或扩展，并直接与应用程序现有的 API Gateway + Lambda 堆栈集成——使其成为运营效率最高的选项。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

**B. 运行 WebSocket 服务器的 EC2 micro 实例** — 在功能上有效，但引入了开发人员必须修补、监控、扩展和保护的始终开启的 EC2 实例。相比由 AWS 为您运营的托管 API Gateway WebSocket，这是运营效率的*相反*情况。Amazon API Gateway 通过 WebSocket API 支持 WebSocket 协议，使我们免去管理客户端和服务器之间连接的责任。

**C. SNS 电子邮件通知** — 电子邮件不是实时浏览器更新机制。仪表板不会刷新；用户必须检查电子邮件，然后返回仪表板。它不满足"立即在用户的仪表板上更新验证结果，无需重新加载"的要求。

**D. DynamoDB Streams + SNS 推送通知"到浏览器"** — 这在技术上是有问题的。DynamoDB Streams 不能是 SNS 的直接目标，而且 **Amazon SNS 不能直接向 Web 浏览器推送消息以更新 UI**。SNS 支持电子邮件、SMS、移动推送（APNs/FCM 等）、HTTP(S) 端点、SQS 和 Lambda——其中没有任何一个能向打开的网页会话提供实时消息。要实际更新浏览器，您仍然需要 WebSocket 风格的通道，所以此答案混淆了服务。它还在不需要的流程中添加了 DynamoDB 和 SNS。

## 考试关键要点

对于"从无服务器后端向 Web 仪表板推送实时更新"，规范的 AWS 模式是 **API Gateway WebSocket API + Lambda + connectionId 映射**，消息通过 API Gateway Management API 发回。选择此选项而不是 EC2 托管的 WebSocket 服务器、电子邮件通知或 SNS-to-浏览器设计。

## 参考资源
- [API Gateway WebSocket APIs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-websocket-api.html)
- [Manage connected users: $connect / $disconnect routes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-websocket-api-route-keys-connect-disconnect.html)
- [Use @connections commands in your backend service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-how-to-call-websocket-api-connections.html)

en.question: A company’s developer is creating an application that uses Amazon API Gateway. The company wants to ensure that only users in the Sales department can use the application. The users authenticate to the application by using federated credentials from a third-party identity provider (IdP) through Amazon Cognito. The developer has set up an attribute mapping to map an attribute that is named Department and to pass the attribute to a custom AWS Lambda authorizer. To test the access limitation, the developer sets their department to Engineering in the IdP and attempts to log in to the application. The developer is denied access. The developer then updates their department to Sales in the IdP and attempts to log in. Again, the developer is denied access. The developer checks the logs and discovers that access is being denied because the developer’s access token has a department value of Engineering. Which of the following is a possible reason that the developer’s department is still being reported as Engineering instead of Sales?

options.A: Authorization caching is enabled in the custom Lambda authorizer.
options.B: Authorization caching is enabled on the Amazon Cognito user pool.
options.C: The IAM role for the custom Lambda authorizer does not have a Department tag.
options.D: The IAM role for the Amazon Cognito user pool does not have a Department tag.

en.explanation:
# Lambda Authorizer Caching Causes Stale Department Attribute

## Scenario
A developer has built a custom Lambda authorizer for API Gateway that reads a `Department` attribute mapped from a third-party IdP via Amazon Cognito. The authorizer should allow only `Sales` users. After changing the IdP value from `Engineering` to `Sales` and re-attempting login, the developer is still denied — and the logs show the access token's department is still reported as `Engineering`.

The question is asking: *why is the stale value still being seen by the authorizer?*

## Correct Answer: A — Authorization caching is enabled in the custom Lambda authorizer

API Gateway Lambda authorizers support **policy caching**. When enabled, API Gateway stores the IAM policy returned by the Lambda authorizer (keyed on the token / identity source) for the configured TTL (default 300 s, max 3600 s) and **does not re-invoke the Lambda function** for subsequent requests with the same key. If access is allowed, API Gateway invokes the method. If you enable authorization caching, API Gateway caches the policy so that the Lambda authorizer function isn't invoked again.

Because the cache key for a TOKEN authorizer is the token value itself, and authorizer caching stores the *output policy* (which was generated when Department=Engineering), the developer continues to be denied even after updating the IdP attribute and obtaining a new login session — until the cache TTL expires or the stage cache is flushed.

The fix is exactly what the highly-voted comment notes: When policy caching is enabled, you can modify the TTL value. Setting the TTL to zero disables policy caching. Setting `authorizerResultTtlInSeconds` to 0 forces every request to re-invoke the Lambda authorizer, ensuring the latest attribute value is evaluated.

You can also flush the cache manually: `aws apigateway flush-stage-authorizers-cache --rest-api-id <id> --stage-name <stage>`.

This caching pitfall is well-documented as a source of stale identity context: If you're using the pattern of using custom authorizers for authentication, your authorizer is mostly about fetching and injecting identity context into a request. If this information can change -- such as by adding a user to a new team, or changing the role of a user -- your Lambda functions could see stale data until your cache expires.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **B. Authorization caching is enabled on the Amazon Cognito user pool.** Amazon Cognito user pools do **not** have an "authorization caching" feature for attribute mappings. Attribute mappings from a federated IdP are evaluated whenever the user authenticates and tokens are issued; there is no cache toggle on the user pool that would freeze a `Department` value. This option describes a feature that doesn't exist.

- **C. The IAM role for the custom Lambda authorizer does not have a Department tag.** IAM role tags on the authorizer's execution role have no effect on the value of attributes inside an OIDC/SAML access token issued by Cognito. The token's claims come from the IdP via attribute mapping — not from IAM role tags. This is unrelated to why the token claim shows `Engineering`.

- **D. The IAM role for the Amazon Cognito user pool does not have a Department tag.** Cognito user pools do not have an IAM role whose tags drive token claims. Even if such a role existed (e.g., for SMS or analytics), tags on it would not influence the `Department` claim mapped from the external IdP. This also describes a non-existent mechanism.

## Key Takeaway
For attribute-driven authorization with custom Lambda authorizers, be aware that policy caching is enabled by default with a 300-second TTL. If user attributes can change at runtime, either disable caching (TTL=0), shorten the TTL, or include changeable attributes in the identity sources / cache key.

## References
- [Use API Gateway Lambda authorizers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-use-lambda-authorizer.html)
- [Configure an API Gateway Lambda authorizer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/configure-api-gateway-lambda-authorization.html)
- [Configure a Lambda authorizer using the API Gateway console](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/configure-api-gateway-lambda-authorization-with-console.html)

zh.question: 一家公司的开发人员正在创建一个使用 Amazon API Gateway 的应用程序。该公司希望确保只有销售部门的用户才能使用该应用程序。用户通过 Amazon Cognito 使用来自第三方身份提供商 (IdP) 的联合身份验证凭证对应用程序进行身份验证。开发人员设置了一个属性映射，将名为“Department”（部门）的属性映射到自定义的 AWS Lambda 授权器。为了测试访问限制，开发人员在 IdP 中将其部门设置为“Engineering”（工程），并尝试登录应用程序。开发人员被拒绝访问。然后，开发人员在 IdP 中将其部门更新为“Sales”（销售），并再次尝试登录。开发人员再次被拒绝访问。开发人员检查日志后发现，访问被拒绝的原因是开发人员的访问令牌的部门值为“Engineering”（工程）。以下哪个可能是导致开发人员的部门仍然被报告为“Engineering”（工程）而不是“Sales”（销售）的原因？

options.A: 自定义 Lambda 授权器中已启用授权缓存。
options.B: Amazon Cognito 用户池已启用授权缓存。
options.C: 自定义 Lambda 授权器的 IAM 角色没有部门标签。
options.D: Amazon Cognito 用户池的 IAM 角色没有部门标签。

zh.explanation:
# Lambda 授权者缓存导致部门属性过期

## 场景
开发人员为 API Gateway 构建了自定义 Lambda 授权者，该授权者读取通过 Amazon Cognito 从第三方身份提供商 (IdP) 映射的 `Department` 属性。授权者应仅允许 `Sales` 用户访问。将 IdP 值从 `Engineering` 更改为 `Sales` 并重新尝试登录后，开发人员仍被拒绝 — 日志显示访问令牌的部门仍报告为 `Engineering`。

问题是：*为什么授权者仍在看到过期的值？*

## 正确答案：A — 自定义 Lambda 授权者中启用了授权缓存

API Gateway Lambda 授权者支持**策略缓存**。启用时，API Gateway 会存储 Lambda 授权者返回的 IAM 策略（以令牌/身份源为键），保存时间为配置的 TTL（默认 300 秒，最大 3600 秒），并且**不会为后续使用相同键的请求重新调用 Lambda 函数**。如果允许访问，API Gateway 调用该方法。如果启用授权缓存，API Gateway 会缓存策略，以便不再调用 Lambda 授权者函数。

因为 TOKEN 授权者的缓存键是令牌值本身，而授权者缓存存储*输出策略*（该策略在 Department=Engineering 时生成），所以即使在更新 IdP 属性并获取新登录会话后，开发人员仍继续被拒绝 — 直到缓存 TTL 过期或刷新阶段缓存。

修复方法正是获赞最多的评论所指出的：启用策略缓存时，可以修改 TTL 值。将 TTL 设置为零将禁用策略缓存。将 `authorizerResultTtlInSeconds` 设置为 0 会强制每个请求重新调用 Lambda 授权者，确保评估最新的属性值。

您还可以手动刷新缓存：`aws apigateway flush-stage-authorizers-cache --rest-api-id <id> --stage-name <stage>`。

这个缓存陷阱已被充分记录为过期身份上下文的来源：如果使用自定义授权者进行身份验证的模式，授权者主要是关于获取身份上下文并将其注入请求。如果此信息可以更改 — 例如将用户添加到新团队，或更改用户角色 — Lambda 函数可能会看到过期数据，直到缓存过期。

## 其他选项为什么错误

- **B. Amazon Cognito 用户池中启用了授权缓存。** Amazon Cognito 用户池对于属性映射**没有** "授权缓存" 功能。来自联合 IdP 的属性映射在用户每次进行身份验证和颁发令牌时都会进行评估；用户池上没有会冻结 `Department` 值的缓存切换。此选项描述的是不存在的功能。

- **C. 自定义 Lambda 授权者的 IAM 角色没有 Department 标签。** 授权者执行角色上的 IAM 角色标签对 Cognito 颁发的 OIDC/SAML 访问令牌内部属性的值没有影响。令牌的声明来自通过属性映射的 IdP — 而不是来自 IAM 角色标签。这与令牌声明显示 `Engineering` 的原因无关。

- **D. Amazon Cognito 用户池的 IAM 角色没有 Department 标签。** Cognito 用户池没有其标签驱动令牌声明的 IAM 角色。即使这样的角色存在（例如用于 SMS 或分析），其上的标签也不会影响从外部 IdP 映射的 `Department` 声明。这也描述的是不存在的机制。

## 关键要点
对于使用自定义 Lambda 授权者的基于属性的授权，请注意策略缓存默认启用，TTL 为 300 秒。如果用户属性可以在运行时更改，请禁用缓存（TTL=0）、缩短 TTL，或在身份源/缓存键中包含可更改的属性。

## 参考资源
- [使用 API Gateway Lambda 授权者](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-use-lambda-authorizer.html)
- [配置 API Gateway Lambda 授权者](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/configure-api-gateway-lambda-authorization.html)
- [使用 API Gateway 控制台配置 Lambda 授权者](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/configure-api-gateway-lambda-authorization-with-console.html)

en.question: A company has migrated an application to Amazon EC2 instances. Automatic scaling is working well for the application user interface. However, the process to deliver shipping requests to the company’s warehouse staff is encountering issues. Duplicate shipping requests are arriving, and some requests are lost or arrive out of order. The company must avoid duplicate shipping requests and must process the requests in the order that the requests arrive. Requests are never more than 250 KB in size and take 5-10 minutes to process. A developer needs to rearchitect the application to improve the reliability of the delivery and processing of the requests. What should the developer do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to process the requests. Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Modify the application to write the requests to the Kinesis data stream.
options.B: Create an AWS Lambda function to process the requests. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the Lambda function to the SNS topic. Modify the application to write the requests to the SNS topic.
options.C: Create an AWS Lambda function to process the requests. Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue. Set the SQS queue as an event source for the Lambda function. Modify the application to write the requests to the SQS queue.
options.D: Create an AWS Lambda function to process the requests. Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Set the SQS queue as an event source for the Lambda function. Modify the application to write the requests to the SQS queue.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A migrated EC2 application has a shipping-request workflow that suffers from three problems:

1. **Duplicate** shipping requests
2. **Lost** requests
3. Requests **arriving out of order**

Additional constraints:
- Message size ≤ 250 KB (well under the 256 KB SQS limit)
- Processing time per message: 5–10 minutes
- Need reliable, ordered, exactly-once delivery

## Correct Answer: D — SQS FIFO queue + Lambda

Amazon SQS FIFO queues are purpose-built for this exact use case. FIFO (First In First Out) queues guarantee that messages are processed exactly once, in the exact order they are sent. FIFO queues also handle automatic deduplication: if a message with a deduplication ID is sent successfully, any subsequent messages with the same ID are accepted but not delivered during a 5-minute deduplication interval.

Lambda fully supports FIFO queues as an event source. AWS expanded the SQS event source feature to include SQS FIFO queues, making it easier to create serverless applications using queues where order matters. FIFO queues ensure that messages are processed in the exact order they are sent, and when you set up a Lambda function to process messages from an SQS FIFO queue, Lambda respects the ordering guarantees provided by the FIFO queue.

The 5–10 minute processing time is acceptable because Lambda's maximum timeout is 15 minutes, and the SQS visibility timeout can be set to cover the processing time. The 250 KB message size also fits within SQS's 256 KB limit.

```text
Producer (EC2 app) ──► SQS FIFO Queue ──► Lambda (event source mapping)
                       (MessageGroupId,
                        MessageDeduplicationId)
```

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

**A. Kinesis Data Firehose + Kinesis Data Streams** — Firehose is a delivery service for loading streaming data into destinations like S3, Redshift, or OpenSearch; it is **not** designed to invoke a custom processing workflow for warehouse staff. Kinesis Data Streams provides ordering per shard but does not provide built-in deduplication; consumers must implement idempotency themselves. This adds unnecessary complexity for a request/processing workload.

**B. SNS topic + Lambda subscription** — Standard SNS is pub/sub and does **not** guarantee ordering or deduplication. Although SNS FIFO topics exist, the option specifies a plain SNS topic. Even SNS FIFO requires a subscriber endpoint like SQS FIFO; subscribing Lambda directly to SNS does not preserve FIFO ordering. SNS also retries deliveries, which can cause duplicates.

**C. SQS Standard queue + Lambda** — Standard queues provide **at-least-once** delivery (duplicates possible) and **best-effort ordering** (out-of-order delivery possible). Lambda event source mappings process each event at least once, and duplicate processing of records can occur; AWS strongly recommends making your function code idempotent. This directly violates both the "no duplicates" and "in-order" requirements.

## References

- [Amazon SQS FIFO queues – Exactly-once processing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/FIFO-queues-exactly-once-processing.html)
- [Amazon SQS FIFO queue and Lambda concurrency behavior](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/fifo-queue-lambda-behavior.html)
- [Using Lambda with Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html)
- [New for AWS Lambda – SQS FIFO as an event source](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/new-for-aws-lambda-sqs-fifo-as-an-event-source/)

zh.question: 一家公司已将应用程序迁移到 Amazon EC2 实例。应用程序用户界面的自动扩展运行良好。然而，向公司仓库人员发送发货请求的流程却遇到了问题。重复的发货请求不断到达，部分请求丢失或到达顺序混乱。公司必须避免重复的发货请求，并按照请求到达的顺序进行处理。每个请求的大小不超过 250 KB，处理时间为 5-10 分钟。开发人员需要重新设计应用程序架构，以提高请求发送和处理的可靠性。开发人员应该如何做才能满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个 Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose 数据流来处理请求。创建一个 Amazon Kinesis 数据流。修改应用程序，使其将请求写入 Kinesis 数据流。
options.B: 创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数来处理请求。创建一个 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题。将 Lambda 函数订阅到该 SNS 主题。修改应用程序，使其将请求写入 SNS 主题。
options.C: 创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数来处理请求。创建一个 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 标准队列。将 SQS 队列设置为 Lambda 函数的事件源。修改应用程序，使其将请求写入 SQS 队列。
options.D: 创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数来处理请求。创建一个 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 先进先出 (FIFO) 队列。将 SQS 队列设置为 Lambda 函数的事件源。修改应用程序，使其将请求写入 SQS 队列。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

一个迁移的 EC2 应用程序的配送请求工作流存在三个问题：

1. **重复的**配送请求
2. **丢失的**请求
3. 请求**到达顺序混乱**

额外约束：
- 消息大小 ≤ 250 KB（远低于 256 KB 的 SQS 限制）
- 每条消息的处理时间：5–10 分钟
- 需要可靠、有序、恰好一次的传递

## 正确答案：D — SQS FIFO 队列 + Lambda

Amazon SQS FIFO 队列正是为这种用例而设计的。FIFO（先进先出）队列保证消息被准确处理一次，并按照发送的确切顺序处理。FIFO 队列还处理自动去重：如果成功发送了具有去重 ID 的消息，任何后续具有相同 ID 的消息都会被接受但在 5 分钟去重间隔内不会被传递。

Lambda 完全支持 FIFO 队列作为事件源。AWS 将 SQS 事件源功能扩展到包括 SQS FIFO 队列，使创建需要考虑顺序的无服务器应用程序变得更加容易。FIFO 队列确保消息按照发送的确切顺序被处理，当您设置 Lambda 函数从 SQS FIFO 队列处理消息时，Lambda 会遵守 FIFO 队列提供的顺序保证。

5–10 分钟的处理时间是可以接受的，因为 Lambda 的最大超时时间为 15 分钟，SQS 可见性超时可以设置为覆盖处理时间。250 KB 的消息大小也符合 SQS 的 256 KB 限制。

```text
生产者（EC2 应用）──► SQS FIFO 队列 ──► Lambda（事件源映射）
                      （MessageGroupId,
                       MessageDeduplicationId）
```

## 为什么其他选项是错的

**A. Kinesis Data Firehose + Kinesis Data Streams** — Firehose 是用于将流数据加载到 S3、Redshift 或 OpenSearch 等目标的传递服务；它**不是**为仓库员工调用自定义处理工作流而设计的。Kinesis Data Streams 提供每个分片的有序性，但不提供内置去重；使用者必须自己实现幂等性。这为请求/处理工作负载增加了不必要的复杂性。

**B. SNS 主题 + Lambda 订阅** — 标准 SNS 是发布/订阅，**不保证**顺序或去重。虽然存在 SNS FIFO 主题，但该选项指定的是普通 SNS 主题。即使是 SNS FIFO，也需要 SQS FIFO 之类的订阅端点；直接向 SNS 订阅 Lambda 不会保留 FIFO 顺序。SNS 还会重试传递，这可能会导致重复。

**C. SQS Standard 队列 + Lambda** — Standard 队列提供**至少一次**传递（可能重复）和**尽力而为的顺序**（可能乱序传递）。Lambda 事件源映射至少处理每个事件一次，记录的重复处理可能会发生；AWS 强烈建议让您的函数代码具有幂等性。这直接违反了"无重复"和"有序"两项要求。

## 参考资源

- [Amazon SQS FIFO 队列 – 恰好一次处理](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/FIFO-queues-exactly-once-processing.html)
- [Amazon SQS FIFO 队列与 Lambda 并发行为](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/fifo-queue-lambda-behavior.html)
- [将 Lambda 与 Amazon SQS 结合使用](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html)
- [AWS Lambda 新增功能 – 将 SQS FIFO 作为事件源](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/new-for-aws-lambda-sqs-fifo-as-an-event-source/)

en.question: A developer is creating a machine learning (ML) pipeline in AWS Step Functions that contains AWS Lambda functions. The developer has configured an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to deliver ML model parameters to the ML pipeline to train ML models. The developer uploads the trained models are uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket. The developer needs a solution that can locally test the ML pipeline without making service integration calls to Amazon SQS and Amazon S3. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use the Amazon CodeGuru Profiler to analyze the Lambda functions used in the AWS Step Functions pipeline.
options.B: Use the AWS Step Functions Local Docker Image to run and locally test the Lambda functions.
options.C: Use the AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM) CLI to run and locally test the Lambda functions.
options.D: Use AWS Step Functions Local with mocked service integrations.

en.explanation:
# Local Testing of Step Functions ML Pipeline Without Real AWS Service Calls

## Scenario
The developer has built a Step Functions–orchestrated ML pipeline that uses Lambda functions, receives ML model parameters from an SQS queue, and uploads trained models to S3. They want to **locally test the entire pipeline** without making actual service-integration calls to SQS and S3.

## Correct Answer: D — Use AWS Step Functions Local with mocked service integrations

AWS released Mocked Service Integrations specifically for this use case. AWS Step Functions Local, a runtime for debugging and testing state machine based workflows locally, is now designed to support mocking for service integrations, allowing you to run state machines without the need to call downstream services. With Step Functions Local, you can mock the responses from your service integrations.

By providing the mock configuration file to Step Functions Local, you can test service integration calls by running state machines that use the mocked responses specified in the test cases instead of making actual service integration calls. A mocked Task will never call the service endpoint.

This precisely matches the requirement: run the Step Functions ML pipeline locally while bypassing SQS and S3 integrations. You author a `MockConfigFile.json` defining mocked responses for the SQS and S3 task states (and Lambda invocations if desired), then start executions against the local endpoint using a state-machine ARN suffixed with `#TestCaseName`.

Example invocation:
```bash
aws stepfunctions start-execution \
  --endpoint http://localhost:8083 \
  --state-machine arn:aws:states:us-east-1:123456789012:stateMachine:MLPipeline#HappyPath \
  --input file://input.json
```

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

**A. Amazon CodeGuru Profiler** — CodeGuru Profiler analyzes application runtime performance (CPU usage, latency hotspots) of running Lambda code. It does not provide local execution of a Step Functions workflow and cannot mock SQS/S3 integrations. It addresses profiling, not local integration testing.

**B. AWS Step Functions Local Docker image to test the Lambda functions** — While the Step Functions Local Docker image is the *runtime* you use, simply running it without mock configuration causes Step Functions Local to still call real service endpoints. If you don't specify mocked service integration responses in the mock configuration file, Step Functions Local will invoke the AWS service integration using the endpoint you configured while setting up Step Functions Local. The key feature that satisfies "without making service integration calls to SQS and S3" is the **mocked service integrations**, not the Docker image itself. Option D is more precise.

**C. AWS SAM CLI to run and locally test the Lambda functions** — `sam local` invokes Lambda functions locally, but it does **not** execute Step Functions state machines, nor does it mock SQS/S3 service integrations called from within the workflow. It only handles Lambda-level local invocation, missing the orchestration layer of the pipeline.

## References
- [Using mocked service integrations for testing in Step Functions Local](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/sfn-local-test-sm-exec.html)
- [Testing state machines with Step Functions Local](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/sfn-local.html)
- [Mocking service integrations with AWS Step Functions Local (AWS Compute Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/mocking-service-integrations-with-aws-step-functions-local/)
- [AWS Step Functions adds mocking support for testing workflows locally](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2022/01/aws-step-functions-support-workflows/)

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在 AWS Step Functions 中创建一个包含 AWS Lambda 函数的机器学习 (ML) 管道。该开发人员已配置 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列，用于将 ML 模型参数传递给 ML 管道以训练 ML 模型。训练好的模型会被上传到 Amazon S3 存储桶。该开发人员需要一个解决方案，能够在本地测试 ML 管道，而无需调用 Amazon SQS 和 Amazon S3 的服务集成。哪个解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 Amazon CodeGuru Profiler 分析 AWS Step Functions 管道中使用的 Lambda 函数。
options.B: 使用 AWS Step Functions 本地 Docker 镜像运行 Lambda 函数并在本地进行测试。
options.C: 使用 AWS 无服务器应用程序模型 (AWS SAM) CLI 运行 Lambda 函数并在本地进行测试。
options.D: 使用 AWS Step Functions Local 进行模拟服务集成。

zh.explanation:
# Step Functions ML 管道的本地测试无需真实 AWS 服务调用

## 场景
开发人员构建了一个由 Step Functions 编排的 ML 管道，该管道使用 Lambda 函数，从 SQS 队列接收 ML 模型参数，并将训练的模型上传到 S3。他们希望**在本地测试整个管道**，无需对 SQS 和 S3 进行实际的服务集成调用。

## 正确答案：D — 使用 AWS Step Functions Local 并使用模拟的服务集成

AWS 发布了模拟的服务集成，专门用于此用例。AWS Step Functions Local 是用于本地调试和测试基于状态机的工作流的运行时环境，现在设计为支持对服务集成进行模拟，允许你运行状态机而无需调用下游服务。通过 Step Functions Local，你可以使用模拟响应来测试服务集成调用。

通过将模拟配置文件提供给 Step Functions Local，你可以测试服务集成调用，运行使用测试用例中指定的模拟响应的状态机，而不是进行实际的服务集成调用。模拟的 Task 永远不会调用服务端点。

这正好符合需求：在本地运行 Step Functions ML 管道，同时绕过 SQS 和 S3 集成。你创建一个 `MockConfigFile.json` 来定义 SQS 和 S3 任务状态（以及 Lambda 调用，如果需要）的模拟响应，然后使用以 `#TestCaseName` 后缀的状态机 ARN 针对本地端点启动执行。

示例调用：
```bash
aws stepfunctions start-execution \
  --endpoint http://localhost:8083 \
  --state-machine arn:aws:states:us-east-1:123456789012:stateMachine:MLPipeline#HappyPath \
  --input file://input.json
```

## 为什么其他选项错误

**A. Amazon CodeGuru Profiler** — CodeGuru Profiler 分析运行中 Lambda 代码的应用运行时性能（CPU 使用率、延迟热点）。它不提供 Step Functions 工作流的本地执行，也无法模拟 SQS/S3 集成。它解决的是性能分析问题，而不是本地集成测试。

**B. AWS Step Functions Local Docker 镜像来测试 Lambda 函数** — 虽然 Step Functions Local Docker 镜像是你使用的*运行时*，但仅运行它而不进行模拟配置会导致 Step Functions Local 仍然调用真实的服务端点。如果你没有在模拟配置文件中指定模拟的服务集成响应，Step Functions Local 将使用你在设置 Step Functions Local 时配置的端点来调用 AWS 服务集成。满足"无需对 SQS 和 S3 进行服务集成调用"的关键特性是**模拟的服务集成**，而不是 Docker 镜像本身。选项 D 更精确。

**C. AWS SAM CLI 来运行和本地测试 Lambda 函数** — `sam local` 在本地调用 Lambda 函数，但它**不**执行 Step Functions 状态机，也不模拟从工作流内调用的 SQS/S3 服务集成。它仅处理 Lambda 级别的本地调用，缺少管道编排层。

## 参考资源
- [在 Step Functions Local 中使用模拟的服务集成进行测试](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/sfn-local-test-sm-exec.html)
- [使用 Step Functions Local 测试状态机](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/sfn-local.html)
- [使用 AWS Step Functions Local 模拟服务集成 (AWS Compute 博客)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/mocking-service-integrations-with-aws-step-functions-local/)
- [AWS Step Functions 增加模拟支持以在本地测试工作流](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2022/01/aws-step-functions-support-workflows/)

en.question: A company runs a batch processing application by using AWS Lambda functions and Amazon API Gateway APIs with deployment stages for development, user acceptance testing, and production. A development team needs to configure the APIs in the deployment stages to connect to third-party service endpoints. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.A: Store the third-party service endpoints in Lambda layers that correspond to the stage.
options.B: Store the third-party service endpoints in API Gateway stage variables that correspond to the stage.
options.C: Encode the third-party service endpoints as query parameters in the API Gateway request URL.
options.D: Store the third-party service endpoint for each environment in AWS AppConfig.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A company runs APIs through Amazon API Gateway with three deployment stages (dev, UAT, prod) backed by Lambda. Each stage must connect to a *different* third-party endpoint URL. The question is essentially: what is the AWS-native, built-in mechanism to vary backend endpoint configuration per stage?

## Correct Answer: B — API Gateway Stage Variables

Stage variables are key-value pairs that you can define as configuration attributes associated with a deployment stage of a REST API. They act like environment variables and can be used in your API setup and mapping templates.

This is exactly the use case shown in the AWS documentation: You can use a stage variable so that when API callers invoke your production endpoint, API Gateway calls example.com. Then, when API callers invoke the beta stage, API Gateway calls a different web host, such as beta.example.com.

A stage variable can be referenced directly in the integration URL, e.g.:

```
http://${stageVariables.url}/resource/operation
```

A stage variable can be used as part of an HTTP integration URL, as shown in the following examples: A full URI without protocol – http://${stageVariables.url} A full domain – http://${stageVariables.url}/resource/operation

So the developers can simply set a `url` stage variable per stage (dev/uat/prod), each pointing to the correct third-party endpoint, with no code changes.

## Why the other options are wrong

- **A. Lambda layers.** Layers package shared code/libraries/runtime dependencies for Lambda functions; they are not stage-specific configuration mechanisms for API Gateway. They cannot be referenced by API Gateway integration URLs and don't map to API Gateway stages at all. Layers also aren't designed to hold environment-specific endpoint values per API stage — using them for this is an anti-pattern that requires re-publishing layer versions per environment.

- **C. Encode endpoints as query parameters in the request URL.** This pushes backend configuration into the *client* request, which is insecure and brittle — any caller could change the third-party target. Query parameters are intended for caller-supplied data, not for configuring the integration target. It also doesn't differentiate dev vs UAT vs prod stages — every caller would have to know and send the right URL.

- **D. AWS AppConfig.** While AppConfig can store environment-specific configuration, API Gateway has no native integration that lets the *integration request URL* read directly from AppConfig. To use it, the Lambda function would have to fetch the endpoint at runtime, adding code, latency, IAM permissions, and operational overhead. It is more complex than the purpose-built stage variables feature, which is the AWS-recommended mechanism for per-stage backend endpoint configuration.

## References

- [Use stage variables for a REST API in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/stage-variables.html)
- [Set up stage variables for REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/amazon-api-gateway-using-stage-variables.html)
- [API Gateway stage variables reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/aws-api-gateway-stage-variables-reference.html)

zh.question: 一家公司使用 AWS Lambda 函数和 Amazon API Gateway API 运行批量处理应用程序，并分开发、用户验收测试和生产三个部署阶段。开发团队需要在部署阶段配置 API 以连接到第三方服务端点。哪种解决方案能够满足此需求？

options.A: 将第三方服务端点存储在与阶段对应的 Lambda 层中。
options.B: 将第三方服务端点存储在与阶段对应的 API 网关阶段变量中。
options.C: 将第三方服务端点编码为 API 网关请求 URL 中的查询参数。
options.D: 将每个环境的第三方服务终端节点存储在 AWS AppConfig 中。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

一家公司通过 Amazon API Gateway 运行 API，有三个部署阶段（dev、UAT、prod），由 Lambda 支持。每个阶段必须连接到*不同的*第三方端点 URL。问题是：什么是 AWS 原生的内置机制来按阶段改变后端端点配置？

## 正确答案：B — API Gateway 阶段变量

阶段变量是可以定义为 REST API 部署阶段的配置属性的键值对。它们的作用类似于环境变量，可以在 API 设置和映射模板中使用。

这正是 AWS 文档中所示的用例：您可以使用阶段变量，以便当 API 调用者调用您的生产端点时，API Gateway 调用 example.com。然后，当 API 调用者调用 beta 阶段时，API Gateway 调用不同的 Web 主机，例如 beta.example.com。

阶段变量可以直接在集成 URL 中引用，例如：

```
http://${stageVariables.url}/resource/operation
```

阶段变量可以用作 HTTP 集成 URL 的一部分，如下例所示：没有协议的完整 URI — http://${stageVariables.url} 完整域 — http://${stageVariables.url}/resource/operation

因此，开发人员可以为每个阶段（dev/uat/prod）简单地设置一个 `url` 阶段变量，每个都指向正确的第三方端点，无需更改代码。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

- **A. Lambda 层。** 层打包 Lambda 函数的共享代码/库/运行时依赖项；它们不是 API Gateway 的特定于阶段的配置机制。它们无法被 API Gateway 集成 URL 引用，也完全不映射到 API Gateway 阶段。层也不是为了保存每个 API 阶段的环境特定端点值而设计的——使用它们来做这件事是一个反模式，需要为每个环境重新发布层版本。

- **C. 将端点编码为请求 URL 中的查询参数。** 这会将后端配置推送到*客户端*请求中，这是不安全且脆弱的——任何调用者都可以更改第三方目标。查询参数旨在用于调用者提供的数据，而不是用于配置集成目标。它也不会区分 dev vs UAT vs prod 阶段——每个调用者都必须知道并发送正确的 URL。

- **D. AWS AppConfig。** 虽然 AppConfig 可以存储环境特定的配置，但 API Gateway 没有原生集成让*集成请求 URL* 直接从 AppConfig 读取。要使用它，Lambda 函数必须在运行时获取端点，这会增加代码、延迟、IAM 权限和操作开销。它比目的为专门针对每个阶段后端端点配置的阶段变量特性更复杂，而阶段变量是 AWS 推荐的机制。

## 参考资源

- [在 API Gateway 中为 REST API 使用阶段变量](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/stage-variables.html)
- [在 API Gateway 中为 REST API 设置阶段变量](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/amazon-api-gateway-using-stage-variables.html)
- [API Gateway 阶段变量参考](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/aws-api-gateway-stage-variables-reference.html)

en.question: A developer is building a serverless application that runs on AWS. The developer wants to create an accelerated development workflow that deploys incremental changes to AWS for testing. The developer wants to deploy the incremental changes but does not want to fully deploy the entire application to AWS for every code commit. What should the developer do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Use the AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM) to build the application. Use the sam sync command to deploy the incremental changes.
options.B: Use the AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM) to build the application. Use the sam init command to deploy the incremental changes.
options.C: Use the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) to build the application. Use the cdk synth command to deploy the incremental changes.
options.D: Use the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) to build the application. Use the cdk bootstrap command to deploy the incremental changes.

en.explanation:
# Accelerated Serverless Development with `sam sync`

## Scenario
A developer building a serverless application wants an **accelerated development workflow** that pushes **incremental changes** to AWS for testing — without performing a full CloudFormation deployment of the entire application on every code commit.

## Correct Answer: A — Use AWS SAM with `sam sync`

The `sam sync` command (part of **AWS SAM Accelerate**) is purpose-built for this exact scenario. The AWS SAM CLI sam sync command provides options to quickly sync local application changes to the AWS Cloud — automatically detect and sync local changes to the AWS Cloud, customize what local changes are synced, and prepare your application in the cloud for testing and validation.

With sam sync, you can create a rapid development workflow that shortens the time it takes to sync your local changes to the cloud for testing and validation. The sam sync command is recommended for development environments.

Crucially, for code-only updates, the sam sync command can also synchronize code changes to the cloud without updating the infrastructure. This code synchronization uses the service APIs and bypasses CloudFormation, allowing AWS SAM to update the code in seconds instead of minutes. This is what makes deployments incremental rather than full stack deployments.

```bash
# Watch local changes and continuously sync them to AWS
sam sync --watch --stack-name my-app

# Sync only code (Lambda function code, layers) — bypasses CloudFormation
sam sync --code --stack-name my-app
```

> Note: Because sync bypasses CloudFormation for code updates, AWS recommends using it **only for development stacks**, since it can introduce drift between the CloudFormation template and the deployed resources.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **B. `sam init`** — This command only **scaffolds a brand-new SAM project** from a template. It does not deploy anything to AWS, let alone incremental changes. From the SAM CLI docs: "Initialize serverless applications in minutes with AWS-provided infrastructure templates with sam init".

- **C. `cdk synth`** — This command only **emits a CloudFormation template** from the CDK app's TypeScript/Python/etc. code. It performs no deployment at all; it just prints/writes the synthesized template to `cdk.out/`. You would still need `cdk deploy` to push it to AWS, and `cdk deploy` does a full CloudFormation update — not the incremental, CFN-bypassing behavior the scenario asks for. (CDK does have `cdk deploy --hotswap` for incremental Lambda updates, but `cdk synth` is not it.)

- **D. `cdk bootstrap`** — This is a **one-time setup** command that provisions the resources (S3 bucket, ECR repo, IAM roles) the CDK uses to deploy assets into an account/region. It does not deploy application code or incremental changes.

## Reference Documentation
- [Introduction to using sam sync to sync to AWS Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/using-sam-cli-sync.html)
- [sam sync command reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/sam-cli-command-reference-sam-sync.html)
- [Accelerating serverless development with AWS SAM Accelerate (AWS Compute Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/accelerating-serverless-development-with-aws-sam-accelerate/)

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在构建一个运行在 AWS 上的无服务器应用程序。他希望创建一个加速开发工作流程，将增量更改部署到 AWS 进行测试。开发人员希望部署这些增量更改，但不希望每次代码提交都将整个应用程序完全部署到 AWS。为了满足这些要求，开发人员应该怎么做？

options.A: 使用 AWS 无服务器应用程序模型 (AWS SAM) 构建应用程序。使用 sam sync 命令部署增量更改。
options.B: 使用 AWS 无服务器应用程序模型 (AWS SAM) 构建应用程序。使用 sam init 命令部署增量更改。
options.C: 使用 AWS 云开发工具包 (AWS CDK) 构建应用程序。使用 cdk synth 命令部署增量更改。
options.D: 使用 AWS 云开发工具包 (AWS CDK) 构建应用程序。使用 cdk bootstrap 命令部署增量更改。

zh.explanation:
# 使用 `sam sync` 加速无服务器开发

## 场景
开发人员构建无服务器应用程序，希望拥有一个**加速开发工作流**，能够将**增量更改**推送到 AWS 进行测试——而无需在每次代码提交时对整个应用程序执行完整的 CloudFormation 部署。

## 正确答案：A — 使用 AWS SAM 和 `sam sync`

`sam sync` 命令（**AWS SAM Accelerate** 的一部分）专为这种场景而设计。AWS SAM CLI 的 sam sync 命令提供了快速同步本地应用程序更改到 AWS 云的选项——自动检测并同步本地更改到 AWS 云、自定义同步哪些本地更改，以及在云中准备应用程序进行测试和验证。

通过 sam sync，您可以创建一个快速开发工作流，缩短将本地更改同步到云进行测试和验证所需的时间。建议在开发环境中使用 sam sync 命令。

关键是，对于仅限代码的更新，sam sync 命令可以在不更新基础设施的情况下将代码更改同步到云端。此代码同步使用服务 API 并绕过 CloudFormation，允许 AWS SAM 在数秒而不是数分钟内更新代码。这就是使部署成为增量部署而不是完整堆栈部署的原因。

```bash
# 监视本地更改并持续将其同步到 AWS
sam sync --watch --stack-name my-app

# 仅同步代码（Lambda 函数代码、层）— 绕过 CloudFormation
sam sync --code --stack-name my-app
```

> 注意：由于同步绕过 CloudFormation 进行代码更新，AWS 建议仅在**开发堆栈**中使用它，因为它可能会导致 CloudFormation 模板与已部署的资源之间出现漂移。

## 其他选项为什么错误

- **B. `sam init`** — 此命令仅从模板**生成全新的 SAM 项目**。它不会向 AWS 部署任何内容，更不用说增量更改了。根据 SAM CLI 文档："使用 sam init 在数分钟内通过 AWS 提供的基础设施模板初始化无服务器应用程序"。

- **C. `cdk synth`** — 此命令仅从 CDK 应用程序的 TypeScript/Python 等代码**生成 CloudFormation 模板**。它根本不执行任何部署；它只是将合成的模板打印/写入 `cdk.out/`。您仍然需要 `cdk deploy` 将其推送到 AWS，而 `cdk deploy` 执行完整的 CloudFormation 更新——而不是场景要求的增量、绕过 CFN 的行为。（CDK 确实有 `cdk deploy --hotswap` 用于增量 Lambda 更新，但 `cdk synth` 不是。）

- **D. `cdk bootstrap`** — 这是一个**一次性设置**命令，用于配置 CDK 用于将资源部署到帐户/区域的资源（S3 桶、ECR 存储库、IAM 角色）。它不会部署应用程序代码或增量更改。

## 参考文档
- [使用 sam sync 同步到 AWS 云简介](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/using-sam-cli-sync.html)
- [sam sync 命令参考](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/sam-cli-command-reference-sam-sync.html)
- [使用 AWS SAM Accelerate 加速无服务器开发（AWS Compute 博客）](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/accelerating-serverless-development-with-aws-sam-accelerate/)

en.question: A developer is building an application that will use an Amazon API Gateway API with an AWS Lambda backend. The team that will develop the frontend requires immediate access to the API endpoints to build the UI. To prepare the backend application for integration, the developer needs to set up endpoints. The endpoints need to return predefined HTTP status codes and JSON responses for the frontend team. The developer creates a method for an API resource. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Set the integration type to AWS_PROXY. Provision Lambda functions to return hardcoded JSON data.
options.B: Set the integration type to MOCK. Configure the method's integration request and integration response to associate a JSON responses with specific HTTP status codes.
options.C: Set the integration type to HTTP_PROXY. Configure API Gateway to pass all requests to an external placeholder API. which the team will build.
options.D: Set the integration type to MOCK. Use a method request to define HTTP status codes. Use an integration request to define JSON responses.

en.explanation:
# API Gateway MOCK Integration for Frontend Unblocking

## Scenario
The frontend team needs immediate access to API endpoints to start building the UI while the backend (Lambda) is still being developed. The developer needs endpoints that return **predefined HTTP status codes and JSON responses** without requiring real backend logic.

## Correct Answer: B
**Set the integration type to MOCK. Configure the method's integration request and integration response to associate JSON responses with specific HTTP status codes.**

API Gateway's MOCK integration is purpose-built for exactly this scenario. Amazon API Gateway supports mock integrations for API methods. This feature enables API developers to generate API responses from API Gateway directly, without the need for an integration backend. As an API developer, you can use this feature to unblock dependent teams that need to work with an API before the project development is complete.

The configuration mechanism described in option B is exactly what AWS documents: As an API developer, you decide how API Gateway responds to a mock integration request. For this, you configure the method's integration request and integration response to associate a response with a given status code.

Typically, the **integration request** uses a mapping template such as `{"statusCode": 200}` to select which **integration response** to return, and the integration response defines the JSON body and headers tied to that status code.

```yaml
Integration:
  Type: MOCK
  RequestTemplates:
    application/json: '{"statusCode": 200}'
IntegrationResponses:
  - StatusCode: 200
    ResponseTemplates:
      application/json: '{"message": "Hello from mock"}'
MethodResponses:
  - StatusCode: 200
```

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A. AWS_PROXY with hardcoded Lambda functions** — This works functionally but is unnecessary overhead. It requires writing, deploying, and maintaining Lambda code (plus IAM/permissions/cold starts/cost) just to return static data. The whole point of MOCK is to avoid provisioning a backend. AWS explicitly positions MOCK as the way to "unblock dependent teams... without the need for an integration backend."

- **C. HTTP_PROXY to an external placeholder API** — HTTP_PROXY forwards requests to an external HTTP endpoint that the frontend team would have to build. This contradicts the requirement (the frontend team builds UI, not backends), defeats the purpose of giving them immediate access, and adds an external dependency that doesn't exist yet.

- **D. MOCK with method request defining status codes and integration request defining JSON responses** — This reverses the actual API Gateway model. The **method request** validates client input (query strings, headers, auth) — it does not define HTTP status codes. Status codes are defined in the **method response** and **integration response**, and JSON response bodies are defined in the **integration response** (via response mapping templates), not the integration request. In API Gateway you have to create Integration Response and Method Response for each status code (200, 302, 400, 500) you want to present. You can get all data from Integration Request into Integration Response except Status Code since API Gateway manages it for you.

## References
- [Mock integrations for REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-mock-integration.html)
- [Enable mock integration using the API Gateway console](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-mock-integration-console.html)
- [Set up REST API integrations - integration types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-integration-types.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在构建一个应用程序，该应用程序将使用 Amazon API Gateway API 和 AWS Lambda 后端。前端开发团队需要立即访问 API 端点来构建用户界面。为了准备后端应用程序以进行集成，开发人员需要设置端点。这些端点需要返回预定义的 HTTP 状态码和 JSON 响应，供前端团队使用。开发人员创建了一个 API 资源方法。哪个解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 将集成类型设置为 AWS_PROXY。配置 Lambda 函数以返回硬编码的 JSON 数据。
options.B: 将集成类型设置为 MOCK。配置方法的集成请求和集成响应，将 JSON 响应与特定的 HTTP 状态代码关联起来。
options.C: 将集成类型设置为 HTTP_PROXY。配置 API 网关，将所有请求转发到团队将构建的外部占位符 API。
options.D: 将集成类型设置为 MOCK。使用方法请求定义 HTTP 状态码。使用集成请求定义 JSON 响应。

zh.explanation:
# API Gateway MOCK 集成用于前端解除阻塞

## 场景
前端团队需要立即访问 API 端点以开始构建 UI，而后端（Lambda）仍在开发中。开发人员需要返回**预定义的 HTTP 状态代码和 JSON 响应**的端点，无需实现真正的后端逻辑。

## 正确答案：B
**将集成类型设置为 MOCK。配置方法的集成请求和集成响应，以将 JSON 响应与特定的 HTTP 状态代码关联。**

API Gateway 的 MOCK 集成正是为这种场景而设计的。Amazon API Gateway 支持 API 方法的模拟集成。此功能使 API 开发人员能够直接从 API Gateway 生成 API 响应，无需集成后端。作为 API 开发人员，您可以使用此功能来解除依赖团队的阻塞，这些团队需要在项目开发完成之前使用 API。

选项 B 中描述的配置机制正是 AWS 文档中的内容：作为 API 开发人员，您决定 API Gateway 如何响应模拟集成请求。为此，您需要配置方法的集成请求和集成响应，以将响应与给定的状态代码关联。

通常，**集成请求**使用映射模板（如 `{"statusCode": 200}`）来选择要返回的**集成响应**，而集成响应定义与该状态代码关联的 JSON 正文和标头。

```yaml
Integration:
  Type: MOCK
  RequestTemplates:
    application/json: '{"statusCode": 200}'
IntegrationResponses:
  - StatusCode: 200
    ResponseTemplates:
      application/json: '{"message": "Hello from mock"}'
MethodResponses:
  - StatusCode: 200
```

## 其他选项为什么错误

- **A. AWS_PROXY 与硬编码 Lambda 函数** — 这在功能上有效，但是不必要的开销。它需要编写、部署和维护 Lambda 代码（加上 IAM/权限/冷启动/成本）才能返回静态数据。MOCK 的整个目的是避免配置后端。AWS 明确将 MOCK 定位为解除依赖团队阻塞的方式，"无需集成后端"。

- **C. HTTP_PROXY 到外部占位符 API** — HTTP_PROXY 将请求转发到前端团队必须构建的外部 HTTP 端点。这违反了要求（前端团队构建 UI，而不是后端），破坏了为其提供即时访问的目的，并添加了尚不存在的外部依赖。

- **D. MOCK，方法请求定义状态代码，集成请求定义 JSON 响应** — 这颠倒了实际的 API Gateway 模型。**方法请求**验证客户端输入（查询字符串、标头、身份验证）— 它不定义 HTTP 状态代码。状态代码在**方法响应**和**集成响应**中定义，JSON 响应正文在**集成响应**中定义（通过响应映射模板），而不是集成请求。在 API Gateway 中，您必须为每个状态代码（200、302、400、500）创建集成响应和方法响应。您可以将集成请求中的所有数据获取到集成响应中，除了状态代码，因为 API Gateway 为您管理它。

## 参考资源
- [REST API 在 API Gateway 中的模拟集成](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-mock-integration.html)
- [使用 API Gateway 控制台启用模拟集成](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-mock-integration-console.html)
- [设置 REST API 集成 - 集成类型](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-integration-types.html)

en.question: A developer is migrating an application to Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The developer migrates the application to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) with an EKS cluster. As part of the application migration to a new backend, the developer creates a new AWS account. The developer makes configuration changes to the application to point the application to the new AWS account and to use new backend resources. The developer successfully tests the changes within the application by deploying the pipeline. The Docker image build and the pipeline deployment are successful, but the application is still connecting to the old backend. The developer finds that the application's configuration is still referencing the original EKS cluster and not referencing the new backend resources. Which reason can explain why the application is not connecting to the new resources?

options.A: The developer did not successfully create the new AWS account.
options.B: The developer added a new tag to the Docker image.
options.C: The developer did not update the Docker image tag to a new version.
options.D: The developer pushed the changes to a new Docker image tag.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A developer migrated an app to Amazon EKS using container images stored in Amazon ECR. They created a new AWS account, modified the application configuration to point to the new backend resources, and successfully ran the CI/CD pipeline (Docker build + deploy succeeded). However, the running application is still connecting to the **old backend / old EKS cluster** configuration.

The question asks: **why did the new configuration not take effect?**

## Correct Answer: C — The developer did not update the Docker image tag to a new version

When a Kubernetes Deployment references an image such as `123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/my-app:v1`, the kubelet decides whether to re-pull the image based on the **image reference (repository:tag or digest)** and the `imagePullPolicy`.

- If the developer rebuilt the image with the new configuration but pushed it under the **same tag** that was already referenced by the running pods, Kubernetes will not see any change in the Deployment spec, so it will not roll out new pods. The existing pods (with the old configuration baked into the old image layers cached on the node) keep running. Updating the image tag is a powerful and straightforward method to trigger Kubernetes to pull a new version of an image. By modifying the tag associated with the image, Kubernetes recognizes it as a distinct image and initiates the process of pulling the updated version.
- If you create a Deployment with an image whose tag is not :latest, and later update that Deployment's image to a :latest tag, the imagePullPolicy field will not change to Always. You must manually change the pull policy of any object after its initial creation. Without `imagePullPolicy: Always` and without a tag change, kubelet uses the cached image on the node.
- To accomplish this, we simply modify the tag value in the Deployment definition to 2.1.0... Kubernetes detects the change in the image tag. It recognizes that the image tag has been updated to 2.1.0 and initiates the process of pulling the new version of the image from the container registry. Once the updated image is successfully pulled, Kubernetes automatically applies the changes to the running pods associated with the Deployment, ensuring that the application is now utilizing the latest image version.

So the symptom — pipeline succeeds, image builds, but pods still run the old configuration pointing at the old backend — is the classic signature of **the image tag not being incremented**, so the Deployment manifest is unchanged and Kubernetes never rolls the pods.

## Why the other options are wrong

**A. The developer did not successfully create the new AWS account.**
The question states the developer created the new account and successfully tested the pipeline; the Docker build and deployment succeeded. The failure mode (old backend still in use) is *runtime configuration*, not account provisioning. There is no AWS service behavior tying "new account" to a silent fallback to the old account.

**B. The developer added a new tag to the Docker image.**
Adding a new tag would actually **help**: pushing under a new tag and updating the Deployment's image reference would force Kubernetes to roll out new pods using the updated image. This is the opposite of the observed problem.

**D. The developer pushed the changes to a new Docker image tag.**
Same reasoning as B — pushing a new tag is part of the *correct* workflow. If the Deployment manifest was also updated to reference that new tag, the pods would have rolled out with the new configuration. Pushing a new tag alone is not a cause of failure; the failure scenario is precisely the *absence* of a new tag (or of updating the manifest's tag reference).

## Key takeaway

In EKS/ECR CI/CD pipelines, simply rebuilding and pushing an image (especially under the same tag like `:latest`) does not guarantee that new pods will run the new code. Best practice is to use **immutable, versioned tags** (or image digests) and update the Deployment's `image:` field to the new tag so Kubernetes performs a rolling update.

### References
- [Kubernetes - Images / imagePullPolicy](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/images/)
- [Pushing a Docker image to Amazon ECR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/docker-push-ecr-image.html)
- [Amazon ECR image tag mutability](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-tag-mutability.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在将应用程序迁移到 Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)。该开发人员将应用程序迁移到 Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) 及其 EKS 集群。作为应用程序迁移到新后端的一部分，开发人员创建了一个新的 AWS 账户。开发人员对应用程序进行了配置更改，使其指向新的 AWS 账户并使用新的后端资源。开发人员通过部署流水线成功测试了应用程序中的更改。Docker 镜像构建和流水线部署均成功，但应用程序仍然连接到旧的后端。开发人员发现应用程序的配置仍然引用原始 EKS 集群，而不是引用新的后端资源。以下哪个原因可以解释应用程序无法连接到新资源的原因？

options.A: 开发人员未能成功创建新的 AWS 账户。
options.B: 开发者向 Docker 镜像添加了一个新标签。
options.C: 开发人员没有将 Docker 镜像标签更新到新版本。
options.D: 开发人员将更改推送到新的 Docker 镜像标签。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

一位开发人员将应用迁移到 Amazon EKS，使用存储在 Amazon ECR 中的容器镜像。他们创建了一个新的 AWS 账户，修改了应用配置以指向新的后端资源，并成功运行了 CI/CD 管道（Docker 构建 + 部署成功）。然而，运行中的应用仍然连接到**旧的后端 / 旧 EKS 集群**配置。

问题要求：**为什么新配置没有生效？**

## 正确答案：C — 开发人员没有将 Docker 镜像标签更新为新版本

当 Kubernetes Deployment 引用镜像（如 `123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/my-app:v1`）时，kubelet 根据**镜像引用（repository:tag 或 digest）**和 `imagePullPolicy` 决定是否重新拉取镜像。

- 如果开发人员使用新配置重建镜像，但以**相同标签**推送到已被运行 Pod 引用的仓库，Kubernetes 将看不到 Deployment 规范的任何变化，因此不会推出新 Pod。现有 Pod（其中旧配置烘烤在节点上缓存的旧镜像层中）继续运行。更新镜像标签是触发 Kubernetes 拉取新镜像版本的强大直接方法。通过修改与镜像关联的标签，Kubernetes 将其识别为不同的镜像并启动拉取更新版本的过程。
- 如果使用非 :latest 标签的镜像创建 Deployment，之后将该 Deployment 的镜像更新为 :latest 标签，imagePullPolicy 字段不会更改为 Always。创建对象后，必须手动更改任何对象的拉取策略。在没有 `imagePullPolicy: Always` 且没有标签更改的情况下，kubelet 使用节点上的缓存镜像。
- 为此，我们只需修改 Deployment 定义中的标签值为 2.1.0...Kubernetes 检测到镜像标签的变化。它认识到镜像标签已更新为 2.1.0 并启动从容器仓库拉取新镜像版本的过程。成功拉取更新镜像后，Kubernetes 自动将更改应用到与 Deployment 关联的运行 Pod，确保应用现在使用最新镜像版本。

因此，该症状——管道成功、镜像已构建，但 Pod 仍运行指向旧后端的旧配置——是**镜像标签未递增**的典型特征，所以 Deployment 清单未变化，Kubernetes 永远不会滚动更新 Pod。

## 其他选项为什么错误

**A. 开发人员没有成功创建新的 AWS 账户。**
问题中明确说明开发人员创建了新账户并成功测试了管道；Docker 构建和部署成功。失败模式（旧后端仍在使用）是*运行时配置*，而非账户配置。没有 AWS 服务行为会导致"新账户"无声地回退到旧账户。

**B. 开发人员为 Docker 镜像添加了新标签。**
添加新标签实际上会**有帮助**：使用新标签推送并更新 Deployment 的镜像引用将强制 Kubernetes 使用更新镜像推出新 Pod。这与观察到的问题相反。

**D. 开发人员将更改推送到新的 Docker 镜像标签。**
与选项 B 相同的推理——推送新标签是*正确*工作流的一部分。如果 Deployment 清单也更新为引用该新标签，Pod 会使用新配置推出。推送新标签本身不是失败原因；失败场景恰恰是*缺少*新标签（或未更新清单的标签引用）。

## 关键要点

在 EKS/ECR CI/CD 管道中，仅重建和推送镜像（尤其是在相同标签如 `:latest` 下）不保证新 Pod 会运行新代码。最佳实践是使用**不可变、版本化标签**（或镜像摘要）并更新 Deployment 的 `image:` 字段为新标签，以便 Kubernetes 执行滚动更新。

### 参考资源
- [Kubernetes - Images / imagePullPolicy](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/images/)
- [将 Docker 镜像推送到 Amazon ECR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/docker-push-ecr-image.html)
- [Amazon ECR 镜像标签不变性](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-tag-mutability.html)

en.question: A developer is creating an application that reads and writes to multiple Amazon S3 buckets. The application will be deployed to an Amazon EC2 instance. The developer wants to make secure API requests from the EC2 instances without the need to manage the security credentials for the application. The developer needs to apply the principle of least privilege. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an IAM user. Create access keys and secret keys for the user. Associate the user with an IAM policy that allows s3:* permissions.
options.B: Associate the EC2 instance with an IAM role that has an IAM policy that allows s3:ListBucket and s3:*Object permissions for specific S3 buckets.
options.C: Associate the EC2 instance with an IAM role that has an AmazonS3FullAccess AWS managed policy.
options.D: Create a bucket policy on the S3 bucket that allows s3:ListBucket and s3:*Object permissions to the EC2 instance.

en.explanation:
## Scenario
A developer needs an EC2-hosted application to read/write to multiple specific S3 buckets without managing long-lived credentials, while applying least privilege.

## Correct Answer: B
Associate the EC2 instance with an IAM role whose policy grants only `s3:ListBucket` and `s3:*Object` permissions on the specific S3 buckets needed.

- Using an **IAM role attached to the EC2 instance** delivers temporary credentials automatically via the instance metadata service, so no static keys need to be managed. When you're building on an AWS compute service, such as Amazon EC2 or Lambda, AWS delivers the temporary credentials of an IAM role to that compute resource. Applications written using an AWS SDK will discover and use these temporary credentials to access AWS resources, and there is no need to distribute long lived credentials for an IAM user to your workloads.
- Scoping actions (`s3:ListBucket`, `s3:*Object`) and resources (specific bucket ARNs) follows least privilege. When creating IAM roles, associate least privilege IAM policies that restrict access to the specific API calls the application requires.

Example IAM policy:
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["s3:ListBucket"],
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:s3:::bucket-1",
        "arn:aws:s3:::bucket-2"
      ]
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:PutObject", "s3:DeleteObject"],
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:s3:::bucket-1/*",
        "arn:aws:s3:::bucket-2/*"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A. IAM user with access keys + `s3:*`**: Violates two requirements. (1) Access keys are long-lived credentials that must be managed/rotated and embedded on the EC2 instance — exactly what the question forbids. AWS explicitly recommends roles over IAM users for workloads on EC2. (2) `s3:*` grants every S3 action on every resource — far broader than least privilege. For applications running on AWS (Lambda, EC2, ECS), never use IAM users — use roles instead.

- **C. IAM role with `AmazonS3FullAccess` managed policy**: Uses a role (good), but the AWS-managed `AmazonS3FullAccess` policy grants all S3 actions on all buckets, which is excessive. AWS managed policies might not grant least-privilege permissions for your specific use cases because they are available for use by all AWS customers. As a result, we recommend that you reduce permissions further by defining customer managed policies that are specific to your use cases.

- **D. S3 bucket policy granting access to "the EC2 instance"**: An S3 bucket policy's `Principal` must be an IAM identity (user, role, account, or service) — you cannot specify an EC2 instance directly as a principal. Without an IAM role/user attached to the EC2, the application still has no credentials to sign API requests. Bucket policies alone do not provide credentials to the application.

## References
- [IAM roles for Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/iam-roles-for-amazon-ec2.html)
- [Use an IAM role to grant permissions to applications running on EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_use_switch-role-ec2.html)
- [Security best practices in IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在创建一个应用程序，该应用程序需要读写多个 Amazon S3 存储桶。该应用程序将部署到 Amazon EC2 实例上。开发人员希望从 EC2 实例发出安全的 API 请求，而无需管理应用程序的安全凭证。开发人员需要应用最小权限原则。哪种解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个 IAM 用户。为该用户创建访问密钥和秘密密钥。将该用户与允许 s3:* 权限的 IAM 策略关联起来。
options.B: 将 EC2 实例与具有 IAM 策略的 IAM 角色关联，该 IAM 策略允许对特定 S3 存储桶拥有 s3:ListBucket 和 s3:*Object 权限。
options.C: 将 EC2 实例与具有 AmazonS3FullAccess AWS 托管策略的 IAM 角色关联。
options.D: 在 S3 存储桶上创建存储桶策略，允许 EC2 实例拥有 s3:ListBucket 和 s3:*Object 权限。

zh.explanation:
## 场景
一个开发者需要在 EC2 托管的应用程序中读/写多个特定的 S3 存储桶，而无需管理长期凭证，同时应用最小权限原则。

## 正确答案：B
将 EC2 实例与一个 IAM 角色相关联，该角色的策略仅授予特定 S3 存储桶上的 `s3:ListBucket` 和 `s3:*Object` 权限。

- 使用**附加到 EC2 实例的 IAM 角色**通过实例元数据服务自动提供临时凭证，因此无需管理静态密钥。在 AWS 计算服务（如 Amazon EC2 或 Lambda）上构建时，AWS 会将 IAM 角色的临时凭证传递到该计算资源。使用 AWS SDK 编写的应用程序将发现并使用这些临时凭证来访问 AWS 资源，无需将 IAM 用户的长期凭证分发到工作负载。
- 限定操作（`s3:ListBucket`、`s3:*Object`）和资源（特定存储桶 ARN）遵循最小权限原则。创建 IAM 角色时，关联限制访问应用程序所需的特定 API 调用的最小权限 IAM 策略。

IAM 策略示例：
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["s3:ListBucket"],
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:s3:::bucket-1",
        "arn:aws:s3:::bucket-2"
      ]
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:PutObject", "s3:DeleteObject"],
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:s3:::bucket-1/*",
        "arn:aws:s3:::bucket-2/*"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## 其他选项为何错误

- **A. IAM 用户带访问密钥 + `s3:*`**：违反两项要求。(1) 访问密钥是长期凭证，必须进行管理/轮换并嵌入到 EC2 实例中——这正是问题所禁止的。AWS 明确建议对 EC2 上的工作负载使用角色而非 IAM 用户。(2) `s3:*` 授予每个资源上的所有 S3 操作权限——远超最小权限原则。对于在 AWS 上运行的应用程序（Lambda、EC2、ECS），切勿使用 IAM 用户——应改用角色。

- **C. IAM 角色带 `AmazonS3FullAccess` 托管策略**：使用角色（很好），但 AWS 托管的 `AmazonS3FullAccess` 策略授予所有存储桶上的所有 S3 操作权限，这过于宽泛。AWS 托管策略可能不会为特定用例授予最小权限，因为它们可供所有 AWS 客户使用。因此，我们建议通过定义特定于用例的客户托管策略来进一步减少权限。

- **D. S3 存储桶策略授予"EC2 实例"访问权限**：S3 存储桶策略的 `Principal` 必须是 IAM 身份（用户、角色、账户或服务）——不能直接将 EC2 实例指定为主体。没有附加到 EC2 的 IAM 角色/用户，应用程序仍然没有凭证来签署 API 请求。仅存储桶策略无法向应用程序提供凭证。

## 参考资料
- [Amazon EC2 的 IAM 角色](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/iam-roles-for-amazon-ec2.html)
- [使用 IAM 角色授予在 EC2 上运行的应用程序权限](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_use_switch-role-ec2.html)
- [IAM 中的安全最佳实践](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html)

en.question: A developer is writing an application that will retrieve sensitive data from a third-party system. The application will format the data into a PDF file. The PDF file could be more than 1 MB. The application will encrypt the data to disk by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). The application will decrypt the file when a user requests to download it. The retrieval and formatting portions of the application are complete. The developer needs to use the GenerateDataKey API to encrypt the PDF file so that the PDF file can be decrypted later. The developer needs to use an AWS KMS symmetric customer managed key for encryption. Which solutions will meet these requirements?

options.A: Write the encrypted key from the GenerateDataKey API to disk for later use. Use the plaintext key from the GenerateDataKey API and a symmetric encryption algorithm to encrypt the file.
options.B: Write the plain text key from the GenerateDataKey API to disk for later use. Use the encrypted key from the GenerateDataKey API and a symmetric encryption algorithm to encrypt the file.
options.C: Write the encrypted key from the GenerateDataKey API to disk for later use. Use the plaintext key from the GenerateDataKey API to encrypt the file by using the KMS Encrypt API.
options.D: Write the plain text key from the GenerateDataKey API to disk for later use. Use the encrypted key from the GenerateDataKey API to encrypt the file by using the KMS Encrypt API.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

The developer needs to encrypt a PDF file (>1 MB) using a KMS symmetric customer managed key, with the ability to decrypt later. The correct pattern here is **envelope encryption** using `GenerateDataKey`.

## Correct Answer: A

The standard envelope encryption workflow with `GenerateDataKey` is:

1. Call `GenerateDataKey` against the symmetric CMK. KMS returns two items: a **plaintext data key** and an **encrypted (CiphertextBlob) data key**.
2. Use the **plaintext data key** with a local symmetric encryption algorithm (e.g., AES-256 via OpenSSL or a crypto library) to encrypt the PDF.
3. **Store the encrypted data key** alongside the encrypted PDF on disk. Erase the plaintext data key from memory.
4. To decrypt later, send the encrypted data key to `KMS Decrypt`, get the plaintext data key back, and decrypt the file locally.

This matches Option A exactly. Per AWS docs: Use the GenerateDataKey operation to get a data key. Use the plaintext data key (in the Plaintext field of the response) to encrypt your data outside of AWS KMS. Then erase the plaintext data key from memory. Store the encrypted data key (in the CiphertextBlob field of the response) with the encrypted data.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

**Option B — Write plaintext key to disk; use encrypted key to encrypt the file:**
This is wrong on two counts. First, you must **never persist the plaintext data key to disk** — it defeats the purpose of KMS, which is to keep the plaintext key ephemeral and protected. Second, the encrypted data key is ciphertext under the CMK; it cannot be used as an encryption key for symmetric encryption — it must first be decrypted by KMS.

**Option C — Write encrypted key to disk; use plaintext key with the KMS Encrypt API:**
The storage half is correct, but the encryption half is wrong. The KMS `Encrypt` API encrypts plaintext of up to 4,096 bytes using a KMS key... You can use this operation to encrypt small amounts of arbitrary data, such as a personal identifier or database password, or other sensitive information. A PDF >1 MB exceeds this 4 KB limit, so calling `Encrypt` on the file fails. Additionally, `KMS Encrypt` uses the CMK directly inside KMS — it does not take a caller-supplied "plaintext data key" as the encryption key. The whole point of envelope encryption is to encrypt large data **locally** with the data key, not via the KMS API. Data size. KMS can only handle 4KB payloads directly. Envelope encryption has no size limit.

**Option D — Write plaintext key to disk; use encrypted key with KMS Encrypt API:**
Combines both mistakes from B and C. Writing the plaintext key to disk violates KMS best practices, and the encrypted data key is not usable as an input key to `KMS Encrypt` (which uses a KMS CMK identified by KeyId, not a caller-supplied key).

## Key Takeaway

Envelope encryption pattern: **plaintext data key encrypts the data locally; the encrypted data key is persisted alongside the ciphertext.** Plaintext data keys are never written to disk.

## References

- [AWS KMS GenerateDataKey API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/APIReference/API_GenerateDataKey.html)
- [AWS KMS Encrypt API Reference (4 KB limit)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/APIReference/API_Encrypt.html)
- [Generate data keys – AWS KMS Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/data-keys.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在编写一个应用程序，该应用程序将从第三方系统检索敏感数据。该应用程序会将数据格式化为 PDF 文件。PDF 文件可能超过 1 MB。应用程序将使用 AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) 对数据进行加密并保存到磁盘。当用户请求下载文件时，应用程序将解密该文件。应用程序的检索和格式化部分已完成。开发人员需要使用 GenerateDataKey API 对 PDF 文件进行加密，以便稍后可以解密该文件。开发人员需要使用 AWS KMS 对称客户管理密钥进行加密。哪些解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 将 GenerateDataKey API 生成的加密密钥写入磁盘以备后用。使用 GenerateDataKey API 生成的明文密钥和对称加密算法对文件进行加密。
options.B: 将 GenerateDataKey API 返回的明文密钥写入磁盘以备后用。使用 GenerateDataKey API 返回的加密密钥和对称加密算法对文件进行加密。
options.C: 将 GenerateDataKey API 生成的加密密钥写入磁盘以备后用。使用 GenerateDataKey API 生成的明文密钥，通过 KMS Encrypt API 对文件进行加密。
options.D: 将 GenerateDataKey API 生成的明文密钥写入磁盘以备后用。使用 GenerateDataKey API 生成的加密密钥，通过 KMS Encrypt API 对文件进行加密。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

开发人员需要使用 KMS 对称客户托管密钥加密 PDF 文件（>1 MB），并且需要能够在以后解密。这里的正确模式是使用 `GenerateDataKey` 的**信封加密**。

## 正确答案：A

使用 `GenerateDataKey` 的标准信封加密工作流程是：

1. 对对称 CMK 调用 `GenerateDataKey`。KMS 返回两项：**明文数据密钥**和**加密的（CiphertextBlob）数据密钥**。
2. 使用**明文数据密钥**和本地对称加密算法（例如通过 OpenSSL 或加密库的 AES-256）加密 PDF。
3. **将加密的数据密钥**与加密的 PDF 一起存储在磁盘上。从内存中清除明文数据密钥。
4. 要在以后解密，将加密的数据密钥发送到 `KMS Decrypt`，获得明文数据密钥，然后在本地解密文件。

这与选项 A 完全匹配。根据 AWS 文档：使用 GenerateDataKey 操作获取数据密钥。使用明文数据密钥（响应的 Plaintext 字段中）在 AWS KMS 外部加密数据。然后从内存中清除明文数据密钥。将加密的数据密钥（响应的 CiphertextBlob 字段中）与加密的数据一起存储。

## 为什么其他选项错误

**选项 B — 将明文密钥写入磁盘；使用加密密钥加密文件：**
这在两个方面都是错误的。首先，你**必须永远不要将明文数据密钥持久化到磁盘** — 这违反了 KMS 的目的，即保持明文密钥短暂且受保护。其次，加密的数据密钥是 CMK 下的密文；它不能用作对称加密的加密密钥 — 必须先由 KMS 解密。

**选项 C — 将加密密钥写入磁盘；使用明文密钥调用 KMS Encrypt API：**
存储部分是正确的，但加密部分是错误的。KMS `Encrypt` API 使用 KMS 密钥加密最多 4,096 字节的明文...你可以使用此操作加密少量任意数据，例如个人标识符或数据库密码或其他敏感信息。大于 1 MB 的 PDF 超过了这个 4 KB 的限制，因此对文件调用 `Encrypt` 会失败。此外，`KMS Encrypt` 在 KMS 内部直接使用 CMK — 它不会将调用方提供的"明文数据密钥"作为加密密钥。信封加密的要点是**在本地**使用数据密钥加密大型数据，而不是通过 KMS API。数据大小。KMS 只能直接处理 4KB 的负载。信封加密没有大小限制。

**选项 D — 将明文密钥写入磁盘；使用加密密钥调用 KMS Encrypt API：**
结合了选项 B 和 C 的两个错误。将明文密钥写入磁盘违反了 KMS 最佳实践，而且加密的数据密钥不能用作 `KMS Encrypt` 的输入密钥（后者使用由 KeyId 标识的 KMS CMK，而不是调用方提供的密钥）。

## 关键要点

信封加密模式：**明文数据密钥在本地加密数据；加密的数据密钥与密文一起持久化。** 明文数据密钥永远不会写入磁盘。

## 参考资源

- [AWS KMS GenerateDataKey API 参考](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/APIReference/API_GenerateDataKey.html)
- [AWS KMS Encrypt API 参考（4 KB 限制）](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/APIReference/API_Encrypt.html)
- [生成数据密钥 – AWS KMS 开发人员指南](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/data-keys.html)

en.question: A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances open connections to an Amazon RDS for SQL Server database. A developer needs to store and access the credentials and wants to automatically rotate the credentials. The developer does not want to store the credentials for the database in the code. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure way?

options.A: Create an IAM role that has permissions to access the database. Attach the IAM role to the EC2 instances.
options.B: Store the credentials as secrets in AWS Secrets Manager. Create an AWS Lambda function to update the secrets and the database. Retrieve the credentials from Secrets Manager as needed.
options.C: Store the credentials in an encrypted text file in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the EC2 instance launch template to download the credentials from Amazon S3 as the instance launches. Create an AWS Lambda function to update the secrets and the database.
options.D: Store the credentials in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Configure an Amazon CloudWatch Events rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to periodically update the secrets and database.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

An application on EC2 connects to RDS for SQL Server. The developer needs to:
1. Securely store DB credentials (not in code)
2. Automatically rotate the credentials
3. Retrieve credentials securely from EC2

## Correct Answer: B

**AWS Secrets Manager** is the AWS-native service designed exactly for this use case. Secrets Manager offers built-in integrations for rotating credentials for all Amazon RDS databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, Microsoft SQL Server, MariaDB, and Amazon Aurora).

When you enable rotation, Secrets Manager creates a Lambda function and attaches an IAM role to this function to execute rotations on a schedule you define. The Lambda function is what updates both the secret in Secrets Manager and the password in the RDS for SQL Server database — exactly what option B describes.

The application on EC2 retrieves credentials at runtime via the Secrets Manager API (using an IAM role on the EC2 instance), so to retrieve secrets, employees replace plaintext secrets with a call to Secrets Manager APIs, eliminating the need to hard-code secrets in source code or update configuration files and redeploy code when secrets are rotated.

AWS provides a pre-built rotation Lambda specifically for SQL Server: the [SecretsManagerRDSSQLServerRotationSingleUser](https://github.com/aws-samples/aws-secrets-manager-rotation-lambdas/blob/master/SecretsManagerRDSSQLServerRotationSingleUser/lambda_function.py) template, which uses the single-user rotation scheme to rotate an RDS SQL Server user credential. This rotation scheme logs into the database as the user and rotates the user's own password.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

**A. IAM role with database access permissions attached to EC2** — IAM database authentication is supported for **RDS MySQL, PostgreSQL, and MariaDB only**. It is **not supported for RDS for SQL Server**, so an IAM role cannot replace SQL Server credentials. Additionally, this option does not address rotation of stored credentials at all.

**C. Encrypted text file in S3, downloaded at instance launch** — This is insecure and operationally fragile:
- Credentials sit on the instance filesystem (broader attack surface than retrieving on demand from Secrets Manager).
- Credentials are only fetched at launch time, so rotated credentials wouldn't propagate to running instances without restart.
- There is no native, managed rotation workflow tied to S3; you would have to build everything yourself. Secrets Manager already provides this securely.

**D. Credentials stored in DynamoDB, rotated by Lambda via CloudWatch Events** — DynamoDB is not designed for secret storage:
- No automatic encryption-context isolation, no fine-grained version staging (AWSCURRENT / AWSPENDING) like Secrets Manager.
- No built-in rotation framework — you would need to write all rotation, staging, and rollback logic yourself.
- Secrets Manager is the purpose-built, more secure managed service for this exact requirement.

## Key Documentation
- [AWS Secrets Manager rotation function templates](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/reference_available-rotation-templates.html)
- [Set up automatic rotation for Amazon RDS secrets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotate-secrets_turn-on-for-db.html)
- [Rotate Amazon RDS database credentials automatically with AWS Secrets Manager](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/rotate-amazon-rds-database-credentials-automatically-with-aws-secrets-manager/)

zh.question: 一家公司在 Amazon EC2 实例上运行一个应用程序。这些 EC2 实例会连接到 Amazon RDS for SQL Server 数据库。开发人员需要存储和访问数据库凭证，并希望自动轮换这些凭证。开发人员不希望将数据库凭证存储在代码中。哪种解决方案能够以最安全的方式满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个具有数据库访问权限的 IAM 角色。将该 IAM 角色附加到 EC2 实例。
options.B: 将凭证作为密钥存储在 AWS Secrets Manager 中。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数来更新密钥和数据库。根据需要从 Secrets Manager 中检索凭证。
options.C: 将凭证存储在 Amazon S3 存储桶中的加密文本文件中。配置 EC2 实例启动模板，以便在实例启动时从 Amazon S3 下载凭证。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数来更新密钥和数据库。
options.D: 将凭证存储在 Amazon DynamoDB 表中。配置 Amazon CloudWatch Events 规则，以调用 AWS Lambda 函数定期更新密钥和数据库。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

EC2 上的应用程序连接到 RDS for SQL Server。开发人员需要：
1. 安全地存储数据库凭证（不在代码中）
2. 自动轮换凭证
3. 从 EC2 安全地检索凭证

## 正确答案：B

**AWS Secrets Manager** 是为这个用例专门设计的 AWS 原生服务。Secrets Manager 为所有 Amazon RDS 数据库（MySQL、PostgreSQL、Oracle、Microsoft SQL Server、MariaDB 和 Amazon Aurora）提供内置集成以轮换凭证。

启用轮换时，Secrets Manager 创建一个 Lambda 函数并将 IAM 角色附加到此函数，以按照您定义的计划执行轮换。Lambda 函数会更新 Secrets Manager 中的凭证和 RDS for SQL Server 数据库中的密码 — 正是选项 B 所描述的内容。

EC2 上的应用程序通过 Secrets Manager API 在运行时检索凭证（使用 EC2 实例上的 IAM 角色），因此为了检索凭证，员工用对 Secrets Manager API 的调用替换纯文本凭证，无需在源代码中硬编码凭证或在轮换凭证时更新配置文件并重新部署代码。

AWS 为 SQL Server 提供了预构建的轮换 Lambda：[SecretsManagerRDSSQLServerRotationSingleUser](https://github.com/aws-samples/aws-secrets-manager-rotation-lambdas/blob/master/SecretsManagerRDSSQLServerRotationSingleUser/lambda_function.py) 模板，使用单用户轮换方案轮换 RDS SQL Server 用户凭证。此轮换方案以该用户身份登录数据库并轮换该用户自己的密码。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

**A. 附加到 EC2 的具有数据库访问权限的 IAM 角色** — IAM 数据库身份验证仅支持 **RDS MySQL、PostgreSQL 和 MariaDB**。**不支持 RDS for SQL Server**，因此 IAM 角色无法替换 SQL Server 凭证。此外，此选项根本不涉及存储凭证的轮换。

**C. S3 中的加密文本文件，在实例启动时下载** — 这既不安全又在操作上很脆弱：
- 凭证位于实例文件系统中（攻击面比从 Secrets Manager 按需检索要宽）。
- 凭证仅在启动时获取一次，因此轮换后的凭证不会传播到运行中的实例，除非重启。
- 没有与 S3 相关的原生、托管式轮换工作流；您必须自己构建所有内容。Secrets Manager 已经安全地提供了这一切。

**D. 存储在 DynamoDB 中的凭证，通过 CloudWatch Events 由 Lambda 轮换** — DynamoDB 不是为凭证存储而设计的：
- 没有自动加密上下文隔离，没有像 Secrets Manager 那样的细粒度版本暂存（AWSCURRENT / AWSPENDING）。
- 没有内置轮换框架 — 您需要自己编写所有轮换、暂存和回滚逻辑。
- Secrets Manager 是为这个确切需求而专门构建的、更加安全的托管服务。

## 关键文档
- [AWS Secrets Manager 轮换函数模板](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/reference_available-rotation-templates.html)
- [为 Amazon RDS 凭证设置自动轮换](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotate-secrets_turn-on-for-db.html)
- [使用 AWS Secrets Manager 自动轮换 Amazon RDS 数据库凭证](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/rotate-amazon-rds-database-credentials-automatically-with-aws-secrets-manager/)

en.question: A company wants to test its web application more frequently. The company deploys the application by using a separate AWS CloudFormation stack for each environment. The company deploys the same CloudFormation template to each stack as the application progresses through the development lifecycle. A developer needs to build in notifications for the quality assurance (QA) team. The developer wants the notifications to occur for new deployments in the final preproduction environment. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the QA team to the Amazon SNS topic. Update the CloudFormation stack options to point to the SNS topic in the pre- production environment.
options.B: Create an AWS Lambda function that notifies the QA team. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function on the default event bus. Filter the events on the CloudFormation service and on the CloudFormation stack Amazon Resource Name (ARN).
options.C: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that monitors the metrics from CloudFormation. Filter the metrics on the stack name and the stack status. Configure the CloudWatch alarm to notify the QA team.
options.D: Create an AWS Lambda function that notifies the QA team. Configure the event source mapping to receive events from CloudFormation. Specify the filtering values to limit invocations to the desired CloudFormation stack.

en.explanation:
# CloudFormation Stack Notifications to QA Team

## Scenario
A company deploys an application across multiple environments using separate CloudFormation stacks. The developer needs the QA team to be notified specifically when new deployments occur in the **final preproduction environment**.

## Correct Answer: A

CloudFormation has **native, built-in integration with Amazon SNS** for stack event notifications. When you create or update a stack, you can specify one or more SNS topic ARNs in the stack options (the `NotificationARNs` parameter, exposed as the "SNS topic ARN" / "Notification options" field in the console, or `--notification-arns` on the CLI). CloudFormation will then publish all stack lifecycle events (CREATE_IN_PROGRESS, CREATE_COMPLETE, UPDATE_COMPLETE, ROLLBACK_*, etc.) to that topic.

The solution is:
1. Create an SNS topic.
2. Subscribe the QA team (e.g., email endpoints) to the topic.
3. Configure the **preproduction** CloudFormation stack only (via stack options) to point to that SNS topic ARN.

Because only the preproduction stack is configured with the topic, the QA team only receives notifications for that environment — exactly what the requirement asks for.

```bash
aws cloudformation update-stack \
  --stack-name preprod-app-stack \
  --use-previous-template \
  --notification-arns arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789012:qa-deploy-topic
```

This native integration is documented and even validated by AWS Config rule [`cloudformation-stack-notification-check`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/cloudformation-stack-notification-check.html), which "checks if your CloudFormation stacks send event notifications to an Amazon SNS topic."

## Why the Other Options Are Incorrect

**B. Lambda + EventBridge rule on default bus filtering on stack ARN** — This works technically (CloudFormation events are published to EventBridge as `aws.cloudformation` / `CloudFormation Stack Status Change`), but it is unnecessarily complex compared with the native CloudFormation→SNS integration described in option A.
