Enhanced User Experience: DynamoDB facilitates rapid session state retrieval, ensuring minimal latency and uninterrupted user connections.

AWS provides first-class session-state providers (e.g., for ASP.NET and PHP) that plug directly into DynamoDB. The DynamoDB Session Handler is a custom session handler for PHP that allows developers to use Amazon DynamoDB as a session store. Using DynamoDB for session storage alleviates issues that occur with session handling in a distributed web application by moving sessions off of the local file system and into a shared location. DynamoDB is fast, scalable, easy to setup, and handles replication of your data automatically.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

**A. Sticky sessions with an ELB target group** — Sticky sessions only ensure that a client is *routed* to the same EC2 instance for the duration of the session; the session data still lives on that one instance. Sticky session is a feature of the Elastic Load Balancer service that binds a user's session to a specific application instance, so that all requests coming from the user during the session will be sent to the same virtual server. If that instance fails, the session data is lost — which is exactly the failure mode the question asks us to prevent.

**B. Use Amazon SQS to save session data** — SQS is a message queue, not a durable key/value session store. Messages have a maximum retention of 14 days, are designed to be consumed and deleted, and there is no efficient way to look up "the session for user X" by key. SQS is not a session-state service.

**D. ELB connection draining (deregistration delay)** — Connection draining only allows *in-flight* requests to complete on an instance that is being deregistered or is unhealthy before the LB stops sending new traffic. It does nothing to persist or replicate session data; if the instance crashes, any in-memory session is gone.

## Reference Architecture

Place EC2 instances behind an ELB (often in an Auto Scaling group across multiple AZs) and have the application read/write session state to a DynamoDB table. Create an Auto Scaling Group (ASG) in AWS, attach instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB), and externalize session state using DynamoDB. By the end of this exercise, you'll have a fault-tolerant, scalable web application where users' session states persist across server restarts.

## References
- [Managing ASP.NET Session State With DynamoDB (AWS Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/managing-aspnet-session-state-with-dynamodb/)
- [Managing ASP.NET session state with Amazon DynamoDB — AWS SDK for .NET Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-net/v3/developer-guide/dynamodb-session-net-sdk.html)
- [Using the DynamoDB session handler — AWS SDK for PHP v3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-php/v3/developer-guide/service_dynamodb-session-handler.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在设计一个容错环境，该环境会保存客户端会话。如果 Amazon EC2 实例发生故障，开发人员如何确保不会丢失任何会话？

options.A: 使用 Elastic Load Balancer 目标组的粘性会话。
options.B: 使用 Amazon SQS 保存会话数据。
options.C: 使用 Amazon DynamoDB 执行可扩展的会话处理。
options.D: 使用 Elastic Load Balancer 连接清空功能停止向故障实例发送请求。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

开发人员需要设计一个容错架构，在 EC2 实例故障时客户端会话数据仍能保存。关键要求是**EC2 实例故障时不丢失会话**，这意味着会话状态必须存储在任何单个 EC2 实例*之外*的持久、共享、高可用数据存储中。

## 正确答案：C — 使用 Amazon DynamoDB 执行可扩展会话处理

在 DynamoDB 中存储会话状态将其从 EC2 实例外化，因此任何单个实例的故障都不会破坏会话数据。开发新的 ASP.NET 应用程序时，一种常见的方法是将会话数据存储在内存中。不幸的是，这种方法的扩展性不太好；一旦应用程序超过单个 Web 服务器，会话状态必须在服务器之间共享。在多个 Web 服务器之间共享会话状态的常见解决方案是使用 SQL Server 设置专用会话状态服务器。当然，这种方法有某些缺点：您必须管理另一台计算机，会话状态服务器是单点故障，会话状态服务器可能成为性能瓶颈。Amazon DynamoDB 是 Amazon Web Services (AWS) 推出的新 NoSQL 数据库存储，旨在解决这些缺点。

DynamoDB 的设计目的是解决这个问题：Amazon DynamoDB 是会话持久化的高可用、可扩展解决方案。作为完全托管的 NoSQL 数据库服务，DynamoDB 在各种负载下提供可靠的性能。使用 DynamoDB 进行会话管理的关键优势包括：高可用性：DynamoDB 的多 AZ 部署确保跨地理位置的数据复制，最大限度降低数据丢失风险。自动可扩展性：它调整吞吐量以适应流量波动，保持一致的性能。增强的用户体验：DynamoDB 便于快速检索会话状态，确保最小的延迟和不间断的用户连接。

AWS 提供第一方会话状态提供程序（例如针对 ASP.NET 和 PHP），可直接插入 DynamoDB。DynamoDB Session Handler 是 PHP 的自定义会话处理程序，允许开发人员使用 Amazon DynamoDB 作为会话存储。使用 DynamoDB 进行会话存储解决了分布式 Web 应用程序中会话处理出现的问题，通过将会话从本地文件系统移到共享位置。DynamoDB 速度快、可扩展、易于设置，并自动处理数据的复制。

## 其他选项为什么错误

**A. 使用 ELB 目标组的粘性会话** — 粘性会话仅确保在会话期间客户端*路由*到同一 EC2 实例；会话数据仍然位于那一个实例上。粘性会话是弹性负载均衡器服务的一项功能，将用户的会话绑定到特定应用程序实例，以便在会话期间来自用户的所有请求都被发送到同一虚拟服务器。如果该实例故障，会话数据将丢失——这正是题目要求我们防止的故障模式。

**B. 使用 Amazon SQS 保存会话数据** — SQS 是消息队列，而不是持久的键/值会话存储。消息的最大保留期为 14 天，设计用于被消费和删除，并且没有有效的方法来按键查询"用户 X 的会话"。SQS 不是会话状态服务。

**D. ELB 连接清空（注销延迟）** — 连接清空仅允许*在途*请求在被注销或不健康的实例上完成，然后负载均衡器停止发送新流量。它对持久化或复制会话数据没有任何作用；如果实例崩溃，任何内存中的会话都会消失。

## 参考架构

将 EC2 实例放置在 ELB 后面（通常在跨多个 AZ 的自动扩展组中），并让应用程序读取/写入会话状态到 DynamoDB 表。在 AWS 中创建自动扩展组 (ASG)，将实例附加到应用程序负载均衡器 (ALB) 后面，并使用 DynamoDB 外化会话状态。完成本练习后，您将拥有一个容错、可扩展的 Web 应用程序，其中用户的会话状态在服务器重启后仍能保持。

## 参考资源
- [Managing ASP.NET Session State With DynamoDB (AWS Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/managing-aspnet-session-state-with-dynamodb/)
- [Managing ASP.NET session state with Amazon DynamoDB — AWS SDK for .NET Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-net/v3/developer-guide/dynamodb-session-net-sdk.html)
- [Using the DynamoDB session handler — AWS SDK for PHP v3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-php/v3/developer-guide/service_dynamodb-session-handler.html)

en.question: A developer is creating AWS CloudFormation templates to manage an application's deployment in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) through AWS CodeDeploy. The developer wants to automatically deploy new versions of the application to a percentage of users before the new version becomes available for all users. How should the developer manage the deployment of the new version?

options.A: Modify the CloudFormation template to include a Transform section and the AWS::CodeDeploy::BlueGreen hook.
options.B: Deploy the new version in a new CloudFormation stack. After testing is complete, update the application's DNS records for the new stack.
options.C: Run CloudFormation stack updates on the application stack to deploy new application versions when they are available.
options.D: Create a nested stack for the new version. Include a Transform section and the AWS::CodeDeploy::BlueGreen hook.

en.explanation:
# ECS Blue/Green Deployment with CloudFormation and CodeDeploy

## Scenario
The developer manages an ECS application via CloudFormation and uses CodeDeploy for deployments. They want to **automatically shift a percentage of traffic** to a new version (canary/linear) before exposing it to all users — this is the classic **blue/green deployment** pattern. The question asks how to model this within the CloudFormation template.

## Correct Answer: A

To enable ECS blue/green deployments through CodeDeploy directly from CloudFormation, you must add **two pieces** to the template:

1. A `Transform` section referencing `AWS::CodeDeployBlueGreen`
2. A `Hooks` section that invokes the `AWS::CodeDeploy::BlueGreen` hook (which defines traffic routing — Canary, Linear, or AllAtOnce — plus stabilization settings)

To perform CodeDeploy blue/green deployments on ECS using CloudFormation, you include a Hooks section that describes an AWS::CodeDeploy::BlueGreen hook and a Transform section that specifies the AWS::CodeDeployBlueGreen transform.

When the stack is later updated with a new task definition / task set, CloudFormation generates the green application environment resources and shifts traffic based on the specified traffic routing parameters; if an error occurs before the green deployment is finalized, CloudFormation rolls the stack back to its state before the green deployment was initiated.

The transform must be declared at the top level: you must declare it at the top level of your CloudFormation template — you can't use AWS::CodeDeployBlueGreen as a transform embedded in any other template section.

Example skeleton:
```yaml
Transform:
  - AWS::CodeDeployBlueGreen
Hooks:
  CodeDeployBlueGreenHook:
    Type: AWS::CodeDeploy::BlueGreen
    Properties:
      TrafficRoutingConfig:
        Type: TimeBasedCanary   # or TimeBasedLinear / AllAtOnce
        TimeBasedCanary:
          StepPercentage: 15
          BakeTimeMins: 5
      ...
```

## Why the other options are wrong

- **B. New stack + DNS swap.** This is a manual stack-level blue/green pattern. It doesn't leverage CodeDeploy's built-in percentage-based traffic shifting and provides no automated, gradual rollout to a percentage of users — it's an all-at-once DNS cutover requiring manual orchestration.

- **C. Plain CloudFormation stack updates.** Without the `AWS::CodeDeployBlueGreen` transform and hook, a stack update to an ECS service performs the default rolling update controller behavior, not a CodeDeploy blue/green deployment with canary/linear traffic shifting. There is no mechanism to gradually expose new versions to a percentage of users.

- **D. Nested stack with the transform and hook.** Nested stacks are explicitly **not supported** for this feature. AWS CloudFormation natively supports performing Blue/Green deployments on ECS using a CodeDeploy Blue/Green hook, but this feature comes with additional considerations including the inability to use CloudFormation nested stacks. The transform must live at the top level of the parent template, not inside a nested stack.

## References
- [Perform ECS blue/green deployments through CodeDeploy using CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/blue-green.html)
- [AWS::CodeDeployBlueGreen transform](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/transform-aws-codedeploybluegreen.html)
- [About blue/green deployments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/about-blue-green-deployments.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在创建 AWS CloudFormation 模板，以通过 AWS CodeDeploy 管理应用程序在 Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) 中的部署。该开发人员希望在新版本面向所有用户发布之前，自动将新版本部署给一部分用户。开发人员应该如何管理新版本的部署？

options.A: 修改 CloudFormation 模板，使其包含转换部分和 AWS::CodeDeploy::BlueGreen 钩子。
options.B: 将新版本部署到新的 CloudFormation 堆栈中。测试完成后，更新应用程序的 DNS 记录以适应新的堆栈。
options.C: 当有新的应用程序版本可用时，在应用程序堆栈上运行 CloudFormation 堆栈更新以部署新版本。
options.D: 为新版本创建一个嵌套堆栈。包含一个转换部分和 AWS::CodeDeploy::BlueGreen 钩子。

zh.explanation:
# ECS 蓝绿部署与 CloudFormation 和 CodeDeploy

## 场景
开发人员通过 CloudFormation 管理 ECS 应用程序，并使用 CodeDeploy 进行部署。他们希望**自动将一定比例的流量**转移到新版本（金丝雀/线性）后再将其暴露给所有用户——这是经典的**蓝绿部署**模式。问题要求在 CloudFormation 模板中如何建模这一点。

## 正确答案：A

要通过 CodeDeploy 从 CloudFormation 直接启用 ECS 蓝绿部署，必须在模板中添加**两个部分**：

1. 引用 `AWS::CodeDeployBlueGreen` 的 `Transform` 部分
2. 调用 `AWS::CodeDeploy::BlueGreen` 钩子的 `Hooks` 部分（该钩子定义流量路由——金丝雀、线性或全量——以及稳定化设置）

要使用 CloudFormation 在 ECS 上执行 CodeDeploy 蓝绿部署，您需要包含描述 AWS::CodeDeploy::BlueGreen 钩子的 Hooks 部分和指定 AWS::CodeDeployBlueGreen 转换的 Transform 部分。

当堆栈稍后更新为新任务定义/任务集时，CloudFormation 生成绿色应用程序环境资源，并根据指定的流量路由参数转移流量；如果在完成绿色部署之前发生错误，CloudFormation 会将堆栈回滚到绿色部署启动前的状态。

转换必须在顶级声明：您必须在 CloudFormation 模板的顶级声明它——不能将 AWS::CodeDeployBlueGreen 用作嵌入在任何其他模板部分中的转换。

示例骨架：
```yaml
Transform:
  - AWS::CodeDeployBlueGreen
Hooks:
  CodeDeployBlueGreenHook:
    Type: AWS::CodeDeploy::BlueGreen
    Properties:
      TrafficRoutingConfig:
        Type: TimeBasedCanary   # 或 TimeBasedLinear / AllAtOnce
        TimeBasedCanary:
          StepPercentage: 15
          BakeTimeMins: 5
      ...
```

## 其他选项为何错误

- **B. 新堆栈 + DNS 切换。** 这是一种手动的堆栈级蓝绿模式。它不利用 CodeDeploy 内置的基于百分比的流量转移，无法提供自动化的、逐步的版本发布到一定百分比的用户——它是一种需要手动编排的全量 DNS 切换。

- **C. 普通 CloudFormation 堆栈更新。** 不使用 `AWS::CodeDeployBlueGreen` 转换和钩子，对 ECS 服务的堆栈更新会执行默认的滚动更新控制器行为，而不是具有金丝雀/线性流量转移的 CodeDeploy 蓝绿部署。没有机制可以逐步将新版本暴露给一定百分比的用户。

- **D. 包含转换和钩子的嵌套堆栈。** 嵌套堆栈**不支持**此功能。AWS CloudFormation 原生支持使用 CodeDeploy 蓝绿钩子在 ECS 上执行蓝绿部署，但此功能存在额外注意事项，包括无法使用 CloudFormation 嵌套堆栈。转换必须位于父模板的顶级，而不是在嵌套堆栈内。

## 参考资源
- [通过 CloudFormation 使用 CodeDeploy 执行 ECS 蓝绿部署](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/blue-green.html)
- [AWS::CodeDeployBlueGreen 转换](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/transform-aws-codedeploybluegreen.html)
- [关于蓝绿部署](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/about-blue-green-deployments.html)

en.question: A developer has written a distributed application that uses microservices. The microservices are running on Amazon EC2 instances. Because of message volume, the developer is unable to match log output from each microservice to a specific transaction. The developer needs to analyze the message flow to debug the application. Which combination of steps should the developer take to meet this requirement? (Choose two.)

options.A: Download the AWS X-Ray daemon. Install the daemon on an EC2 instance. Ensure that the EC2 instance allows UDP traffic on port 2000.
options.B: Configure an interface VPC endpoint to allow traffic to reach the global AWS X-Ray daemon on TCP port 2000.
options.C: Enable AWS X-Ray. Configure Amazon CloudWatch to push logs to X-Ray.
options.D: Add the AWS X-Ray software development kit (SDK) to the microservices. Use X-Ray to trace requests that each microservice makes.
options.E: Set up Amazon CloudWatch metric streams to collect streaming data from the microservices.

en.explanation:
# Tracing Microservice Transactions with AWS X-Ray

## Scenario
A developer has microservices on EC2 that produce so many logs they can't correlate log lines back to a single end-to-end transaction. They need to trace the message flow across services for debugging. AWS X-Ray is purpose-built for this — it provides distributed tracing with trace IDs that follow a request through every microservice, producing a service map and per-segment timing.

## Correct Answers: A and D

### A. Install the X-Ray daemon on EC2 and allow UDP port 2000
The X-Ray SDK does not call the X-Ray API directly. Instead it emits segment documents over UDP to a local daemon, which buffers and uploads them. The AWS X-Ray daemon is a software application that listens for traffic on UDP port 2000, gathers raw segment data, and relays it to the AWS X-Ray API. The daemon works in conjunction with the AWS X-Ray SDKs and must be running so that data sent by the SDKs can reach the X-Ray service. When running on EC2, on Amazon EC2, the daemon uses the instance's instance profile role automatically, so installing the daemon and ensuring UDP/2000 is reachable (security group / local firewall) is required.

### D. Add the X-Ray SDK to the microservices
The SDK is what actually instruments each service so trace IDs propagate between calls. Your application uses the X-Ray SDK to instrument HTTP calls, database queries, and other operations. The SDK generates trace segments and sends them as UDP packets to the X-Ray daemon running on the same host. The daemon collects these segments, batches them, and forwards them to the X-Ray API over HTTPS. This is precisely what lets the developer correlate activity across microservices for one transaction.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

### B. Interface VPC endpoint for the "global" daemon on TCP port 2000
There is no "global AWS X-Ray daemon" — the daemon is software you run yourself on your compute. The SDK communicates with the local daemon over **UDP** port 2000, not TCP, and a VPC interface endpoint is used to reach the X-Ray *service API* privately, not the daemon. The AWS X-Ray daemon listens for traffic on UDP port 2000, gathers raw segment data, and relays it to the AWS X-Ray API.

### C. Enable X-Ray and configure CloudWatch to push logs to X-Ray
CloudWatch Logs cannot "push logs to X-Ray." X-Ray ingests trace segments produced by the X-Ray SDK/daemon (or OpenTelemetry/ADOT), not CloudWatch log events. This integration simply does not exist as described.

### E. CloudWatch metric streams from microservices
Metric streams continuously deliver CloudWatch *metrics* to destinations like Kinesis Data Firehose for monitoring/analytics dashboards. They produce numeric metric data, not per-request traces, and cannot be used to correlate a specific transaction across microservices.

## Reference Architecture
```
[Microservice + X-Ray SDK]  --UDP:2000-->  [X-Ray Daemon on EC2]  --HTTPS-->  [AWS X-Ray service]
```
IAM: attach the `AWSXRayDaemonWriteAccess` managed policy to the EC2 instance profile so the daemon can call `PutTraceSegments` / `PutTelemetryRecords`.

## Documentation
- [AWS X-Ray daemon](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-daemon.html)
- [Configuring the AWS X-Ray daemon](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-daemon-configuration.html)
- [Running the X-Ray daemon locally](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-daemon-local.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员编写了一个使用微服务的分布式应用程序。这些微服务运行在 Amazon EC2 实例上。由于消息量巨大，开发人员无法将每个微服务的日志输出与特定事务匹配。开发人员需要分析消息流以调试应用程序。为了满足此要求，开发人员应该采取哪些步骤组合？（选择两项。）

options.A: 下载 AWS X-Ray 守护程序。将该守护程序安装到 EC2 实例上。确保 EC2 实例允许端口 2000 上的 UDP 流量。
options.B: 配置接口 VPC 端点，允许流量通过 TCP 端口 2000 访问全球 AWS X-Ray 守护程序。
options.C: 启用 AWS X-Ray。配置 Amazon CloudWatch 将日志推送至 X-Ray。
options.D: 将 AWS X-Ray 软件开发工具包 (SDK) 添加到微服务中。使用 X-Ray 跟踪每个微服务发出的请求。
options.E: 设置 Amazon CloudWatch 指标流，以从微服务收集流数据。

zh.explanation:
# 使用 AWS X-Ray 追踪微服务事务

## 场景
一位开发人员在 EC2 上运行微服务，产生了大量日志，导致无法将日志行关联回单个端到端事务。他们需要追踪消息在服务间的流动以进行调试。AWS X-Ray 专为此目的而构建——它提供分布式追踪，带有追踪 ID 在每个微服务中跟踪请求，生成服务映射和分段级别的计时。

## 正确答案：A 和 D

### A. 在 EC2 上安装 X-Ray 守护程序并允许 UDP 端口 2000
X-Ray SDK 不直接调用 X-Ray API。相反，它通过 UDP 将段文档发送到本地守护程序，由守护程序缓冲并上传。AWS X-Ray 守护程序是一个软件应用程序，监听 UDP 端口 2000 上的流量，收集原始段数据，并将其转发到 AWS X-Ray API。守护程序与 AWS X-Ray SDK 配合工作，必须运行以便 SDK 发送的数据可以到达 X-Ray 服务。在 EC2 上运行时，在 Amazon EC2 上，守护程序自动使用实例的实例配置文件角色，因此安装守护程序并确保 UDP/2000 可访问（安全组/本地防火墙）是必需的。

### D. 将 X-Ray SDK 添加到微服务
SDK 是实际上对每个服务进行检测的工具，以便追踪 ID 在调用之间传播。您的应用程序使用 X-Ray SDK 来检测 HTTP 调用、数据库查询和其他操作。SDK 生成追踪段并以 UDP 数据包的形式发送到运行在同一主机上的 X-Ray 守护程序。守护程序收集这些段，将其批处理，并通过 HTTPS 转发到 X-Ray API。这正是让开发人员能够关联一个事务中跨微服务活动的方式。

## 其他选项为什么错误

### B. "全局"守护程序的 VPC 接口端点，使用 TCP 端口 2000
不存在"全局 AWS X-Ray 守护程序"——守护程序是您自己在计算上运行的软件。SDK 通过 **UDP** 端口 2000 与本地守护程序通信，而不是 TCP，VPC 接口端点用于私密访问 X-Ray *服务 API*，而不是守护程序。AWS X-Ray 守护程序监听 UDP 端口 2000 上的流量，收集原始段数据，并将其转发到 AWS X-Ray API。

### C. 启用 X-Ray 并配置 CloudWatch 将日志推送到 X-Ray
CloudWatch Logs 无法"将日志推送到 X-Ray"。X-Ray 接收由 X-Ray SDK/守护程序（或 OpenTelemetry/ADOT）生成的追踪段，而不是 CloudWatch 日志事件。如所述，这种集成根本不存在。

### E. 来自微服务的 CloudWatch 指标流
指标流连续将 CloudWatch *指标* 传送到目标，如 Kinesis Data Firehose 以进行监控/分析仪表板。它们生成数值指标数据，而不是每个请求的追踪，无法用于关联跨微服务的特定事务。

## 参考架构
```
[微服务 + X-Ray SDK]  --UDP:2000-->  [EC2 上的 X-Ray 守护程序]  --HTTPS-->  [AWS X-Ray 服务]
```
IAM：将 `AWSXRayDaemonWriteAccess` 受管策略附加到 EC2 实例配置文件，以便守护程序可以调用 `PutTraceSegments` / `PutTelemetryRecords`。

## 文档
- [AWS X-Ray 守护程序](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-daemon.html)
- [配置 AWS X-Ray 守护程序](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-daemon-configuration.html)
- [本地运行 X-Ray 守护程序](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-daemon-local.html)

en.question: A company is working on a new serverless application. A developer needs to find an automated way to deploy AWS Lambda functions and the dependent infrastructure with minimum coding effort. The application also needs to be reliable. Which method will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Build the application by using shell scripts to create .zip files for each Lambda function. Manually upload the .zip files to the AWS Management Console.
options.B: Build the application by using the AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM). Use a continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline and the SAM CLI to deploy the Lambda functions.
options.C: Build the application by using shell scripts to create .zip files for each Lambda function. Upload the .zip files. Deploy the .zip files as Lambda functions by using the AWS CLI in a continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline.
options.D: Build a container for each Lambda function. Store the container images in AWS CodeArtifact. Deploy the containers as Lambda functions by using the AWS CLI in a continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline.

en.explanation:
# Serverless Deployment with AWS SAM and CI/CD

## Scenario
A developer needs an automated way to deploy AWS Lambda functions **and the dependent infrastructure** with minimum coding effort, while ensuring reliability and the **least operational overhead**.

## Correct Answer: B

**AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM)** is purpose-built for defining serverless applications. It provides a simplified, declarative syntax (an extension of CloudFormation) to describe Lambda functions, API Gateway, DynamoDB tables, IAM roles, and other dependent infrastructure with minimum code. Combined with the SAM CLI in a CI/CD pipeline, deployments become fully automated, repeatable, and reliable.

Per AWS documentation, with AWS SAM you can automate deployment using a CI/CD system, and SAM provides default pipeline templates for multiple CI/CD systems that encapsulate AWS deployment best practices, including multi-account/multi-region deployments and safeguards against unintended infrastructure changes. The SAM CLI also supports generating starter pipelines: you can generate pipelines in minutes using the `sam pipeline init` command, and SAM CLI supports generating starter CI/CD pipeline configurations for AWS CodePipeline and other CI/CD systems.

A typical SAM build/deploy step in a pipeline is just:
```bash
sam build
sam deploy --no-confirm-changeset --no-fail-on-empty-changeset
```

This satisfies all three requirements: **automation** (CI/CD pipeline), **minimum coding effort** (declarative SAM template handles Lambda + dependent infra), and **reliability** (CloudFormation-managed stack with rollback).

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A. Shell scripts + manual upload via the Console** — This is entirely manual (no automation), error-prone, does not provision dependent infrastructure (IAM roles, API Gateway, DynamoDB, etc.), and has the highest operational overhead. Fails the "automated" and "reliable" requirements.

- **C. Shell scripts + AWS CLI in a CI/CD pipeline** — While this adds CI/CD automation, it requires writing and maintaining custom shell scripts to package each function and a separate mechanism (CLI calls) to provision Lambda *and* its dependent infrastructure. This is significantly more coding effort than declaratively defining everything in a SAM template, and it lacks the safety/reliability guarantees of CloudFormation-managed stacks.

- **D. Container images stored in CodeArtifact** — This is technically incorrect: **AWS CodeArtifact is a package repository for software packages (npm, Maven, PyPI, NuGet, etc.), not a container image registry.** Container images for Lambda must be stored in **Amazon ECR**, not CodeArtifact. Even if ECR were used, building containers for every Lambda adds operational overhead compared to SAM-managed zip-packaged functions, and you'd still need separate tooling to provision dependent infrastructure.

## References
- [Using CI/CD systems and pipelines to deploy with AWS SAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/deploying-cicd-overview.html)
- [Generate a starter CI/CD pipeline with AWS SAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/serverless-generating-example-ci-cd.html)
- [Introducing AWS SAM Pipelines (AWS Compute Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/introducing-aws-sam-pipelines-automatically-generate-deployment-pipelines-for-serverless-applications/)

zh.question: 一家公司正在开发一款新的无服务器应用程序。开发人员需要找到一种自动化方法来部署 AWS Lambda 函数及其依赖的基础设施，同时尽可能减少编码工作量。此外，该应用程序还需要具备高可靠性。哪种方法能够以最小的运维开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 shell 脚本构建应用程序，为每个 Lambda 函数创建 .zip 文件。手动将这些 .zip 文件上传到 AWS 管理控制台。
options.B: 使用 AWS 无服务器应用程序模型 (AWS SAM) 构建应用程序。使用持续集成和持续交付 (CI/CD) 流水线以及 SAM CLI 部署 Lambda 函数。
options.C: 使用 shell 脚本构建应用程序，为每个 Lambda 函数创建 .zip 文件。上传这些 .zip 文件。使用 AWS CLI 在持续集成和持续交付 (CI/CD) 管道中将这些 .zip 文件部署为 Lambda 函数。
options.D: 为每个 Lambda 函数构建一个容器。将容器镜像存储在 AWS CodeArtifact 中。使用 AWS CLI 在持续集成和持续交付 (CI/CD) 管道中将容器部署为 Lambda 函数。

zh.explanation:
# 使用 AWS SAM 和 CI/CD 的无服务器部署

## 场景
开发者需要一种自动化的方式来部署 AWS Lambda 函数**和相关的基础设施**，同时要求编码工作量最少，并确保可靠性和**最小的运维开销**。

## 正确答案：B

**AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM)** 专为定义无服务器应用而设计。它提供简化的声明式语法（CloudFormation 的扩展），可以用最少的代码描述 Lambda 函数、API Gateway、DynamoDB 表、IAM 角色和其他相关基础设施。结合 CI/CD 管道中的 SAM CLI，部署变得完全自动化、可重复和可靠。

根据 AWS 文档，使用 AWS SAM，您可以通过 CI/CD 系统自动化部署，SAM 为多个 CI/CD 系统提供默认管道模板，这些模板包含 AWS 部署最佳实践，包括多账户/多区域部署和防止意外基础设施更改的保护措施。SAM CLI 还支持生成初始管道：您可以使用 `sam pipeline init` 命令在数分钟内生成管道，SAM CLI 支持为 AWS CodePipeline 和其他 CI/CD 系统生成初始 CI/CD 管道配置。

典型的 SAM 管道中的构建/部署步骤仅为：
```bash
sam build
sam deploy --no-confirm-changeset --no-fail-on-empty-changeset
```

这满足所有三个要求：**自动化**（CI/CD 管道）、**最小编码工作量**（声明式 SAM 模板处理 Lambda + 相关基础设施）和**可靠性**（CloudFormation 管理的堆栈具有回滚功能）。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

- **A. Shell 脚本 + 通过控制台手动上传** — 这完全是手动的（无自动化），容易出错，不能配置相关基础设施（IAM 角色、API Gateway、DynamoDB 等），运维开销最高。不符合"自动化"和"可靠"的要求。

- **C. Shell 脚本 + CI/CD 管道中的 AWS CLI** — 虽然这增加了 CI/CD 自动化，但需要编写和维护自定义 shell 脚本来打包每个函数，以及单独的机制（CLI 调用）来配置 Lambda *和*其相关基础设施。这比在 SAM 模板中声明式定义所有内容需要更多编码工作，并且缺乏 CloudFormation 管理堆栈的安全性/可靠性保证。

- **D. 存储在 CodeArtifact 中的容器镜像** — 这在技术上是错误的：**AWS CodeArtifact 是软件包的包存储库（npm、Maven、PyPI、NuGet 等），不是容器镜像注册表。** Lambda 的容器镜像必须存储在 **Amazon ECR** 中，而不是 CodeArtifact。即使使用 ECR，为每个 Lambda 构建容器也会增加运维开销，相比之下 SAM 管理的 zip 打包函数更优越，而且您仍然需要单独的工具来配置相关基础设施。

## 参考资源
- [使用 CI/CD 系统和管道通过 AWS SAM 部署](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/deploying-cicd-overview.html)
- [使用 AWS SAM 生成初始 CI/CD 管道](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/serverless-generating-example-ci-cd.html)
- [AWS SAM 管道介绍（AWS Compute 博客）](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/introducing-aws-sam-pipelines-automatically-generate-deployment-pipelines-for-serverless-applications/)

en.question: A developer needs to modify an application architecture to meet new functional requirements. Application data is stored in Amazon DynamoDB and processed for analysis in a nightly batch. The system analysts do not want to wait until the next day to view the processed data and have asked to have it available in near-real time. Which application architecture pattern would enable the data to be processed as it is received?

options.A: Event driven
options.B: Client-server driven
options.C: Fan-out driven
options.D: Schedule driven

en.explanation:
# Event-Driven Architecture for Near Real-Time DynamoDB Processing

## Scenario
An application stores data in Amazon DynamoDB and currently processes it in a nightly batch. Analysts want to view processed data in **near real-time** rather than waiting for the next day. The question asks which **architecture pattern** allows data to be processed **as it is received**.

## Correct Answer: A. Event driven

In an event-driven architecture, components react to events (such as data writes) the moment they occur, instead of waiting for a scheduled batch run. For a DynamoDB-backed application, the canonical AWS implementation is **DynamoDB Streams + AWS Lambda**: each item-level change (INSERT, MODIFY, REMOVE) is captured as a stream record, and Lambda is automatically invoked to process it in near real-time.

Event-driven architectures, common in microservices-based applications, use events to invoke actions across decoupled services. Amazon DynamoDB streams captures changes to items in a table, creating a flow of event data. AWS Lambda can then consume these events to run custom logic without the need for server management. By combining DynamoDB streams with Lambda, you can build responsive, scalable, and cost-effective systems that automatically react to data changes in real time.

This perfectly matches the requirement: instead of running a nightly batch, each new/changed item triggers downstream analytics processing immediately.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **B. Client-server driven** — A request/response pattern where a client must explicitly query the server for data. It does not push data to consumers when changes occur, so the analyst would still have to poll for updates. It is not designed for asynchronous, push-based processing of data changes.

- **C. Fan-out driven** — "Fan-out" describes a *messaging topology* (e.g., one SNS topic delivering to many subscribers, or one Kinesis stream feeding many consumers), not a top-level architecture pattern that determines *when* data is processed. Fan-out is typically implemented **within** an event-driven architecture; by itself it doesn't address the batch-vs-real-time problem the question is asking about.

- **D. Schedule driven** — This is the *current* problem. A schedule-driven (cron/batch) pattern runs at fixed intervals (e.g., nightly), which is exactly what the analysts want to move away from. It cannot deliver near real-time results.

## Key AWS References
- [Build scalable, event-driven architectures with Amazon DynamoDB and AWS Lambda](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/build-scalable-event-driven-architectures-with-amazon-dynamodb-and-aws-lambda/)
- [Implement event-driven architectures with Amazon DynamoDB](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/implement-event-driven-architectures-with-amazon-dynamodb/)
- [DynamoDB Streams – Change Data Capture for DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Streams.html)

zh.question: 开发人员需要修改应用程序架构以满足新的功能需求。应用程序数据存储在 Amazon DynamoDB 中，并以夜间批处理的方式进行分析。系统分析师不希望等到第二天才能查看处理后的数据，他们要求能够近乎实时地获取数据。哪种应用程序架构模式能够实现数据接收后立即进行处理？

options.A: 事件驱动
options.B: 客户端-服务器驱动
options.C: 扇出驱动
options.D: 进度驱动

zh.explanation:
# 针对 DynamoDB 近实时处理的事件驱动架构

## 场景
某个应用程序在 Amazon DynamoDB 中存储数据，目前在每晚进行批处理。分析师希望以**近实时**方式查看处理后的数据，而不是等待第二天。该题目询问哪种**架构模式**允许数据在接收时立即被处理。

## 正确答案：A. 事件驱动

在事件驱动架构中，组件在事件发生的瞬间做出反应（例如数据写入），而不是等待计划的批处理运行。对于由 DynamoDB 支持的应用程序，规范的 AWS 实现是 **DynamoDB Streams + AWS Lambda**：每个项目级别的更改（INSERT、MODIFY、REMOVE）都被捕获为流记录，Lambda 会自动被调用以近实时方式处理它。

事件驱动架构常见于基于微服务的应用程序中，使用事件在解耦的服务之间调用操作。Amazon DynamoDB Streams 捕获表中项目的更改，创建事件数据流。AWS Lambda 可以消费这些事件来运行自定义逻辑，无需服务器管理。通过结合 DynamoDB Streams 与 Lambda，你可以构建响应迅速、高度可扩展和成本高效的系统，该系统自动对实时发生的数据更改做出反应。

这完全符合要求：每个新的或更改的项目立即触发下游分析处理，而不是运行每晚的批处理。

## 为什么其他选项错误

- **B. 客户端-服务器驱动** — 一种请求/响应模式，其中客户端必须显式查询服务器获取数据。它不会在更改发生时将数据推送给消费者，因此分析师仍然必须轮询更新。它不是为异步、基于推送的数据更改处理而设计的。

- **C. 扇出驱动** — "扇出"描述的是*消息传递拓扑*（例如，一个 SNS 主题传递给多个订阅者，或一个 Kinesis 流供多个消费者使用），而不是决定*何时*处理数据的顶级架构模式。扇出通常在事件驱动架构**内部**实现；单独使用它无法解决题目询问的批处理与实时问题。

- **D. 计划驱动** — 这是*现有*问题。计划驱动（cron/批处理）模式以固定间隔运行（例如每晚），这正是分析师想要放弃的方式。它无法提供近实时结果。

## AWS 关键参考资源
- [Build scalable, event-driven architectures with Amazon DynamoDB and AWS Lambda](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/build-scalable-event-driven-architectures-with-amazon-dynamodb-and-aws-lambda/)
- [Implement event-driven architectures with Amazon DynamoDB](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/implement-event-driven-architectures-with-amazon-dynamodb/)
- [DynamoDB Streams – Change Data Capture for DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Streams.html)

en.question: A company hosts its application in the us-west-1 Region. The company wants to add redundancy in the us-east-1 Region. The application secrets are stored in AWS Secrets Manager in us-west-1. A developer needs to replicate the secrets to us-east-1. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.A: Configure secret replication for each secret. Add us-east-1 as a replication Region. Choose an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key in us-east-1 to encrypt the replicated secrets.
options.B: Create a new secret in us-east-1 for each secret. Configure secret replication in us-east-1. Set the source to be the corresponding secret in us-west-1. Choose an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key in us-west-1 to encrypt the replicated secrets.
options.C: Create a replication rule for each secret. Set us-east-1 as the destination Region. Configure the rule to run during secret rotation. Choose an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key in us-east-1 to encrypt the replicated secrets.
options.D: Create a Secrets Manager lifecycle rule to replicate each secret to a new Amazon S3 bucket in us- west-1. Configure an S3 replication rule to replicate the secrets to us-east-1.

en.explanation:
# AWS Secrets Manager Cross-Region Replication

## Scenario
The application secrets live in **AWS Secrets Manager in us-west-1**. The company wants disaster recovery / redundancy in **us-east-1**, so the developer needs to make those secrets available in the second Region with minimal operational overhead.

## Correct Answer: A

AWS Secrets Manager has a built-in **multi-Region (cross-Region) replication** feature. You configure replication on the primary secret and add destination Region(s); Secrets Manager keeps replicas in sync automatically, including propagation of rotated values.

From the AWS documentation, when configuring replication you choose the AWS Region you want to replicate the secret to and (optionally) choose a KMS key to encrypt the secret with — the key must be in the replica Region. This matches option A exactly: enable replication on each secret, set us-east-1 as the replica Region, and pick a KMS key **in us-east-1** for encryption of the replica.

Additional benefits: if you turn on rotation for your primary secret, Secrets Manager rotates the secret in the primary Region, and the new secret value propagates to all of the associated replica secrets — you don't have to manage rotation individually for all of the replica secrets.

The CLI equivalent is `replicate-secret-to-regions`:

```bash
aws secretsmanager replicate-secret-to-regions \
  --secret-id MySecret \
  --add-replica-regions Region=us-east-1,KmsKeyId=<us-east-1-kms-key-arn>
```

The KmsKeyId parameter is the ARN, key ID, or alias of the KMS key to encrypt the secret; if you don't include this field, Secrets Manager uses aws/secretsmanager.

## Why the other options are wrong

- **B – Wrong direction and wrong KMS Region.** You don't create a new secret in the destination Region and then "pull" from us-west-1. Replication is configured on the **primary** secret in us-west-1, with us-east-1 added as a replica. Also, the KMS key used for the replica must reside in the **replica Region** (us-east-1), not us-west-1, because the KMS key chosen for encryption must be in the replica Region.

- **C – "Replication rule that runs during secret rotation" is not a real Secrets Manager feature.** Secrets Manager replication is continuous and automatic, not a rule tied to rotation events. Rotation of the primary automatically propagates to existing replicas; there is no "replication rule" object you create.

- **D – Wrong service pattern.** Secrets Manager has no "lifecycle rule" that exports secrets to S3. Copying secret material to an S3 bucket and using S3 cross-Region replication exposes the secrets outside Secrets Manager, defeats KMS-based access control on the secret, and creates significant operational overhead and security risk. The native Secrets Manager replication feature exists specifically to avoid this pattern.

## References
- [Replicate AWS Secrets Manager secrets across Regions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/replicate-secrets.html)
- [ReplicateSecretToRegions API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/apireference/API_ReplicateSecretToRegions.html)
- [AWS CLI: replicate-secret-to-regions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/secretsmanager/replicate-secret-to-regions.html)

zh.question: 一家公司将其应用程序托管在 us-west-1 区域。该公司希望在 us-east-1 区域增加冗余。应用程序密钥存储在 us-west-1 区域的 AWS Secrets Manager 中。开发人员需要将这些密钥复制到 us-east-1 区域。哪种解决方案可以满足此要求？

options.A: 为每个密钥配置密钥复制。添加 us-east-1 作为复制区域。选择 us-east-1 中的 AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) 密钥来加密复制的密钥。
options.B: 为每个密钥在 us-east-1 中创建一个新的密钥。在 us-east-1 中配置密钥复制。将源设置为 us-west-1 中对应的密钥。在 us-west-1 中选择一个 AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) 密钥来加密复制的密钥。
options.C: 为每个密钥创建复制规则。将目标区域设置为 us-east-1。配置该规则在密钥轮换期间运行。选择 us- east-1 区域中的 AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) 密钥来加密复制的密钥。
options.D: 创建 Secrets Manager 生命周期规则，将每个密钥复制到 us-west-1 中的新 Amazon S3 存储桶。配置 S3 复制规则，将密钥复制到 us-east-1。

zh.explanation:
# AWS Secrets Manager 跨区域复制

## 场景
应用程序的密钥存储在 **us-west-1 的 AWS Secrets Manager 中**。公司希望在 **us-east-1** 实现灾难恢复/冗余，因此开发人员需要以最少的运维开销在第二个区域中提供这些密钥。

## 正确答案：A

AWS Secrets Manager 具有内置的**多区域（跨区域）复制**功能。您在主密钥上配置复制并添加目标区域；Secrets Manager 会自动保持副本同步，包括传播轮换的值。

根据 AWS 文档，在配置复制时选择要将密钥复制到的 AWS 区域，并（可选）选择用于加密密钥的 KMS 密钥——该密钥必须位于副本区域中。这与选项 A 完全匹配：在每个密钥上启用复制，将 us-east-1 设置为副本区域，并选择 **us-east-1 中的** KMS 密钥来加密副本。

其他优势：如果您为主密钥启用轮换，Secrets Manager 会在主区域中轮换密钥，新的密钥值会传播到所有关联的副本密钥——您无需单独为所有副本密钥管理轮换。

等效的 CLI 命令是 `replicate-secret-to-regions`：

```bash
aws secretsmanager replicate-secret-to-regions \
  --secret-id MySecret \
  --add-replica-regions Region=us-east-1,KmsKeyId=<us-east-1-kms-key-arn>
```

KmsKeyId 参数是用于加密密钥的 KMS 密钥的 ARN、密钥 ID 或别名；如果您不包含此字段，Secrets Manager 将使用 aws/secretsmanager。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

- **B – 方向错误且 KMS 区域错误。** 您不需要在目标区域中创建新密钥，然后从 us-west-1 "拉取"。复制是在 **us-west-1 的主**密钥上配置的，并将 us-east-1 作为副本添加。此外，用于副本的 KMS 密钥必须位于**副本区域**（us-east-1）中，而不是 us-west-1，因为为加密选择的 KMS 密钥必须位于副本区域中。

- **C – "在密钥轮换期间运行的复制规则"不是真实的 Secrets Manager 功能。** Secrets Manager 复制是连续的且自动的，不是与轮换事件绑定的规则。主密钥的轮换自动传播到现有副本；没有您创建的 "复制规则" 对象。

- **D – 错误的服务模式。** Secrets Manager 没有将密钥导出到 S3 的 "生命周期规则"。将密钥材料复制到 S3 存储桶并使用 S3 跨区域复制会将密钥暴露在 Secrets Manager 之外，破坏对密钥的基于 KMS 的访问控制，并造成显著的运维开销和安全风险。原生 Secrets Manager 复制功能的存在正是为了避免这种模式。

## 参考资源
- [在区域间复制 AWS Secrets Manager 密钥](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/replicate-secrets.html)
- [ReplicateSecretToRegions API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/apireference/API_ReplicateSecretToRegions.html)
- [AWS CLI: replicate-secret-to-regions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/secretsmanager/replicate-secret-to-regions.html)

en.question: A company runs an ecommerce application on AWS. The application stores data in an Amazon Aurora database. A developer is adding a caching layer to the application. The caching strategy must ensure that the application always uses the most recent value for each data item. Which caching strategy will meet these requirements?

options.A: Implement a TTL strategy for every item that is saved in the cache.
options.B: Implement a write-through strategy for every item that is created and updated.
options.C: Implement a lazy loading strategy for every item that is loaded.
options.D: Implement a read-through strategy for every item that is loaded.

en.explanation:
# Caching Strategy for Most Recent Values

## Scenario
An ecommerce application uses Amazon Aurora as its primary database. A caching layer is being added, and the requirement is that **the application must always read the most recent value** for each item. The question asks which caching strategy guarantees freshness of cached data.

## Correct Answer: B — Write-Through Strategy

With a **write-through** strategy, every write/update operation writes the data both to the database **and** to the cache simultaneously. Subsequent reads always retrieve the latest value from the cache.

According to AWS documentation, the write-through strategy adds data or updates data in the cache whenever data is written to the database. Data in the cache is never stale because the data in the cache is updated every time it's written to the database, so the data in the cache is always current.

This directly satisfies the requirement that the application **always uses the most recent value**.

### Trade-offs to be aware of (still correct for this scenario)
- Every write involves two trips, a write to the cache and a write to the database, which adds latency to the process.
- When spinning up a new node (failure or scale-out), there is missing data which continues to be missing until it is added or updated on the database.
- Most data may never be read, leading to cache churn — a waste of resources.

These trade-offs do not violate the freshness requirement.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

### A. TTL (Time To Live) on every cached item — Incorrect
TTL only ensures cached items eventually expire. Between the time data is updated in the database and the time the cached item's TTL expires, reads can return stale data. This approach doesn't guarantee that a value isn't stale; it only keeps data from getting too stale and requires that values in the cache are occasionally refreshed from the database. This violates the "always most recent value" requirement.

### C. Lazy Loading — Incorrect
Lazy loading only loads data into the cache on a cache miss. If the underlying database row is updated after the cache was populated, the cache is **not** refreshed. If data is written to the cache only when there is a cache miss, data in the cache can become stale because there are no updates to the cache when data is changed in the database.

### D. Read-Through — Incorrect
Read-through is a variant of lazy loading where the cache itself fetches from the database on a miss. It still suffers from the same staleness problem: once the value is cached, subsequent updates to the database are not propagated to the cache until the entry is evicted or expires. It does not guarantee the most recent value on every read.

## Key Reference
- [Caching strategies — Amazon ElastiCache Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/Strategies.html)
- [AWS Database Blog — Use ElastiCache as a write-through cache](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/use-amazon-elasticache-as-a-cache-for-amazon-keyspaces-for-apache-cassandra/)

zh.question: 一家公司在 AWS 上运行一个电子商务应用程序。该应用程序将数据存储在 Amazon Aurora 数据库中。开发人员正在为该应用程序添加缓存层。缓存策略必须确保应用程序始终使用每个数据项的最新值。哪种缓存策略能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 对缓存中保存的每个项目实施 TTL 策略。
options.B: 对创建和更新的每个项目实施贯穿策略。
options.C: 对加载的每个项目实施延迟加载策略。
options.D: 对加载的每个项目实施逐行读取策略。

zh.explanation:
# 最近值的缓存策略

## 场景
一个电子商务应用使用 Amazon Aurora 作为主数据库。现在要添加缓存层，要求是**应用必须始终读取每个项目的最新值**。问题要求哪种缓存策略能保证缓存数据的新鲜性。

## 正确答案：B — Write-Through 策略

使用 **write-through** 策略，每次写入/更新操作都会同时将数据写入数据库**和**缓存。后续读取始终从缓存中检索最新值。

根据 AWS 文档，write-through 策略在向数据库写入数据时，也会在缓存中添加或更新数据。缓存中的数据永远不会过期，因为缓存中的数据在每次写入数据库时都会更新，所以缓存中的数据始终是最新的。

这直接满足了应用**始终使用最新值**的要求。

### 需要注意的权衡（对于此场景仍然正确）
- 每次写入都涉及两次往返，一次写入缓存，一次写入数据库，这增加了处理延迟。
- 当启动新节点（故障或扩展）时，存在缺失数据，这些数据会一直缺失直到在数据库中被添加或更新。
- 大多数数据可能永远不会被读取，导致缓存流失——浪费资源。

这些权衡不会违反新鲜性要求。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

### A. 在每个缓存项上使用 TTL（生存时间）— 错误
TTL 只确保缓存项最终过期。在数据库中更新数据到缓存项的 TTL 过期之间的时间段内，读取可能返回陈旧数据。这种方法不能保证值不陈旧；它只是防止数据变得太陈旧，需要定期从数据库刷新缓存中的值。这违反了"始终为最新值"的要求。

### C. Lazy Loading — 错误
Lazy Loading 仅在缓存未命中时将数据加载到缓存中。如果在缓存填充后更新了底层数据库行，缓存**不会**被刷新。如果缓存中的数据仅在缓存未命中时写入，那么缓存中的数据可能会变得陈旧，因为当数据库中的数据更改时，缓存不会更新。

### D. Read-Through — 错误
Read-Through 是 Lazy Loading 的一种变体，其中缓存本身在未命中时从数据库中获取。它仍然存在相同的陈旧问题：一旦值被缓存，后续对数据库的更新不会传播到缓存，直到条目被逐出或过期。它不能保证每次读取时都获得最新值。

## 关键参考
- [缓存策略 — Amazon ElastiCache 开发者指南](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/Strategies.html)
- [AWS 数据库博客 — 使用 ElastiCache 作为 write-through 缓存](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/use-amazon-elasticache-as-a-cache-for-amazon-keyspaces-for-apache-cassandra/)

en.question: A company has a serverless application that uses Amazon API Gateway backed by AWS Lambda proxy integration. The company is developing several backend APIs. The company needs a landing page to provide an overview of navigation to the APIs. A developer creates a new/LandingPage resource and a new GET method that uses mock integration. What should the developer do next to meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure the integration request mapping template with Content-Type of text/html and statusCode of 200. Configure the integration response mapping template with Content-Type of application/json. In the integration response mapping template, include the LandingPage HTML code that references the APIs.
options.B: Configure the integration request mapping template with Content-Type of application/json. In the integration request mapping template, include the LandingPage HMTL code that references the APIs. Configure the integration response mapping template with Content-Type of text/html and statusCode of 200.
options.C: Configure the integration request mapping template with Content-Type of application/json and statusCode of 200. Configure the integration response mapping template with Content-Type of text/html. In the integration response mapping template, include the LandingPage HTML code that references the APIs.
options.D: Configure the integration request mapping template with Content-Type of text/html. In the integration request mapping template, include the LandingPage HTML code that references the APIs. Configure the integration response mapping template with Content-Type of application/json and statusCode of 200.

en.explanation:
# API Gateway Mock Integration Returning HTML Landing Page ## Scenario The developer needs a `/LandingPage` GET endpoint that returns a static HTML page (with links to other backend APIs) using API Gateway's **mock integration** — meaning no Lambda or backend is invoked. The behavior is fully driven by mapping templates configured on the integration request and integration response. ## How Mock Integration Works As an API developer, you decide how API Gateway responds to a mock integration request. For this, you configure the method's integration request and integration response to associate a response with a given status code. For a method with the mock integration to return a 200 response, configure the integration request body mapping template to return the following. The standard pattern is: **Integration Request mapping template** (Content-Type `application/json`) — tells API Gateway which integration response to pick by emitting a `statusCode`: ```json { "statusCode": 200 } ``` **Integration Response mapping template** (Content-Type `text/html`) — contains the actual HTML body returned to the caller: ```html Landing Page

API Overview

  • API 1
  • API 2
``` This matches the documented community practice: Select the Integration Request and select Mock. In the method response, change the default response body content type to text/html. In the Integration Response, replace the Mapping Template with Content-Type text/html. ## Correct Answer: **C** - **Integration Request**: `Content-Type: application/json` with `{"statusCode": 200}` — this is the JSON template the mock integration uses to determine which response to return. - **Integration Response**: `Content-Type: text/html` with the HTML payload — what the client browser actually receives and renders. ## Why the Other Options Are Wrong - **A.** Reverses the content types. The integration **request** template for a mock integration must be `application/json` (it carries the `{"statusCode": 200}` JSON), not `text/html`. Also placing the HTML body in a JSON-typed integration response template prevents the browser from rendering it as HTML. - **B.** Puts the HTML in the **integration request** template. The request template is consumed internally by API Gateway to route to a response — it is never sent to the client. The HTML must live in the **integration response** template. The content types are also inverted. - **D.** Same root error as B — the HTML is placed in the integration request template (wrong), and the response template is set to `application/json` (wrong content type for an HTML page). ## References - [Mock integrations for REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-mock-integration.html) - [Enable mock integration using the API Gateway console](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-mock-integration-console.html) - [API Gateway mapping template reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-mapping-template-reference.html)

zh.question: 一家公司有一个使用 Amazon API Gateway 的无服务器应用程序，该应用程序由 AWS Lambda 代理集成提供支持。该公司正在开发多个后端 API。该公司需要一个着陆页来提供 API 导航概览。开发人员创建了一个新的 LandingPage 资源和一个使用模拟集成的 GET 方法。为了满足这些要求，开发人员接下来应该做什么？

options.A: 配置集成请求映射模板，使其内容类型为 text/html，状态码为 200。配置集成响应映射模板，使其内容类型为 application/json。在集成响应映射模板中，包含引用 API 的 LandingPage HTML 代码。
options.B: 配置集成请求映射模板，使其内容类型为 application/json。在集成请求映射模板中，包含引用 API 的 LandingPage HTML 代码。配置集成响应映射模板，使其内容类型为 text/html，状态码为 200。
options.C: 配置集成请求映射模板，使其内容类型为 application/json，状态码为 200。配置集成响应映射模板，使其内容类型为 text/html。在集成响应映射模板中，包含引用 API 的 LandingPage HTML 代码。
options.D: 配置集成请求映射模板，使其内容类型为 text/html。在集成请求映射模板中，包含引用 API 的 LandingPage HTML 代码。配置集成响应映射模板，使其内容类型为 application/json，状态码为 200。

zh.explanation:
# API Gateway 模拟集成返回 HTML 登陆页面 ## 场景 开发人员需要一个 `/LandingPage` GET 端点，使用 API Gateway 的**模拟集成**返回静态 HTML 页面（包含指向其他后端 API 的链接）—— 这意味着不会调用 Lambda 或后端服务。该行为完全由集成请求和集成响应中配置的映射模板驱动。 ## 模拟集成的工作原理 作为 API 开发人员，您可以决定 API Gateway 如何响应模拟集成请求。为此，您需要配置方法的集成请求和集成响应，将响应与给定的状态码关联。对于使用模拟集成的方法要返回 200 响应，请配置集成请求体映射模板以返回以下内容。 标准模式是： **集成请求映射模板**（Content-Type `application/json`）—— 告诉 API Gateway 通过发出 `statusCode` 来选择哪个集成响应： ```json { "statusCode": 200 } ``` **集成响应映射模板**（Content-Type `text/html`）—— 包含返回给调用者的实际 HTML 正文： ```html Landing Page

API Overview

  • API 1
  • API 2
``` 这符合记录的社区实践：选择"集成请求"并选择"Mock"。在方法响应中，将默认响应正文内容类型更改为 text/html。在集成响应中，将映射模板替换为 Content-Type text/html。 ## 正确答案：**C** - **集成请求**：`Content-Type: application/json`，包含 `{"statusCode": 200}` —— 这是模拟集成用来确定返回哪个响应的 JSON 模板。 - **集成响应**：`Content-Type: text/html`，包含 HTML 有效负载 —— 客户端浏览器实际接收并呈现的内容。 ## 其他选项为什么是错误的 - **A.** 颠倒了内容类型。模拟集成的集成**请求**模板必须是 `application/json`（它包含 `{"statusCode": 200}` JSON），而不是 `text/html`。同样，在 JSON 类型的集成响应模板中放置 HTML 正文会阻止浏览器将其呈现为 HTML。 - **B.** 将 HTML 放在**集成请求**模板中。请求模板由 API Gateway 在内部使用以路由到响应 —— 它永远不会发送给客户端。HTML 必须位于**集成响应**模板中。内容类型也是反向的。 - **D.** 与 B 存在相同的根本错误 —— HTML 放在集成请求模板中（错误），响应模板设置为 `application/json`（HTML 页面的错误内容类型）。 ## 参考资源 - [API Gateway 中 REST API 的模拟集成](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-mock-integration.html) - [使用 API Gateway 控制台启用模拟集成](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-mock-integration-console.html) - [API Gateway 映射模板参考](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-mapping-template-reference.html)

en.question: A developer creates an AWS Lambda function that is written in Java. During testing, the Lambda function does not work how the developer expected. The developer wants to use tracing capabilities to troubleshoot the problem. Which AWS service should the developer use to accomplish this goal?

options.A: AWS Trusted Advisor
options.B: Amazon CloudWatch
options.C: AWS X-Ray
options.D: AWS CloudTrail

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A developer has built a Java-based AWS Lambda function. During testing, the function does not behave as expected, and the developer wants to use **tracing** to troubleshoot the issue. The question asks which AWS service provides tracing capabilities.

## Correct Answer: C — AWS X-Ray

AWS X-Ray is the AWS service purpose-built for distributed tracing. Lambda integrates with AWS X-Ray to help you trace, debug, and optimize Lambda applications. You can use X-Ray to trace a request as it traverses resources in your application, which may include Lambda functions and other AWS services.

For Java specifically, AWS provides the X-Ray SDK for Java to generate and send trace data: To send tracing data to X-Ray, you can use one of two SDK libraries: AWS X-Ray SDK for Java – An SDK for generating and sending trace data to X-Ray. X-Ray helps developers visualize the components of your application, identify performance bottlenecks, and troubleshoot requests that resulted in an error, which is exactly what is needed when a Lambda function "does not work how the developer expected."

To enable tracing on a Lambda function, you turn on **Active tracing** in the function configuration, and the function's execution role needs the `AWSXRayDaemonWriteAccess` managed policy (Lambda adds this automatically when activated via the console).

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A. AWS Trusted Advisor** — Trusted Advisor is an account-level inspection service that gives recommendations across cost optimization, performance, security, fault tolerance, service limits, and operational excellence. It does **not** trace requests through application code or provide per-invocation execution insight for a Lambda function.

- **B. Amazon CloudWatch** — CloudWatch provides **metrics, logs, alarms, and dashboards**. While Lambda automatically writes execution logs to CloudWatch Logs and metrics like Invocations/Errors/Duration to CloudWatch Metrics, CloudWatch by itself is not a distributed **tracing** service. (CloudWatch ServiceLens and Application Signals integrate with X-Ray for trace visualization, but the underlying tracing capability is still X-Ray.) The keyword "tracing" maps directly to X-Ray.

- **D. AWS CloudTrail** — CloudTrail records **AWS API calls** made against your account (management and data events) for governance, compliance, and auditing. It logs *who called which AWS API*, not the internal execution path, latency, or downstream service calls *inside* your Lambda function. It cannot be used to trace application logic or pinpoint performance bottlenecks within the function.

## Key Takeaway

For DVA-C02, remember the mapping:
- **Tracing / latency analysis / service map** → **AWS X-Ray**
- **Logs & metrics** → **CloudWatch**
- **API audit history** → **CloudTrail**
- **Account best-practice checks** → **Trusted Advisor**

## References

- [Visualize Lambda function invocations using AWS X-Ray](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-xray.html)
- [Instrumenting Java code in AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/java-tracing.html)
- [AWS Lambda and AWS X-Ray (X-Ray Developer Guide)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-services-lambda.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员创建了一个用 Java 编写的 AWS Lambda 函数。在测试过程中，该 Lambda 函数的运行结果与开发人员的预期不符。开发人员希望使用跟踪功能来排查问题。开发人员应该使用哪项 AWS 服务来实现此目标？

options.A: AWS Trusted Advisor
options.B: Amazon CloudWatch
options.C: AWS X射线
options.D: AWS CloudTrail

zh.explanation:
## 场景

一名开发者构建了一个基于Java的AWS Lambda函数。在测试期间，该函数的行为不符合预期，开发者想使用**追踪**来排查问题。问题要求确定哪个AWS服务提供追踪功能。

## 正确答案：C — AWS X-Ray

AWS X-Ray是专为分布式追踪而设计的AWS服务。Lambda与AWS X-Ray集成，以帮助您追踪、调试和优化Lambda应用。您可以使用X-Ray追踪请求在应用中的资源间传递情况，这些资源可能包括Lambda函数和其他AWS服务。

对于Java，AWS提供了X-Ray SDK for Java来生成并发送追踪数据：要将追踪数据发送到X-Ray，您可以使用两个SDK库之一：AWS X-Ray SDK for Java – 用于生成追踪数据并将其发送到X-Ray的SDK。 X-Ray帮助开发者可视化应用的组件、确定性能瓶颈，以及排查导致错误的请求，这正是当Lambda函数"行为不符合开发者预期"时所需要的。

要在Lambda函数上启用追踪，您需要在函数配置中打开**Active tracing**，该函数的执行角色需要`AWSXRayDaemonWriteAccess`托管策略（通过控制台激活时Lambda会自动添加）。

## 为什么其他选项错误

- **A. AWS Trusted Advisor** — Trusted Advisor是一项账户级的检查服务，提供有关成本优化、性能、安全、容错能力、服务限制和运维卓越的建议。它**不会**追踪通过应用代码的请求，也不提供Lambda函数的每次调用执行洞察。

- **B. Amazon CloudWatch** — CloudWatch提供**指标、日志、警报和仪表板**。虽然Lambda会自动将执行日志写入CloudWatch Logs，并将调用次数/错误/持续时间等指标写入CloudWatch Metrics，但CloudWatch本身不是分布式**追踪**服务。（CloudWatch ServiceLens和Application Signals与X-Ray集成以显示追踪，但底层追踪功能仍然是X-Ray。）关键词"追踪"直接指向X-Ray。

- **D. AWS CloudTrail** — CloudTrail记录针对您账户进行的**AWS API调用**（管理事件和数据事件），用于治理、合规和审计。它记录的是*谁调用了哪个AWS API*，而不是Lambda函数*内部*的执行路径、延迟或下游服务调用。它无法用于追踪应用逻辑或定位函数内的性能瓶颈。

## 核心要点

对于DVA-C02，请记住以下映射：
- **追踪/延迟分析/服务地图** → **AWS X-Ray**
- **日志与指标** → **CloudWatch**
- **API审计历史** → **CloudTrail**
- **账户最佳实践检查** → **Trusted Advisor**

## 参考资源

- [使用AWS X-Ray可视化Lambda函数调用](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-xray.html)
- [在AWS Lambda中检测Java代码](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/java-tracing.html)
- [AWS Lambda和AWS X-Ray（X-Ray开发者指南）](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-services-lambda.html)

en.question: A company is developing an application that will be accessed through the Amazon API Gateway REST API. Registered users should be the only ones who can access certain resources of this API. The token being used should expire automatically and needs to be refreshed periodically. How can a developer meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Amazon Cognito identity pool, configure the Amazon Cognito Authorizer in API Gateway, and use the temporary credentials generated by the identity pool.
options.B: Create and maintain a database record for each user with a corresponding token and use an AWS Lambda authorizer in API Gateway.
options.C: Create an Amazon Cognito user pool, configure the Cognito Authorizer in API Gateway, and use the identity or access token.
options.D: Create an IAM user for each API user, attach an invoke permissions policy to the API, and use an IAM authorizer in API Gateway.

en.explanation:
# Securing API Gateway with Cognito for Registered Users with Auto-Expiring Tokens

## Scenario
The application exposes an API Gateway REST API. Only **registered users** should access certain resources. The token used must **expire automatically** and be **refreshed periodically**. This is a classic use case for Amazon Cognito **user pools** acting as an OIDC identity provider, combined with API Gateway's **COGNITO_USER_POOLS** authorizer.

## Correct Answer: C

Cognito **user pools** provide user directory/sign-in functionality and issue OIDC JSON Web Tokens after authentication. When a user signs into your app, Amazon Cognito verifies the login information. If the login is successful, Amazon Cognito creates a session and returns an ID token, an access token, and a refresh token for the authenticated user. You can use the tokens to grant your users access to downstream resources and APIs like Amazon API Gateway.

To wire this up to API Gateway: you must first create an authorizer of the COGNITO_USER_POOLS type and then configure an API method to use that authorizer. After the API is deployed, the client must first sign the user in to the user pool, obtain an identity or access token for the user, and then call the API method with one of the tokens, which are typically set to the request's Authorization header. The API call succeeds only if the required token is supplied and the supplied token is valid.

The auto-expire / refresh requirement is built in: You can set the access token expiration to any value between 5 minutes and 1 day. You can set this value per app client. The longer-lived refresh token is then used to obtain new tokens: The refresh token is a longer-lived JWT token with that the client can generate new ID and access tokens. This allows you to have short-lived ID or access tokens without having to collect the user credentials every time when ID or access tokens expire. By default, the refresh token expires 30 days after your application user signs into your user pool.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

### A. Cognito **identity pool** + Cognito Authorizer
The Cognito Authorizer in API Gateway works with **user pools**, not identity pools. Identity pools (Federated Identities) exchange an existing identity for **temporary AWS IAM credentials** (SigV4) — they do not issue OIDC JWTs that the COGNITO_USER_POOLS authorizer validates. To let a user sign in using Amazon Cognito credentials and also obtain temporary credentials to use with the permissions of an IAM role, use Amazon Cognito Federated Identities. Identity pools alone don't perform user authentication or manage user sign-up/sign-in token lifecycles.

### B. Database of users + Lambda authorizer
While technically possible, this requires the developer to build and maintain custom authentication, token issuance, expiration, and refresh logic — exactly what Cognito user pools provide out of the box. It's far more operational overhead and re-implements an authentication system instead of using a managed one. The question asks for the simplest way to meet the requirements with built-in token expiry/refresh, which Cognito user pools provide natively.

### D. IAM user per API user + IAM authorizer
IAM users are intended for AWS principals (developers, services), not for application end users. AWS strongly recommends against creating IAM users for every application user — IAM has a hard limit (5,000 users per account) and IAM long-term access keys do **not** auto-expire or refresh on the schedule the question requires. This pattern doesn't scale and doesn't match the "token expires automatically and is refreshed periodically" requirement.

## Reference Links
- [Control access to REST APIs using Amazon Cognito user pools as an authorizer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-integrate-with-cognito.html)
- [Integrate a REST API with an Amazon Cognito user pool](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-enable-cognito-user-pool.html)
- [Understanding user pool JSON web tokens (JWTs)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/amazon-cognito-user-pools-using-tokens-with-identity-providers.html)
- [Understanding the access token](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/amazon-cognito-user-pools-using-the-access-token.html)

zh.question: 一家公司正在开发一个应用程序，该应用程序将通过 Amazon API Gateway REST API 访问。只有注册用户才能访问此 API 的某些资源。所使用的令牌应自动过期，并且需要定期刷新。开发人员如何满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个 Amazon Cognito 身份池，在 API Gateway 中配置 Amazon Cognito 授权器，并使用身份池生成的临时凭证。
options.B: 为每个用户创建并维护一个数据库记录，并为其分配一个相应的令牌，然后在 API Gateway 中使用 AWS Lambda 授权器。
options.C: 创建一个 Amazon Cognito 用户池，在 API Gateway 中配置 Cognito 授权器，并使用身份或访问令牌。
options.D: 为每个 API 用户创建一个 IAM 用户，将调用权限策略附加到 API，并在 API 网关中使用 IAM 授权器。

zh.explanation:
# 使用 Cognito 为注册用户保护 API Gateway 并自动过期令牌

## 场景
应用程序公开一个 API Gateway REST API。只有**注册用户**应该能访问某些资源。使用的令牌必须**自动过期**并**定期刷新**。这是 Amazon Cognito **用户池**作为 OIDC 身份提供者的典型用例，结合 API Gateway 的 **COGNITO_USER_POOLS** 授权器。

## 正确答案：C

Cognito **用户池**提供用户目录/登录功能，并在身份验证后发放 OIDC JSON Web Token。当用户登录到您的应用时，Amazon Cognito 会验证登录信息。如果登录成功，Amazon Cognito 会创建一个会话，并为身份验证的用户返回一个 ID 令牌、一个访问令牌和一个刷新令牌。您可以使用这些令牌向下游资源和 API（如 Amazon API Gateway）授予用户访问权限。

要将其连接到 API Gateway：您必须首先创建一个 COGNITO_USER_POOLS 类型的授权器，然后配置一个 API 方法来使用该授权器。部署 API 后，客户端必须首先将用户登录到用户池，为该用户获取身份令牌或访问令牌，然后使用其中一个令牌调用 API 方法，这些令牌通常设置在请求的 Authorization 标头中。只有当提供了所需的令牌且该令牌有效时，API 调用才会成功。

自动过期/刷新要求是内置的：您可以将访问令牌过期时间设置为 5 分钟到 1 天之间的任何值。您可以按应用客户端设置此值。寿命更长的刷新令牌用于获取新令牌：刷新令牌是一个寿命更长的 JWT 令牌，客户端可以使用它生成新的 ID 和访问令牌。这允许您拥有短期的 ID 或访问令牌，而不必在 ID 或访问令牌过期时每次都收集用户凭证。默认情况下，刷新令牌在您的应用用户登录到用户池后 30 天后过期。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

### A. Cognito **身份池** + Cognito 授权器
API Gateway 中的 Cognito 授权器与**用户池**配合使用，不与身份池配合使用。身份池（联合身份）用现有身份交换**临时 AWS IAM 凭证**（SigV4）— 它们不发放 COGNITO_USER_POOLS 授权器验证的 OIDC JWT。要让用户使用 Amazon Cognito 凭证登录，同时获得临时凭证以与 IAM 角色的权限一起使用，请使用 Amazon Cognito 联合身份。仅身份池不会执行用户身份验证或管理用户注册/登录令牌生命周期。

### B. 用户数据库 + Lambda 授权器
虽然在技术上可行，但这需要开发者构建和维护自定义身份验证、令牌发放、过期和刷新逻辑 — 这正是 Cognito 用户池开箱即用提供的功能。这会产生更多的运营开销，并重新实现身份验证系统，而不是使用托管服务。问题要求以满足内置令牌过期/刷新要求的最简单方式进行操作，而 Cognito 用户池本身就提供这一点。

### D. 每个 API 用户对应一个 IAM 用户 + IAM 授权器
IAM 用户旨在用于 AWS 主体（开发者、服务），而不是应用最终用户。AWS 强烈建议不要为每个应用用户创建 IAM 用户 — IAM 有硬限制（每个账户 5,000 个用户），并且 IAM 长期访问密钥**不会**按照问题要求的计划自动过期或刷新。此模式无法扩展，也不符合"令牌自动过期并定期刷新"的要求。

## 参考链接
- [使用 Amazon Cognito 用户池作为授权器来控制对 REST API 的访问](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-integrate-with-cognito.html)
- [将 REST API 与 Amazon Cognito 用户池集成](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-enable-cognito-user-pool.html)
- [了解用户池 JSON Web 令牌 (JWT)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/amazon-cognito-user-pools-using-tokens-with-identity-providers.html)
- [了解访问令牌](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/amazon-cognito-user-pools-using-the-access-token.html)

en.question: A company used AWS to develop an application for customers. The application includes an Amazon API Gateway API that invokes AWS Lambda functions. The Lambda functions process data and store the data in Amazon DynamoDB tables. The company must monitor the entire application to identify potential bottlenecks in the architecture that can negatively affect customers. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST development effort?

options.A: Instrument the application with AWS X-Ray. Inspect the service map to identify errors and issues.
options.B: Configure Lambda exceptions and additional logging to Amazon CloudWatch. Use CloudWatch Logs Insights to query the logs.
options.C: Configure API Gateway to log responses to Amazon CloudWatch. Create a metric filter for the TooManyRequestsException error message.
options.D: Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics for the DynamoDB tables to identify all the ProvisionedThroughputExceededException error messages.

en.explanation:
## Scenario
A serverless application uses **API Gateway → Lambda → DynamoDB**. The company needs to monitor the **entire** application end-to-end to identify **bottlenecks** with the **least development effort**.

## Correct Answer: A — Instrument with AWS X-Ray and inspect the service map

AWS X-Ray is purpose-built for distributed tracing across serverless components. You can use AWS X-Ray to visualize the components of your application, identify performance bottlenecks, and troubleshoot requests that resulted in an error. Your Lambda functions send trace data to X-Ray, and X-Ray processes the data to generate a service map and searchable trace summaries.

Enabling X-Ray for this stack is a configuration change rather than custom development:
- API Gateway: enable tracing on the stage.
- Lambda: set tracing mode to Active (e.g., `--tracing-config Mode=Active`).
- DynamoDB calls made via the AWS SDK are auto-instrumented when the X-Ray SDK wraps the AWS SDK.

The resulting service map shows every hop. AWS X-Ray service maps show information about your API and all of its downstream services. When X-Ray is enabled for an API stage in API Gateway, you'll see a node in the service map containing information about the overall time spent in the API Gateway service. You can get detailed information about the response status and a histogram of the API response time for the selected timeframe. For APIs integrating with AWS services such as AWS Lambda and Amazon DynamoDB, you will see more nodes providing performance metrics related to those services.

This directly satisfies "monitor the entire application to identify potential bottlenecks" with minimal effort, because X-Ray automatically correlates latency, errors, and throttles across API Gateway, Lambda, and DynamoDB into a single visual map and trace timeline.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

**B. Lambda exceptions + CloudWatch Logs Insights queries** — Requires writing custom logging code in every Lambda, designing log formats, and authoring/maintaining Logs Insights queries. It only covers the Lambda layer, not API Gateway latency or DynamoDB call timing, so it cannot identify cross-service bottlenecks. This is *more* development effort and less coverage than X-Ray.

**C. API Gateway access logs + metric filter for `TooManyRequestsException`** — Only inspects API Gateway responses for one specific throttling error. It doesn't trace requests through Lambda or DynamoDB and won't reveal latency hotspots (e.g., slow DynamoDB queries or Lambda cold starts). It's a narrow alarm, not end-to-end monitoring.

**D. CloudWatch metrics for `ProvisionedThroughputExceededException` on DynamoDB** — Only surfaces DynamoDB capacity throttling. It misses API Gateway integration latency, Lambda duration/cold-starts, and any non-throttle bottlenecks. Doesn't meet the "entire application" requirement.

## Key AWS Docs
- [Visualize Lambda function invocations using AWS X-Ray](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-xray.html)
- [Use AWS X-Ray service maps and trace views with API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-using-xray-maps.html)

zh.question: 一家公司使用 AWS 为客户开发应用程序。该应用程序包含一个 Amazon API Gateway API，用于调用 AWS Lambda 函数。Lambda 函数处理数据并将其存储在 Amazon DynamoDB 表中。该公司必须监控整个应用程序，以识别架构中可能对客户产生负面影响的潜在瓶颈。哪种解决方案能够以最少的开发工作量满足此要求？

options.A: 使用 AWS X-Ray 对应用程序进行检测。检查服务映射以识别错误和问题。
options.B: 配置 Lambda 异常和额外的日志记录到 Amazon CloudWatch。使用 CloudWatch Logs Insights 查询日志。
options.C: 配置 API Gateway 将响应记录到 Amazon CloudWatch。为 TooManyRequestsException 错误消息创建指标过滤器。
options.D: 使用 Amazon CloudWatch 指标来监控 DynamoDB 表，以识别所有 ProvisionedThroughputExceededException 错误消息。

zh.explanation:
## 场景
一个无服务器应用使用 **API Gateway → Lambda → DynamoDB**。公司需要监控**整个**应用的端到端流程，以识别**瓶颈**，同时**最小化开发工作量**。

## 正确答案：A — 使用 AWS X-Ray 进行检测并查看服务地图

AWS X-Ray 专为跨无服务器组件的分布式追踪而设计。您可以使用 AWS X-Ray 可视化应用的组件、识别性能瓶颈，并排查导致错误的请求。您的 Lambda 函数将追踪数据发送到 X-Ray，X-Ray 处理数据以生成服务地图和可搜索的追踪摘要。

为此堆栈启用 X-Ray 是一项配置更改，而不是自定义开发：
- API Gateway：在阶段上启用追踪。
- Lambda：将追踪模式设置为 Active（例如，`--tracing-config Mode=Active`）。
- 通过 AWS SDK 发出的 DynamoDB 调用在 X-Ray SDK 包装 AWS SDK 时会自动检测。

生成的服务地图显示每一跳的信息。AWS X-Ray 服务地图显示关于您的 API 及其所有下游服务的信息。在 API Gateway 中为 API 阶段启用 X-Ray 时，您将在服务地图中看到一个包含 API Gateway 服务中总时间信息的节点。您可以获得有关响应状态的详细信息以及所选时间范围内 API 响应时间的直方图。对于与 AWS Lambda 和 Amazon DynamoDB 等 AWS 服务集成的 API，您将看到更多节点，提供与这些服务相关的性能指标。

这直接满足了"监控整个应用以识别潜在瓶颈"的要求，工作量最少，因为 X-Ray 会自动将 API Gateway、Lambda 和 DynamoDB 中的延迟、错误和限制关联到单个可视地图和追踪时间线中。

## 其他选项为何错误

**B. Lambda 异常 + CloudWatch Logs Insights 查询** — 需要在每个 Lambda 中编写自定义日志代码、设计日志格式以及创建/维护 Logs Insights 查询。它仅覆盖 Lambda 层，不涵盖 API Gateway 延迟或 DynamoDB 调用计时，因此无法识别跨服务瓶颈。相比 X-Ray，这需要*更多*开发工作量且覆盖范围更窄。

**C. API Gateway 访问日志 + `TooManyRequestsException` 的指标过滤器** — 仅检查 API Gateway 响应中的一个特定限制错误。它不追踪通过 Lambda 或 DynamoDB 的请求，也不会显示延迟热点（例如缓慢的 DynamoDB 查询或 Lambda 冷启动）。这是一个狭隘的告警，而不是端到端监控。

**D. DynamoDB 上 `ProvisionedThroughputExceededException` 的 CloudWatch 指标** — 仅显示 DynamoDB 容量限制。它忽略 API Gateway 集成延迟、Lambda 持续时间/冷启动以及任何非限制瓶颈。不满足"整个应用"的要求。

## 关键 AWS 文档
- [使用 AWS X-Ray 可视化 Lambda 函数调用](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-xray.html)
- [在 API Gateway 中使用 AWS X-Ray 服务地图和追踪视图](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-using-xray-maps.html)

en.question: A company launched an online portal to announce a new product that the company will release in 6 months. The portal requests that users enter an email address to receive communications about the product. The company needs to create a REST API that will store the email addresses in Amazon DynamoDB. A developer has created an AWS Lambda function that can store the email addresses. The developer will deploy the Lambda function by using the AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM). The developer must provide access to the Lambda function over HTTP. Which solutions will meet these requirements with the LEAST additional configuration? (Choose two.)

options.A: Expose the Lambda function by using function URLs.
options.B: Expose the Lambda function by using a Gateway Load Balancer.
options.C: Expose the Lambda function by using a Network Load Balancer.
options.D: Expose the Lambda function by using AWS Global Accelerator.
options.E: Expose the Lambda function by using Amazon API Gateway.

en.explanation:
# Exposing a Lambda Function over HTTP via SAM — Least Configuration

## Scenario
The developer needs to expose a Lambda function over HTTP so that the portal can submit user email addresses to be stored in DynamoDB. The deployment is done with AWS SAM, and the goal is the **least additional configuration**.

## Correct Answers: A and E

### A. Lambda Function URLs ✅
A Lambda function URL is the simplest way to add an HTTP(S) endpoint to a Lambda function. It creates an AWS Lambda function URL with the specified configuration parameters — a function URL is an HTTPS endpoint that you can use to invoke your function. 

In AWS SAM, this requires only a few lines added to the `AWS::Serverless::Function` resource via the `FunctionUrlConfig` property:

```yaml
HelloWorldFunction:
  Type: AWS::Serverless::Function
  Properties:
    CodeUri: hello_world/
    Handler: index.handler
    Runtime: nodejs20.x
    FunctionUrlConfig:
      AuthType: NONE
```

Sometimes all you need is a simple way to configure an HTTPS endpoint in front of your function without having to learn, configure, and operate additional services besides Lambda — Lambda Function URLs let you add HTTPS endpoints to any Lambda function and optionally configure CORS headers.

### E. Amazon API Gateway ✅
API Gateway is natively integrated with AWS SAM through the `Events` property of `AWS::Serverless::Function` (e.g., `Type: Api` or `Type: HttpApi`). SAM automatically creates the API Gateway resource, the integration, and the necessary Lambda permissions, so no additional manual configuration is needed. API Gateway is the traditional, well-supported way to expose a Lambda function via REST. Each function is mapped to API endpoints, methods, and resources using services such as Amazon API Gateway and Application Load Balancer.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

### B. Gateway Load Balancer ❌
Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) is designed for deploying, scaling, and managing **third-party virtual network appliances** (firewalls, IDS/IPS, deep packet inspection) using the GENEVE protocol on port 6081. It is **not** a generic HTTP entry point and **does not support Lambda as a target**. It cannot be used to expose a Lambda function via HTTP.

### C. Network Load Balancer ❌
Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 (TCP/UDP/TLS) and **does not support Lambda functions as targets** — only Application Load Balancer (ALB) supports Lambda targets. Even if NLB could be used (via custom integrations), it would require significantly more setup (target groups, listeners, VPC configuration) than function URLs or API Gateway.

### D. AWS Global Accelerator ❌
Global Accelerator provides static anycast IP addresses and routes traffic across AWS Regions for performance/failover. It does **not** directly target Lambda functions; it routes to ALB, NLB, EC2, or Elastic IPs. Using it to front a Lambda would require an additional load balancer in between, increasing rather than decreasing configuration.

## Key Takeaway
For HTTP access to a Lambda function deployed via SAM with **minimum configuration**:
- **Function URLs** = simplest, built-in HTTPS endpoint, configured by a single `FunctionUrlConfig` block.
- **API Gateway** = native SAM `Events` integration, automatically wires up everything for a REST API.

## References
- [SAM FunctionUrlConfig](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/sam-property-function-functionurlconfig.html)
- [Creating and managing Lambda function URLs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/urls-configuration.html)
- [Announcing AWS Lambda Function URLs](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/announcing-aws-lambda-function-urls-built-in-https-endpoints-for-single-function-microservices/)
- [AWS::Lambda::Url CloudFormation resource](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-resource-lambda-url.html)

zh.question: 一家公司上线了一个在线门户网站，用于发布一款将在 6 个月后上市的新产品。该门户网站要求用户输入电子邮件地址以接收有关该产品的通知。该公司需要创建一个 REST API，用于将这些电子邮件地址存储在 Amazon DynamoDB 中。一位开发人员创建了一个可以存储这些电子邮件地址的 AWS Lambda 函数。该开发人员将使用 AWS 无服务器应用程序模型 (AWS SAM) 部署该 Lambda 函数。开发人员必须通过 HTTP 提供对 Lambda 函数的访问。哪些解决方案能够以最少的额外配置满足这些要求？（选择两个。）

options.A: 使用函数 URL 公开 Lambda 函数。
options.B: 使用网关负载均衡器公开 Lambda 函数。
options.C: 使用网络负载均衡器公开 Lambda 函数。
options.D: 使用 AWS Global Accelerator 公开 Lambda 函数。
options.E: 使用 Amazon API Gateway 公开 Lambda 函数。

zh.explanation:
# 通过 SAM 以 HTTP 方式暴露 Lambda 函数 — 最少配置

## 场景
开发人员需要通过 HTTP 暴露 Lambda 函数，以便门户网站可以提交用户电子邮件地址存储到 DynamoDB。部署使用 AWS SAM，目标是**最少的额外配置**。

## 正确答案：A 和 E

### A. Lambda Function URLs ✅
Lambda 函数 URL 是向 Lambda 函数添加 HTTP(S) 端点的最简单方式。它使用指定的配置参数创建 AWS Lambda 函数 URL — 函数 URL 是一个 HTTPS 端点，可用于调用函数。

在 AWS SAM 中，这仅需通过 `FunctionUrlConfig` 属性向 `AWS::Serverless::Function` 资源添加几行代码：

```yaml
HelloWorldFunction:
  Type: AWS::Serverless::Function
  Properties:
    CodeUri: hello_world/
    Handler: index.handler
    Runtime: nodejs20.x
    FunctionUrlConfig:
      AuthType: NONE
```

有时，你只需要一个简单的方式在函数前面配置 HTTPS 端点，无需学习、配置和操作 Lambda 以外的其他服务 — Lambda Function URLs 允许为任何 Lambda 函数添加 HTTPS 端点，并可选择配置 CORS 标头。

### E. Amazon API Gateway ✅
API Gateway 通过 `AWS::Serverless::Function` 的 `Events` 属性（例如 `Type: Api` 或 `Type: HttpApi`）与 AWS SAM 本地集成。SAM 自动创建 API Gateway 资源、集成和必要的 Lambda 权限，因此无需手动配置。API Gateway 是暴露 Lambda 函数通过 REST 的传统、广泛支持的方式。每个函数都通过 Amazon API Gateway 和应用程序负载均衡器等服务映射到 API 端点、方法和资源。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

### B. Gateway Load Balancer ❌
Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) 设计用于部署、扩展和管理**第三方虚拟网络设备**（防火墙、IDS/IPS、深度数据包检查），使用 GENEVE 协议在 6081 端口上运行。它**不是**通用 HTTP 入口点，**不支持 Lambda 作为目标**。无法用于通过 HTTP 暴露 Lambda 函数。

### C. Network Load Balancer ❌
Network Load Balancer 在第 4 层（TCP/UDP/TLS）运行，**不支持 Lambda 函数作为目标** — 仅应用程序负载均衡器 (ALB) 支持 Lambda 目标。即使 NLB 可以使用（通过自定义集成），也需要比函数 URL 或 API Gateway 显著更多的设置（目标组、侦听器、VPC 配置）。

### D. AWS Global Accelerator ❌
Global Accelerator 提供静态任播 IP 地址，并在 AWS 区域间路由流量以实现性能/故障转移。它**不直接针对 Lambda 函数**；它路由到 ALB、NLB、EC2 或弹性 IP。使用它来前置 Lambda 将需要中间额外的负载均衡器，增加而非减少配置。

## 关键要点
对于通过 SAM 部署的 Lambda 函数以**最少配置**访问 HTTP：
- **Function URLs** = 最简单，内置 HTTPS 端点，通过单个 `FunctionUrlConfig` 块配置。
- **API Gateway** = 本地 SAM `Events` 集成，自动为 REST API 连接所有内容。

## 参考资源
- [SAM FunctionUrlConfig](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/sam-property-function-functionurlconfig.html)
- [创建和管理 Lambda 函数 URL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/urls-configuration.html)
- [宣布 AWS Lambda Function URLs](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/announcing-aws-lambda-function-urls-built-in-https-endpoints-for-single-function-microservices/)
- [AWS::Lambda::Url CloudFormation 资源](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-resource-lambda-url.html)

en.question: A company has a website that displays a daily newsletter. When a user visits the website, an AWS Lambda function processes the browser's request and queries the company's on-premises database to obtain the current newsletter. The newsletters are stored in English. The Lambda function uses the Amazon Translate TranslateText API operation to translate the newsletters, and the translation is displayed to the user. Due to an increase in popularity, the website's response time has slowed. The database is overloaded. The company cannot change the database and needs a solution that improves the response time of the Lambda function. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Change to asynchronous Lambda function invocation.
options.B: Cache the translated newsletters in the Lambda/tmp directory.
options.C: Enable TranslateText API caching.
options.D: Change the Lambda function to use parallel processing.

en.explanation:
# Caching Translated Newsletters in Lambda /tmp

## Scenario
A Lambda function fetches a daily newsletter from an overloaded on-premises database, then calls Amazon Translate's `TranslateText` API to translate it before returning to the user. The website is slow because the database is overloaded. Since the newsletter is the **same content all day** (only changes daily), every invocation re-queries the DB and re-calls Translate for identical input. The fix must reduce database load and improve Lambda response time, without modifying the database.

## Correct Answer: B — Cache the translated newsletters in the Lambda /tmp directory

The Lambda execution environment is reused across invocations when warm. The same Lambda execution environment may be reused by multiple Lambda invocations to optimize performance. The /tmp area is preserved for the lifetime of the execution environment and provides a transient cache for data between invocations. This makes `/tmp` a valid place to cache the day's translated newsletter so that subsequent warm invocations avoid both the database query and the Translate API call.

You can use the same execution environment to cache static assets in /tmp between invocations. Because the newsletter only changes once per day, caching the translated text (keyed by date and target language) dramatically reduces both DB load and TranslateText latency/cost. Accessing data in Lambda ephemeral storage does not require an external internet request, making it faster and cheaper than accessing data from object storage like S3, which requires a network request.
