- [Atlassian: Gitflow Workflow](https://www.atlassian.com/git/tutorials/comparing-workflows/gitflow-workflow)
- [Vincent Driessen: A successful Git branching model](https://nvie.com/posts/a-successful-git-branching-model/)

zh.question: 开发人员需要在正式发布前冻结对 AWS CodeCommit 代码库的更改。开发人员将在质量保证 (QA) 团队测试发布版本的同时开发新功能。QA 测试和所有错误修复都必须与主分支隔离进行。发布后，开发人员必须将所有错误修复集成到主分支中。哪种解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 从即将发布版本中包含的最新 Git 提交创建一个发布分支。将修复程序应用到该发布分支。继续开发新功能，并将这些功能合并到主分支。发布完成后，将发布分支合并到主分支。
options.B: 在即将发布版本的最新 Git 提交上创建一个 Git 标签。继续开发新功能，并将这些功能合并到主分支。将修复应用到主分支。更新发布版本的 Git 标签，使其指向主分支上的最新提交。
options.C: 从即将发布版本中包含的最新 Git 提交创建一个发布分支。将修复应用到发布分支。继续开发新功能，并将这些功能合并到主分支。发布完成后，将主分支变基到发布分支。
options.D: 在即将发布版本的最新 Git 提交上创建一个 Git 标签。继续开发新功能，并将这些功能合并到主分支。将修复的 Git 提交应用到该发布版本的 Git 标签上。

zh.explanation:
# CodeCommit 的 Git 发布分支策略

## 场景
开发人员需要为生产发布"冻结"代码库，同时：
1. 允许 QA 隔离测试发布
2. 允许针对发布进行错误修复，而不影响主分支
3. 让开发人员继续在主分支上进行功能开发
4. 最终将发布错误修复集成回主分支

这是经典的 **Gitflow 发布分支**模式。

## 正确答案：A

从准备发布的最新提交创建**发布分支**。QA 团队测试此分支，任何错误修复都提交到发布分支（与主分支隔离）。同时，开发人员继续开发新功能并将其合并到主分支。发布上线后，发布分支合并回主分支，以便错误修复被集成。

这与 AWS 规范指南中的 Gitflow 一致，"在发布分支已部署到生产后，应将其合并回开发分支和主分支，以确保任何错误修复或紧急修复都被合并到未来的开发工作中。"

也与规范的 Gitflow 定义一致："创建此分支启动下一个发布周期，因此之后不能添加新功能—只有错误修复、文档生成和其他面向发布的任务应该进入此分支。"以及"一旦准备好发布，发布分支合并到主分支并使用版本号标记。此外，应将其合并回开发分支，该分支可能在发起发布后已有进展。"

## 其他选项错误的原因

**B. Git 标签 + 在主分支应用修复** — Git 标签只是一个指向提交的不可变指针；它无法隔离工作。如果在主分支应用错误修复，它们会与新功能提交混合，因此 QA 无法隔离测试，"冻结"需求被违反。将标签更新为指向后续提交也违反了发布标记的目的。

**C. 将主分支变基到发布分支** — 将主分支变基到发布分支会重写共享主分支的历史（对已发布分支的破坏性操作），并会在发布分支之上重放主分支的新功能提交，实际上使发布分支成为新基础。这对共享/受保护的主分支很危险，不是发布分支的集成方式。标准做法是**合并**回主分支，而不是变基主分支。

**D. 向 Git 标签应用提交** — 您不能向标签提交。标签是对特定提交的静态引用；它们不是分支，无法接收新提交。此选项在 Git 中技术上不可能。

## 参考资源
- [AWS 规范指南：Gitflow 策略中的分支](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/choosing-git-branch-approach/branches-in-a-gitflow-strategy.html)
- [Atlassian：Gitflow 工作流](https://www.atlassian.com/git/tutorials/comparing-workflows/gitflow-workflow)
- [Vincent Driessen：成功的 Git 分支模型](https://nvie.com/posts/a-successful-git-branching-model/)

en.question: A developer is setting up AWS CodePipeline for a new application. During each build, the developer must generate a test report. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.A: Create an AWS CodeBuild build project that runs tests. Configure the buildspec file with the test report information.
options.B: Create an AWS CodeDeploy deployment that runs tests. Configure the AppSpec file with the test report information.
options.C: Run the builds on an Amazon EC2 instance that has AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) installed and activated.
options.D: Create a repository in AWS CodeArtifact. Select the test report template.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

The developer needs to generate a **test report** during each build in an AWS CodePipeline. The question asks which AWS service and configuration is appropriate for producing test reports as part of the pipeline build stage.

## Correct Answer: A — Create a CodeBuild project that runs tests, and configure the buildspec with test report information

AWS CodeBuild has a native **Test Reports** feature. You can create reports in CodeBuild that contain details about tests that are run during builds, such as unit tests, configuration tests, and functional tests. To create a test report, you add a report group name to the buildspec file of a build project with information about your test cases. When you run the build project, the test cases are run and a test report is created. A new test report is created in the report group each time the test cases run.

A `reports:` section is added to the buildspec file:

```yaml
version: 0.2
phases:
  install:
    runtime-versions:
      java: openjdk8
  build:
    commands:
      - echo Running tests
      - <commands to run tests>
reports:
  my-report-group:
    files:
      - '**/*'
    base-directory: 'target/surefire-reports'
    file-format: JUNITXML
    discard-paths: false
```

CodeBuild supports formats including JUnit XML, NUnit XML, Cucumber JSON, TestNG, and others. The reports section specifies the report group that the reports are sent to. A project can have a maximum of five report groups. You specify the ARN of an existing report group, or the name of a new report group.

CodeBuild integrates as a build/test action in CodePipeline, making this the correct fit.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **B. CodeDeploy with AppSpec file** — CodeDeploy handles deployment (copying artifacts to EC2/Lambda/ECS, running lifecycle hooks). The `appspec.yml` controls deployment lifecycle hooks (BeforeInstall, AfterInstall, etc.); it does **not** have a test report feature. Test reports are a CodeBuild capability, not CodeDeploy's.

- **C. EC2 with SSM Agent** — Running builds on a self-managed EC2 instance with SSM Agent does not natively produce test reports integrated into the pipeline. SSM Agent is for instance management (Run Command, Patch Manager, etc.), unrelated to producing build/test reports. This is also far more operational overhead than the managed CodeBuild service.

- **D. CodeArtifact repository with test report template** — CodeArtifact is a managed **artifact repository** for software packages (npm, Maven, PyPI, NuGet, etc.). It does not run tests and has no "test report template." This option is fabricated functionality.

## References

- [Test reports in AWS CodeBuild](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/test-reporting.html)
- [Create test reports](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/report-create.html)
- [Buildspec reference – reports section](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/build-spec-ref.html)
- [Test report sample (CLI)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/sample-test-report-cli.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在为新应用程序配置 AWS CodePipeline。每次构建时，开发人员都必须生成测试报告。哪种解决方案可以满足此要求？

options.A: 创建一个运行测试的 AWS CodeBuild 构建项目。使用测试报告信息配置构建规范文件。
options.B: 创建一个运行测试的 AWS CodeDeploy 部署。使用测试报告信息配置 AppSpec 文件。
options.C: 在已安装并激活 AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) 的 Amazon EC2 实例上运行构建。
options.D: 在 AWS CodeArtifact 中创建一个代码仓库。选择测试报告模板。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

开发人员需要在 AWS CodePipeline 的每次构建期间生成**测试报告**。问题询问哪个 AWS 服务和配置适合在管道构建阶段生成测试报告。

## 正确答案：A — 创建运行测试的 CodeBuild 项目，并使用测试报告信息配置 buildspec

AWS CodeBuild 具有原生的**测试报告**功能。您可以在 CodeBuild 中创建报告，其中包含构建期间运行的测试的详细信息，例如单元测试、配置测试和功能测试。要创建测试报告，需要在构建项目的 buildspec 文件中添加报告组名称以及有关测试用例的信息。运行构建项目时，测试用例将运行并生成测试报告。每次测试用例运行时，都会在报告组中创建一个新的测试报告。

在 buildspec 文件中添加 `reports:` 部分：

```yaml
version: 0.2
phases:
  install:
    runtime-versions:
      java: openjdk8
  build:
    commands:
      - echo Running tests
      - <commands to run tests>
reports:
  my-report-group:
    files:
      - '**/*'
    base-directory: 'target/surefire-reports'
    file-format: JUNITXML
    discard-paths: false
```

CodeBuild 支持多种格式，包括 JUnit XML、NUnit XML、Cucumber JSON、TestNG 等。reports 部分指定报告发送到的报告组。一个项目最多可以有五个报告组。您可以指定现有报告组的 ARN 或新报告组的名称。

CodeBuild 在 CodePipeline 中集成为构建/测试操作，这是正确的解决方案。

## 为什么其他选项不正确

- **B. CodeDeploy 搭配 AppSpec 文件** — CodeDeploy 处理部署（将工件复制到 EC2/Lambda/ECS，运行生命周期钩子）。`appspec.yml` 控制部署生命周期钩子（BeforeInstall、AfterInstall 等）；它**没有**测试报告功能。测试报告是 CodeBuild 的功能，而非 CodeDeploy 的。

- **C. 使用 SSM Agent 的 EC2** — 在自管理的 EC2 实例上使用 SSM Agent 运行构建不会原生生成集成到管道中的测试报告。SSM Agent 用于实例管理（Run Command、Patch Manager 等），与生成构建/测试报告无关。这样做的运营开销也远大于托管的 CodeBuild 服务。

- **D. CodeArtifact 存储库搭配测试报告模板** — CodeArtifact 是托管的**工件存储库**，用于软件包（npm、Maven、PyPI、NuGet 等）。它不运行测试，也没有"测试报告模板"。这个选项属于虚构功能。

## 参考资源

- [AWS CodeBuild 中的测试报告](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/test-reporting.html)
- [创建测试报告](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/report-create.html)
- [Buildspec 参考 – reports 部分](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/build-spec-ref.html)
- [测试报告示例 (CLI)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/sample-test-report-cli.html)

en.question: A developer built an application by using multiple AWS Lambda functions. The Lambda functions must access dynamic configuration data at runtime. The data is maintained as a 6 KB JSON document in AWS AppConfig. The configuration data needs to be updated without requiring the redeployment of the application. The developer needs a solution that will give the Lambda functions access to the dynamic configuration data. What should the developer do to meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

options.A: Migrate the document from AWS AppConfig to a Lambda environment variable. Read the document at the runtime.
options.B: Configure the AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda extension. Access the dynamic configuration data by calling the extension on a local host.
options.C: Use the AWS X-Ray SDK to call the AWS AppConfig APIs. Retrieve the configuration file at runtime.
options.D: Migrate the configuration file to a Lambda deployment package. Read the file from the file system at runtime.

en.explanation:
# AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda Extension for Dynamic Configuration

## Scenario
A developer has multiple Lambda functions that need access to dynamic configuration data (a 6 KB JSON document) stored in AWS AppConfig. The configuration must be updatable without redeploying the application, and the solution must require the **least development effort**.

## Correct Answer: B

The **AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda extension** is purpose-built for this exact scenario. Integrating the AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda extension with your Lambda function simplifies this process. The extension takes care of calling the AWS AppConfig service, managing a local cache of retrieved data, tracking the configuration tokens needed for the next service calls, and periodically checking for configuration updates in the background.

To use it: To use the AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda extension, you add the extension to your Lambda function as a layer. Then you configure the AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda extension as a layer of your Lambda function. To access its configuration data, your function calls the AWS AppConfig extension at an HTTP endpoint running on localhost:2772.

This means the developer only needs to:
1. Attach the AWS-AppConfig-Extension Lambda layer.
2. Make an HTTP GET request to `http://localhost:2772/applications/{app}/environments/{env}/configurations/{config}` from the function code.

The extension handles caching, polling for updates, and token management automatically — minimizing development effort while supporting dynamic updates without redeployment.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

**A. Migrate to a Lambda environment variable** — This is incorrect for two reasons:
- Lambda environment variables have a hard total size limit of 4 KB per function, which is **insufficient for a 6 KB JSON document**.
- Updating an environment variable requires redeploying/updating the function configuration, which violates the "no redeployment" requirement and removes the dynamic update capability AppConfig provides.

**C. Use the AWS X-Ray SDK to call AppConfig APIs** — The X-Ray SDK is a tracing/observability library used to instrument applications for distributed tracing; it has no functionality for retrieving AppConfig configuration data. The correct APIs would be `StartConfigurationSession` and `GetLatestConfiguration`, but calling them directly requires more development effort than using the agent extension. If you use AWS AppConfig to manage configurations for a Lambda function without Lambda extensions, then you must configure your Lambda function to receive configuration updates by integrating with the StartConfigurationSession and GetLatestConfiguration API actions.

**D. Migrate the configuration to a Lambda deployment package** — Bundling the JSON file into the deployment package means **every configuration change requires repackaging and redeploying the Lambda function**, which directly violates the requirement that configuration updates must not require redeployment. It also abandons AppConfig entirely.

## Reference

- [Using AWS AppConfig Agent with AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appconfig/latest/userguide/appconfig-integration-lambda-extensions.html)
- [Understanding how the AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda extension works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appconfig/latest/userguide/appconfig-integration-lambda-extensions-how-it-works.html)
- [Adding the AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda extension](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appconfig/latest/userguide/appconfig-integration-lambda-extensions-add.html)
- [AWS Lambda environment variables limits](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-envvars.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员使用多个 AWS Lambda 函数构建了一个应用程序。这些 Lambda 函数需要在运行时访问动态配置数据。该数据以 6 KB 的 JSON 文档形式保存在 AWS AppConfig 中。需要在不重新部署应用程序的情况下更新配置数据。开发人员需要一个解决方案，使 Lambda 函数能够访问这些动态配置数据。为了以最小的开发工作量满足这些要求，开发人员应该怎么做？

options.A: 将文档从 AWS AppConfig 迁移到 Lambda 环境变量。在运行时读取该文档。
options.B: 配置 AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda 扩展。通过在本地主机上调用该扩展来访问动态配置数据。
options.C: 使用 AWS X-Ray SDK 调用 AWS AppConfig API。在运行时检索配置文件。
options.D: 将配置文件迁移到 Lambda 部署包中。在运行时从文件系统中读取该文件。

zh.explanation:
# AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda 扩展用于动态配置

## 场景
开发者拥有多个 Lambda 函数，需要访问存储在 AWS AppConfig 中的动态配置数据（一个 6 KB 的 JSON 文档）。配置必须可更新而无需重新部署应用程序，且解决方案必须**需要最少的开发工作量**。

## 正确答案：B

**AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda 扩展**是为这个确切场景而专门构建的。将 AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda 扩展与 Lambda 函数集成可以简化此过程。该扩展负责调用 AWS AppConfig 服务、管理检索数据的本地缓存、跟踪下一次服务调用所需的配置令牌，以及在后台定期检查配置更新。

使用方法：要使用 AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda 扩展，需要将扩展作为层添加到 Lambda 函数。然后将 AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda 扩展配置为 Lambda 函数的一个层。要访问其配置数据，函数需要在 localhost:2772 上运行的 HTTP 端点处调用 AWS AppConfig 扩展。

这意味着开发者只需：
1. 附加 AWS-AppConfig-Extension Lambda 层。
2. 从函数代码向 `http://localhost:2772/applications/{app}/environments/{env}/configurations/{config}` 发出 HTTP GET 请求。

该扩展会自动处理缓存、轮询更新和令牌管理 — 在最小化开发工作量的同时支持动态更新而无需重新部署。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

**A. 迁移到 Lambda 环境变量** — 这是错误的，原因有两个：
- Lambda 环境变量的硬性总大小限制为每个函数 4 KB，**不足以容纳 6 KB 的 JSON 文档**。
- 更新环境变量需要重新部署/更新函数配置，这违反了"无需重新部署"的要求，并移除了 AppConfig 提供的动态更新功能。

**C. 使用 AWS X-Ray SDK 调用 AppConfig API** — X-Ray SDK 是用于应用程序检测的跟踪/可观测性库，用于分布式跟踪；它没有检索 AppConfig 配置数据的功能。正确的 API 应该是 `StartConfigurationSession` 和 `GetLatestConfiguration`，但直接调用它们需要比使用代理扩展更多的开发工作量。如果使用 AWS AppConfig 管理 Lambda 函数的配置而不使用 Lambda 扩展，则必须通过与 StartConfigurationSession 和 GetLatestConfiguration API 操作集成来配置 Lambda 函数以接收配置更新。

**D. 将配置迁移到 Lambda 部署包** — 将 JSON 文件捆绑到部署包中意味着**每次配置更改都需要重新打包和重新部署 Lambda 函数**，这直接违反了配置更新无需重新部署的要求。它也完全放弃了 AppConfig。

## 参考资源

- [在 AWS Lambda 中使用 AWS AppConfig Agent](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appconfig/latest/userguide/appconfig-integration-lambda-extensions.html)
- [了解 AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda 扩展的工作原理](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appconfig/latest/userguide/appconfig-integration-lambda-extensions-how-it-works.html)
- [添加 AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda 扩展](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appconfig/latest/userguide/appconfig-integration-lambda-extensions-add.html)
- [AWS Lambda 环境变量限制](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-envvars.html)

en.question: A developer has AWS Lambda functions that need to access a company's internal data science libraries and reference data. Separate teams manage the libraries and the data. The teams must be able to update and upload new data independently. The Lambda functions are connected to the company's central VPC. Which solution will provide the Lambda functions with access to the libraries and data?

options.A: Attach an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume to the Lambda functions by using EBS Multi-Attach in the central VPC. Update the Lambda function execution roles to give the functions to access the EBS volume. Update the Lambda function code to reference the files in the EBS volume.
options.B: Compress the libraries and reference data in a Lambda /tmp folder. Update the Lambda function code to reference the files in the /tmp folder.
options.C: Set up an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system with mount targets in the central VPConfigure the Lambda functions to mount the EFS file system. Update the Lambda function execution roles to give the functions to access the EFS file system.
options.D: Set up an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system with mount targets in the central VPC. Configure the Lambda functions to mount the Amazon FSx file system. Update the Lambda function execution roles to give the functions to access the Amazon FSx file system.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

Lambda functions in a central VPC need shared access to:
- **Internal data science libraries** maintained by one team
- **Reference data** maintained by another team

Both teams must be able to **independently update and upload** content. The solution must allow Lambda functions to read this shared content at runtime.

## Correct Answer: C — Amazon EFS

Amazon EFS is the AWS-native shared file system that integrates directly with Lambda. EFS for Lambda allows you to share data across function invocations, read large reference data files, and write function output to a persistent and shared store. Lambda securely connects the function instances to the EFS mount targets in the same Availability Zone and subnet.

This perfectly fits the scenario:
- Both teams can independently mount EFS (from EC2, Cloud9, or other clients) and upload/update files at any time without redeploying Lambda.
- Lambda functions read the latest content directly from the mounted path.
- ML model loading: Store large models (sometimes several gigabytes) on EFS instead of packaging them in the Lambda deployment or downloading from S3 on every cold start — the same pattern applies to data science libraries.

Configuration requirements:
- Create a file system in Amazon EFS with a mount target in every Availability Zone that your function connects to. For performance and resilience, use at least two Availability Zones.
- Ensure that NFS traffic (port 2049) is allowed by the security groups used by the function and mount targets.
- The Lambda function's execution role must have elasticfilesystem:ClientMount permission for read and write connections and elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite permission for write-only connections.

## Why the other options are wrong

**A. EBS Multi-Attach** — Lambda **cannot** attach EBS volumes. EBS is block storage designed for EC2 instances; Multi-Attach is restricted to specific io1/io2 volumes attached to multiple EC2 instances in the same AZ. Lambda has no API to attach an EBS volume. Unlike EBS which is block-based storage, EFS is file-based storage.

**B. Compress libraries in /tmp** — `/tmp` is **ephemeral and per-execution-environment**, capped at 10 GB and not shared across function instances. Teams cannot independently upload there; content would have to be baked into the deployment package or downloaded on every cold start. Lambda functions are stateless by nature. Each invocation starts fresh, and when it ends, any files you wrote to /tmp are gone (or might be reused if the execution environment is warm, but you can't rely on that). The /tmp directory also has a size limit - 10 GB as of recent updates, but that's still not enough for many use cases.

**D. FSx for Windows File Server** — FSx for Windows uses the SMB protocol and is designed for Windows-based workloads (Active Directory integration, Windows ACLs). **Lambda does not natively support mounting FSx for Windows file systems.** Lambda's native file-system integration is only with Amazon EFS (NFS). Configure your Lambda function to access a file system such as Amazon EFS or Amazon S3 Files.

## References

- [Configuring file system access for Lambda functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-filesystem.html)
- [Using Amazon EFS for AWS Lambda in your serverless applications (AWS Compute Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/using-amazon-efs-for-aws-lambda-in-your-serverless-applications/)
- [Use a Lambda function to create an EFS access point mount (AWS re:Post)](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/efs-mount-with-lambda-function)

zh.question: 一位开发人员的 AWS Lambda 函数需要访问公司内部的数据科学库和参考数据。这些库和数据由不同的团队管理。这些团队必须能够独立地更新和上传新数据。Lambda 函数连接到公司的中央 VPC。哪种解决方案能够为 Lambda 函数提供对库和数据的访问权限？

options.A: 使用中央 VPC 中的 EBS 多重附加功能，将 Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) 卷附加到 Lambda 函数。更新 Lambda 函数的执行角色，赋予函数访问 EBS 卷的权限。更新 Lambda 函数代码，使其引用 EBS 卷中的文件。
options.B: 将库文件和引用数据压缩到 Lambda 的 /tmp 文件夹中。更新 Lambda 函数代码，使其引用 /tmp 文件夹中的文件。
options.C: 在中央虚拟专用网 (VP) 中设置 Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) 文件系统，并配置 Lambda 函数以挂载 EFS 文件系统。更新 Lambda 函数的执行角色，授予这些函数访问 EFS 文件系统的权限。
options.D: 在中央 VPC 中设置 Amazon FSx for Windows 文件服务器文件系统及其挂载目标。配置 Lambda 函数以挂载 Amazon FSx 文件系统。更新 Lambda 函数的执行角色，授予这些函数访问 Amazon FSx 文件系统的权限。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

中央 VPC 中的 Lambda 函数需要共享访问：
- **内部数据科学库**（由一个团队维护）
- **参考数据**（由另一个团队维护）

两个团队都必须能够**独立更新和上传**内容。该解决方案必须允许 Lambda 函数在运行时读取此共享内容。

## 正确答案：C — Amazon EFS

Amazon EFS 是与 Lambda 直接集成的 AWS 原生共享文件系统。EFS for Lambda 允许您在函数调用之间共享数据、读取大型参考数据文件，以及将函数输出写入持久和共享存储。Lambda 安全地将函数实例连接到同一可用区和子网中的 EFS 挂载目标。

这完全符合该场景：
- 两个团队都可以独立挂载 EFS（从 EC2、Cloud9 或其他客户端），并可以随时上传/更新文件，而无需重新部署 Lambda。
- Lambda 函数直接从挂载路径读取最新内容。
- ML 模型加载：将大型模型（有时为几个 GB）存储在 EFS 上，而不是将其打包在 Lambda 部署中或在每次冷启动时从 S3 下载 — 相同的模式适用于数据科学库。

配置要求：
- 在 Amazon EFS 中创建文件系统，并在您的函数连接到的每个可用区中创建挂载目标。为了获得最佳性能和弹性，请至少使用两个可用区。
- 确保安全组允许 NFS 流量（端口 2049），该安全组由函数和挂载目标使用。
- Lambda 函数的执行角色必须具有 elasticfilesystem:ClientMount 权限以进行读写连接，以及 elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite 权限以进行仅写入连接。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

**A. EBS Multi-Attach** — Lambda **无法**附加 EBS 卷。EBS 是为 EC2 实例设计的块存储；Multi-Attach 仅限于在同一 AZ 中附加到多个 EC2 实例的特定 io1/io2 卷。Lambda 没有 API 来附加 EBS 卷。与基于块的存储 EBS 不同，EFS 是基于文件的存储。

**B. 在 /tmp 中压缩库** — `/tmp` **是短暂的，且针对每个执行环境**，上限为 10 GB，不在函数实例之间共享。团队无法独立在其中上传；内容必须烘焙到部署包中或在每次冷启动时下载。Lambda 函数本质上是无状态的。每次调用都是从新开始的，当调用结束时，您写入 /tmp 的任何文件都消失了（或如果执行环境处于预热状态可能被重用，但您不能依赖这一点）。/tmp 目录也有大小限制 — 截至最近更新为 10 GB，但这对许多用例仍然不够。

**D. FSx for Windows File Server** — FSx for Windows 使用 SMB 协议，专为基于 Windows 的工作负载设计（Active Directory 集成、Windows ACL）。**Lambda 本身不支持挂载 FSx for Windows 文件系统。**Lambda 的原生文件系统集成仅支持 Amazon EFS（NFS）。配置您的 Lambda 函数以访问文件系统，例如 Amazon EFS 或 Amazon S3 Files。

## 参考资源

- [为 Lambda 函数配置文件系统访问](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-filesystem.html)
- [在无服务器应用程序中为 AWS Lambda 使用 Amazon EFS（AWS 计算博客）](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/using-amazon-efs-for-aws-lambda-in-your-serverless-applications/)
- [使用 Lambda 函数创建 EFS 访问点挂载（AWS re:Post）](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/efs-mount-with-lambda-function)

en.question: A company has an application that uses an AWS Lambda function to consume messages from an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. The SQS queue is configured with a dead-letter queue. Due to a defect in the application, AWS Lambda failed to process some messages. A developer fixed the bug and wants to process the failed messages again. How should the developer resolve this issue?

options.A: Use the SendMessageBatch API to send messages from the dead-letter queue to the original SQS queue.
options.B: Use the ChangeMessageVisibility API to configure messages in the dead-letter queue to be visible in the original SQS queue.
options.C: Use the StartMessageMoveTask API to move messages from the dead-letter queue to the original SQS queue.
options.D: Use the PurgeQueue API to remove messages from the dead-letter queue and return the messages to the original SQS queue.

en.explanation:
# Reprocessing Failed Messages from an SQS Dead-Letter Queue

## Scenario
A Lambda function consumed messages from an SQS queue, and failures (caused by an application bug) sent some messages to the configured **dead-letter queue (DLQ)**. After fixing the bug, the developer needs to **redrive** those messages from the DLQ back to the original source queue so Lambda can process them again.

## Correct Answer: C — Use `StartMessageMoveTask`

In June 2023, AWS released programmatic DLQ redrive support via the AWS SDK/CLI. The actions added are StartMessageMoveTask (to start a new message movement task from the dead-letter queue), CancelMessageMoveTask, and ListMessageMoveTasks.

This action is currently limited to supporting message redrive from queues that are configured as dead-letter queues (DLQs) of other Amazon SQS queues only. In the dead-letter queue redrive context, the StartMessageMoveTask source queue is the DLQ, while the destination queue can be the original source queue (from which the messages were driven to the dead-letter-queue), or a custom destination queue.

You can use the DestinationArn field to specify the destination queue where you would like to redrive messages. If this field is left blank, the messages will be redriven back to their respective original source queues.

Example CLI invocation:

```bash
aws sqs start-message-move-task \
  --source-arn arn:aws:sqs:us-east-1:111122223333:MyDLQ \
  --max-number-of-messages-per-second 10
```

This is the AWS-recommended, purpose-built mechanism for the exact scenario in the question — see [StartMessageMoveTask API reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/APIReference/API_StartMessageMoveTask.html) and [DLQ redrive guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-configure-dead-letter-queue-redrive.html).

## Why the other options are wrong

- **A. `SendMessageBatch`** — This API only sends *new* messages to a queue (up to 10 per call, 256 KB total). Manually receiving from the DLQ and re-sending via SendMessageBatch is a custom workaround that does **not** preserve original message metadata cleanly, and it is not the AWS-purpose-built redrive mechanism. It would also still require deleting messages from the DLQ separately.

- **B. `ChangeMessageVisibility`** — This API only changes the visibility timeout of a message in the queue it currently resides in. It does **not** move messages between queues. A message in the DLQ stays in the DLQ; changing its visibility cannot make it appear in the source queue. See [ChangeMessageVisibility](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/APIReference/API_ChangeMessageVisibility.html).

- **D. `PurgeQueue`** — This API **deletes all messages** in a queue. If used on the DLQ, the messages would be permanently lost, not returned to the source queue. It does not move or redrive messages.

## Key Limits to Remember
A dead-letter queue redrive task can run a maximum of 36 hours, and Amazon SQS supports a maximum of 100 active redrive tasks per account. SQS supports dead-letter queue redrive only for standard queues and does not support filtering and modifying messages while reprocessing them.

zh.question: 一家公司有一个应用程序，该应用程序使用 AWS Lambda 函数从 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列中消费消息。该 SQS 队列配置了死信队列。由于应用程序存在缺陷，AWS Lambda 未能处理某些消息。开发人员修复了该缺陷，并希望再次处理这些失败的消息。开发人员应该如何解决这个问题？

options.A: 使用 SendMessageBatch API 将消息从死信队列发送到原始 SQS 队列。
options.B: 使用 ChangeMessageVisibility API 配置死信队列中的消息，使其在原始 SQS 队列中可见。
options.C: 使用 StartMessageMoveTask API 将消息从死信队列移动到原始 SQS 队列。
options.D: 使用 PurgeQueue API 从死信队列中删除消息，并将消息返回到原始 SQS 队列。

zh.explanation:
# 从 SQS 死信队列重新处理失败的消息

## 场景
Lambda 函数从 SQS 队列中消费消息，由于应用程序错误导致的失败将某些消息发送到了配置的**死信队列 (DLQ)**。修复错误后，开发人员需要**重新驱动**那些消息从 DLQ 回到原始源队列，以便 Lambda 可以再次处理它们。

## 正确答案：C — 使用 `StartMessageMoveTask`

2023 年 6 月，AWS 通过 AWS SDK/CLI 发布了编程式 DLQ 重新驱动支持。添加的操作包括 StartMessageMoveTask（启动从死信队列的新消息移动任务）、CancelMessageMoveTask 和 ListMessageMoveTasks。

此操作目前仅限于支持从配置为其他 Amazon SQS 队列的死信队列 (DLQ) 的队列重新驱动消息。在死信队列重新驱动的上下文中，StartMessageMoveTask 源队列是 DLQ，而目标队列可以是原始源队列（消息被驱动到死信队列的队列），或自定义目标队列。

您可以使用 DestinationArn 字段指定要重新驱动消息的目标队列。如果留空此字段，消息将被重新驱动回各自的原始源队列。

示例 CLI 调用：

```bash
aws sqs start-message-move-task \
  --source-arn arn:aws:sqs:us-east-1:111122223333:MyDLQ \
  --max-number-of-messages-per-second 10
```

这是 AWS 推荐的、为此问题中的确切场景而构建的专用机制 — 请参阅 [StartMessageMoveTask API 参考](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/APIReference/API_StartMessageMoveTask.html)和 [DLQ 重新驱动指南](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-configure-dead-letter-queue-redrive.html)。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

- **A. `SendMessageBatch`** — 此 API 仅向队列发送*新*消息（每次调用最多 10 条，总共 256 KB）。手动从 DLQ 接收并通过 SendMessageBatch 重新发送是一个自定义解决方法，不能**很好地**保留原始消息元数据，并且它不是 AWS 专用的重新驱动机制。它还需要单独从 DLQ 删除消息。

- **B. `ChangeMessageVisibility`** — 此 API 仅更改消息当前所在队列中的可见性超时。它**不**在队列之间移动消息。DLQ 中的消息保留在 DLQ 中；更改其可见性不能使其出现在源队列中。请参阅 [ChangeMessageVisibility](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/APIReference/API_ChangeMessageVisibility.html)。

- **D. `PurgeQueue`** — 此 API **删除队列中的所有消息**。如果在 DLQ 上使用，消息将被永久删除，而不是返回到源队列。它不会移动或重新驱动消息。

## 需要记住的关键限制
死信队列重新驱动任务最长可运行 36 小时，Amazon SQS 支持每个账户最多 100 个活跃重新驱动任务。SQS 仅支持标准队列的死信队列重新驱动，不支持在重新处理消息时过滤和修改消息。

en.question: A developer is working on an application that will be deployed on AWS. The developer needs to test and debug the code locally. The code is packaged and stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. How can the developer test and debug the code locally with the LEAST amount of configuration?

options.A: Create an application and a deployment group in AWS CodeDeploy. For the compute platform, specify the local machine as the individual instance for the deployment. For the repository type, specify that the application is stored in Amazon S3. Start the deployment to test on the local machine.
options.B: Create a repository in AWS CodeArtifact. Publish the application code package to the repository. Before deployment, create an upstream repository to test and validate the code.
options.C: Create a build project in AWS CodeBuild. In AWS CodePipeline, add a CodeBuild test action by adding a stage and an action. For the action provider, specify a CodeBuild test and the build project. View the build log to see the test results.
options.D: Install the AWS CodeDeploy agent locally to validate the deployment package. Run the codedeploy- local command. Specify the S3 bucket where the code package is located by using the --bundle- location option.

en.explanation:
# Test and Debug CodeDeploy Application Locally

## Scenario
The developer has an application package stored in an Amazon S3 bucket and wants to **test and debug locally** with the **least configuration**.

## Correct Answer: D

Install the CodeDeploy agent locally and use the `codedeploy-local` command (a developer utility bundled with the agent) to validate the deployment package directly from S3.

By validating a deployment package on a local machine you can: Test the integrity of an application revision. Test the contents of an AppSpec file. Try out CodeDeploy for the first time with your existing application code. Deploy content rapidly when you are already logged in to an instance.

You can use deploy content that is stored on the local instance or in a supported remote repository type (Amazon S3 buckets or public GitHub repositories).

The `--bundle-location` option accepts an S3 URI directly, so no manual download step is needed:

```bash
codedeploy-local -l s3://my-bucket/MyApp.zip -t zip
```

If the application package is stored in an S3 bucket or GitHub repository, codedeploy-local can be executed without downloading the file onto the local machine. You can do this using the -l, –bundle-location and -t, –type with the codedeploy-local command. Here is an example for deploying a sample application package located in an S3 bucket: codedeploy-local -l s3://aws-codedeploy-us-east-1/samples/latest/SampleApp_Linux.zip -t zip

This delivers the **least configuration** since you only need to install the CodeDeploy agent — no application, deployment group, pipeline, or repository setup is required.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A. Create an application and deployment group in CodeDeploy with the local machine as an instance** — CodeDeploy compute platforms are EC2/On-Premises, AWS Lambda, or Amazon ECS. You cannot specify "the local machine" as a compute platform via the managed CodeDeploy service. To use an on-premises instance, you must register it with CodeDeploy, install the agent, configure IAM session credentials, and create application/deployment group resources — far more configuration than option D.

- **B. Use AWS CodeArtifact with an upstream repository** — CodeArtifact is a managed artifact repository for software packages (npm, Maven, PyPI, NuGet, etc.). It does not execute or "test/debug" deployment bundles, and upstream repositories simply chain repos together. It does not solve local testing of a CodeDeploy package.

- **C. Use CodeBuild action in CodePipeline** — This adds a build/test stage in the cloud pipeline, not a local debug capability. It requires significant setup (build project, pipeline, stages, actions, buildspec) and runs in CodeBuild's managed environment — the opposite of "least configuration" for local testing.

## References
- [Use the CodeDeploy agent to validate a deployment package on a local machine](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployments-local.html)
- [How to Test and Debug AWS CodeDeploy Locally Before You Ship Your Code (AWS Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/devops/how-to-test-and-debug-aws-codedeploy-locally-before-you-ship-your-code/)

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在开发一个将部署在 AWS 上的应用程序。他需要在本地测试和调试代码。代码已打包并存储在 Amazon S3 存储桶中。开发人员如何才能以最少的配置在本地测试和调试代码？

options.A: 在 AWS CodeDeploy 中创建应用程序和部署组。对于计算平台，指定本地计算机作为部署的独立实例。对于存储库类型，指定应用程序存储在 Amazon S3 中。启动部署以在本地计算机上进行测试。
options.B: 在 AWS CodeArtifact 中创建一个代码仓库。将应用程序代码包发布到该仓库。部署之前，创建一个上游代码仓库来测试和验证代码。
options.C: 在 AWS CodeBuild 中创建一个构建项目。在 AWS CodePipeline 中，通过添加阶段和操作来添加 CodeBuild 测试操作。对于操作提供程序，指定 CodeBuild 测试和构建项目。查看构建日志以查看测试结果。
options.D: 在本地安装 AWS CodeDeploy 代理以验证部署包。运行 codedeploy-local 命令。使用 --bundle-location 选项指定代码包所在的 S3 存储桶。

zh.explanation:
# 在本地测试和调试 CodeDeploy 应用程序

## 场景
开发人员在 Amazon S3 存储桶中存储了应用程序包，并希望**在本地测试和调试**，配置**最少**。

## 正确答案：D

在本地安装 CodeDeploy agent，并使用 `codedeploy-local` 命令（与 agent 捆绑的开发人员实用程序）直接从 S3 验证部署包。

通过在本地计算机上验证部署包，您可以：测试应用程序修订版的完整性。测试 AppSpec 文件的内容。首次尝试 CodeDeploy 与现有应用程序代码。在已登录到实例时快速部署内容。

您可以部署存储在本地实例或受支持的远程存储库类型（Amazon S3 存储桶或公共 GitHub 存储库）中的内容。

`--bundle-location` 选项直接接受 S3 URI，因此无需手动下载步骤：

```bash
codedeploy-local -l s3://my-bucket/MyApp.zip -t zip
```

如果应用程序包存储在 S3 存储桶或 GitHub 存储库中，可以在不将文件下载到本地计算机的情况下执行 codedeploy-local。您可以使用 -l、–bundle-location 和 -t、–type 与 codedeploy-local 命令一起执行此操作。以下是部署位于 S3 存储桶中的示例应用程序包的示例：codedeploy-local -l s3://aws-codedeploy-us-east-1/samples/latest/SampleApp_Linux.zip -t zip

这提供了**最少配置**，因为您只需要安装 CodeDeploy agent — 无需应用程序、部署组、管道或存储库设置。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

- **A. 在 CodeDeploy 中创建应用程序和部署组，将本地计算机作为实例** — CodeDeploy 计算平台是 EC2/On-Premises、AWS Lambda 或 Amazon ECS。您不能通过托管 CodeDeploy 服务将"本地计算机"指定为计算平台。要使用本地实例，您必须向 CodeDeploy 注册该实例、安装 agent、配置 IAM 会话凭证，以及创建应用程序/部署组资源 — 比选项 D 需要更多的配置。

- **B. 使用 AWS CodeArtifact 与上游存储库** — CodeArtifact 是用于软件包的托管工件存储库（npm、Maven、PyPI、NuGet 等）。它不执行或"测试/调试"部署包，上游存储库只是链接存储库。它不能解决 CodeDeploy 包的本地测试问题。

- **C. 在 CodePipeline 中使用 CodeBuild 操作** — 这在云管道中添加了构建/测试阶段，而不是本地调试功能。它需要大量设置（构建项目、管道、阶段、操作、buildspec），并在 CodeBuild 的托管环境中运行 — 与本地测试的"最少配置"相反。

## 参考资源
- [使用 CodeDeploy agent 在本地计算机上验证部署包](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployments-local.html)
- [How to Test and Debug AWS CodeDeploy Locally Before You Ship Your Code (AWS Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/devops/how-to-test-and-debug-aws-codedeploy-locally-before-you-ship-your-code/)

en.question: A developer is creating an application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). The developer needs to configure the application parameters. The developer must configure limits for the application's maximum number of simultaneous connections and maximum number of transactions per second. The maximum number of connections and transactions can change in the future. The developer needs a solution that can automatically deploy these changes to the application, as needed, without causing downtime. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Make the configuration changes for the application. Use AWS CodeDeploy to create a deployment configuration. Specify an in-place deployment to deploy the changes.
options.B: Bootstrap the application to use the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) and make the configuration changes. Specify the ECSCanary10Percent15Minutes launch type in the properties section of the ECS resource. Deploy the application by using the AWS CDK to implement the changes.
options.C: Install the AWS AppConfig agent on Amazon ECS. Configure an IAM role with access to AWS AppConfig. Make the deployment changes by using AWS AppConfig. Specify Canary10Percent20Minutes as the deployment strategy.
options.D: Create an AWS Lambda function to make the configuration changes. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that monitors the Lambda function every 5 minutes to check if the Lambda function has been updated. When the Lambda function is updated, deploy the changes by using AWS CodeDeploy.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

The developer is building an ECS-based application that has runtime configuration parameters (max simultaneous connections and max transactions per second). These values may change over time and the new values must be pushed to the running application **without downtime** and ideally with a **gradual / safe rollout**.

The question is fundamentally about **dynamic configuration management** — not application code deployment. The clue is that only configuration *values* (limits) are changing, not the application binary or container image.

## Correct Answer: C

**AWS AppConfig** is purpose-built for exactly this use case: deploying configuration data (feature flags, operational tuning parameters like connection/throughput limits) to running applications in a controlled, monitored, and gradual way — with no application redeploy.

- The **AWS AppConfig Agent** runs alongside the application on ECS (as a sidecar) and continuously polls AppConfig for new configuration versions. An AppConfig Agent runs as a sidecar in every ECS task and polls for configuration updates (the default interval is 45 seconds). The application itself just calls localhost:2772; all SDK calls are hidden inside the sidecar.
- The agent uses an **IAM role** to call AppConfig on the application's behalf and caches data locally for fast, resilient retrieval.
- AppConfig supports predefined **deployment strategies** including `Canary10Percent20Minutes`. A deployment strategy enables you to slowly release changes to all targets or specific segments over minutes or hours. A canary strategy such as Canary10Percent20minutes works like this: At 0 minutes → apply the new config to 10 percent of traffic.
- This produces a zero-downtime, gradual rollout of the new connection/TPS limits with automatic rollback support via CloudWatch alarms.

See: [AWS AppConfig integration with ECS/EKS containers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appconfig/latest/userguide/appconfig-integration-containers-agent.html) and [AppConfig deployment strategies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appconfig/latest/userguide/appconfig-creating-deployment-strategy.html).

## Why the other options are wrong

**A. CodeDeploy in-place deployment** — An in-place deployment stops the application on each instance, installs the latest revision, and restarts it. This is a code/artifact deployment pattern, **causes downtime per instance**, and is overkill for changing two configuration values. It does not address dynamic configuration management.

**B. CDK with `ECSCanary10Percent15Minutes` launch type** — There is **no such property** as `ECSCanary10Percent15Minutes` on an "ECS resource" in CDK. `CodeDeployDefault.ECSCanary10Percent15Minutes` is a CodeDeploy *deployment configuration* used for **Lambda or ECS code deployments via CodeDeploy blue/green**, not a CDK ECS resource property. Additionally, this still re-deploys the task/container image rather than dynamically updating configuration — wrong tool for tunable runtime parameters.

**C. ✅** — Correct, as explained above.

**D. Lambda + CloudWatch alarm + CodeDeploy** — This is a contrived workflow: monitoring a Lambda function "every 5 minutes to check if it has been updated" is not how CloudWatch alarms work (alarms watch metrics, not code-update events). CodeDeploy doesn't deploy configuration to a running ECS task in a hot-reload fashion either. The architecture is convoluted, fragile, and does not provide a controlled canary rollout of configuration values. AppConfig is the AWS-native, purpose-built solution for this exact problem.

## Key takeaway

When the question describes **changing operational/tuning parameters of a running app with no downtime and gradual rollout**, the answer is almost always **AWS AppConfig** (with the AppConfig Agent on ECS and a Canary deployment strategy).

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在 Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) 上创建一个应用程序。该开发人员需要配置应用程序参数。他们必须配置应用程序的最大并发连接数和每秒最大事务数的限制。这些最大连接数和事务数将来可能会发生变化。开发人员需要一个解决方案，能够根据需要自动将这些更改部署到应用程序，而不会造成停机。哪个解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 对应用程序进行配置更改。使用 AWS CodeDeploy 创建部署配置。指定就地部署以应用更改。
options.B: 使用 AWS 云开发工具包 (AWS CDK) 引导应用程序并进行配置更改。在 ECS 资源的属性部分指定 ECSCanary10Percent15Minutes 启动类型。使用 AWS CDK 部署应用程序以应用这些更改。
options.C: 在 Amazon ECS 上安装 AWS AppConfig 代理。配置具有 AWS AppConfig 访问权限的 IAM 角色。使用 AWS AppConfig 进行部署更改。将部署策略指定为 Canary10Percent20Minutes。
options.D: 创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数来进行配置更改。创建一个 Amazon CloudWatch 警报，每 5 分钟监控一次 Lambda 函数，检查其是否已更新。Lambda 函数更新后，使用 AWS CodeDeploy 部署更改。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

开发人员正在构建一个基于 ECS 的应用程序，该应用程序具有运行时配置参数（最大并发连接数和每秒最大事务数）。这些值可能随时间变化，新值必须在**无停机时间**的情况下推送到正在运行的应用程序，理想情况下还要**逐步/安全地推出**。

这个问题从根本上讲是关于**动态配置管理**——而不是应用程序代码部署。线索是只有配置*值*（限制）在改变，而不是应用程序二进制文件或容器镜像。

## 正确答案：C

**AWS AppConfig** 正是为这个用例专门设计的：以受控、受监控和逐步的方式将配置数据（功能标志、操作调整参数如连接/吞吐量限制）部署到正在运行的应用程序，无需重新部署应用程序。

- **AWS AppConfig Agent** 作为 sidecar 在 ECS 上运行，并持续轮询 AppConfig 以获取新的配置版本。AppConfig Agent 作为 sidecar 在每个 ECS 任务中运行，并轮询配置更新（默认间隔为 45 秒）。应用程序本身只需调用 localhost:2772；所有 SDK 调用都隐藏在 sidecar 内。
- Agent 使用 **IAM 角色**代表应用程序调用 AppConfig，并在本地缓存数据以实现快速、有弹性的检索。
- AppConfig 支持预定义的**部署策略**，包括 `Canary10Percent20Minutes`。部署策略使您能够在几分钟或几小时内缓慢地将更改发布到所有目标或特定段。 金丝雀策略如 Canary10Percent20minutes 的工作方式如下：在 0 分钟时 → 将新配置应用于 10% 的流量。
- 这实现了新连接/TPS 限制的零停机时间、逐步推出，并支持通过 CloudWatch 告警进行自动回滚。

参见：[AWS AppConfig 与 ECS/EKS 容器的集成](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appconfig/latest/userguide/appconfig-integration-containers-agent.html)和 [AppConfig 部署策略](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appconfig/latest/userguide/appconfig-creating-deployment-strategy.html)。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

**A. CodeDeploy 原地部署** — 原地部署会停止每个实例上的应用程序、安装最新的修订版本并重新启动它。这是一个代码/工件部署模式，**每个实例都会造成停机时间**，并且对于改变两个配置值来说太重了。它不能解决动态配置管理问题。

**B. CDK 的 `ECSCanary10Percent15Minutes` 启动类型** — CDK 中的 ECS 资源上**不存在** `ECSCanary10Percent15Minutes` 这样的属性。`CodeDeployDefault.ECSCanary10Percent15Minutes` 是 CodeDeploy 的*部署配置*，用于**通过 CodeDeploy 蓝/绿进行 Lambda 或 ECS 代码部署**，不是 CDK ECS 资源属性。此外，这仍然是重新部署任务/容器镜像，而不是动态更新配置——对于可调的运行时参数来说是错误的工具。

**C. ✅** — 正确，如上所述。

**D. Lambda + CloudWatch 告警 + CodeDeploy** — 这是一个繁琐的工作流：监控一个 Lambda 函数"每 5 分钟检查它是否已被更新"不是 CloudWatch 告警的工作方式（告警监控指标，而不是代码更新事件）。CodeDeploy 也不能以热重载方式将配置部署到正在运行的 ECS 任务。该架构很复杂、脆弱，不能提供配置值的受控金丝雀推出。AppConfig 是 AWS 原生的、为这个确切问题专门设计的解决方案。

## 关键要点

当问题描述**更改正在运行的应用程序的操作/调整参数，无停机时间且逐步推出**时，答案几乎总是 **AWS AppConfig**（在 ECS 上配合 AppConfig Agent 和金丝雀部署策略）。

en.question: A developer has built an application running on AWS Lambda using AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM). What is the correct sequence of steps to successfully deploy the application?

options.A: 1. Build the SAM template in Amazon EC2. 2. Package the SAM template to Amazon EBS storage. 3. Deploy the SAM template from Amazon EBS.
options.B: 1. Build the SAM template locally. 2. Package the SAM template onto Amazon S3. 3. Deploy the SAM template from Amazon S3.
options.C: 1. Build the SAM template locally. 2. Deploy the SAM template from Amazon S3. 3. Package the SAM template for use.
options.D: 1. Build the SAM template locally. 2. Package the SAM template from AWS CodeCommit. 3. Deploy the SAM template to CodeCommit.

en.explanation:
# AWS SAM Deployment Sequence

## Scenario
A developer has built a Lambda application using AWS SAM and needs to know the proper order of steps to deploy it to AWS.

## Standard SAM Workflow
The AWS SAM CLI provides three core commands that form the deployment workflow:

1. **`sam build`** – The sam build command prepares an application for subsequent steps in the developer workflow, such as local testing or deploying to the AWS Cloud. This step runs **locally** (optionally inside Docker).
2. **`sam package`** – Zips the code and dependencies and uploads them to an Amazon S3 bucket. It then returns a copy of your AWS SAM template, replacing references to local artifacts with the Amazon S3 location where the command uploaded the artifacts.
3. **`sam deploy`** – For applications with AWS Lambda functions packaged as a .zip file archive, the AWS SAM CLI zips and uploads the package to an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket. If necessary, the AWS SAM CLI will create a new bucket. Then the AWS SAM CLI creates an AWS CloudFormation change set and deploys your application to CloudFormation as a stack.

This corresponds exactly to **Option B**: Build locally → Package to S3 → Deploy from S3.

Example commands:
```bash
sam build
sam package --template-file template.yaml \
            --output-template-file packaged.yaml \
            --s3-bucket my-bucket
sam deploy  --template-file packaged.yaml \
            --stack-name my-stack \
            --capabilities CAPABILITY_IAM
```

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A. Build on EC2 → Package to EBS → Deploy from EBS.** SAM templates are built **locally** with the SAM CLI, not on EC2 instances. EBS is block storage attached to EC2 instances and is **not** used by SAM as an artifact store; SAM uses S3 (or ECR for container image package types). The name of the Amazon S3 bucket where this command uploads your artifact.

- **C. Build locally → Deploy from S3 → Package for use.** The order is wrong. You must **package before deploy** because deploy consumes the packaged template (which contains S3 references to the uploaded code artifacts). The output of the command is a new file called package.yml. This file is used by the AWS SAM sam deploy command in the next step.

- **D. Package from CodeCommit → Deploy to CodeCommit.** CodeCommit is a Git source-control service for storing source code; it is not an artifact storage destination for SAM packaged Lambda zip files. SAM uploads packaged artifacts to **S3** (or images to **ECR**), not to CodeCommit.

## Correct Answer: **B**

## References
- [sam build – AWS SAM Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/sam-cli-command-reference-sam-build.html)
- [sam package – AWS SAM Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/sam-cli-command-reference-sam-package.html)
- [sam deploy – AWS SAM Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/sam-cli-command-reference-sam-deploy.html)
- [Introduction to deploying with AWS SAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/using-sam-cli-deploy.html)
- [Package the AWS SAM application – CodeDeploy tutorial](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/tutorial-lambda-sam-package.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员使用 AWS 无服务器应用程序模型 (AWS SAM) 构建了一个运行在 AWS Lambda 上的应用程序。成功部署该应用程序的正确步骤顺序是什么？

options.A: 1. 在 Amazon EC2 中构建 SAM 模板。2 . 将 SAM 模板打包到 Amazon EBS 存储。3 . 从 Amazon EBS 部署 SAM 模板。
options.B: 1. 在本地构建 SAM 模板。2 . 将 SAM 模板打包到 Amazon S3。3 . 从 Amazon S3 部署 SAM 模板。
options.C: 1. 在本地构建 SAM 模板。2 . 从 Amazon S3 部署 SAM 模板。3 . 将 SAM 模板打包以供使用。
options.D: 1. 在本地构建 SAM 模板。2 . 从 AWS CodeCommit 打包 SAM 模板。3 . 将 SAM 模板部署到 CodeCommit。

zh.explanation:
# AWS SAM 部署序列

## 场景
开发人员使用 AWS SAM 构建了 Lambda 应用程序，需要了解部署到 AWS 的正确步骤顺序。

## 标准 SAM 工作流
AWS SAM CLI 提供了三个核心命令，形成部署工作流：

1. **`sam build`** – sam build 命令为应用程序准备后续的开发人员工作流步骤，例如本地测试或部署到 AWS Cloud。 此步骤在**本地**运行（可选地在 Docker 内部）。
2. **`sam package`** – 将代码和依赖项压缩并上传到 Amazon S3 存储桶。然后返回 AWS SAM 模板的副本，将本地工件引用替换为命令上传工件的 Amazon S3 位置。
3. **`sam deploy`** – 对于将 AWS Lambda 函数打包为 .zip 文件存档的应用程序，AWS SAM CLI 将包压缩并上传到 Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) 存储桶。如有必要，AWS SAM CLI 将创建新的存储桶。 然后AWS SAM CLI 创建 AWS CloudFormation 变更集并将应用程序部署到 CloudFormation 作为一个堆栈。

这正好对应**选项 B**：本地构建 → 打包到 S3 → 从 S3 部署。

示例命令：
```bash
sam build
sam package --template-file template.yaml \
            --output-template-file packaged.yaml \
            --s3-bucket my-bucket
sam deploy  --template-file packaged.yaml \
            --stack-name my-stack \
            --capabilities CAPABILITY_IAM
```

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

- **A. 在 EC2 上构建 → 打包到 EBS → 从 EBS 部署。** SAM 模板使用 SAM CLI 在**本地**构建，而不是在 EC2 实例上。EBS 是连接到 EC2 实例的块存储，**不被** SAM 用作工件存储；SAM 使用 S3（或 ECR 用于容器镜像包类型）。此命令上传工件的 Amazon S3 存储桶的名称。

- **C. 本地构建 → 从 S3 部署 → 打包以供使用。** 顺序错误。你必须**在部署之前打包**，因为部署使用打包后的模板（其中包含上传代码工件的 S3 引用）。命令的输出是一个名为 package.yml 的新文件。此文件由 AWS SAM sam deploy 命令在下一步中使用。

- **D. 从 CodeCommit 打包 → 部署到 CodeCommit。** CodeCommit 是用于存储源代码的 Git 源代码控制服务；它不是 SAM 打包 Lambda zip 文件的工件存储目标。SAM 将打包后的工件上传到 **S3**（或镜像到 **ECR**），而不是 CodeCommit。

## 正确答案：**B**

## 参考资源
- [sam build – AWS SAM Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/sam-cli-command-reference-sam-build.html)
- [sam package – AWS SAM Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/sam-cli-command-reference-sam-package.html)
- [sam deploy – AWS SAM Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/sam-cli-command-reference-sam-deploy.html)
- [Introduction to deploying with AWS SAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/using-sam-cli-deploy.html)
- [Package the AWS SAM application – CodeDeploy tutorial](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/tutorial-lambda-sam-package.html)

en.question: A developer needs to deploy the code for a new application on an AWS Lambda function. The application needs a dependency file that is 500 MB to run the business logic. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Compress the application code and dependencies into a .zip file. Directly upload the .zip file as a deployment package for the Lambda function instead of copying the code.
options.B: Compress the application code and dependencies into a .zip file. Upload the .zip file to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the Lambda function to run the code from the .zip file in the S3 bucket.
options.C: Package the application code and dependencies into a container image. Upload the image to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the Lambda function to run the code in the image.
options.D: Package the application code and dependencies into a container image. Push the image to an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Deploy the image to the Lambda function.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A developer must deploy a Lambda function whose **dependency file alone is 500 MB**. The question asks which packaging/deployment approach can actually accommodate that size.

## Key AWS Lambda Limits

- **.zip deployment package**: 250 MB unzipped (combined function code + layers). This limit applies whether the .zip is uploaded directly or via Amazon S3 — uploading via S3 only bypasses the 50 MB **direct console upload** limit, not the 250 MB unzipped limit.
- **Container image**: up to **10 GB**, and the image **must be stored in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR)** — Lambda cannot pull container images from S3.

A 500 MB dependency therefore cannot fit in any .zip-based deployment, regardless of whether it's uploaded directly or staged in S3.

## Correct Answer: D

Package the application code and the 500 MB dependency into a **container image**, push it to **Amazon ECR**, and configure the Lambda function to use that image. Lambda container images support up to 10 GB, which easily accommodates the 500 MB dependency. This is the AWS-recommended approach for large dependencies, as documented in the [Lambda quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-limits.html) and [Creating Lambda container images](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/images-create.html) guides.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

**A. Direct .zip upload** — Direct console upload is limited to **50 MB** (zipped), and the overall **unzipped** deployment package is limited to **250 MB**. A 500 MB dependency cannot fit, and uploads larger than 50 MB cannot be made directly; they must go via S3. See [Deploying Lambda functions as .zip file archives](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-function-zip.html).

**B. Upload .zip to S3 and reference it** — Using S3 only removes the 50 MB *direct upload* restriction; the **250 MB unzipped package size limit still applies**. A 500 MB dependency in a .zip package will be rejected by Lambda regardless of whether it is staged in S3. See [Working with .zip file archives for Python](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/python-package.html).

**C. Container image stored in S3** — Lambda **does not support pulling container images from Amazon S3**. Container images for Lambda must be stored in **Amazon ECR** (a private ECR repository in the same account/region as the function). See [Deploying Lambda functions as container images](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/images-create.html).

## Reference Implementation Outline

```bash
# Build the image from a Lambda base image (e.g., Python)
docker build -t my-lambda-fn .

# Authenticate and push to ECR
aws ecr get-login-password --region us-east-1 | \
  docker login --username AWS --password-stdin <acct>.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
docker tag my-lambda-fn:latest <acct>.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/my-lambda-fn:latest
docker push <acct>.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/my-lambda-fn:latest

# Create the Lambda from the ECR image
aws lambda create-function \
  --function-name my-lambda-fn \
  --package-type Image \
  --code ImageUri=<acct>.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/my-lambda-fn:latest \
  --role arn:aws:iam::<acct>:role/lambda-exec
```

## Note on Community Comments

Some commenters argued for B by interpreting the 500 MB as the *uncompressed* dependency that, when zipped, might be smaller. Even so, Lambda's hard limit is **250 MB unzipped** (function + layers combined), so a 500 MB uncompressed dependency cannot be deployed via a .zip package even when staged in S3. Option D is the only universally correct, supported solution.

zh.question: 开发人员需要将新应用程序的代码部署到 AWS Lambda 函数上。该应用程序需要一个 500 MB 的依赖文件来运行业务逻辑。哪种解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 将应用程序代码及其依赖项压缩到一个 .zip 文件中。直接将该 .zip 文件作为 Lambda 函数的部署包上传，而不是复制代码。
options.B: 将应用程序代码及其依赖项压缩到一个 .zip 文件中。将该 .zip 文件上传到 Amazon S3 存储桶。配置 Lambda 函数以运行 S3 存储桶中 .zip 文件中的代码。
options.C: 将应用程序代码及其依赖项打包到容器镜像中。将镜像上传到 Amazon S3 存储桶。配置 Lambda 函数以运行镜像中的代码。
options.D: 将应用程序代码及其依赖项打包到容器镜像中。将镜像推送到 Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) 存储库。将镜像部署到 Lambda 函数。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

开发人员必须部署一个 Lambda 函数，其**依赖文件本身为 500 MB**。问题要求确定哪种打包/部署方法实际上可以容纳该大小。

## 关键 AWS Lambda 限制

- **.zip 部署包**：250 MB 未压缩（函数代码 + 层的总和）。无论 .zip 是直接上传还是通过 Amazon S3 上传，此限制都适用——通过 S3 上传只会绕过 50 MB **直接控制台上传**限制，而不是 250 MB 未压缩限制。
- **容器镜像**：最大 **10 GB**，镜像**必须存储在 Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR)** 中——Lambda 无法从 S3 拉取容器镜像。

因此，500 MB 的依赖无法放入任何基于 .zip 的部署包中，无论是直接上传还是在 S3 中暂存。

## 正确答案：D

将应用程序代码和 500 MB 依赖打包到**容器镜像**中，将其推送到 **Amazon ECR**，并配置 Lambda 函数使用该镜像。Lambda 容器镜像支持最大 10 GB，轻松容纳 500 MB 的依赖。这是 AWS 推荐的大型依赖处理方法，具体见 [Lambda 配额](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-limits.html)和[创建 Lambda 容器镜像](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/images-create.html)文档。

## 为什么其他选项都不对

**A. 直接 .zip 上传** — 直接控制台上传限制为 **50 MB**（压缩状态），整体**未压缩**部署包限制为 **250 MB**。500 MB 的依赖无法放入，且大于 50 MB 的上传无法直接进行，必须通过 S3。详见[以 .zip 文件存档方式部署 Lambda 函数](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-function-zip.html)。

**B. 将 .zip 上传到 S3 并引用它** — 使用 S3 仅消除了 50 MB *直接上传*限制；**250 MB 未压缩包大小限制仍然适用**。包含 500 MB 依赖的 .zip 包将被 Lambda 拒绝，无论是否在 S3 中暂存。详见[使用 Python 的 .zip 文件存档](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/python-package.html)。

**C. 存储在 S3 中的容器镜像** — Lambda **不支持从 Amazon S3 拉取容器镜像**。Lambda 的容器镜像必须存储在 **Amazon ECR**（与函数同账户/地域的私有 ECR 仓库）中。详见[以容器镜像方式部署 Lambda 函数](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/images-create.html)。

## 参考实现概述

```bash
# 从 Lambda 基础镜像（如 Python）构建镜像
docker build -t my-lambda-fn .

# 验证并推送到 ECR
aws ecr get-login-password --region us-east-1 | \
  docker login --username AWS --password-stdin <acct>.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
docker tag my-lambda-fn:latest <acct>.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/my-lambda-fn:latest
docker push <acct>.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/my-lambda-fn:latest

# 从 ECR 镜像创建 Lambda
aws lambda create-function \
  --function-name my-lambda-fn \
  --package-type Image \
  --code ImageUri=<acct>.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/my-lambda-fn:latest \
  --role arn:aws:iam::<acct>:role/lambda-exec
```

## 关于社区评论的说明

有些评论者通过将 500 MB 解释为压缩后可能较小的*未压缩*依赖来为 B 辩护。即便如此，Lambda 的硬限制是**250 MB 未压缩**（函数 + 层合计），因此 500 MB 未压缩的依赖即使在 S3 中暂存也无法通过 .zip 包部署。选项 D 是唯一通用、受支持的解决方案。

en.question: A company is developing a publicly accessible single-page application. The application makes calls from a client web browser to backend services to provide a user interface to customers. The application depends on a third-party web service exposed as an HTTP API. The web client must provide an API key to the third- party web service by using the HTTP header as part of the HTTP request. The company's API key must not be exposed to the users of the web application. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Use Amazon API Gateway to create a private REST API. Create an HTTP integration to integrate with the third-party HTTP API. Add the company’s API key to the HTTP headers list of the integration request configuration.
options.B: Use Amazon API Gateway to create a private REST API. Create an AWS Lambda proxy integration. Make calls to the third-party HTTP API from the Lambda function. Pass the company's API key as an HTTP request header.
options.C: Use Amazon API Gateway to create a REST API. Create an HTTP integration to integrate with the third-party HTTP API. Add the company's API key to the HTTP headers list of the integration request configuration.
options.D: Use Amazon API Gateway to create a REST API. Create an AWS Lambda proxy integration. Make calls to the third-party HTTP API from the Lambda function. Pass the company's API key as an HTTP request header.

en.explanation:
# Securing a Third-Party API Key Behind API Gateway

## Scenario
A publicly accessible single-page application (SPA) running in a customer's web browser must call a third-party HTTP API that requires an API key to be sent in an HTTP header. The company's API key must **not** be exposed to end-users (so it cannot be embedded in the JavaScript). The solution must be the **most cost-effective**.

## Why C is correct
**Option C** uses a public (regional/edge-optimized) **REST API in API Gateway** with an **HTTP integration** that points directly to the third-party API. The company's API key is added to the integration request's HTTP headers — this happens server-side inside API Gateway, so the browser never sees the key.

Key reasons this is the best fit:
- **Public REST API** is reachable directly from a browser over the internet — exactly what an SPA needs.
- **HTTP integration** lets API Gateway call any HTTP endpoint and inject static or mapped headers (such as the third-party API key) on the **integration request**, transparently to the client. See [API Gateway integration types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-integration-types.html).
- **No Lambda** is involved, so there are no Lambda invocation charges or cold-start latency — only API Gateway request charges. This makes it cheaper than option D for the same functionality.

## Why the other options are wrong

### A — Private REST API with HTTP integration
A **private REST API can only be invoked from within a VPC through an interface VPC endpoint** ([Private REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-private-apis.html)). A browser on the public internet cannot reach it. In addition, the interface VPC endpoint incurs hourly + per-GB charges, which makes it *less* cost-effective, not more. The "publicly accessible single-page application" requirement is violated.

### B — Private REST API with Lambda proxy integration
Same blocker as A: private APIs are not reachable from a public web browser without a VPC endpoint. Adding Lambda on top also increases cost and complexity. Fails both the accessibility and cost requirements.

### D — Public REST API with Lambda proxy integration
This **would functionally work** — the Lambda would inject the API key when calling the third party — but it is **not the most cost-effective**. Every browser request now triggers a Lambda invocation (Lambda request + duration charges) plus the API Gateway request charge. Since the only task is to add a static header to a passthrough call, API Gateway's native HTTP integration in option C accomplishes the same thing with no Lambda cost. See [Set up Lambda proxy integrations in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/set-up-lambda-proxy-integrations.html).

## Summary
- ✅ **C**: Public REST API + HTTP integration with header injection — secure (key stays server-side), publicly reachable from the SPA, and cheapest because no Lambda is invoked per request.
- ❌ A, B: private APIs require VPC endpoints, breaking public browser access.
- ❌ D: works but adds unnecessary Lambda cost.

zh.question: 一家公司正在开发一个面向公众的单页应用程序。该应用程序通过客户端浏览器调用后端服务，为客户提供用户界面。该应用程序依赖于一个以 HTTP API 形式公开的第三方 Web 服务。Web 客户端必须通过在 HTTP 请求中使用 HTTP 标头来向第三方 Web 服务提供 API 密钥。公司的 API 密钥不得暴露给 Web 应用程序的用户。哪种解决方案能够以最具成本效益的方式满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 Amazon API Gateway 创建私有 REST API。创建 HTTP 集成以与第三方 HTTP API 集成。将公司的 API 密钥添加到集成请求配置的 HTTP 标头列表中。
options.B: 使用 Amazon API Gateway 创建私有 REST API。创建 AWS Lambda 代理集成。从 Lambda 函数调用第三方 HTTP API。将公司的 API 密钥作为 HTTP 请求标头传递。
options.C: 使用 Amazon API Gateway 创建 REST API。创建 HTTP 集成以与第三方 HTTP API 集成。将公司的 API 密钥添加到集成请求配置的 HTTP 标头列表中。
options.D: 使用 Amazon API Gateway 创建 REST API。创建 AWS Lambda 代理集成。从 Lambda 函数调用第三方 HTTP API。将公司的 API 密钥作为 HTTP 请求标头传递。

zh.explanation:
# 在 API Gateway 后面保护第三方 API 密钥

## 场景
在客户 Web 浏览器中运行的公开可访问单页应用程序 (SPA) 必须调用需要在 HTTP 头中发送 API 密钥的第三方 HTTP API。公司的 API 密钥**不能**暴露给最终用户（因此不能嵌入在 JavaScript 中）。该解决方案必须是**最经济高效的**。

## 为什么 C 是正确的
**选项 C** 使用公开（区域/边缘优化）的 **REST API in API Gateway**，包含指向第三方 API 的 **HTTP 集成**。公司的 API 密钥被添加到集成请求的 HTTP 头中 — 这发生在 API Gateway 内部的服务器端，所以浏览器永远看不到该密钥。

这是最佳选择的关键原因：
- **公开 REST API** 可以从浏览器通过互联网直接访问 — 正是 SPA 所需的。
- **HTTP 集成** 让 API Gateway 可以调用任何 HTTP 端点，并在**集成请求**中注入静态或映射的头（如第三方 API 密钥），对客户端完全透明。参见 [API Gateway 集成类型](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-integration-types.html)。
- **无需 Lambda**，因此没有 Lambda 调用费用或冷启动延迟 — 只需支付 API Gateway 请求费用。这使其比选项 D 更便宜。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

### A — 私有 REST API 配合 HTTP 集成
**私有 REST API 只能通过接口 VPC 端点从 VPC 内部调用** ([API Gateway 中的私有 REST API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-private-apis.html))。公网上的浏览器无法访问它。此外，接口 VPC 端点会产生按小时 + 按 GB 计费，这使得成本*更高*，而非更低。违反了"公开可访问单页应用程序"的要求。

### B — 私有 REST API 配合 Lambda 代理集成
与 A 相同的阻碍：私有 API 无法从公网浏览器访问，除非使用 VPC 端点。在此基础上添加 Lambda 还会增加成本和复杂性。同时违反了可访问性和成本要求。

### D — 公开 REST API 配合 Lambda 代理集成
这**在功能上可行** — Lambda 会在调用第三方时注入 API 密钥 — 但它**不是最经济高效的**。现在每个浏览器请求都会触发 Lambda 调用（Lambda 请求 + 时长费用）加上 API Gateway 请求费用。由于唯一的任务是向传递调用添加静态头，选项 C 中 API Gateway 原生的 HTTP 集成可以完成相同的事情，而无需 Lambda 成本。参见 [在 API Gateway 中设置 Lambda 代理集成](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/set-up-lambda-proxy-integrations.html)。

## 总结
- ✅ **C**：公开 REST API + HTTP 集成（包含头注入） — 安全（密钥保持在服务器端）、可从 SPA 公开访问，且成本最低，因为每个请求无需调用 Lambda。
- ❌ A、B：私有 API 需要 VPC 端点，打破公网浏览器访问。
- ❌ D：可行但增加不必要的 Lambda 成本。

en.question: A developer is setting up the deployment of application stacks to new test environments by using the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK). The application contains the code for several AWS Lambda functions that will be deployed as assets. Each Lambda function is defined by using the AWS CDK Lambda construct library. The developer has already successfully deployed the application stacks to the alpha environment in the first account by using the AWS CDK CLI's cdk deploy command. The developer is preparing to deploy to the beta environment in a second account for the first time. The developer makes no significant changes to the CDK code between deployments, but the initial deployment in the second account is unsuccessful and returns a NoSuchBucket error. Which command should the developer run before redeployment to resolve this error?

options.A: cdk synth
options.B: cdk bootstrap
options.C: cdk init
options.D: cdk destroy

en.explanation:
# CDK Bootstrap for Multi-Account Deployments

## Scenario
The developer has successfully deployed a CDK app (with Lambda function assets) to an alpha account. When attempting the first deployment to a beta account, deployment fails with a `NoSuchBucket` error. CDK Lambda assets (zipped function code) must be uploaded to an S3 staging bucket created in the target account by the bootstrap process.

## Correct Answer: B — `cdk bootstrap`

Each AWS account/region pair must be bootstrapped before CDK can deploy stacks that contain assets. When deploying a stack that requires bootstrap resources, the staging bucket is used when deploying stacks that contain assets or that synthesize an AWS CloudFormation template larger than 50K.

The bootstrap process provisions a CloudFormation stack named `CDKToolkit` that creates the S3 staging bucket (e.g., `cdk-hnb659fds-assets-<account>-<region>`), an ECR repository, and IAM roles needed by CDK to publish and deploy assets. Because the developer is deploying to a *new* second account for the first time, that account has never been bootstrapped — hence the `NoSuchBucket` error when CDK tries to upload the Lambda asset zip files.

The fix is to run:

```bash
cdk bootstrap aws://<ACCOUNT-ID>/<REGION>
```

(typically with appropriate `--profile` / `--trust` parameters for cross‑account pipelines).

See the [AWS CDK Troubleshooting guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cdk/v2/guide/troubleshooting.html) and [AWS CDK Bootstrapping](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cdk/v2/guide/bootstrapping.html).

## Why the other options are wrong

- **A. `cdk synth`** — This only synthesizes the CloudFormation template (and asset manifest) from the CDK app code into the `cdk.out` directory. It does not create any AWS resources in the target account, so it cannot resolve a missing S3 staging bucket. The developer has already successfully synthesized/deployed in the alpha environment, proving synth works.

- **C. `cdk init`** — This command scaffolds a *new* CDK project (creates `cdk.json`, sample app files, etc.) in an empty directory. Running it on an existing project would be inappropriate and does nothing to provision bootstrap resources in the second account.

- **D. `cdk destroy`** — This tears down a deployed stack via CloudFormation. The beta deployment never succeeded and there is no stack to remove; destroying would not create the missing S3 bucket needed for assets.

## Key takeaway
For DVA-C02: any CDK app that uses **assets** (Lambda code, Docker images, file assets) requires `cdk bootstrap` to be run **once per account/region** before the first `cdk deploy`. A `NoSuchBucket` error on first deployment in a new account is the classic symptom of a missing bootstrap.

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在使用 AWS 云开发工具包 (AWS CDK) 将应用程序堆栈部署到新的测试环境。该应用程序包含多个 AWS Lambda 函数的代码，这些函数将作为资产进行部署。每个 Lambda 函数都使用 AWS CDK Lambda 构造库进行定义。开发人员已使用 AWS CDK CLI 的 `cdk deploy` 命令成功地将应用程序堆栈部署到第一个账户的 alpha 环境中。开发人员正准备首次将其部署到第二个账户的 beta 环境中。两次部署之间，开发人员没有对 CDK 代码进行任何重大更改，但第二个账户中的初始部署失败，并返回 NoSuchBucket 错误。开发人员在重新部署之前应该运行哪个命令来解决此错误？

options.A: cdk合成
options.B: cdk引导程序
options.C: cdk 初始化
options.D: cdk 销毁

zh.explanation:
# CDK Bootstrap for Multi-Account Deployments

## Scenario
开发者已成功将一个 CDK 应用程序（包含 Lambda 函数资产）部署到 alpha 账户。首次尝试部署到 beta 账户时，部署失败并报出 `NoSuchBucket` 错误。CDK Lambda 资产（压缩的函数代码）必须上传到由目标账户中的 bootstrap 流程创建的 S3 暂存桶。

## 正确答案：B — `cdk bootstrap`

在 CDK 可以部署包含资产的栈之前，每个 AWS 账户/区域对必须进行 bootstrap。部署需要 bootstrap 资源的栈时，暂存桶用于部署包含资产的栈或合成大于 50K 的 AWS CloudFormation 模板。

bootstrap 流程预置一个名为 `CDKToolkit` 的 CloudFormation 栈，该栈创建 S3 暂存桶（例如 `cdk-hnb659fds-assets-<account>-<region>`）、一个 ECR 存储库以及 CDK 发布和部署资产所需的 IAM 角色。由于开发者首次部署到*新的*第二个账户，该账户从未进行过 bootstrap —— 因此当 CDK 尝试上传 Lambda 资产 zip 文件时会出现 `NoSuchBucket` 错误。

解决方案是运行：

```bash
cdk bootstrap aws://<ACCOUNT-ID>/<REGION>
```

（通常使用相应的 `--profile` / `--trust` 参数来支持跨账户管道）。

参考 [AWS CDK Troubleshooting guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cdk/v2/guide/troubleshooting.html) 和 [AWS CDK Bootstrapping](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cdk/v2/guide/bootstrapping.html)。

## 其他选项为何错误

- **A. `cdk synth`** —— 该命令仅将 CloudFormation 模板（和资产清单）从 CDK 应用程序代码合成到 `cdk.out` 目录中。它不会在目标账户中创建任何 AWS 资源，因此无法解决缺失的 S3 暂存桶问题。开发者已在 alpha 环境中成功完成合成/部署，证明 synth 工作正常。

- **C. `cdk init`** —— 该命令在空目录中构建*新的* CDK 项目（创建 `cdk.json`、示例应用文件等）。在现有项目上运行它是不恰当的，并且无法在第二个账户中预置 bootstrap 资源。

- **D. `cdk destroy`** —— 该命令通过 CloudFormation 卸载已部署的栈。beta 部署从未成功，也没有栈可删除；销毁无法创建资产所需的缺失 S3 桶。

## 关键要点
对于 DVA-C02：任何使用**资产**（Lambda 代码、Docker 镜像、文件资产）的 CDK 应用都需要**每个账户/区域运行一次** `cdk bootstrap`，然后再进行首次 `cdk deploy`。在新账户中首次部署时出现 `NoSuchBucket` 错误是缺失 bootstrap 的典型症状。

en.question: A developer is automating a new application deployment with AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM). The new application has one AWS Lambda function and one Amazon S3 bucket. The Lambda function must access the S3 bucket to only read objects. How should the developer configure AWS SAM to grant the necessary read privilege to the S3 bucket?

options.A: Reference a second Lambda authorizer function.
options.B: Add a custom S3 bucket policy to the Lambda function.
options.C: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) topic for only S3 object reads. Reference the topic in the template.
options.D: Add the S3ReadPolicy template to the Lambda function's execution role.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A developer is using AWS SAM to deploy a serverless application that contains one Lambda function and one S3 bucket. The Lambda function needs **read-only** access to the S3 bucket. The question is asking the simplest, idiomatic SAM way to grant this permission.

## Correct Answer: D — Add the `S3ReadPolicy` template to the Lambda function's execution role

AWS SAM provides a curated list of **policy templates** that can be attached to a `AWS::Serverless::Function` via the `Policies` property. These templates are converted by the SAM transform into scoped IAM policies that are attached to the function's execution role. AWS SAM allows you to choose from a list of policy templates to scope the permissions of your Lambda functions and AWS Step Functions state machines to the resources that are used by your application.

`S3ReadPolicy` is one of those built-in templates. S3 Read Policy grants permissions required for reading objects from an S3 bucket. It is referenced in the official SAM [policy template list](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/serverless-policy-template-list.html).

Typical SAM usage:

```yaml
MyFunction:
  Type: AWS::Serverless::Function
  Properties:
    CodeUri: src/
    Handler: app.handler
    Runtime: python3.11
    Policies:
      - S3ReadPolicy:
          BucketName: !Ref MyBucket
```

This pattern is shown in numerous AWS sample templates, e.g. the SAM template uses `S3ReadPolicy` with `BucketName: !Ref ValidationFilesS3Bucket` under the function's Policies property.

## Why the other options are wrong

- **A. Reference a second Lambda authorizer function.** Lambda authorizers are an **API Gateway** feature used to authorize HTTP API/REST API callers. They do not grant a Lambda function permissions to call S3 — they evaluate caller identity for API Gateway requests. Completely irrelevant to S3 read access.

- **B. Add a custom S3 bucket policy to the Lambda function.** A bucket policy is a **resource-based** policy attached to the S3 bucket, not to a Lambda function. You cannot "attach" a bucket policy to a Lambda function. While a bucket policy can grant access to a Lambda's IAM role, the SAM-idiomatic and least-effort way is the predefined `S3ReadPolicy` template applied to the function's execution role. The wording of option B (attaching a bucket policy to the function) is technically incorrect.

- **C. Create an SQS topic for only S3 object reads.** SQS is a queueing service (and "topic" is SNS terminology, not SQS). SQS has nothing to do with granting S3 read permission to a Lambda function. The option is nonsensical for the stated requirement.

## References

- [AWS SAM policy template list](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/serverless-policy-template-list.html)
- [AWS SAM policy templates](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/serverless-policy-templates.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在使用 AWS 无服务器应用程序模型 (AWS SAM) 自动化部署一个新的应用程序。该应用程序包含一个 AWS Lambda 函数和一个 Amazon S3 存储桶。Lambda 函数必须访问 S3 存储桶，但只能读取对象。开发人员应该如何配置 AWS SAM 以授予对 S3 存储桶必要的读取权限？

options.A: 引用第二个 Lambda 授权函数。
options.B: 向 Lambda 函数添加自定义 S3 存储桶策略。
options.C: 创建一个仅用于读取 S3 对象的 Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) 主题。在模板中引用该主题。
options.D: 将 S3ReadPolicy 模板添加到 Lambda 函数的执行角色。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

一名开发人员正在使用 AWS SAM 部署一个包含一个 Lambda 函数和一个 S3 存储桶的无服务器应用程序。Lambda 函数需要对 S3 存储桶的**只读**访问权限。问题询问的是使用 SAM 授予此权限的最简单、最惯用的方法。

## 正确答案：D — 将 `S3ReadPolicy` 模板添加到 Lambda 函数的执行角色

AWS SAM 提供了一个精选的**策略模板**列表，可以通过 `Policies` 属性附加到 `AWS::Serverless::Function`。这些模板由 SAM 转换转换为范围限定的 IAM 策略，然后附加到函数的执行角色。AWS SAM 允许你从策略模板列表中选择，以限制 Lambda 函数和 AWS Step Functions 状态机的权限范围，使其仅限于应用程序使用的资源。

`S3ReadPolicy` 是其中一个内置模板。S3 Read Policy 授予从 S3 存储桶读取对象所需的权限。它在官方 SAM [策略模板列表](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/serverless-policy-template-list.html)中被引用。

典型的 SAM 用法：

```yaml
MyFunction:
  Type: AWS::Serverless::Function
  Properties:
    CodeUri: src/
    Handler: app.handler
    Runtime: python3.11
    Policies:
      - S3ReadPolicy:
          BucketName: !Ref MyBucket
```

这种模式在许多 AWS 示例模板中都有展示，例如 SAM 模板在函数的 Policies 属性下使用 `S3ReadPolicy` 和 `BucketName: !Ref ValidationFilesS3Bucket`。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

- **A. 引用第二个 Lambda 授权方函数。** Lambda 授权方是 **API Gateway** 功能，用于授权 HTTP API/REST API 调用者。它们不会向 Lambda 函数授予调用 S3 的权限 — 它们评估 API Gateway 请求的调用者身份。与 S3 读取访问权限完全无关。

- **B. 向 Lambda 函数添加自定义 S3 存储桶策略。** 存储桶策略是附加到 S3 存储桶的**基于资源**的策略，而不是附加到 Lambda 函数的策略。你不能将存储桶策略"附加"到 Lambda 函数。虽然存储桶策略可以授予权限给 Lambda 的 IAM 角色，但 SAM 的惯用做法和最少工作量的方法是将预定义的 `S3ReadPolicy` 模板应用于函数的执行角色。选项 B 的措辞（将存储桶策略附加到函数）在技术上是不正确的。

- **C. 为仅 S3 对象读取创建一个 SQS 主题。** SQS 是一个队列服务（"主题"是 SNS 术语，不是 SQS）。SQS 与向 Lambda 函数授予 S3 读取权限无关。该选项对于所述要求来说毫无意义。

## 参考资源

- [AWS SAM 策略模板列表](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/serverless-policy-template-list.html)
- [AWS SAM 策略模板](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/serverless-policy-templates.html)

en.question: A development team wants to immediately build and deploy an application whenever there is a change to the source code. Which approaches could be used to trigger the deployment? (Choose two.)

options.A: Store the source code in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure AWS CodePipeline to start whenever a file in the bucket changes.
options.B: Store the source code in an encrypted Amazon EBS volume. Configure AWS CodePipeline to start whenever a file in the volume changes.
options.C: Store the source code in an AWS CodeCommit repository. Configure AWS CodePipeline to start whenever a change is committed to the repository.
options.D: Store the source code in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure AWS CodePipeline to start every 15 minutes.
options.E: Store the source code in an Amazon EC2 instance’s ephemeral storage. Configure the instance to start AWS CodePipeline whenever there are changes to the source code.

en.explanation:
# Triggering CodePipeline on Source Code Changes

## Scenario
The team wants to **immediately** build and deploy whenever the source code changes. We need to identify which two approaches give CodePipeline a valid source provider with automated, event-driven change detection.

## Correct Answers: A and C

CodePipeline natively supports automated change detection for two AWS-native source providers: **Amazon S3** and **AWS CodeCommit**. This trigger type uses automated change detection. The source action providers that use this trigger type are S3 and CodeCommit.

### A. S3 bucket as source
CodePipeline triggers the pipeline when a new object is uploaded to the configured bucket and object key. This source action requires the Amazon S3 bucket to be configured for versioning. If you use the console to create or edit your pipeline, CodePipeline creates an EventBridge rule that starts your pipeline when a change occurs in the S3 source bucket. This satisfies the "immediately on change" requirement.

### C. CodeCommit repository as source
CodePipeline starts the pipeline when a new commit is made on the configured CodeCommit repository and branch. If you use the console to create or edit the pipeline, CodePipeline creates an EventBridge rule that starts your pipeline when a change occurs in the repository.

## Why the other options are wrong

### B. Encrypted EBS volume
EBS volumes are block-storage devices attached to EC2 instances. **EBS is not a supported source provider for CodePipeline** — there is no event mechanism to fire on file changes inside a volume. Triggers are configurable for source actions with connections that use the CodeStarSourceConnection action in CodePipeline, such as GitHub, Bitbucket, and GitLab. Source actions, such as CodeCommit and S3, use automated change detection to start pipelines when a change is made. EBS is not in this list.

### D. S3 bucket polled every 15 minutes
While S3 is a valid source, configuring CodePipeline on a 15-minute schedule does **not** trigger the pipeline *immediately* upon change — it only runs on the schedule. The requirement is "immediately build and deploy whenever there is a change," which a fixed 15-minute schedule fails to meet (and would also waste executions when no change occurred).

### E. EC2 instance ephemeral storage
Ephemeral (instance store) storage is non-persistent and not a CodePipeline source provider. There is no managed event integration for EC2 ephemeral storage that can start CodePipeline. This requires custom code on the instance and is not a supported, reliable trigger pattern. Also, ephemeral storage is lost on instance stop/terminate, making it unsuitable for source code.

## References
- [Start a pipeline in CodePipeline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/pipelines-about-starting.html)
- [Amazon S3 source action reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/action-reference-S3.html)
- [CodeCommit source action reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/action-reference-CodeCommit.html)
- [CodeCommit source actions and EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/triggering.html)

zh.question: 开发团队希望在源代码发生变更时立即构建并部署应用程序。可以使用哪些方法来触发部署？（选择两种。）

options.A: 将源代码存储在 Amazon S3 存储桶中。配置 AWS CodePipeline，使其在存储桶中的文件发生更改时启动。
options.B: 将源代码存储在加密的 Amazon EBS 卷中。配置 AWS CodePipeline，使其在卷中的文件发生更改时启动。
options.C: 将源代码存储在 AWS CodeCommit 代码库中。配置 AWS CodePipeline，使其在每次代码库提交更改时启动。
options.D: 将源代码存储在 Amazon S3 存储桶中。配置 AWS CodePipeline 每 15 分钟启动一次。
