This requires **no code** — API Gateway validates the JWT token signature, expiration, and claims against the user pool on your behalf. Using a Cognito User Pool for OAuth token authentication allows API Gateway to validate access tokens without the need for a custom Lambda Authorizer, reducing complexity and improving performance.

A typical CloudFormation snippet of this authorizer:

```yaml
CogAuthorizer:
  Type: AWS::ApiGateway::Authorizer
  Properties:
    Name: CognitoAuthorizer
    RestApiId: !Ref Api
    Type: COGNITO_USER_POOLS
    IdentitySource: method.request.header.Authorization
    ProviderARNs:
      - !GetAtt UserPool.Arn
```

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A. API key + usage plan** — API keys are used for **identifying client applications and applying throttling/quota limits**, not for authenticating end users. They do not validate Cognito tokens or user identity, so they fail to meet the authentication requirement.

- **C. Lambda TOKEN authorizer** — A Lambda token authorizer requires the developer to **write, deploy, and maintain custom Lambda code** to decode and verify the JWT (signature check against JWKS, claims validation, etc.). Lambda Authorizer with JWT Token provides fine-grained access control by enabling custom logic, but it introduces increased request latency, requires additional infrastructure and maintenance, and can lead to higher AWS costs from Lambda invocation fees. This is significantly more development effort than the built-in Cognito authorizer.

- **D. Lambda REQUEST authorizer calling the Cognito API** — This is even more effort: write custom Lambda code, parse the header, and make calls to Cognito for every request. Cognito's `GetUser` API doesn't validate signed JWTs the way API Gateway's native authorizer does, and this adds latency, cost, and code maintenance overhead.

## Key Takeaway
For DVA-C02: when you see "Cognito user pool" + "REST API" + "least effort," the answer is almost always to use the built-in **COGNITO_USER_POOLS authorizer** with the token in the `Authorization` header.

## References
- [Control access to REST APIs using Amazon Cognito user pools as an authorizer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-integrate-with-cognito.html)
- [Integrate a REST API with an Amazon Cognito user pool](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-enable-cognito-user-pool.html)
- [Create an Amazon Cognito authorizer for a REST API using CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-cognito-authorizer-cfn.html)
- [Set up Amazon Cognito user pools as an API Gateway authorizer (AWS re:Post)](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/api-gateway-cognito-user-pool-authorizer)

zh.question: 一家公司有一个使用 Amazon Cognito 用户池进行身份验证的应用程序。开发人员需要添加一个新的 REST API，该 API 将使用该用户池来验证请求。哪种解决方案能够以最少的开发工作量满足此要求？

options.A: 创建新的 API 密钥和新的使用计划。将 API 密钥和 REST API 与使用计划关联起来。
options.B: 为正确的用户池创建 Cognito 授权器。引用包含 Cognito 令牌的标头。
options.C: 创建 AWS Lambda 令牌授权器。在事件有效负载中引用授权令牌。根据令牌值对请求进行身份验证。
options.D: 创建一个 AWS Lambda 请求授权器。在事件有效负载中引用授权标头。通过使用向 Cognito API 发送的请求中的标头值来验证请求。

zh.explanation:
# Cognito User Pool Authorizer for API Gateway REST API

## 场景
一家公司已经拥有用于身份验证的 Amazon Cognito 用户池。开发人员需要在 API Gateway 中添加新的 REST API，使用**相同的** Cognito 用户池进行请求身份验证。问题要求**开发工作量最少**的解决方案。

## 正确答案：B — 为用户池创建 Cognito authorizer 并引用包含 Cognito 令牌的标头

API Gateway 通过内置的 **COGNITO_USER_POOLS** authorizer 类型与 Amazon Cognito 用户池原生集成。作为使用 IAM 角色和策略或 Lambda authorizer 的替代方案，您可以使用 Amazon Cognito 用户池来控制谁可以访问 Amazon API Gateway 中的 API。要在 API 中使用 Amazon Cognito 用户池，必须首先创建 COGNITO_USER_POOLS 类型的 authorizer，然后配置 API 方法以使用该 authorizer。

部署后，客户端必须首先将用户登录到用户池，为用户获取身份令牌或访问令牌，然后使用该令牌调用 API 方法，该令牌通常设置在请求的 Authorization 标头中。只有在提供了所需令牌且令牌有效时，API 调用才会成功。

这**不需要编写代码** — API Gateway 代表您验证 JWT 令牌签名、过期时间和声明是否与用户池匹配。使用 Cognito User Pool 进行 OAuth 令牌身份验证允许 API Gateway 验证访问令牌而无需自定义 Lambda Authorizer，降低了复杂性并改进了性能。

这个 authorizer 的典型 CloudFormation 代码段：

```yaml
CogAuthorizer:
  Type: AWS::ApiGateway::Authorizer
  Properties:
    Name: CognitoAuthorizer
    RestApiId: !Ref Api
    Type: COGNITO_USER_POOLS
    IdentitySource: method.request.header.Authorization
    ProviderARNs:
      - !GetAtt UserPool.Arn
```

## 其他选项错误的原因

- **A. API 密钥 + 使用计划** — API 密钥用于**识别客户端应用程序并应用限流/配额限制**，而不是用于对最终用户进行身份验证。它们不验证 Cognito 令牌或用户身份，因此无法满足身份验证要求。

- **C. Lambda TOKEN authorizer** — Lambda token authorizer 需要开发人员**编写、部署和维护自定义 Lambda 代码**来解码和验证 JWT（针对 JWKS 的签名检查、声明验证等）。Lambda Authorizer with JWT Token 通过启用自定义逻辑提供细粒度访问控制，但它会增加请求延迟、需要额外的基础设施和维护，并且可能导致来自 Lambda 调用费用的更高 AWS 成本。这比内置 Cognito authorizer 需要更多的开发工作。

- **D. 调用 Cognito API 的 Lambda REQUEST authorizer** — 这需要更多的工作：编写自定义 Lambda 代码、解析标头，并为每个请求调用 Cognito。Cognito 的 `GetUser` API 不能像 API Gateway 的原生 authorizer 那样验证签名的 JWT，这增加了延迟、成本和代码维护开销。

## 关键要点
对于 DVA-C02：当您看到"Cognito 用户池" + "REST API" + "最少工作量"时，答案几乎总是使用内置的 **COGNITO_USER_POOLS authorizer** 并在 `Authorization` 标头中传递令牌。

## 参考资源
- [使用 Amazon Cognito 用户池作为 authorizer 来控制对 REST API 的访问](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-integrate-with-cognito.html)
- [将 REST API 与 Amazon Cognito 用户池集成](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-enable-cognito-user-pool.html)
- [使用 CloudFormation 为 REST API 创建 Amazon Cognito authorizer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-cognito-authorizer-cfn.html)
- [将 Amazon Cognito 用户池设置为 API Gateway authorizer (AWS re:Post)](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/api-gateway-cognito-user-pool-authorizer)

en.question: A developer is testing an AWS Lambda function that has an event source of an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. The developer notices that some of the messages the Lambda function processes re-appear in the queue while the messages are being processed. The developer must correct this behavior. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.A: Increase the timeout of the Lambda function.
options.B: Increase the visibility timeout of the SQS queue.
options.C: Increase the memory allocation of the Lambda function.
options.D: Increase the batch size in the event source mapping.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A Lambda function is triggered by an Amazon SQS queue via an event source mapping. While Lambda is still processing messages, those same messages re-appear in the queue and get picked up again. The developer wants to stop this duplicate processing.

## Why this happens

When Lambda's event source mapping receives messages from SQS, the messages are not deleted immediately — they are made invisible for the duration of the queue's **visibility timeout**. Lambda only deletes messages from the queue after the function returns successfully. The visibility timeout starts as soon as a message is delivered to you. During this period, you're expected to process and delete the message. If you don't delete it before the timeout expires, the message becomes visible again in the queue and can be retrieved by another consumer.

If the Lambda function takes longer than the queue's visibility timeout, SQS makes the message visible again — even though Lambda is still processing it — causing duplicate processing. "If Lambda takes longer than the visibility timeout, SQS assumes processing failed and makes the message visible again."

## Correct answer: B — Increase the visibility timeout of the SQS queue

AWS specifically recommends sizing the queue's visibility timeout to safely cover the Lambda function's processing time. To allow your function time to process each batch of records, set the source queue's visibility timeout to at least six times the configuration timeout on your function. The extra time allows Lambda to retry if your function is throttled while processing a previous batch. Your function's timeout must be less than or equal to the queue's visibility timeout. Lambda validates this requirement when you create or update an event source mapping and will return an error if the function timeout exceeds the queue's visibility timeout.

Raising the visibility timeout keeps in-flight messages hidden from other consumers/pollers while Lambda is processing them, preventing the duplicate-delivery symptom described.

## Why the other options are wrong

- **A. Increase the timeout of the Lambda function.** This only changes how long Lambda is allowed to run; it does not change how long SQS hides the message. In fact, AWS *requires* that the function timeout be ≤ the queue's visibility timeout, so simply increasing the Lambda timeout (without raising the visibility timeout) will either be rejected or actually make the duplicate-delivery problem worse, because the function will run past the moment SQS re-exposes the message.

- **C. Increase the memory allocation of the Lambda function.** More memory may make the function run faster, but the root cause is the *visibility timeout vs. processing time* relationship. Memory does not control SQS in-flight visibility, and there is no guarantee that more memory will reduce processing time below the visibility timeout.

- **D. Increase the batch size in the event source mapping.** Larger batches typically *increase* per-invocation processing time, making it more likely (not less) that processing will exceed the visibility timeout. AWS even notes that with larger batches/batching windows, you should *raise* the visibility timeout accordingly. This option does not address the duplicate-visibility behavior.

## Key references
- [Using Lambda with Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html)
- [Creating and configuring an Amazon SQS event source mapping](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-configure.html)
- [Amazon SQS visibility timeout](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-visibility-timeout.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在测试一个 AWS Lambda 函数，该函数的事件源是 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列。开发人员注意到，Lambda 函数处理的部分消息在处理过程中会重新出现在队列中。开发人员必须纠正这种行为。哪种解决方案能够满足此要求？

options.A: 增加 Lambda 函数的超时时间。
options.B: 增加 SQS 队列的可见性超时时间。
options.C: 增加 Lambda 函数的内存分配。
options.D: 增加事件源映射中的批处理大小。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

Lambda 函数由 Amazon SQS 队列通过事件源映射触发。当 Lambda 仍在处理消息时，这些相同的消息重新出现在队列中并被再次拾取。开发人员想要停止这种重复处理。

## 为什么会发生这种情况

当 Lambda 的事件源映射从 SQS 接收消息时，消息不会立即删除——它们在队列的**可见性超时**期间内变得不可见。Lambda 仅在函数成功返回后才从队列中删除消息。可见性超时在消息传递给你时开始。在此期间，你需要处理和删除消息。如果你在超时过期前没有删除它，消息将再次在队列中变为可见，并可被另一个使用者检索。

如果 Lambda 函数的处理时间超过队列的可见性超时，SQS 会再次使消息可见——即使 Lambda 仍在处理它——导致重复处理。"如果 Lambda 的处理时间超过可见性超时，SQS 认为处理失败并使消息再次可见。"

## 正确答案：B——增加 SQS 队列的可见性超时

AWS 特别建议将队列的可见性超时设置为足以覆盖 Lambda 函数处理时间的值。为了给你的函数留出处理每批记录的时间，将源队列的可见性超时设置为至少是函数配置超时的六倍。额外的时间允许 Lambda 在处理前一批时被限制的情况下重试。你的函数超时必须小于或等于队列的可见性超时。Lambda 在创建或更新事件源映射时会验证此要求，如果函数超时超过队列的可见性超时，将返回错误。

提高可见性超时可以在 Lambda 处理消息时将其从其他使用者/轮询器中隐藏，从而防止所描述的重复交付问题。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

- **A. 增加 Lambda 函数的超时。** 这只会改变 Lambda 允许运行的时间；它不会改变 SQS 隐藏消息的时间。实际上，AWS *要求*函数超时小于或等于队列的可见性超时，所以仅仅增加 Lambda 超时（不提高可见性超时）要么会被拒绝，要么实际上会使重复交付问题更糟，因为函数将在 SQS 重新公开消息的时刻之后运行。

- **C. 增加 Lambda 函数的内存分配。** 更多内存可能会使函数运行更快，但根本原因是*可见性超时与处理时间*的关系。内存不控制 SQS 进行中的可见性，也不能保证更多内存会将处理时间减少到可见性超时以下。

- **D. 增加事件源映射中的批大小。** 较大的批次通常会*增加*每次调用的处理时间，使得处理超过可见性超时的可能性更大（而非更小）。AWS 甚至指出，对于较大的批次/批处理窗口，你应该*提高*可见性超时。此选项不能解决重复可见性行为。

## 关键参考
- [将 Lambda 与 Amazon SQS 结合使用](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html)
- [创建和配置 Amazon SQS 事件源映射](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-configure.html)
- [Amazon SQS 可见性超时](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-visibility-timeout.html)

en.question: A developer created reusable code that several AWS Lambda functions need to use. The developer bundled the code into a zip archive. The developer needs to deploy the code to AWS and update the Lambda functions to use the code. Which solution will meet this requirement in the MOST operationally efficient way?

options.A: Upload the zip archive to Amazon S3. Configure an import path on the Lambda functions to point to the zip archive.
options.B: Create a new Lambda function that contains and runs the shared code. Update the existing Lambda functions to invoke the new Lambda function synchronously.
options.C: Create a Lambda layer that contains the zip archive. Attach the Lambda layer to the Lambda functions.
options.D: Create a Lambda container image that includes the shared code. Use the container image as a Lambda base image for all the functions.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A developer has reusable code that needs to be shared across multiple Lambda functions. The code is already bundled into a zip archive. The goal is to deploy this shared code in the **most operationally efficient** way and update the Lambda functions to use it.

## Correct Answer: C — Create a Lambda layer that contains the zip archive. Attach the Lambda layer to the Lambda functions.

Lambda layers are the AWS-recommended mechanism for this exact use case. To share dependencies across multiple functions, after you create a layer, you can apply it to any number of functions in your account. Without layers, you need to include the same dependencies in each individual deployment package.

When a function with a layer executes, Lambda extracts the layer contents into the /opt directory in your function's execution environment. All natively supported Lambda runtimes include paths to specific directories within the /opt directory, giving your function access to your layer content.

A layer fits the requirement perfectly because a Lambda layer is a .zip file archive that contains supplementary code or data. Layers usually contain library dependencies, a custom runtime, or configuration files — exactly what the developer already has prepared.

Operational benefits include: enforcing separation of concerns between dependencies and your custom business logic, making your function code smaller and more focused, and speeding up deployments because less code must be packaged and uploaded, and dependencies can be reused.

You can attach up to five layers to a Lambda function, with a total unzipped size of the function and all layers not exceeding the unzipped deployment package size quota of 250 MB, which is sufficient for typical shared-code use cases.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

**A. Upload the zip archive to S3 and configure an "import path" on the Lambda functions.**
Lambda has no concept of an "import path" pointing to an S3 zip archive that automatically loads at runtime. While you can specify an S3 location as the *deployment package* (`S3Bucket`/`S3Key`) when creating/updating a function, that replaces the function's own code — it doesn't act as shared, reusable code attached to multiple functions. Each function would still need to bundle/download the code separately, and Lambda functions cannot dynamically import code from arbitrary S3 paths at invocation time. This is not an operationally efficient sharing pattern.

**B. Create a new Lambda function that runs the shared code; have other functions invoke it synchronously.**
This adds significant operational overhead: extra invocation latency, double Lambda billing (caller + callee), additional IAM permissions (`lambda:InvokeFunction`), error-handling complexity, and tight runtime coupling. It's appropriate when you need an independent service boundary, not when you simply want to share library code that's already packaged as a zip.

**D. Create a Lambda container image that includes the shared code and use it as a base image.**
This requires re-architecting all functions from zip-based deployment to the container image packaging model, building/pushing images to Amazon ECR, and rebuilding/redeploying every dependent function image whenever the shared code changes. The developer already has a zip archive ready — switching deployment models is the opposite of operationally efficient. Layers are designed precisely to avoid this overhead.

## References

- [Managing Lambda dependencies with layers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/chapter-layers.html)
- [Adding layers to functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/adding-layers.html)
- [AWS Lambda – Use Any Programming Language and Share Common Components](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/new-for-aws-lambda-use-any-programming-language-and-share-common-components/)

zh.question: 一位开发人员创建了多个 AWS Lambda 函数需要使用的可重用代码。开发人员将代码打包成一个 zip 压缩包。现在，开发人员需要将该代码部署到 AWS，并更新 Lambda 函数以使用该代码。哪种解决方案能够以最高效的方式满足此需求？

options.A: 将 zip 存档上传到 Amazon S3。在 Lambda 函数中配置导入路径，使其指向该 zip 存档。
options.B: 创建一个包含并运行共享代码的新 Lambda 函数。更新现有 Lambda 函数，使其同步调用新 Lambda 函数。
options.C: 创建一个包含 zip 压缩文件的 Lambda 层。将 Lambda 层附加到 Lambda 函数。
options.D: 创建一个包含共享代码的 Lambda 容器镜像。将该容器镜像用作所有 Lambda 函数的基础镜像。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

一名开发者拥有需要在多个 Lambda 函数中共享的可重用代码。该代码已打包成 zip 压缩文件。目标是以**最具操作效率的方式**部署这些共享代码，并更新 Lambda 函数以使用它。

## 正确答案：C — 创建包含 zip 压缩文件的 Lambda 层。将 Lambda 层附加到 Lambda 函数。

Lambda 层是 AWS 为此确切用例推荐的机制。要在多个函数之间共享依赖项，创建层后，您可以将其应用于账户中的任意数量函数。如果不使用层，您需要在每个单独的部署包中包含相同的依赖项。

当带有层的函数执行时，Lambda 将层内容提取到函数执行环境中的 /opt 目录中。所有原生支持的 Lambda 运行时都包含指向 /opt 目录中特定目录的路径，使您的函数能够访问层内容。

层完全符合需求，因为Lambda 层是包含补充代码或数据的 .zip 文件压缩文件。层通常包含库依赖项、自定义运行时或配置文件 — 正好是开发者已准备好的内容。

运营优势包括：在依赖项和自定义业务逻辑之间强制实施关注点分离，使函数代码更小且更专注，以及加快部署速度，因为需要打包和上传的代码更少，并且依赖项可以重用。

您可以将最多五个层附加到 Lambda 函数，函数和所有层的总解压大小不超过 250 MB 的解压部署包大小配额，这对于典型的共享代码用例来说已足够。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

**A. 将 zip 压缩文件上传到 S3 并在 Lambda 函数上配置"导入路径"。**
Lambda 没有指向自动在运行时加载的 S3 zip 压缩文件的"导入路径"概念。虽然您可以在创建/更新函数时将 S3 位置指定为*部署包*（`S3Bucket`/`S3Key`），但这会替换函数自己的代码 — 它不充当附加到多个函数的共享可重用代码。每个函数仍然需要单独捆绑/下载代码，而 Lambda 函数无法在调用时从任意 S3 路径动态导入代码。这不是一个在操作上高效的共享模式。

**B. 创建运行共享代码的新 Lambda 函数；让其他函数同步调用它。**
这增加了大量运营开销：额外的调用延迟、双倍 Lambda 计费（调用方 + 被调用方）、额外的 IAM 权限（`lambda:InvokeFunction`）、错误处理复杂性和紧密的运行时耦合。当您需要独立的服务边界时合适，而不是当您只想共享已打包为 zip 的库代码时。

**D. 创建包含共享代码的 Lambda 容器镜像并将其用作基础镜像。**
这需要将所有函数从基于 zip 的部署重新架构为容器镜像打包模型，构建/推送镜像到 Amazon ECR，以及每当共享代码更改时重建/重新部署每个从属函数镜像。开发者已准备好 zip 压缩文件 — 切换部署模型与操作效率相反。层设计目的正是为了避免这种开销。

## 参考资源

- [使用层管理 Lambda 依赖项](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/chapter-layers.html)
- [向函数添加层](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/adding-layers.html)
- [AWS Lambda – 使用任何编程语言并共享通用组件](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/new-for-aws-lambda-use-any-programming-language-and-share-common-components/)

en.question: A team has an Amazon API Gateway REST API that consists of a single resource and a GET method that is backed by an AWS Lambda integration. A developer makes a change to the Lambda function and deploys the function as a new version. The developer needs to set up a process to test the new version of the function before using the new version in production. The tests must not affect the production REST API. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create a new resource in the REST API. Add a GET method to the new resource, and add a Lambda integration to the updated version of the Lambda function. Deploy the new version.
options.B: Create a new stage for the REST API. Create a stage variable. Assign the stage variable to the Lambda function. Set the API Gateway integrated Lambda function name to the stage variable. Deploy the new version.
options.C: Create a new REST API. Add a resource that has a single GET method that is integrated with the updated version of the Lambda function.
options.D: Update the Lambda integration of the existing GET method to point to the updated version of the Lambda function. Deploy the new version.

en.explanation:
# API Gateway Stage Variables for Testing Lambda Versions

## Scenario
A team has an API Gateway REST API with a single GET method backed by a Lambda integration. A new Lambda version was published. The team needs to test the new version **without affecting production** and with the **least operational overhead**.

## Correct Answer: B

Create a new **stage** for the REST API and use a **stage variable** that resolves to the Lambda function/alias/version. The same API definition can then be deployed to the new stage where the stage variable points to the new Lambda version, while the production stage continues to point to the existing version.

Stage variables act like environment variables and can be used to change the behavior of your API Gateway methods for each deployment stage; for example, making it possible to reach a different back end depending on which stage the API is running on.

A stage variable can be used in place of a Lambda function name, or version/alias, allowing the integration URI such as:

```
arn:aws:apigateway:<region>:lambda:path/2015-03-31/functions/arn:aws:lambda:<region>:<account_id>:function:<function_name>:${stageVariables.<version_variable_name>}/invocations
```

This means a single API definition can serve multiple stages (e.g., `prod` and `test`), each pointing at a different Lambda version simply by changing the stage variable value — no duplicated resources, no duplicate APIs.

We can do this by using API Gateway stage variables (REST API & HTTP API) and Lambda function alias without creating environment-wise redundant Lambda functions. In short, different Lambda alias, like TEST and PROD can be used as two different deployment targets for the Lambda function.

> Note: When using a stage variable to qualify the Lambda function, you must add `lambda:InvokeFunction` permission for each Lambda function/version/alias referenced, since API Gateway can no longer auto-create the resource policy. See [Set up stage variables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-set-stage-variables-aws-console.html).

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A. Create a new resource with a GET method pointing to the new version** — This change is made in the same REST API. When you "Deploy the new version", you must deploy to a stage; if deployed to the production stage, the new (untested) resource is now exposed in production, violating the requirement that tests must not affect the production REST API. It also adds unnecessary resources to the API surface.

- **C. Create a new REST API** — Duplicating the entire API in a separate REST API is the highest operational overhead option (separate API ID, separate URL, separate deployments, separate IAM/permissions, separate stages). Stage variables on the same API achieve the same isolation with far less work.

- **D. Update the existing GET method's integration to point to the new version and deploy** — This directly replaces the production integration target. Once deployed to production, all live traffic hits the untested new version, which is exactly the opposite of "must not affect the production REST API".

## Key Documentation
- [Set up stage variables for REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-set-stage-variables-aws-console.html)
- [API Gateway stage variables reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/aws-api-gateway-stage-variables-reference.html)
- [Using API Gateway stage variables to manage Lambda functions (AWS Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/using-api-gateway-stage-variables-to-manage-lambda-functions/)

zh.question: 一个团队使用 Amazon API Gateway REST API，该 API 包含一个资源和一个 GET 方法，并由 AWS Lambda 集成提供支持。开发人员对 Lambda 函数进行了更改，并将其部署为新版本。开发人员需要设置一个流程，在将新版本投入生产环境之前对其进行测试。测试不得影响生产环境的 REST API。哪种解决方案能够以最小的运维开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 在 REST API 中创建一个新资源。为新资源添加一个 GET 方法，并为更新后的 Lambda 函数版本添加 Lambda 集成。部署新版本。
options.B: 为 REST API 创建一个新阶段。创建一个阶段变量。将该阶段变量分配给 Lambda 函数。将 API 网关集成的 Lambda 函数名称设置为该阶段变量。部署新版本。
options.C: 创建一个新的 REST API。添加一个资源，该资源具有一个与更新后的 Lambda 函数版本集成的 GET 方法。
options.D: 更新现有 GET 方法的 Lambda 集成，使其指向更新后的 Lambda 函数版本。部署新版本。

zh.explanation:
# API Gateway 阶段变量用于测试 Lambda 版本

## 场景
一个团队有一个 API Gateway REST API，其中有一个 GET 方法由 Lambda 集成支持。发布了一个新的 Lambda 版本。团队需要测试新版本**而不影响生产环境**，并且**运维开销最小**。

## 正确答案：B

为 REST API 创建一个新的**阶段**，并使用**阶段变量**来解析 Lambda 函数/别名/版本。然后可以将同一个 API 定义部署到新阶段，其中阶段变量指向新的 Lambda 版本，而生产阶段继续指向现有版本。

阶段变量的作用类似环境变量，可用于为每个部署阶段更改 API Gateway 方法的行为；例如，根据 API 运行的阶段访问不同的后端。

阶段变量可用于代替 Lambda 函数名称或版本/别名，允许集成 URI，如：

```
arn:aws:apigateway:<region>:lambda:path/2015-03-31/functions/arn:aws:lambda:<region>:<account_id>:function:<function_name>:${stageVariables.<version_variable_name>}/invocations
```

这意味着单个 API 定义可以服务多个阶段（例如 `prod` 和 `test`），每个阶段只需更改阶段变量值即可指向不同的 Lambda 版本——无需重复资源，无需重复 API。

我们可以通过使用 API Gateway 阶段变量（REST API 和 HTTP API）以及 Lambda 函数别名来实现这一点，无需创建冗余的环境专用 Lambda 函数。简而言之，可以使用不同的 Lambda 别名（如 TEST 和 PROD）作为 Lambda 函数的两个不同部署目标。

> 注意：使用阶段变量来限定 Lambda 函数时，必须为每个引用的 Lambda 函数/版本/别名添加 `lambda:InvokeFunction` 权限，因为 API Gateway 无法再自动创建资源策略。请参阅[设置阶段变量](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-set-stage-variables-aws-console.html)。

## 其他选项为何错误

- **A. 创建指向新版本的 GET 方法的新资源** — 此更改在同一 REST API 中进行。当你"部署新版本"时，必须部署到某个阶段；如果部署到生产阶段，新的（未测试）资源现在暴露在生产中，违反了测试不能影响生产 REST API 的要求。它还会向 API 表面添加不必要的资源。

- **C. 创建新的 REST API** — 在单独的 REST API 中复制整个 API 是运维开销最高的选项（单独的 API ID、单独的 URL、单独的部署、单独的 IAM/权限、单独的阶段）。同一 API 上的阶段变量能以更少的工作量实现相同的隔离。

- **D. 更新现有 GET 方法的集成以指向新版本并部署** — 这直接替换了生产集成目标。部署到生产后，所有实时流量都击中未测试的新版本，这正好与"不能影响生产 REST API"的要求相反。

## 关键文档
- [在 API Gateway 中为 REST API 设置阶段变量](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-set-stage-variables-aws-console.html)
- [API Gateway 阶段变量参考](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/aws-api-gateway-stage-variables-reference.html)
- [使用 API Gateway 阶段变量管理 Lambda 函数（AWS 博客）](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/using-api-gateway-stage-variables-to-manage-lambda-functions/)

en.question: A developer manages encryption keys in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). The developer must ensure that all encryption keys can be deleted immediately when the keys are no longer required. The developer wants a solution that is highly available and does not require manual management for compute infrastructure. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use AWS KMS managed keys. When the keys are no longer required, schedule the keys for immediate deletion.
options.B: Use customer managed keys with imported key material. When the keys are no longer required, delete the imported key material.
options.C: Use customer managed keys. When the keys are no longer required, delete the key material.
options.D: Use customer managed keys and an AWS CloudHSM key store. When the keys are no longer required, schedule the keys for immediate deletion.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A developer needs to manage encryption keys in AWS KMS with three requirements:
1. **Immediate deletion** when keys are no longer needed (no waiting period).
2. **Highly available** infrastructure.
3. **No manual management of compute infrastructure** (rules out CloudHSM clusters).

## Correct Answer: B — Customer managed keys with imported key material; delete the imported key material

When you create a KMS key with `Origin = EXTERNAL` and import your own key material, AWS provides the `DeleteImportedKeyMaterial` API. AWS KMS has a copy of your imported key and will keep it highly available while you need it, and imported keys offer a special API for deletion – DeleteImportedKeyMaterial – which immediately deletes all copies of the imported key material that AWS KMS has, with no option for AWS to recover the key.

The KMS FAQ confirms this is on-demand and bypasses the waiting period: For customer KMS keys with imported key material, you can delete the key material without deleting the AWS KMS key id or metadata; you can delete your imported key material on demand without a waiting period.

Because KMS itself is a fully managed, highly available service, this satisfies the "no manual compute infrastructure management" and "highly available" requirements.

## Why the other options are wrong

### A. AWS KMS managed keys, schedule for immediate deletion — **Incorrect**
AWS-managed keys cannot be deleted by the customer at all. AWS Managed Keys are managed by AWS for use with AWS services, you do not have the ability to delete them, and you are not charged for them either. Even for keys you can schedule for deletion, AWS KMS applies a waiting period of 30 days by default, but you can specify a waiting period of 7-30 days; when successful, the key state changes to PendingDeletion and the key can't be used in any cryptographic operations. Immediate deletion is not possible.

### C. Customer managed keys, delete the key material — **Incorrect**
For standard customer managed keys (where AWS KMS generates the key material), there is no API to delete key material on demand. The `DeleteImportedKeyMaterial` operation is restricted to keys whose Origin of the KMS key must be EXTERNAL. Deletion of a non-imported customer managed key requires `ScheduleKeyDeletion` with a 7–30 day waiting period.

### D. Customer managed keys in a CloudHSM key store — **Incorrect**
Two problems:
1. CloudHSM custom key stores still require `ScheduleKeyDeletion` with a 7–30 day waiting period — immediate deletion is not supported. When KMS deletes a KMS key from a CloudHSM key store, it makes a best effort to delete the associated key material from the associated CloudHSM cluster, but you might need to manually delete the orphaned key material from the cluster and its backups.
2. CloudHSM requires you to provision and manage an HSM cluster, which violates the "does not require manual management for compute infrastructure" requirement.

## Key takeaway

Only **imported key material** (Origin = EXTERNAL) supports immediate, on-demand deletion via `DeleteImportedKeyMaterial`, while still using the fully managed, highly available AWS KMS service.

## References
- [Delete imported key material](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/importing-keys-delete-key-material.html)
- [DeleteImportedKeyMaterial API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/APIReference/API_DeleteImportedKeyMaterial.html)
- [ScheduleKeyDeletion API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/APIReference/API_ScheduleKeyDeletion.html)
- [AWS KMS Key stores overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/key-store-overview.html)
- [AWS KMS FAQs](https://aws.amazon.com/kms/faqs/)

zh.question: 开发人员使用 AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) 管理加密密钥。开发人员必须确保所有加密密钥在不再需要时都能立即删除。开发人员希望找到一种高可用性且无需手动管理计算基础设施的解决方案。哪种解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 AWS KMS 托管密钥。当不再需要这些密钥时，安排立即删除这些密钥。
options.B: 使用客户管理的密钥和导入的密钥材料。当不再需要这些密钥时，请删除导入的密钥材料。
options.C: 使用客户管理的密钥。当不再需要密钥时，删除密钥资料。
options.D: 使用客户管理的密钥和 AWS CloudHSM 密钥库。当不再需要这些密钥时，安排立即删除这些密钥。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

一个开发人员需要在 AWS KMS 中管理加密密钥，有三个要求：
1. **立即删除**不再需要的密钥（无等待期）。
2. **高度可用**的基础设施。
3. **不需要手动管理计算基础设施**（排除 CloudHSM 集群）。

## 正确答案：B — 客户管理密钥且导入密钥材料；删除导入的密钥材料

当你创建 Origin = EXTERNAL 的 KMS 密钥并导入自己的密钥材料时，AWS 提供 `DeleteImportedKeyMaterial` API。AWS KMS 拥有你导入的密钥的副本，并在你需要时保持其高度可用性；导入的密钥提供一个特殊的删除 API – DeleteImportedKeyMaterial – 它立即删除 AWS KMS 拥有的所有导入密钥材料副本，AWS 无法恢复该密钥。

KMS FAQ 确认这是按需进行且绕过等待期的：对于具有导入密钥材料的客户 KMS 密钥，你可以删除密钥材料而不删除 AWS KMS 密钥 ID 或元数据；你可以按需删除导入的密钥材料，无需等待期。

由于 KMS 本身是一个完全托管的高可用服务，这满足了"不需要手动管理计算基础设施"和"高度可用"的要求。

## 其他选项为何错误

### A. AWS KMS 托管密钥，计划立即删除 — **错误**
AWS 托管密钥根本不能由客户删除。AWS 托管密钥由 AWS 管理以供 AWS 服务使用，你无法删除它们，也不需要为它们付费。即使对于可以计划删除的密钥，AWS KMS 默认应用 30 天的等待期，但你可以指定 7-30 天的等待期；成功后，密钥状态变为 PendingDeletion，密钥无法用于任何加密操作。不支持立即删除。

### C. 客户管理密钥，删除密钥材料 — **错误**
对于标准客户管理密钥（AWS KMS 生成密钥材料），不存在按需删除密钥材料的 API。`DeleteImportedKeyMaterial` 操作限制于 KMS 密钥的 Origin 必须是 EXTERNAL 的密钥。删除非导入的客户管理密钥需要使用 `ScheduleKeyDeletion`，等待期为 7–30 天。

### D. CloudHSM 密钥存储中的客户管理密钥 — **错误**
有两个问题：
1. CloudHSM 自定义密钥存储仍需要 `ScheduleKeyDeletion`，等待期为 7–30 天——不支持立即删除。当 KMS 从 CloudHSM 密钥存储中删除 KMS 密钥时，它尽力从关联的 CloudHSM 集群中删除关联的密钥材料，但你可能需要从集群及其备份中手动删除孤立的密钥材料。
2. CloudHSM 要求你配置和管理 HSM 集群，这违反了"不需要手动管理计算基础设施"的要求。

## 关键要点

只有**导入的密钥材料**（Origin = EXTERNAL）支持通过 `DeleteImportedKeyMaterial` 进行立即按需删除，同时仍在使用完全托管、高度可用的 AWS KMS 服务。

## 参考资源
- [Delete imported key material](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/importing-keys-delete-key-material.html)
- [DeleteImportedKeyMaterial API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/APIReference/API_DeleteImportedKeyMaterial.html)
- [ScheduleKeyDeletion API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/APIReference/API_ScheduleKeyDeletion.html)
- [AWS KMS Key stores overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/key-store-overview.html)
- [AWS KMS FAQs](https://aws.amazon.com/kms/faqs/)

en.question: A company has an ecommerce application. The application's API sends order data to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SOS) queue. A developer needs to modify the application to enrich the order data before the application sends the order data to a fulfillment system. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST development effort?

options.A: Create an AWS Lambda function to poll the SQS queue. enrich the message data, and send the enriched data to the fulfilment system, Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the Lambda function to the SNS topic.
options.B: Create an AWS Step Functions state machine. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to run the state machine when an order is published to the SQS queue. Map the orders to an AWS Lambda function. Program the Lambda function to perform the data enrichment and to invoke the state machine. Configure the last step of the state machine to send the enriched data to the fulfilment system,
options.C: Create an Amazon EMR cluster to read messages from the SQS queue. Configure an EMR job to enrich the order data. Create and configure an Amazon S3 bucket as the output location. Adjust the order fulfilment system to retrieve the enriched files from the S3 bucket.
options.D: Create an Amazon EventBridge pipe that uses event enrichment. Configure the SQS queue as a source for the pipe. Set the fulfillment system as the target of the pipe.

en.explanation:
# Enriching SQS Order Data with Least Development Effort

## Scenario
An ecommerce API sends order data to an Amazon SQS queue. The developer needs to **enrich** the order data before forwarding it to a fulfillment system, with the **LEAST development effort**.

## Correct Answer: D — Use an Amazon EventBridge Pipe with event enrichment

Amazon EventBridge Pipes is purpose-built for exactly this scenario. Pipes are intended for point-to-point integrations between supported sources and targets, with support for advanced transformations and enrichment. It reduces the need for specialized knowledge and integration code when developing event-driven architectures. To set up a pipe, you choose the source, add optional filtering, define optional enrichment, and choose the target for the event data.

A pipe has four stages — Source, Filtering, Enrichment, and Target. Only Source and Target are required.

For this scenario:
- **Source** = the existing SQS order queue (You can use EventBridge Pipes to receive records from an Amazon SQS queue. You can then optionally filter or enhance these records before sending them to an available destination for processing.)
- **Enrichment** = a configured enrichment step (Lambda, Step Functions, API destination, or API Gateway) that adds the extra fields
- **Target** = the fulfillment system

This eliminates the need to write polling code, message deletion logic, or "glue" Lambda code, which is exactly why Pipes was created. EventBridge Pipes fills the gap between simple point-to-point integrations and full event bus architectures. The built-in filtering and enrichment stages handle common patterns that previously required custom Lambda glue code. If you're building a pipeline that reads from one source, optionally transforms the data, and writes to one destination, Pipes is probably the simplest way to do it.

Reference: [Amazon EventBridge Pipes — User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-pipes.html)

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

### A. Lambda polling SQS + SNS topic subscription
- Requires writing and maintaining custom Lambda code to poll SQS, parse messages, perform enrichment, handle errors/retries, delete messages, and call the fulfillment system.
- The SNS topic in the design is nonsensical — Lambda is "subscribed to the SNS topic," but messages flow into SQS, not SNS, so the SNS piece does not connect to the actual data flow. This is architecturally broken.
- More development effort than a managed EventBridge Pipe.

### B. Step Functions + EventBridge rule + Lambda
- EventBridge **rules** cannot be triggered directly by SQS messages — SQS is not an event source for the EventBridge default bus (this is precisely the gap that EventBridge **Pipes** was created to fill: Pipes connect a source directly to a target without needing an event bus at all. Pipes can read from SQS queues, DynamoDB streams, Kinesis streams, Kafka topics, and other event sources that Rules can't.).
- The flow is also circular/illogical: Lambda enriches and "invokes the state machine," but the state machine was supposed to invoke the Lambda. This adds many components (Step Functions, EventBridge rule, Lambda) and significantly more development effort.

### C. Amazon EMR cluster reading from SQS, output to S3
- EMR is a big-data Hadoop/Spark processing service — wildly oversized for per-message enrichment of order events.
- EMR does not natively read from SQS; you would have to build custom Spark/Hadoop integrations.
- Changes the delivery model (S3 file pull) and forces modifications to the fulfillment system, which adds development effort rather than reducing it.

## Summary
EventBridge Pipes natively integrates SQS as a source, supports a built‑in enrichment stage, and delivers to a target — providing the entire requirement as a managed, low-code, point-to-point integration.

zh.question: 一家公司有一个电子商务应用程序。该应用程序的 API 会将订单数据发送到 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SOS) 队列。开发人员需要修改应用程序，以便在将订单数据发送到履行系统之前丰富订单数据。哪种解决方案能够以最少的开发工作量满足此要求？

options.A: 创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数来轮询 SQS 队列，丰富消息数据，并将丰富后的数据发送到交付系统。创建一个 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题，并将 Lambda 函数订阅到该 SNS 主题。
options.B: 创建一个 AWS Step Functions 状态机。配置一条 Amazon EventBridge 规则，以便在订单发布到 SQS 队列时运行该状态机。将订单映射到一个 AWS Lambda 函数。编写 Lambda 函数程序，使其执行数据增强并调用该状态机。配置状态机的最后一步，将增强后的数据发送到履行系统。
options.C: 创建一个 Amazon EMR 集群，用于从 SQS 队列读取消息。配置一个 EMR 作业来丰富订单数据。创建并配置一个 Amazon S3 存储桶作为输出位置。调整订单履行系统，使其从 S3 存储桶中检索丰富后的文件。
options.D: 创建一个使用事件增强功能的 Amazon EventBridge 管道。将 SQS 队列配置为管道的源。将履行系统设置为管道的目标。

zh.explanation:
# 通过最少开发工作量丰富 SQS 订单数据

## 场景
电商 API 将订单数据发送到 Amazon SQS 队列。开发人员需要**丰富**订单数据，然后将其转发到履行系统，并要求**开发工作量最少**。

## 正确答案：D — 使用 Amazon EventBridge Pipe 和事件丰富

Amazon EventBridge Pipes 正是为此场景而设计的。Pipes 用于在支持的源和目标之间进行点对点集成，支持高级转换和丰富。在开发事件驱动架构时，减少了对专业知识和集成代码的需求。要设置管道，您需要选择源、添加可选的过滤、定义可选的丰富，以及为事件数据选择目标。

管道有四个阶段——源、过滤、丰富和目标。只有源和目标是必需的。

对于此场景：
- **源** = 现有 SQS 订单队列（您可以使用 EventBridge Pipes 从 Amazon SQS 队列接收记录。然后可以选择过滤或增强这些记录，然后再将其发送到可用目标进行处理。）
- **丰富** = 配置的丰富步骤（Lambda、Step Functions、API 目标或 API Gateway），用于添加额外字段
- **目标** = 履行系统

这消除了编写轮询代码、消息删除逻辑或"胶合"Lambda 代码的需求，这正是 Pipes 创建的原因。EventBridge Pipes 填补了简单点对点集成和完整事件总线架构之间的空白。内置的过滤和丰富阶段处理了以前需要自定义 Lambda 胶合代码的常见模式。如果您构建的管道从一个源读取，可选地转换数据，并写入一个目标，Pipes 可能是最简单的方法。

参考资料：[Amazon EventBridge Pipes — 用户指南](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-pipes.html)

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

### A. Lambda 轮询 SQS + SNS 主题订阅
- 需要编写和维护自定义 Lambda 代码以轮询 SQS、解析消息、执行丰富、处理错误/重试、删除消息并调用履行系统。
- 设计中的 SNS 主题不合理——Lambda "订阅到 SNS 主题"，但消息流入 SQS 而不是 SNS，所以 SNS 部分与实际数据流不连接。这在架构上是错误的。
- 开发工作量比托管 EventBridge Pipe 更多。

### B. Step Functions + EventBridge 规则 + Lambda
- EventBridge **规则**无法直接由 SQS 消息触发——SQS 不是 EventBridge 默认总线的事件源（这正是 EventBridge **Pipes** 创建的目的：Pipes 将源直接连接到目标，无需事件总线。Pipes 可以从 SQS 队列、DynamoDB 流、Kinesis 流、Kafka 主题和其他规则无法支持的事件源读取。）。
- 流程也是循环/不合逻辑的：Lambda 丰富并"调用状态机"，但状态机应该调用 Lambda。这添加了许多组件（Step Functions、EventBridge 规则、Lambda），显著增加了开发工作量。

### C. Amazon EMR 集群从 SQS 读取，输出到 S3
- EMR 是大数据 Hadoop/Spark 处理服务——对于按消息订单事件丰富来说远过度设计。
- EMR 本身不能从 SQS 本地读取；您需要构建自定义 Spark/Hadoop 集成。
- 改变交付模式（S3 文件拉取）并强制修改履行系统，这会增加开发工作量而不是减少工作量。

## 总结
EventBridge Pipes 本地集成 SQS 作为源，支持内置丰富阶段，并交付到目标——以托管的、低代码的点对点集成形式提供整个需求。

en.question: An application interacts with Amazon Aurora to store and track customer information. The primary database is set up with multiple read replicas for improving the performance of the read queries. However, one of the Aurora replicas is receiving most or all of the traffic, while the other Aurora replica remains idle. How can this issue be resolved?

options.A: Disable application-level DNS caching.
options.B: Enable application-level DNS caching.
options.C: Enable application pooling
options.D: Disable application pooling

en.explanation:
## Scenario

An application uses Amazon Aurora with multiple read replicas behind the **reader endpoint** to scale read traffic. The problem: one Aurora replica is receiving most/all of the traffic while the other replica sits idle. The question asks how to fix this uneven distribution.

## Why A is Correct — Disable application-level DNS caching

The Aurora reader endpoint distributes connections across read replicas via **DNS round-robin**, not at the IP/TCP or database protocol layer. Aurora reader endpoints are DNS CNAME entries. If a cluster has multiple reader instances, then when you resolve the reader endpoint, you get an instance IP that's chosen in round robin fashion. This is because the reader endpoint contains all Aurora replicas, and it provides DNS-based, round-robin load balancing for new connections. Make sure that you keep resolving the endpoint without caching DNS to get a different instance IP on each resolution.

The key issue: You must keep resolving the endpoint without caching DNS to get a different instance IP on each resolution. If you only resolve the endpoint once and then keep the connection in your pool, every query on that connection goes to the same instance. If you cache DNS, you receive the same instance IP each time you resolve the endpoint.

This is the exact symptom described in the question. The Aurora MySQL DBA Handbook explicitly lists this scenario: Unequal use of Aurora Replicas, for example, one of the Aurora Replicas is receiving most or all of the traffic while the other Aurora Replicas sit idle. The recommended fix is to disable (or significantly shorten the TTL of) DNS caching at the application layer (e.g., for JVM-based apps, override the `networkaddress.cache.ttl` security property). If your client application is caching the DNS data of your DB instances, then set a TTL value of less than 30 seconds.

Aurora's own DNS records use a 5-second TTL, but client-side caches (OS resolver, JVM default of "cache forever", connection pools) often extend this far longer, pinning all connections to a single replica IP.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **B. Enable application-level DNS caching** — This is the *opposite* of the fix. Enabling/extending DNS caching is precisely what causes the imbalance, because the cached IP keeps pointing the application at the same single replica.

- **C. Enable application pooling** — Connection pooling actually makes the problem **worse**, not better. A pool resolves the reader endpoint once when a connection is created and then reuses that long-lived connection, so every query on that connection goes to the same replica. AWS notes: If you use any form of connection pooling or other multiplexing, you might need to flush or reduce the time-to-live for any cached DNS information.

- **D. Disable application pooling** — While disabling pooling could force new DNS lookups, it's not the recommended or efficient solution and would severely degrade application performance by forcing a TCP/TLS/auth handshake for every query. The root-cause fix called out by AWS documentation is to disable/shorten DNS caching, not to abandon connection pooling.

## Best-Practice Alternatives (beyond the answer choices)

- Use **Amazon RDS Proxy** in front of Aurora to manage connections and load balancing.
- Use a **smart driver** (e.g., AWS JDBC Driver for MySQL, MariaDB Connector/J) that is topology-aware and bypasses DNS for replica selection.

## References

- [Aurora MySQL DBA Handbook – Load balancing with the reader endpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/amazon-aurora-mysql-db-admin-handbook/load-balancing-with-the-reader-endpoint.html)
- [Aurora MySQL DBA Handbook – DNS caching](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/amazon-aurora-mysql-db-admin-handbook/dns-caching.html)
- [AWS re:Post – Why is my connection redirected to the reader instance](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/aurora-mysql-redirected-endpoint-writer)
- [AWS re:Post – How Aurora distributes workload between reader nodes](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/aurora-mysql-postgresql-reader-nodes)
- [Amazon Aurora endpoint connections](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Overview.Endpoints.html)

zh.question: 一个应用程序与 Amazon Aurora 交互以存储和跟踪客户信息。主数据库配置了多个只读副本，以提高读取查询的性能。然而，其中一个 Aurora 副本接收了大部分或全部流量，而另一个 Aurora 副本则处于空闲状态。如何解决这个问题？

options.A: 禁用应用程序级别的 DNS 缓存。
options.B: 启用应用级 DNS 缓存。
options.C: 启用应用程序池
options.D: 禁用应用程序池

zh.explanation:
## 场景

一个应用程序使用 Amazon Aurora，配备了多个只读副本，这些副本位于**读取端点**后面，用于扩展读取流量。问题是：一个 Aurora 副本收到了大部分或全部流量，而其他副本处于空闲状态。问题要求如何修复这种不均衡的分布。

## 为什么 A 正确 — 禁用应用级 DNS 缓存

Aurora 读取端点通过 **DNS 轮询**（而非在 IP/TCP 或数据库协议层）在读取副本之间分发连接。Aurora 读取端点是 DNS CNAME 条目。如果集群有多个读取实例，则在解析读取端点时，您会获得一个以轮询方式选择的实例 IP。这是因为读取端点包含所有 Aurora 副本，并为新连接提供基于 DNS 的轮询负载均衡。请确保持续解析端点，不缓存 DNS，以便在每次解析端点时获得不同的实例 IP。

关键问题是：您必须持续解析端点，不缓存 DNS，以便在每次解析端点时获得不同的实例 IP。如果您只解析一次端点，然后在连接池中保留该连接，则该连接上的每个查询都会转到同一实例。如果您缓存 DNS，每次解析端点时都会收到相同的实例 IP。

这正是问题中描述的症状。Aurora MySQL DBA Handbook 明确列出了这个场景：Aurora 副本的不均衡使用，例如，一个 Aurora 副本收到了大部分或全部流量，而其他 Aurora 副本处于空闲状态。 推荐的修复方法是在应用层禁用（或显著缩短 TTL）DNS 缓存（例如，对于基于 JVM 的应用，覆盖 `networkaddress.cache.ttl` 安全属性）。如果客户端应用正在缓存 DB 实例的 DNS 数据，则将 TTL 值设置为少于 30 秒。

Aurora 自己的 DNS 记录使用 5 秒 TTL，但客户端缓存（操作系统解析器、JVM 默认的"永久缓存"、连接池）通常会将其延长得更久，从而将所有连接固定到单个副本 IP。

## 为什么其他选项错误

- **B. 启用应用级 DNS 缓存** — 这与修复方法相反。启用/延长 DNS 缓存正是导致不平衡的原因，因为缓存的 IP 持续将应用指向同一单个副本。

- **C. 启用应用连接池** — 连接池实际上会加剧问题，而非改善问题。连接池在创建连接时解析一次读取端点，然后重复使用该长期存活的连接，因此该连接上的每个查询都转到同一副本。AWS 指出：如果您使用任何形式的连接池或其他复用，您可能需要刷新或降低任何缓存 DNS 信息的生存时间。

- **D. 禁用应用连接池** — 虽然禁用连接池可能会强制进行新的 DNS 查询，但这不是推荐或高效的解决方案，会因强制每个查询都进行 TCP/TLS/身份验证握手而严重降低应用性能。AWS 文档指出的根本原因修复是禁用/缩短 DNS 缓存，而非放弃连接池。

## 最佳实践替代方案（超出答案选择）

- 在 Aurora 前面使用 **Amazon RDS Proxy** 来管理连接和负载均衡。
- 使用**智能驱动程序**（例如 AWS JDBC Driver for MySQL、MariaDB Connector/J），它具有拓扑感知能力，并绕过 DNS 进行副本选择。

## 参考资源

- [Aurora MySQL DBA Handbook – Load balancing with the reader endpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/amazon-aurora-mysql-db-admin-handbook/load-balancing-with-the-reader-endpoint.html)
- [Aurora MySQL DBA Handbook – DNS caching](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/amazon-aurora-mysql-db-admin-handbook/dns-caching.html)
- [AWS re:Post – Why is my connection redirected to the reader instance](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/aurora-mysql-redirected-endpoint-writer)
- [AWS re:Post – How Aurora distributes workload between reader nodes](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/aurora-mysql-postgresql-reader-nodes)
- [Amazon Aurora endpoint connections](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Overview.Endpoints.html)

en.question: A company runs continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines for its application on AWS CodePipeline. A developer must write unit tests and run them as part of the pipelines before staging the artifacts for testing. How should the developer incorporate unit tests as part of CI/CD pipelines?

options.A: Create a separate CodePipeline pipeline to run unit tests.
options.B: Update the AWS CodeBuild build specification to include a phase for running unit tests.
options.C: Install the AWS CodeDeploy agent on an Amazon EC2 instance to run unit tests.
options.D: Create a testing branch in a git repository for the pipelines to run unit tests.

en.explanation:
# Running Unit Tests in a CodePipeline CI/CD Pipeline

## Scenario
The team has a CodePipeline-based CI/CD pipeline. The developer needs to **run unit tests as part of the pipeline before staging artifacts for testing**. The question asks for the simplest, most idiomatic way to incorporate unit tests into the pipeline.

## Correct Answer: B — Update the AWS CodeBuild buildspec to include a phase for running unit tests

AWS CodeBuild is the native build/test service in the AWS CI/CD suite, and it is driven by a `buildspec.yml` file that defines phases (`install`, `pre_build`, `build`, `post_build`). Unit-test commands are simply added to one of these phases (typically `build` or `post_build`).

This sample shows you how to use the AWS CLI to incorporate tests into builds in CodeBuild. You can use JUnit to create unit tests, or you can use another tool to create configuration tests. You can then evaluate the test results to fix issues or optimize your application.

You can specify the unit tests in either the build or the post_build sequence in the buildspec.yml file. CodeBuild can also publish results via the `reports` section so test results appear in the CodeBuild console.

Example buildspec snippet:

```yaml
version: 0.2
phases:
  install:
    runtime-versions:
      python: 3.9
    commands:
      - pip install -r requirements.txt
  build:
    commands:
      - python setup.py build
  post_build:
    commands:
      - python -m unittest discover     # run unit tests
reports:
  UnitTests:
    files:
      - 'unittests.xml'
    file-format: JUNITXML
```

When this CodeBuild project is wired into a CodePipeline stage (typically right after Source and before Deploy/Staging), the pipeline will fail fast if unit tests fail, preventing bad artifacts from being staged.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A. Create a separate CodePipeline pipeline for unit tests.** A separate pipeline would not gate the staging of artifacts in the main pipeline. Tests must run as a stage/action within the same pipeline so that failures stop progression to staging. This also adds operational overhead with no benefit.

- **C. Install the CodeDeploy agent on EC2 to run unit tests.** The CodeDeploy agent is for deploying application revisions to compute targets — it is not a test runner. Unit tests should run during build, not after deployment, and certainly not via the deployment agent.

- **D. Create a testing branch in git for the pipelines to run unit tests.** A git branch is a source-control construct; merely creating a branch does not execute tests. You would still need a build/test stage (CodeBuild) to actually run them. The branch alone solves nothing.

## References
- [AWS CodeBuild – Test report using the AWS CLI sample](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/sample-test-report-cli.html)
- [AWS CodeBuild – Specify test commands](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/report-group-test-case-commands.html)
- [AWS CodeBuild – Build specification reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/build-spec-ref.html)
- [Test Reports with AWS CodeBuild (AWS DevOps Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/devops/test-reports-with-aws-codebuild/)

zh.question: 一家公司在 AWS CodePipeline 上为其应用程序运行持续集成/持续交付 (CI/CD) 流水线。开发人员必须编写单元测试，并在将测试工件部署到流水线之前运行这些测试。开发人员应该如何将单元测试集成到 CI/CD 流水线中？

options.A: 创建一个单独的 CodePipeline 管道来运行单元测试。
options.B: 更新 AWS CodeBuild 构建规范，使其包含运行单元测试的阶段。
options.C: 在 Amazon EC2 实例上安装 AWS CodeDeploy 代理以运行单元测试。
options.D: 在 git 仓库中创建一个测试分支，供流水线运行单元测试。

zh.explanation:
# 在 CodePipeline CI/CD 管道中运行单元测试

## 场景
团队有一个基于 CodePipeline 的 CI/CD 管道。开发人员需要**在管道中作为构建阶段的一部分运行单元测试，然后才能暂存工件进行测试**。问题要求以最简单、最符合 AWS 惯例的方式将单元测试集成到管道中。

## 正确答案：B — 更新 AWS CodeBuild buildspec 以包含运行单元测试的阶段

AWS CodeBuild 是 AWS CI/CD 套件中原生的构建/测试服务，由 `buildspec.yml` 文件驱动，该文件定义了阶段（`install`、`pre_build`、`build`、`post_build`）。单元测试命令只需添加到这些阶段之一（通常是 `build` 或 `post_build`）。

本示例展示了如何使用 AWS CLI 在 CodeBuild 中将测试集成到构建中。您可以使用 JUnit 创建单元测试，也可以使用其他工具创建配置测试。然后您可以评估测试结果以修复问题或优化应用程序。

您可以在 buildspec.yml 文件的 build 或 post_build 序列中指定单元测试。CodeBuild 还可以通过 `reports` 部分发布结果，以便测试结果显示在 CodeBuild 控制台中。

buildspec 示例片段：

```yaml
version: 0.2
phases:
  install:
    runtime-versions:
      python: 3.9
    commands:
      - pip install -r requirements.txt
  build:
    commands:
      - python setup.py build
  post_build:
    commands:
      - python -m unittest discover     # 运行单元测试
reports:
  UnitTests:
    files:
      - 'unittests.xml'
    file-format: JUNITXML
```

当此 CodeBuild 项目被集成到 CodePipeline 阶段（通常在 Source 之后和 Deploy/Staging 之前）时，如果单元测试失败，管道将快速失败，防止坏的工件被暂存。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

- **A. 为单元测试创建单独的 CodePipeline 管道。** 单独的管道不会阻止主管道中工件的暂存。测试必须作为同一管道中的阶段/操作运行，以便故障阻止向暂存推进。这也增加了操作开销，没有任何益处。

- **C. 在 EC2 上安装 CodeDeploy 代理以运行单元测试。** CodeDeploy 代理用于将应用程序修订部署到计算目标——它不是测试运行器。单元测试应在构建期间运行，而不是在部署后运行，当然也不能通过部署代理运行。

- **D. 在 git 中创建测试分支以运行单元测试。** git 分支是源代码控制构造；仅创建分支不会执行测试。您仍然需要构建/测试阶段（CodeBuild）来实际运行测试。分支本身解决不了任何问题。

## 参考资源
- [AWS CodeBuild – 使用 AWS CLI 的测试报告示例](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/sample-test-report-cli.html)
- [AWS CodeBuild – 指定测试命令](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/report-group-test-case-commands.html)
- [AWS CodeBuild – 构建规范参考](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/build-spec-ref.html)
- [AWS CodeBuild 测试报告（AWS DevOps 博客）](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/devops/test-reports-with-aws-codebuild/)

en.question: A developer is troubleshooting a three-tier application, which is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances. There is a connectivity problem between the application servers and the database servers. Which AWS services or tools should be used to identity the faulty component? (Choose two.)

options.A: AWS CloudTrail
options.B: AWS Trusted Advisor
options.C: Amazon VPC Flow Logs
options.D: Network access control lists
options.E: AWS Config rules

en.explanation:
# Troubleshooting EC2-to-Database Connectivity in a 3-Tier Application

## Scenario
A developer is troubleshooting a network connectivity issue between the application tier (EC2) and the database tier of a three-tier app. The question asks which two AWS services/tools help **identify the faulty component** at the network level.

## Correct Answers: C and D

### C. Amazon VPC Flow Logs ✅
VPC Flow Logs capture metadata about IP traffic going to and from network interfaces in a VPC. Many organizations collect, store, and analyze network flow logs and use this information to troubleshoot connectivity and security issues, and to make sure that network access rules are working as expected.

By inspecting `ACCEPT`/`REJECT` records on the ENIs of the app and DB instances, you can determine whether traffic is reaching the database. If the flow log entry shows REJECT this means that either the NACL or Security Group is blocking the flow. This makes Flow Logs the primary tool for pinpointing the faulty network component.

See [Logging IP traffic using VPC Flow Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs.html).

### D. Network Access Control Lists (NACLs) ✅
NACLs are subnet-level, **stateless** firewalls. They are a very common cause of broken tier-to-tier connectivity because both inbound *and* outbound (including ephemeral return ports) must be permitted. Network Access Control Lists (NACLs) are stateless, so ensure they allow both inbound HTTPS traffic and outbound traffic on the ephemeral port ranges. A common mistake is permitting outbound connections but blocking return traffic on these high-numbered ports.

Reviewing the NACL rules attached to the application and database subnets is essential to identify whether they are the faulty component blocking the traffic. See [Control subnet traffic with network ACLs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-network-acls.html).

Together, **VPC Flow Logs** show *what* traffic is being dropped, and inspecting the **NACLs** (along with security groups) shows *why* — the two tools work hand-in-hand for connectivity troubleshooting.

## Why the Other Options Are Incorrect

### A. AWS CloudTrail ❌
CloudTrail logs **API calls** (control plane), not network packets. AWS CloudTrail operates at the control plane layer. It captures API calls — who created a Security Group rule, who modified a NACL, who launched an EC2 instance. CloudTrail tells you what changes were made to your infrastructure and by whom. Flow logs tell you what traffic traversed your infrastructure. CloudTrail might tell you *who* changed a config, but it cannot identify the faulty network component carrying the traffic.

### B. AWS Trusted Advisor ❌
Trusted Advisor provides best-practice checks across cost, performance, security, fault tolerance, and service limits. It does **not** inspect live network traffic between EC2 instances and cannot diagnose a specific connectivity failure between an app server and a database. See [AWS Trusted Advisor](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/trusted-advisor.html).

### E. AWS Config rules ❌
AWS Config tracks **configuration state and compliance** of AWS resources over time. While a Config rule could flag a non-compliant security group or NACL, it is not a real-time network troubleshooting tool. It does not show traffic accept/reject events or pinpoint which network component is currently dropping packets between the two tiers. See [AWS Config Rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/evaluate-config.html).

## Summary
For diagnosing a connectivity problem between EC2 application servers and database servers, the developer should:
1. **Enable/inspect VPC Flow Logs** to see whether traffic is being accepted or rejected and where.
2. **Review the NACLs** on the relevant subnets to confirm they allow the required inbound *and* outbound (ephemeral) traffic.

**Correct answers: C and D.**

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在排查一个部署在 Amazon EC2 实例上的三层应用程序的故障。应用程序服务器和数据库服务器之间存在连接问题。应该使用哪些 AWS 服务或工具来识别故障组件？（选择两项。）

options.A: AWS CloudTrail
options.B: AWS Trusted Advisor
options.C: Amazon VPC 流日志
options.D: 网络访问控制列表
options.E: AWS 配置规则

zh.explanation:
# EC2 到数据库连接故障排查（3 层应用）

## 场景
开发人员正在排查三层应用中应用层（EC2）和数据库层之间的网络连接问题。问题要求选择两个 AWS 服务/工具来**识别网络级别的故障组件**。

## 正确答案：C 和 D

### C. Amazon VPC Flow Logs ✅
VPC Flow Logs 捕获流向 VPC 中网络接口的 IP 流量的元数据。许多组织收集、存储和分析网络流日志，利用这些信息排查连接和安全问题，并确保网络访问规则按预期工作。

通过检查应用和数据库实例的 ENI 上的 `ACCEPT`/`REJECT` 记录，你可以确定流量是否到达数据库。如果流日志条目显示 REJECT，这意味着 NACL 或安全组正在阻止该流。这使得 Flow Logs 成为精确定位故障网络组件的主要工具。

参见 [Logging IP traffic using VPC Flow Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs.html)。

### D. Network Access Control Lists (NACLs) ✅
NACL 是子网级别的**无状态**防火墙。它们是导致层间连接中断的常见原因，因为入站和出站（包括临时端口）都必须被允许。网络访问控制列表 (NACL) 是无状态的，因此需要确保它们允许入站 HTTPS 流量和临时端口范围上的出站流量。常见错误是允许出站连接但阻止这些高编号端口上的返回流量。

检查应用和数据库子网上关联的 NACL 规则，以识别它们是否是阻止流量的故障组件。参见 [Control subnet traffic with network ACLs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-network-acls.html)。

**VPC Flow Logs** 显示*哪些*流量被丢弃，检查 **NACL**（以及安全组）显示*为什么* — 这两个工具协同工作以进行连接故障排查。

## 其他选项为何不正确

### A. AWS CloudTrail ❌
CloudTrail 记录的是 **API 调用**（控制平面），而非网络数据包。AWS CloudTrail 在控制平面层运行。它捕获 API 调用 — 谁创建了安全组规则，谁修改了 NACL，谁启动了 EC2 实例。CloudTrail 告诉你基础设施进行了什么更改以及由谁进行的。Flow Logs 告诉你什么流量穿过了基础设施。CloudTrail 可能会告诉你*谁*更改了配置，但它无法识别传输流量的故障网络组件。

### B. AWS Trusted Advisor ❌
Trusted Advisor 在成本、性能、安全、容错性和服务限制方面提供最佳实践检查。它**不能**检查 EC2 实例之间的实时网络流量，也无法诊断应用服务器和数据库之间的特定连接故障。参见 [AWS Trusted Advisor](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/trusted-advisor.html)。

### E. AWS Config Rules ❌
AWS Config 追踪 AWS 资源在一段时间内的**配置状态和合规性**。虽然 Config 规则可以标记不符合规定的安全组或 NACL，但它不是实时网络故障排查工具。它不显示流量接受/拒绝事件，也无法精确指出两层之间的哪个网络组件正在丢弃数据包。参见 [AWS Config Rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/evaluate-config.html)。

## 总结
为了诊断 EC2 应用服务器和数据库服务器之间的连接问题，开发人员应该：
1. **启用/检查 VPC Flow Logs**，查看流量是否被接受或拒绝以及在哪里被拒绝。
2. **审查相关子网上的 NACL**，确认它们允许所需的入站*和*出站（临时）流量。

**正确答案：C 和 D。**

en.question: A company runs a new application on AWS Elastic Beanstalk. The company needs to deploy updates to the application. The updates must not cause any downtime for application users. The deployment must forward a specified percentage of incoming client traffic to a new application version during an evaluation period. Which deployment type will meet these requirements?

options.A: rolling
options.B: traffic-splitting
options.C: in-place
options.D: immutable

en.explanation:
# Elastic Beanstalk Traffic-Splitting Deployment

## Scenario
The company needs a deployment strategy on AWS Elastic Beanstalk that:
1. Causes **no downtime** for users.
2. Routes a **specified percentage of incoming client traffic** to the new application version.
3. Has an **evaluation period** to assess the new version before full rollout.

This describes a **canary deployment** pattern.

## Correct Answer: B – Traffic-splitting

Elastic Beanstalk's **Traffic Splitting** deployment policy is purpose-built for canary testing. Traffic-splitting deployments let you perform canary testing as part of your application deployment. In a traffic-splitting deployment, Elastic Beanstalk launches a full set of new instances just like during an immutable deployment. It then forwards a specified percentage of incoming client traffic to the new application version for a specified evaluation period. If the new instances stay healthy, Elastic Beanstalk forwards all traffic to them and terminates the old ones.

Because the new version runs on a **separate temporary Auto Scaling group** alongside the old one, there is no downtime — the old fleet keeps serving traffic until the cutover. During a traffic-splitting deployment, Elastic Beanstalk creates a new set of instances in a separate temporary Auto Scaling group.

Example configuration via `.ebextensions`:

```yaml
option_settings:
  aws:elasticbeanstalk:command:
    DeploymentPolicy: TrafficSplitting
    Timeout: 600
  aws:elasticbeanstalk:trafficsplitting:
    NewVersionPercent: 10
    EvaluationTime: 10
```

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A. Rolling** — Updates instances **in batches** on the existing fleet. It does not split traffic by percentage to a new version for evaluation; instead the entire batch of instances is replaced and serves 100% of its share. Capacity is reduced during deployment, and there is no canary/evaluation phase. Use rolling application deployments to deploy new application versions to Amazon EC2 instances in your Elastic Beanstalk environment in batches of instances.

- **C. In-place** — Not a named Elastic Beanstalk deployment policy. The actual EB policies are AllAtOnce, Rolling, RollingWithAdditionalBatch, Immutable, and TrafficSplitting. The following values are supported: AllAtOnce – Disables rolling deployments and always deploys to all instances simultaneously. Rolling – Enables standard rolling deployments. RollingWithAdditionalBatch – Launches an extra batch of instances, before starting the deployment, to maintain full capacity. Immutable – Performs an immutable update for every deployment. TrafficSplitting – Performs traffic-splitting deployments to canary-test your application deployments. "In-place" is a generic CodeDeploy term, not an EB option.

- **D. Immutable** — Launches a full set of new instances in a separate Auto Scaling group (no downtime), but it does **not** split traffic by percentage for an evaluation period. Once the new instances pass health checks, traffic shifts entirely; there is no canary phase. Immutable deployments perform an immutable update to launch a full set of new instances running the new version of the application in a separate Auto Scaling group, alongside the instances running the old version. Immutable deployments can prevent issues caused by partially completed rolling deployments. If the new instances don't pass health checks, Elastic Beanstalk terminates them, leaving the original instances untouched.

## Reference
- [Deployment policies and settings – AWS Elastic Beanstalk](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.rolling-version-deploy.html)
- [Release: Elastic Beanstalk support for traffic-splitting deployments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/relnotes/release-2020-05-18-ts-deploy.html)

zh.question: 一家公司在 AWS Elastic Beanstalk 上运行一个新应用程序。该公司需要部署应用程序更新。更新不得导致应用程序用户中断。在评估期内，部署必须将指定比例的传入客户端流量转发到新版本的应用程序。哪种部署类型能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 滚动
options.B: 交通分流
options.C: 就地
options.D: 不变的

zh.explanation:
# Elastic Beanstalk 流量分割部署

## 场景
公司需要在 AWS Elastic Beanstalk 上实现一个部署策略，具有以下特点：
1. 对用户**无停机时间**。
2. 将**指定百分比的传入客户端流量**路由到新应用程序版本。
3. 具有**评估期**，以在完全推出前评估新版本。

这描述了一个**金丝雀部署**模式。

## 正确答案：B – Traffic Splitting（流量分割）

Elastic Beanstalk 的 **Traffic Splitting** 部署策略是为金丝雀测试而专门设计的。流量分割部署允许您在应用程序部署中执行金丝雀测试。在流量分割部署中，Elastic Beanstalk 启动一整组新实例，就像在不可变部署期间一样。然后，它在指定的评估期间内将指定百分比的传入客户端流量转发到新应用程序版本。如果新实例保持健康，Elastic Beanstalk 会将所有流量转发到它们，并终止旧实例。

由于新版本运行在一个**独立的临时 Auto Scaling 组**中，与旧版本并行运行，因此不会导致停机 — 旧队列继续提供流量，直到切换完成。在流量分割部署期间，Elastic Beanstalk 在单独的临时 Auto Scaling 组中创建一组新实例。

通过 `.ebextensions` 的示例配置：

```yaml
option_settings:
  aws:elasticbeanstalk:command:
    DeploymentPolicy: TrafficSplitting
    Timeout: 600
  aws:elasticbeanstalk:trafficsplitting:
    NewVersionPercent: 10
    EvaluationTime: 10
```

## 其他选项为什么错误

- **A. Rolling（滚动）** — 在现有队列上**以批次**更新实例。它不会按百分比将流量分割到新版本进行评估；相反，整个实例批次被替换并为其份额提供 100% 的流量。部署期间容量会减少，且没有金丝雀/评估阶段。使用滚动应用程序部署将新应用程序版本部署到 Amazon EC2 实例（在 Elastic Beanstalk 环境中分批）。

- **C. In-place（原地）** — 不是命名的 Elastic Beanstalk 部署策略。实际的 EB 策略有 AllAtOnce、Rolling、RollingWithAdditionalBatch、Immutable 和 TrafficSplitting。支持以下值：AllAtOnce – 禁用滚动部署，始终同时部署到所有实例。Rolling – 启用标准滚动部署。RollingWithAdditionalBatch – 在开始部署前启动一个额外的实例批次，以保持全容量。Immutable – 对每个部署执行不可变更新。TrafficSplitting – 执行流量分割部署以金丝雀测试您的应用程序部署。"In-place"是一个通用的 CodeDeploy 术语，不是 EB 选项。

- **D. Immutable（不可变）** — 在一个独立的 Auto Scaling 组中启动一整组新实例（无停机时间），但它**不会**按百分比分割流量进行评估期。一旦新实例通过健康检查，流量完全切换；没有金丝雀阶段。不可变部署执行不可变更新，以启动运行新应用程序版本的一整组新实例，这些实例在一个独立的 Auto Scaling 组中，与运行旧版本的实例并行。不可变部署可以防止因部分完成的滚动部署而造成的问题。如果新实例未通过健康检查，Elastic Beanstalk 会终止它们，使原始实例保持不变。

## 参考资源
- [Deployment policies and settings – AWS Elastic Beanstalk](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.rolling-version-deploy.html)
- [Release: Elastic Beanstalk support for traffic-splitting deployments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/relnotes/release-2020-05-18-ts-deploy.html)

en.question: A developer is making changes to a custom application that uses AWS Elastic Beanstalk. Which solutions will update the Elastic Beanstalk environment with the new application version after the developer completes the changes? (Choose two.)

options.A: Package the application code into a zip file. Use the AWS Management Console to upload the .zip file and deploy the packaged application.
options.B: Package the application code into a .tar file. Use the AWS Management Console to create a new application version from the .tar file. Update the environment by using the AWS CLI.
options.C: Package the application code into a .tar file. Use the AWS Management Console to upload the .tar file and deploy the packaged application.
options.D: Package the application code into a .zip file. Use the AWS CLI to create a new application version from the .zip file and to update the environment.
options.E: Package the application code into a .zip file. Use the AWS Management Console to create a new application version from the .zip file. Rebuild the environment by using the AWS CLI.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A developer made changes to a custom application that runs on AWS Elastic Beanstalk and needs to deploy the new version to the existing Elastic Beanstalk environment. The question asks which two methods will successfully update the environment.

## Key Elastic Beanstalk Requirements

An Elastic Beanstalk **source bundle must be a single ZIP file or WAR file** (you can include multiple WAR files inside a ZIP). A source bundle must consist of a single ZIP file or WAR file (you can include multiple WAR files inside your ZIP file). The source bundle's file size limit is 500 MB. The source bundle's file size limit is 500 MB.

`.tar` files are **not supported** as Elastic Beanstalk source bundles, which immediately disqualifies options B and C.

There are multiple supported deployment paths:
- **Console**: Upload the .zip via the Elastic Beanstalk console (Upload and Deploy).
- **AWS CLI**: Use `aws elasticbeanstalk create-application-version` (pointing to a source bundle in S3) followed by `aws elasticbeanstalk update-environment` to deploy that version. Creating an environment with the AWS CLI requires commands such as aws elasticbeanstalk create-application-version with --source-bundle S3Bucket=...,S3Key=...zip.
- **EB CLI**: `eb deploy`.

## Correct Answers: A and D

**A. Package the application code into a .zip file. Use the AWS Management Console to upload the .zip file and deploy the packaged application.** ✅
This is the standard "Upload and deploy" workflow in the Elastic Beanstalk console. The .zip is a valid source bundle format and the console deploys it directly to the environment.

**D. Package the application code into a .zip file. Use the AWS CLI to create a new application version from the .zip file and to update the environment.** ✅
This matches the documented two-step CLI flow: `aws elasticbeanstalk create-application-version` (referencing the zip uploaded to S3), then `aws elasticbeanstalk update-environment --version-label …` to deploy that version onto the running environment.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

**B. .tar file + console + AWS CLI update.** ❌
Elastic Beanstalk source bundles must be ZIP or WAR files. A `.tar` file is not an accepted source bundle format, so creating an application version from a .tar will fail.

**C. .tar file + console upload and deploy.** ❌
Same reason as B — `.tar` is not a supported Elastic Beanstalk source bundle format. Only ZIP/WAR are accepted.

**E. .zip + console creates a new application version + AWS CLI rebuild environment.** ❌
The "rebuild environment" action (`aws elasticbeanstalk rebuild-environment`) terminates and recreates the environment's resources running the **currently deployed** version — it does not switch to a new application version. To deploy a newly created application version you must call `update-environment` (specifying the new `--version-label`), not `rebuild-environment`. So this sequence will not update the environment to the new version.

## References
- [Create an Elastic Beanstalk application source bundle](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/applications-sourcebundle.html)
- [Managing application versions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/applications-versions.html)
- [Setting up the EB CLI / AWS CLI examples](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/eb-cli3.html)
- [aws elasticbeanstalk create-application-version](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/elasticbeanstalk/create-application-version.html)
