The requirement is to publish events to the event bus **only when** `status = "ready"`.

> **Note on the originally-listed answer (A):** The previously published answer key marked option **A** (add a pipe filter step matching `status = ready`) as correct. This is technically wrong on the facts of this question because of the fixed execution order of pipe stages — see below.

## Pipe Stage Order Is the Key

EventBridge Pipes execute stages in a strict, documented order:

**Source → Filter → Enrichment → Target (with optional input transformer)**

The [Amazon EventBridge Pipes overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-pipes.html) and the [Pipes concepts page](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/pipes-concepts.html) both describe filtering as occurring on the **source** event, before any enrichment enhances the payload. The [knowledge center article on Pipes filtering](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/eventbridge-filter-events-with-pipes) confirms that filter patterns are matched against the original source message body.

Because the question explicitly states the Lambda *retrieves the stream status from a database and adds it to each source event*, the `status` field does **not** exist on the SQS message at the time the filter stage runs. A filter pattern matching `status = "ready"` would therefore not match any events.

## Why B Is Correct

The [Event enrichment in Amazon EventBridge Pipes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/pipes-enrichment.html) documentation explicitly documents using enrichment as a filter:

> "You can also use your enrichment as a filter and pass fewer events than were received from the source. If you don't want to invoke the target, return an empty response, such as `""`, `{}`, or `[]`."

The Lambda is the only component with knowledge of the stream status (it just queried the database). Updating it to return only events whose status is `ready` — and returning an empty response otherwise — is the documented, idiomatic pattern. Non-ready events never reach the target event bus, satisfying the requirement.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A. Add a pipe filter step matching `status = ready`** — Incorrect because the pipe filter runs **before** the enrichment Lambda. The SQS source event has no `status` field at filter time (Lambda is what adds it), so the filter pattern would match nothing and drop all events. This is why the originally-stated answer is wrong. See the [EventBridge Pipes tutorial](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/pipes-tutorial-create-dynamodb-sqs.html), which states: "The pipe only sends events that match the event pattern on to enrichment or the target."

- **C. Filter on EventBridge rules subscribed to the bus** — This filters at the wrong place. Events would already be **published to the event bus** before any rule evaluates them, violating the explicit requirement that only ready events be published to the bus. It also wastes bus PutEvents capacity on non-ready events.

- **D. Add an input transformer to the pipe output** — Per the [Pipes input transformation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-pipes-input-transformation.html) documentation, input transformers reshape the payload sent to the target; they have **no filtering capability** and cannot drop events.

## Reference Flow

```
SQS (source — no status field yet)
        ↓
[Filter step]          ← can only see source fields; cannot match status
        ↓
[Enrichment: Lambda]   ← looks up status; returns [] if not "ready"  ✅
        ↓
EventBridge event bus  ← only invoked when Lambda returns a non-empty result
```

## Answer

**B. Update the Lambda function to return only video streams that have a status of ready.**

zh.question: 一家视频流媒体公司在 Amazon EventBridge Pipes 中有一个管道，该管道使用 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列作为事件源。该管道将所有源事件发布到目标 EventBridge 事件总线。在发布事件之前，该管道使用 AWS Lambda 函数从数据库中检索每个事件的流状态，并将该流状态添加到每个源事件中。该公司希望管道仅在视频流状态为“就绪”时才将事件发布到事件总线。哪种解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 向管道添加一个过滤器步骤，该步骤将与流状态为“就绪”进行匹配。
options.B: 更新 Lambda 函数，使其仅返回状态为 ready 的视频流。
options.C: 在所有订阅事件总线的 EventBridge 规则中添加一个“就绪”状态的过滤器。
options.D: 向管道输出添加一个输入转换器，用于过滤状态为“就绪”的流。

zh.explanation:
# EventBridge Pipes：对富化派生数据进行过滤

## 场景概述

EventBridge Pipe 配置为：

- **源**：Amazon SQS 队列
- **富化**：AWS Lambda 函数在数据库中查找流状态并**将**该状态添加到每个源事件
- **目标**：EventBridge 事件总线

要求是仅当 `status = "ready"` 时才将事件发布到事件总线。

> **注意原始答案选项（A）**：先前发布的答案密钥将选项 **A**（添加匹配 `status = ready` 的管道过滤步骤）标记为正确。由于管道阶段的固定执行顺序，这在此问题的事实上在技术上是错误的——请参阅下文。

## 管道阶段顺序是关键

EventBridge Pipes 按严格的文档顺序执行阶段：

**源 → 过滤 → 富化 → 目标（带可选输入转换器）**

[Amazon EventBridge Pipes 概述](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-pipes.html)和[Pipes 概念页面](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/pipes-concepts.html)都描述过滤作用于**源**事件，在任何富化增强负载之前。[关于 Pipes 过滤的知识中心文章](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/eventbridge-filter-events-with-pipes)确认过滤模式与原始源消息体匹配。

由于问题明确说明 Lambda *从数据库检索流状态并将其添加到每个源事件*，`status` 字段在过滤阶段运行时**不存在**于 SQS 消息上。匹配 `status = "ready"` 的过滤模式因此不会匹配任何事件。

## 为什么 B 是正确的

[Amazon EventBridge Pipes 中的事件富化](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/pipes-enrichment.html)文档明确文档记录了将富化用作过滤器：

> "您还可以使用富化作为过滤器，传递比从源接收的事件更少的事件。如果不想调用目标，请返回空响应，例如 `""`、`{}` 或 `[]`。"

Lambda 是唯一具有流状态知识的组件（它刚刚查询了数据库）。将其更新为仅返回状态为 `ready` 的事件——否则返回空响应——是文档中的、习惯用法的模式。非就绪事件永远不会到达目标事件总线，满足要求。

## 其他选项为什么是错误的

- **A. 添加匹配 `status = ready` 的管道过滤步骤** —— 错误，因为管道过滤运行**在**富化 Lambda **之前**。SQS 源事件在过滤时没有 `status` 字段（Lambda 是添加它的），所以过滤模式将不匹配任何内容并删除所有事件。这就是为什么原始说明的答案是错误的。参阅[EventBridge Pipes 教程](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/pipes-tutorial-create-dynamodb-sqs.html)，其中说："管道仅将匹配事件模式的事件发送到富化或目标。"

- **C. 对订阅到总线的 EventBridge 规则进行过滤** —— 这在错误的地方进行过滤。事件将在任何规则评估它们之前**已发布到事件总线**，违反了仅有就绪事件发布到总线的明确要求。它还在非就绪事件上浪费了总线 PutEvents 容量。

- **D. 向管道输出添加输入转换器** —— 根据[Pipes 输入转换](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-pipes-input-transformation.html)文档，输入转换器重塑发送到目标的负载；它们**没有过滤能力**且无法删除事件。

## 参考流程

```
SQS（源——还没有状态字段）
        ↓
[过滤步骤]          ← 只能看到源字段；无法匹配状态
        ↓
[富化：Lambda]   ← 查找状态；如果不是"ready"则返回 []  ✅
        ↓
EventBridge 事件总线  ← 仅在 Lambda 返回非空结果时调用
```

## 答案

**B. 更新 Lambda 函数以仅返回状态为 ready 的视频流。**

en.question: A developer needs to build a workflow to handle messages that are sent to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. When a message reaches the queue, the workflow must implement a delay before invoking an AWS Lambda function to process the message. Which solution will meet this requirement in the MOST operationally efficient way?

options.A: Create an AWS Step Functions state machine to process the SQS queue. Use a Wait state to delay the Lambda function’s processing for the required number of seconds after message delivery to the SQS queue. Use Amazon EventBridge to invoke the state machine every 5 minutes.
options.B: Configure the Lambda function to poll the SQS queue. Update the Lambda code to republish each message with a custom attribute that contains a future time when the message should be fully processed. Update the Lambda code to fully process messages when the custom attribute’s future time has passed.
options.C: Set the DelaySeconds value of the SQS queue to be the number of seconds required to delay delivery of the messages. Add an event source mapping for the Lambda function. Specify the SQS queue as a source.
options.D: Set the Visibility Timeout value of the SQS queue to be the number of seconds required to delay delivery of the messages. Add an event source mapping for the Lambda function. Specify the SQS queue as a source.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A developer needs messages placed on an SQS queue to be processed by a Lambda function only **after a delay**. The goal is the **most operationally efficient** solution (i.e., minimal custom code, minimal infrastructure).

## Correct answer: C

Amazon SQS has a built-in queue attribute called **DelaySeconds** (Delivery Delay) that postpones the visibility of newly enqueued messages for up to 15 minutes. Combined with a Lambda **event source mapping**, this is a fully managed, code-free way to delay processing.

- [Amazon SQS message timers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-message-timers.html) — sets a delivery delay (0–15 min) at the queue or message level.
- [Using Lambda with Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html) — Lambda polls the queue via an event source mapping and invokes the function only when messages become visible.

Because Lambda's event source mapping uses long polling on the queue, it will not see (and therefore not invoke the function with) a message until the DelaySeconds period has elapsed and the message becomes visible. This requires zero custom code.

## Why the other options are wrong

**A. Step Functions with a Wait state, triggered by EventBridge every 5 minutes** — This adds two extra services (Step Functions + EventBridge), introduces scheduling drift (up to 5 minutes), couples processing to a polling cron, and requires the state machine to read SQS itself (not a native integration that pulls from SQS as an event source). Far more operational overhead than simply setting DelaySeconds.

**B. Lambda re-publishes each message with a future-time attribute** — This requires custom code to inspect timestamps and either re-queue messages or sleep, which wastes Lambda execution time/cost (Lambda is billed by duration). It is fragile and clearly not "operationally efficient" compared to a single queue setting.

**D. Visibility Timeout** — Visibility Timeout controls how long an **already-received** message is hidden from other consumers while being processed; it does **not** delay the *initial* delivery of new messages. Setting it would not delay first-time invocation of Lambda. The correct attribute for delaying delivery is **DelaySeconds** (Delivery Delay), not Visibility Timeout.

## Key configuration

```bash
aws sqs create-queue \
  --queue-name delayed-queue \
  --attributes '{"DelaySeconds":"300"}'

aws lambda create-event-source-mapping \
  --function-name MyProcessor \
  --event-source-arn arn:aws:sqs:us-east-1:123456789012:delayed-queue \
  --batch-size 10
```

References:
- [Amazon SQS Delay Queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-delay-queues.html)
- [Amazon SQS Visibility Timeout](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-visibility-timeout.html)
- [Lambda SQS event source mapping](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html)

zh.question: 开发人员需要构建一个工作流来处理发送到 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列的消息。当消息到达队列时，工作流必须在调用 AWS Lambda 函数处理消息之前执行延迟。哪种解决方案能够以最高效的方式满足此要求？

options.A: 创建一个 AWS Step Functions 状态机来处理 SQS 队列。使用 Wait 状态，在消息传递到 SQS 队列后，延迟 Lambda 函数的处理时间（以秒为单位）。使用 Amazon EventBridge 每 5 分钟调用一次该状态机。
options.B: 配置 Lambda 函数轮询 SQS 队列。更新 Lambda 代码，使其重新发布每条消息，并添加一个自定义属性，该属性包含消息应完全处理的未来时间。更新 Lambda 代码，使其在自定义属性指定的未来时间过后完全处理消息。
options.C: 将 SQS 队列的 DelaySeconds 值设置为消息延迟传递所需的秒数。为 Lambda 函数添加事件源映射。指定 SQS 队列作为事件源。
options.D: 将 SQS 队列的可见性超时值设置为延迟消息传递所需的秒数。为 Lambda 函数添加事件源映射。指定 SQS 队列作为事件源。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

开发人员需要将放在 SQS 队列中的消息**延迟后**由 Lambda 函数处理。目标是实现**操作效率最高**的解决方案（即最少自定义代码、最少基础设施）。

## 正确答案：C

Amazon SQS 有一个名为 **DelaySeconds**（传输延迟）的内置队列属性，可将新加入队列的消息的可见性延迟长达 15 分钟。结合 Lambda **事件源映射**，这是一种完全托管的、无需代码的延迟处理方式。

- [Amazon SQS 消息计时器](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-message-timers.html) — 在队列或消息级别设置传输延迟（0-15 分钟）。
- [将 Lambda 与 Amazon SQS 结合使用](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html) — Lambda 通过事件源映射轮询队列，仅当消息变为可见时才调用函数。

由于 Lambda 的事件源映射对队列使用长轮询，在 DelaySeconds 期间结束且消息变为可见之前，它不会看到（因此也不会用该消息调用函数）消息。这不需要任何自定义代码。

## 其他选项为何错误

**A. Step Functions 配合 Wait 状态，由 EventBridge 每 5 分钟触发一次** — 这增加了两个额外的服务（Step Functions + EventBridge），引入了调度漂移（最多 5 分钟），将处理耦合到轮询 cron，并要求状态机自行读取 SQS（不是从 SQS 作为事件源拉取的原生集成）。相比简单设置 DelaySeconds，操作开销要大得多。

**B. Lambda 使用未来时间属性重新发布每条消息** — 这需要自定义代码来检查时间戳，然后重新加入队列或休眠，这浪费了 Lambda 执行时间/成本（Lambda 按持续时间计费）。相比单一队列设置，这很脆弱且显然不"操作高效"。

**D. 可见性超时** — 可见性超时控制**已接收的**消息在被处理时对其他消费者隐藏的时长；它**不会**延迟新消息的*初始*传输。设置它无法延迟 Lambda 的首次调用。延迟传输的正确属性是 **DelaySeconds**（传输延迟），而非可见性超时。

## 关键配置

```bash
aws sqs create-queue \
  --queue-name delayed-queue \
  --attributes '{"DelaySeconds":"300"}'

aws lambda create-event-source-mapping \
  --function-name MyProcessor \
  --event-source-arn arn:aws:sqs:us-east-1:123456789012:delayed-queue \
  --batch-size 10
```

参考资源：
- [Amazon SQS 延迟队列](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-delay-queues.html)
- [Amazon SQS 可见性超时](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-visibility-timeout.html)
- [Lambda SQS 事件源映射](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html)

en.question: A company is building an application to accept data from customers. The data must be encrypted at rest and in transit. The application uses an Amazon API Gateway API that resolves to AWS Lambda functions. The Lambda functions store the data in an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster. The application worked properly during testing. A developer configured an Amazon CloudFront distribution with field-level encryption that uses an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. After the configuration of the distribution, the application behaved unexpectedly. All the data in the database changed from plaintext to ciphertext. The developer must ensure that the data is not stored in the database as the ciphertext from the CloudFront field-level encryption. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.A: Change the CloudFront Viewer protocol policy from “HTTP and HTTPS” to “HTTPS only.”
options.B: Add a Lambda function that uses the KMS key to decrypt the data fields before saving the data to the database.
options.C: Enable encryption on the DB cluster by using the same KMS key that is used in CloudFront.
options.D: Request and deploy a new SSL certificate to use with the CloudFront distribution.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

The application accepts customer data through API Gateway → Lambda → Aurora MySQL. After enabling **CloudFront field-level encryption (FLE)** with a KMS key, the sensitive form fields arrive at the origin already encrypted as ciphertext, and the Lambda function is writing that ciphertext directly into Aurora. The developer wants the data stored in plaintext in the database (still encrypted at rest by Aurora), not as the FLE ciphertext.

## Correct Answer: B

**Add a Lambda function (or logic in the existing Lambda) that uses the KMS key to decrypt the field-level encrypted data before saving it to the database.**

CloudFront field-level encryption is designed precisely so that sensitive fields are [encrypted at the edge with a public key and remain encrypted as they travel through the application stack](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/field-level-encryption.html). Per AWS documentation, [the sensitive information is encrypted at the edge and remains encrypted throughout the entire application stack, and only applications with credentials to decrypt the data can do so](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/field-level-encryption.html). CloudFront uses asymmetric (RSA) encryption — the public key encrypts at the edge, and only the private key (held by your origin/decryption component) can decrypt.

So the only way to get plaintext into Aurora is to have a component at or before the database write step decrypt the FLE ciphertext using the private key/KMS. A Lambda function with permission to use the KMS key (and the AWS Encryption SDK, which CloudFront FLE uses for the cipher format) is the standard pattern.

```python
# Pseudocode in the Lambda before INSERT
import aws_encryption_sdk, base64
ciphertext = base64.b64decode(event['encrypted_field'])
plaintext, _ = client.decrypt(source=ciphertext, key_provider=kms_key_provider)
cursor.execute("INSERT INTO customers (ssn) VALUES (%s)", (plaintext,))
```

## Why the other options are wrong

- **A. Change Viewer Protocol Policy from "HTTP and HTTPS" to "HTTPS only."** This only enforces TLS in transit between the viewer and CloudFront. It has no effect on FLE behavior — fields would still be encrypted at the edge and still arrive as ciphertext at the origin. It addresses encryption-in-transit, not the storage-of-ciphertext problem.

- **C. Enable encryption on the DB cluster using the same KMS key as CloudFront.** Aurora storage encryption uses a symmetric KMS key for transparent encryption at rest. CloudFront FLE uses asymmetric RSA keys via the AWS Encryption SDK. Even if you "enabled encryption" on the cluster, the column values written by Lambda would still be the FLE ciphertext stored on disk — Aurora encryption-at-rest does not decrypt application payloads.

- **D. Request and deploy a new SSL certificate for the CloudFront distribution.** A new TLS certificate addresses transport security between viewer and CloudFront. It does not change how FLE encrypts fields nor cause the origin to receive plaintext.

## References

- [Use field-level encryption to help protect sensitive data – Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/field-level-encryption.html)
- [How to Enhance the Security of Sensitive Customer Data by Using Amazon CloudFront Field-Level Encryption – AWS Security Blog](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/how-to-enhance-the-security-of-sensitive-customer-data-by-using-amazon-cloudfront-field-level-encryption/)
- [How to protect sensitive data for its entire lifecycle in AWS – AWS Security Blog](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/how-to-protect-sensitive-data-for-its-entire-lifecycle-in-aws/)

zh.question: 一家公司正在开发一个用于接收客户数据的应用程序。数据在静态存储和传输过程中都必须加密。该应用程序使用 Amazon API Gateway API，该 API 会解析为 AWS Lambda 函数。Lambda 函数将数据存储在 Amazon Aurora MySQL 数据库集群中。该应用程序在测试期间运行正常。开发人员配置了一个使用 AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) 密钥的字段级加密的 Amazon CloudFront 分发。配置分发后，应用程序的行为异常。数据库中的所有数据都从明文变成了密文。开发人员必须确保数据不会以 CloudFront 字段级加密后的密文形式存储在数据库中。哪种解决方案能够满足此要求？

options.A: 将 CloudFront Viewer 协议策略从“HTTP 和 HTTPS”更改为“仅 HTTPS”。
options.B: 添加一个 Lambda 函数，该函数使用 KMS 密钥解密数据字段，然后再将数据保存到数据库。
options.C: 使用与 CloudFront 相同的 KMS 密钥在数据库集群上启用加密。
options.D: 请求并部署新的 SSL 证书以与 CloudFront 分发一起使用。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

应用程序通过 API Gateway → Lambda → Aurora MySQL 接受客户数据。启用 **CloudFront 字段级加密 (FLE)** 与 KMS 密钥后，敏感表单字段以密文形式到达源站，Lambda 函数将该密文直接写入 Aurora。开发人员希望数据以明文形式存储在数据库中（仍由 Aurora 进行静态加密），而不是 FLE 密文。

## 正确答案：B

**添加一个 Lambda 函数（或在现有 Lambda 中添加逻辑），使用 KMS 密钥在保存到数据库前解密字段级加密的数据。**

CloudFront 字段级加密的设计目的是让敏感字段[在边缘用公钥加密，并在应用程序堆栈中保持加密状态](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/field-level-encryption.html)。根据 AWS 文档，[敏感信息在边缘加密，并在整个应用程序堆栈中保持加密状态，只有拥有解密凭证的应用程序才能解密](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/field-level-encryption.html)。CloudFront 使用非对称 (RSA) 加密 — 公钥在边缘加密，只有私钥（由源站/解密组件保持）才能解密。

因此，将明文写入 Aurora 的唯一方法是在数据库写入步骤之前或之处使用私钥/KMS 解密 FLE 密文的组件。具有 KMS 密钥使用权限的 Lambda 函数（以及使用 CloudFront FLE 的 AWS Encryption SDK）是标准做法。

```python
# Lambda 中 INSERT 前的伪代码
import aws_encryption_sdk, base64
ciphertext = base64.b64decode(event['encrypted_field'])
plaintext, _ = client.decrypt(source=ciphertext, key_provider=kms_key_provider)
cursor.execute("INSERT INTO customers (ssn) VALUES (%s)", (plaintext,))
```

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

- **A. 将查看器协议策略从"HTTP 和 HTTPS"更改为"仅 HTTPS"。** 这只在查看器和 CloudFront 之间强制执行 TLS。它对 FLE 行为没有影响 — 字段仍会在边缘加密，仍会以密文形式到达源站。它解决的是传输中的加密，而不是密文存储问题。

- **C. 使用与 CloudFront 相同的 KMS 密钥在 DB 集群上启用加密。** Aurora 存储加密使用对称 KMS 密钥进行透明的静态加密。CloudFront FLE 通过 AWS Encryption SDK 使用非对称 RSA 密钥。即使您在集群上"启用加密"，Lambda 写入的列值仍然是存储在磁盘上的 FLE 密文 — Aurora 静态加密不会解密应用程序负载。

- **D. 请求并为 CloudFront 分布部署新的 SSL 证书。** 新的 TLS 证书处理查看器和 CloudFront 之间的传输安全。它不会改变 FLE 如何加密字段，也不会导致源站接收明文。

## 参考资源

- [使用字段级加密帮助保护敏感数据 – Amazon CloudFront 开发人员指南](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/field-level-encryption.html)
- [如何使用 Amazon CloudFront 字段级加密增强敏感客户数据的安全性 – AWS 安全博客](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/how-to-enhance-the-security-of-sensitive-customer-data-by-using-amazon-cloudfront-field-level-encryption/)
- [如何在 AWS 中保护敏感数据的完整生命周期 – AWS 安全博客](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/how-to-protect-sensitive-data-for-its-entire-lifecycle-in-aws/)

en.question: A company offers a business-to-business software service that runs on dedicated infrastructure deployed in each customer’s AWS account. Before a feature release, the company needs to run integration tests on real AWS test infrastructure. The test infrastructure consists of Amazon EC2 instances and an Amazon RDS database. A developer must set up a continuous delivery process that will provision the test infrastructure across the different AWS accounts. The developer then must run the integration tests. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative effort?

options.A: Use AWS CodeDeploy with AWS CloudFormation StackSets to deploy the infrastructure. Use Amazon CodeGuru to run the tests.
options.B: Use AWS CodePipeline with AWS CloudFormation StackSets to deploy the infrastructure. Use AWS CodeBuild to run the tests.
options.C: Use AWS CodePipeline with AWS CloudFormation change sets to deploy the infrastructure. Use a CloudFormation custom resource to run the tests.
options.D: Use AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM) templates with AWS CloudFormation change sets to deploy the infrastructure. Use AWS CodeDeploy to run the tests.

en.explanation:
## Scenario
A B2B SaaS company deploys dedicated infrastructure (EC2 + RDS) in each customer's AWS account. Before releasing features, they need integration tests on real AWS infrastructure spanning multiple accounts. The developer needs a CD process that:
1. Provisions test infrastructure across multiple AWS accounts
2. Runs integration tests
3. Requires the **least administrative effort**

## Correct Answer: B
**Use AWS CodePipeline with AWS CloudFormation StackSets to deploy the infrastructure. Use AWS CodeBuild to run the tests.**

### Why B is correct
- **CloudFormation StackSets** is purpose-built for multi-account, multi-region deployments. AWS CloudFormation StackSets allows you to create, update, or delete CloudFormation stacks across multiple AWS accounts and regions with a single operation. It's essentially a way to manage infrastructure at scale across your AWS organization.
- **CodePipeline natively integrates with StackSets** via a built-in deploy action. CodePipeline offers the ability to perform CloudFormation StackSets operations as part of your CI/CD process. You use a stack set to create stacks in AWS accounts across AWS Regions by using a single CloudFormation template. All the resources included in each stack are defined by the stack set's CloudFormation template.
- **CodeBuild** is the natural fit to execute integration test scripts in a managed build environment as a CI/CD pipeline stage — no servers to manage.
- With service-managed permissions, this can be fully automated: SERVICE_MANAGED: CloudFormation StackSets automatically creates the IAM roles required to deploy to accounts managed by AWS Organizations. This requires an account to be a member of an Organization.

This combination gives a fully managed, low-maintenance CI/CD path: source → CodeBuild (tests) → CloudFormation StackSets (multi-account deploy).

## Why the other options are wrong

### A. CodeDeploy + StackSets + CodeGuru
- **CodeDeploy** doesn't deploy infrastructure — it deploys application code revisions to compute (EC2/Lambda/ECS). It cannot launch StackSets or provision EC2/RDS infrastructure.
- **Amazon CodeGuru** is a code review and application performance profiler (powered by ML). It is **not** a test runner for integration tests. It analyzes code for quality/performance issues, not executing test suites.

### C. CodePipeline + CloudFormation **change sets** + custom resource
- **Change sets** operate on a single stack in a single account — they do not natively deploy across multiple AWS accounts the way StackSets do. You would need to wire up custom cross-account roles per target, increasing administrative effort.
- Using a **CloudFormation custom resource** to run integration tests is an anti-pattern. Custom resources are intended for provisioning logic, are bound to stack lifecycle events, have a 1-hour timeout, and are difficult to debug — much higher administrative effort than CodeBuild.

### D. SAM + change sets + CodeDeploy for tests
- **AWS SAM** is for serverless applications (Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB). The workload here is **EC2 + RDS**, which isn't SAM's target.
- **Change sets** again don't natively span multiple accounts.
- **CodeDeploy does not run integration tests** — it deploys application revisions and supports lifecycle hooks, but it is not a test execution service.

## Key takeaway
For multi-account infrastructure provisioning in a CD pipeline + integration tests, the canonical, lowest-effort AWS pattern is **CodePipeline → CodeBuild (tests) → CloudFormation StackSets (multi-account deploy)**.

## References
- [CloudFormation StackSets deploy action - CodePipeline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/action-reference-StackSets.html)
- [Tutorial: Pipeline with StackSets deployment actions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/tutorials-stackset-deployment.html)
- [Building a CI/CD pipeline to update CloudFormation StackSets (AWS Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/devops/building-a-ci-cd-pipeline-to-update-an-aws-cloudformation-stacksets/)
- [Streamlining Multi-Account Infrastructure with StackSets (AWS Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/devops/streamlining-multi-account-infrastructure-with-aws-cloudformation-stacksets-and-aws-cdk/)

zh.question: 一家公司提供企业对企业 (B2B) 软件服务，该服务运行在部署于每个客户 AWS 账户中的专用基础设施上。在发布新功能之前，该公司需要在真实的 AWS 测试基础设施上运行集成测试。该测试基础设施由 Amazon EC2 实例和 Amazon RDS 数据库组成。开发人员必须设置一个持续交付流程，以便在不同的 AWS 账户中配置测试基础设施。然后，开发人员必须运行集成测试。哪种解决方案能够以最少的管理工作量满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 AWS CodeDeploy 和 AWS CloudFormation StackSets 部署基础设施。使用 Amazon CodeGuru 运行测试。
options.B: 使用 AWS CodePipeline 和 AWS CloudFormation StackSets 部署基础设施。使用 AWS CodeBuild 运行测试。
options.C: 使用 AWS CodePipeline 和 AWS CloudFormation 变更集部署基础设施。使用 CloudFormation 自定义资源运行测试。
options.D: 使用 AWS 无服务器应用程序模型 (AWS SAM) 模板和 AWS CloudFormation 变更集部署基础设施。使用 AWS CodeDeploy 运行测试。

zh.explanation:
## 场景
一家B2B SaaS公司在每个客户的AWS账户中部署专用基础设施（EC2 + RDS）。在发布功能前，他们需要在跨越多个账户的真实AWS基础设施上进行集成测试。开发人员需要一个CD流程，能够：
1. 在多个AWS账户间配置测试基础设施
2. 运行集成测试
3. 需要**最少的管理工作量**

## 正确答案：B
**使用AWS CodePipeline与AWS CloudFormation StackSets部署基础设施。使用AWS CodeBuild运行测试。**

### 为什么B正确
- **CloudFormation StackSets** 专为跨多个账户和地区的部署而设计。AWS CloudFormation StackSets 允许您通过单一操作在多个AWS账户和地区内创建、更新或删除CloudFormation栈。它本质上是一种在AWS组织规模内管理基础设施的方式。
- **CodePipeline原生集成StackSets**，通过内置部署操作实现。CodePipeline 能够在CI/CD流程中执行CloudFormation StackSets操作。您可以使用栈集通过单一CloudFormation模板在AWS区域间跨AWS账户创建栈。每个栈中包含的所有资源都由栈集的CloudFormation模板定义。
- **CodeBuild** 是在托管构建环境中执行集成测试脚本的自然选择，作为CI/CD流程的一个阶段——无需管理服务器。
- 通过服务管理权限，可以完全自动化：SERVICE_MANAGED：CloudFormation StackSets 自动创建跨AWS组织所管理账户部署所需的IAM角色。这要求账户是组织的成员。

这个组合提供了一条完全托管的、低维护的CI/CD路径：源代码 → CodeBuild（测试）→ CloudFormation StackSets（跨账户部署）。

## 为什么其他选项错误

### A. CodeDeploy + StackSets + CodeGuru
- **CodeDeploy** 不部署基础设施——它部署应用代码版本到计算资源（EC2/Lambda/ECS）。它无法启动StackSets或配置EC2/RDS基础设施。
- **Amazon CodeGuru** 是代码审查和应用性能分析器（由ML驱动）。它**不是**集成测试的测试运行器。它分析代码质量/性能问题，不执行测试套件。

### C. CodePipeline + CloudFormation **变更集** + 自定义资源
- **变更集** 只作用于单个账户内的单个栈——与StackSets的跨多个AWS账户原生部署方式不同。您需要为每个目标账户设置自定义跨账户角色，增加了管理工作量。
- 使用 **CloudFormation自定义资源** 运行集成测试是反模式。自定义资源用于配置逻辑，受栈生命周期事件限制，有1小时超时限制，调试困难——比CodeBuild的管理工作量大得多。

### D. SAM + 变更集 + CodeDeploy运行测试
- **AWS SAM** 用于无服务器应用（Lambda、API Gateway、DynamoDB）。这里的工作负载是 **EC2 + RDS**，不在SAM的目标范围内。
- **变更集** 同样不原生跨越多个账户。
- **CodeDeploy不运行集成测试**——它部署应用版本并支持生命周期钩子，但不是测试执行服务。

## 关键要点
对于CD流程中的跨账户基础设施配置 + 集成测试，规范的、最低工作量的AWS模式是 **CodePipeline → CodeBuild（测试）→ CloudFormation StackSets（跨账户部署）**。

## 参考资源
- [CloudFormation StackSets 部署操作 - CodePipeline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/action-reference-StackSets.html)
- [教程：包含StackSets部署操作的流程](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/tutorials-stackset-deployment.html)
- [构建CI/CD流程更新CloudFormation StackSets (AWS博客)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/devops/building-a-ci-cd-pipeline-to-update-an-aws-cloudformation-stacksets/)
- [使用StackSets简化跨账户基础设施 (AWS博客)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/devops/streamlining-multi-account-infrastructure-with-aws-cloudformation-stacksets-and-aws-cdk/)

en.question: A developer is creating an application that uses an AWS Lambda function to transform and load data from an Amazon S3 bucket. When the developer tests the application, the developer finds that some invocations of the Lambda function are slower than others. The developer needs to update the Lambda function to have predictable invocation durations that run with low latency. Any initialization activities, such as loading libraries and instantiating clients, must run during allocation time rather than during actual function invocations. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Create a schedule group in Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to invoke the Lambda function.
options.B: Configure provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function to have the necessary number of execution environments.
options.C: Use the $LATEST version of the Lambda function.
options.D: Configure reserved concurrency for the Lambda function to have the necessary number of execution environments.
options.E: Deploy changes, and publish a new version of the Lambda function.

en.explanation:
# Lambda Provisioned Concurrency for Predictable Latency

## Scenario
The developer has a Lambda function that transforms and loads S3 data. Some invocations are slower (cold starts). The requirements are:
1. **Predictable invocation durations with low latency**
2. **Initialization activities (loading libraries, instantiating clients) must run during allocation time**, not during actual invocations.

This is the textbook use case for **Provisioned Concurrency**.

## Correct Answers: B and E

### B. Configure provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function
For functions using provisioned concurrency, Lambda runs any initialization code, such as loading libraries and instantiating clients, during allocation time. This directly matches the requirement. Provisioned concurrency is useful for reducing cold start latencies for functions and designed to make functions available with double-digit millisecond response times.

### E. Deploy changes, and publish a new version of the Lambda function
Provisioned concurrency cannot be applied to `$LATEST`. Provisioned concurrency must be applied to a specific version or alias of a function, not the $LATEST version. In cases where you continue to see cold start behavior, ensure that you are invoking the version of alias with provisioned concurrency configured. Therefore, you must publish a new version (or use an alias pointing at a published version) before configuring provisioned concurrency.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

### A. Create a schedule group in EventBridge Scheduler to invoke the Lambda function
EventBridge Scheduler triggers functions on a schedule. It does not pre-initialize execution environments or eliminate cold starts; you would still incur initialization latency on each new environment. It does not satisfy the "initialization during allocation time" requirement.

### C. Use the $LATEST version of the Lambda function
This is explicitly incompatible with provisioned concurrency. Verify that the Lambda function that you use to configure provisioned concurrency isn't set to $LATEST. Unpublished versions of Lambda functions don't support provisioned concurrency.

### D. Configure reserved concurrency
Reserved concurrency only **caps/guarantees** the maximum concurrent executions for a function — it does **not** pre-initialize execution environments. Reserved concurrency limits a function's ability to scale up. Cold starts still occur, so it does not meet the "predictable low latency" or "initialization during allocation time" requirements.

## Summary
Combine **B** (provisioned concurrency keeps environments warm and runs init code during allocation) with **E** (publish a version since provisioned concurrency cannot target `$LATEST`).

## References
- [Configuring provisioned concurrency for a function](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/provisioned-concurrency.html)
- [Troubleshoot Lambda provisioned concurrency issues](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/lambda-provisioned-concurrency)
- [New – Provisioned Concurrency for Lambda Functions (AWS Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/new-provisioned-concurrency-for-lambda-functions/)

zh.question: 一位开发人员正在创建一个应用程序，该应用程序使用 AWS Lambda 函数来转换和加载 Amazon S3 存储桶中的数据。在测试应用程序时，开发人员发现 Lambda 函数的某些调用速度比其他调用慢。开发人员需要更新 Lambda 函数，使其具有可预测的调用持续时间和低延迟。任何初始化活动（例如加载库和实例化客户端）都必须在分配时间期间运行，而不是在实际函数调用期间运行。以下哪些步骤组合可以满足这些要求？（选择两项。）

options.A: 在 Amazon EventBridge Scheduler 中创建一个调度组来调用 Lambda 函数。
options.B: 为 Lambda 函数配置预置并发，使其具有必要的执行环境数量。
options.C: 使用 Lambda 函数的最新版本。
options.D: 为 Lambda 函数配置预留并发，使其具有必要的执行环境数量。
options.E: 部署变更，并发布 Lambda 函数的新版本。

zh.explanation:
# Lambda 预配并发以实现可预测的延迟

## 场景
开发人员有一个转换和加载 S3 数据的 Lambda 函数。某些调用速度较慢（冷启动）。要求是：
1. **可预测的调用持续时间，低延迟**
2. **初始化活动（加载库、实例化客户端）必须在分配时间运行**，而不是在实际调用期间运行。

这是 **Provisioned Concurrency** 的典型用例。

## 正确答案：B 和 E

### B. 为 Lambda 函数配置预配并发
对于使用预配并发的函数，Lambda 在分配时运行任何初始化代码，例如加载库和实例化客户端。这直接满足该要求。预配并发对于减少函数的冷启动延迟非常有用，旨在使函数以两位数毫秒的响应时间可用。

### E. 部署更改并发布 Lambda 函数的新版本
预配并发无法应用于 `$LATEST`。预配并发必须应用于函数的特定版本或别名，而不是 $LATEST 版本。如果您继续看到冷启动行为，请确保您调用的是配置了预配并发的版本或别名。因此，在配置预配并发之前，必须发布新版本（或使用指向已发布版本的别名）。

## 为什么其他选项错误

### A. 在 EventBridge Scheduler 中创建计划组以调用 Lambda 函数
EventBridge Scheduler 按计划触发函数。它不会预初始化执行环境或消除冷启动；您仍然会在每个新环境上产生初始化延迟。它不满足"初始化期间分配时间"的要求。

### C. 使用 Lambda 函数的 $LATEST 版本
这明确与预配并发不兼容。验证用于配置预配并发的 Lambda 函数未设置为 $LATEST。Lambda 函数的未发布版本不支持预配并发。

### D. 配置保留并发
保留并发只**限制/保证**函数的最大并发执行数——它**不**预初始化执行环境。保留并发限制函数的扩展能力。仍然会出现冷启动，因此不满足"可预测的低延迟"或"初始化期间分配时间"的要求。

## 摘要
结合 **B**（预配并发使环境保持温暖并在分配期间运行初始化代码）和 **E**（发布版本，因为预配并发无法针对 `$LATEST`）。

## 参考资源
- [为函数配置预配并发](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/provisioned-concurrency.html)
- [排查 Lambda 预配并发问题](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/lambda-provisioned-concurrency)
- [新增 – Lambda 函数的预配并发（AWS 博客）](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/new-provisioned-concurrency-for-lambda-functions/)

en.question: A developer created an AWS Lambda function named ProcessMessages. The Lambda function is invoked asynchronously when a message is published to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic named InputTopic. The developer uses a second SNS topic named ErrorTopic to handle alerts of failures for other services. The developer wants to receive notifications from the ErrorTopic SNS topic when the ProcessMessages Lambda function fails to process a message. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.A: Configure a subscription for the ErrorTopic SNS topic. Configure a filter policy for failures. Specify the ProcessMessages Lambda function as the endpoint.
options.B: Configure a failure destination for the ProcessMessages Lambda function. Specify the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the ErrorTopic SNS topic as the destination ARN.
options.C: Configure a trigger for the ProcessMessages Lambda function. Specify the ErrorTopic SNS topic as the trigger topic. Configure a filter policy on the topic for failures
options.D: Configure a delivery policy on the ErrorTopic SNS topic. Configure a filter policy for failures. Specify the Lambda function as the input endpoint.

en.explanation:
# Lambda Failure Destination to SNS Topic

## Scenario
The `ProcessMessages` Lambda function is invoked **asynchronously** by SNS topic `InputTopic`. When the function fails to process a message, the developer wants notifications sent to a separate SNS topic (`ErrorTopic`).

## Correct Answer: B

When a Lambda function is invoked asynchronously, you can configure **Lambda Destinations** to route execution results to another AWS service. AWS Lambda Destinations for asynchronous invocations is a feature that provides visibility into Lambda function invocations and routes the execution results to AWS services, simplifying event-driven applications and reducing code complexity.

For each execution status such as Success or Failure you can choose one of four destinations: another Lambda function, SNS, SQS, or EventBridge. The on-failure destination receives events that exhausted retries or exceeded the maximum age, so configuring `ErrorTopic`'s ARN as the **OnFailure** destination ARN of `ProcessMessages` directly meets the requirement. The onFailure destination receives events that exhausted retries or exceeded the maximum age.

Example CloudFormation snippet:
```yaml
Resources:
  EventInvokeConfig:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::EventInvokeConfig
    Properties:
      FunctionName: ProcessMessages
      Qualifier: "$LATEST"
      DestinationConfig:
        OnFailure:
          Destination: arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789012:ErrorTopic
```

The Lambda execution role must have `sns:Publish` permission on `ErrorTopic`. Lambda writes to these destinations automatically; your execution role needs the appropriate permissions (sqs:SendMessage for SQS, sns:Publish for SNS).

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A. Subscribe ErrorTopic with a "failure" filter policy, endpoint = ProcessMessages.** This reverses the flow — it would make `ProcessMessages` a *subscriber* of `ErrorTopic`, not a publisher to it. SNS filter policies only filter messages already published to the topic; they cannot detect Lambda failures. There is no mechanism here that publishes failure events to `ErrorTopic`.

- **C. Configure ErrorTopic as a trigger for ProcessMessages with a filter policy for failures.** This is also reversed — it would invoke `ProcessMessages` whenever a message is published to `ErrorTopic`. Again, nothing publishes failure events to `ErrorTopic`, and SNS filter policies do not understand Lambda failure semantics.

- **D. Configure a delivery policy on ErrorTopic with a filter policy for failures, Lambda as endpoint.** SNS *delivery policies* control retry behavior for HTTP/S subscriptions; they have nothing to do with capturing Lambda failures. Like A and C, this option also flows in the wrong direction (Lambda as subscriber rather than publisher).

Only option B uses the proper AWS Lambda feature — **on-failure destinations** — which is the purpose-built mechanism for this scenario. It is considered best-practice to use failure destinations on all your asynchronous Lambda functions (for data retention and notification purposes).

## References
- [Capturing records of Lambda asynchronous invocations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-async-retain-records.html)
- [Introducing AWS Lambda Destinations (AWS Compute Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/introducing-aws-lambda-destinations/)
- [Invoking Lambda functions with Amazon SNS notifications](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sns.html)

zh.question: 一位开发人员创建了一个名为 ProcessMessages 的 AWS Lambda 函数。当消息发布到名为 InputTopic 的 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题时，该 Lambda 函数会异步调用。开发人员使用另一个名为 ErrorTopic 的 SNS 主题来处理其他服务的故障警报。开发人员希望在 ProcessMessages Lambda 函数处理消息失败时，能够从 ErrorTopic SNS 主题接收通知。哪种解决方案能够满足此要求？

options.A: 配置 ErrorTopic SNS 主题的订阅。配置故障过滤策略。指定 ProcessMessages Lambda 函数作为端点。
options.B: 为 ProcessMessages Lambda 函数配置失败目标。将 ErrorTopic SNS 主题的 Amazon 资源名称 (ARN) 指定为目标 ARN。
options.C: 为 ProcessMessages Lambda 函数配置触发器。指定 ErrorTopic SNS 主题作为触发主题。为该主题配置失败过滤策略。
options.D: 在 ErrorTopic SNS 主题上配置传递策略。配置失败过滤策略。指定 Lambda 函数作为输入端点。

zh.explanation:
# Lambda 失败目标到 SNS 主题

## 场景
`ProcessMessages` Lambda 函数由 SNS 主题 `InputTopic` **异步**调用。当函数无法处理消息时，开发人员希望通知发送到单独的 SNS 主题（`ErrorTopic`）。

## 正确答案：B

当 Lambda 函数被异步调用时，你可以配置 **Lambda Destinations** 将执行结果路由到另一个 AWS 服务。AWS Lambda Destinations for asynchronous invocations 是一项功能，它提供对 Lambda 函数调用的可见性，并将执行结果路由到 AWS 服务，简化了事件驱动应用程序并降低了代码复杂性。

对于每种执行状态（如成功或失败），你可以选择四个目标之一：另一个 Lambda 函数、SNS、SQS 或 EventBridge。失败目标接收耗尽重试或超过最大存活期的事件，因此将 `ErrorTopic` 的 ARN 配置为 `ProcessMessages` 的 **OnFailure** 目标 ARN 直接满足要求。onFailure 目标接收耗尽重试或超过最大存活期的事件。

CloudFormation 代码段示例：
```yaml
Resources:
  EventInvokeConfig:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::EventInvokeConfig
    Properties:
      FunctionName: ProcessMessages
      Qualifier: "$LATEST"
      DestinationConfig:
        OnFailure:
          Destination: arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789012:ErrorTopic
```

Lambda 执行角色必须对 `ErrorTopic` 具有 `sns:Publish` 权限。Lambda 自动写入这些目标；你的执行角色需要相应的权限（SQS 使用 sqs:SendMessage，SNS 使用 sns:Publish）。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

- **A. 使用"失败"筛选策略订阅 ErrorTopic，端点 = ProcessMessages。** 这逆转了流程——它会使 `ProcessMessages` 成为 `ErrorTopic` 的*订阅者*，而不是发布者。SNS 筛选策略只能筛选已发布到主题的消息；它们无法检测 Lambda 失败。这里没有机制将失败事件发布到 `ErrorTopic`。

- **C. 将 ErrorTopic 配置为 ProcessMessages 的触发器，并使用失败筛选策略。** 这也是逆转了——它会在每次消息发布到 `ErrorTopic` 时调用 `ProcessMessages`。同样，没有任何内容将失败事件发布到 `ErrorTopic`，SNS 筛选策略也不理解 Lambda 失败语义。

- **D. 在 ErrorTopic 上配置传递策略，其中包含失败筛选策略，Lambda 作为端点。** SNS *传递策略*控制 HTTP/S 订阅的重试行为；它们与捕获 Lambda 失败无关。与 A 和 C 类似，此选项的流程也是错误的（Lambda 作为订阅者而非发布者）。

只有选项 B 使用了适当的 AWS Lambda 功能——**失败目标**——这是此场景的专用机制。最佳实践是在所有异步 Lambda 函数上使用失败目标（用于数据保留和通知目的）。

## 参考资源
- [Capturing records of Lambda asynchronous invocations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-async-retain-records.html)
- [Introducing AWS Lambda Destinations (AWS Compute Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/introducing-aws-lambda-destinations/)
- [Invoking Lambda functions with Amazon SNS notifications](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sns.html)

en.question: A company is developing a new application that uses Amazon EC2, Amazon S3, and AWS Lambda resources. The company wants to allow employees to access the AWS Management Console by using existing credentials that the company stores and manages in an on-premises Microsoft Active Directory. Each employee must have a specific level of access to the AWS resources that is based on the employee’s role. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Configure AWS Directory Service to create an Active Directory in AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory. Establish a trust relationship with the on-premises Active Directory. Configure IAM roles and trust policies to give the employees access to the AWS resources.
options.B: Use LDAP to directly integrate the on-premises Active Directory with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). Map Active Directory groups to IAM roles to control access to AWS resources.
options.C: Implement a custom identity broker to authenticate users into the on-premises Active Directory. Configure the identity broker to use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to grant authorized users IAM role based access to the AWS resources.
options.D: Configure Amazon Cognito to federate users into the on-premises Active Directory. Use Cognito user pools to manage user identities and to manage user access to the AWS resources.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

The company wants employees to sign in to the **AWS Management Console** using credentials that already exist in an **on-premises Microsoft Active Directory**, with role-based access to EC2, S3, and Lambda. The goal is **least operational overhead**.

## Correct Answer: A

Create an **AWS Managed Microsoft AD** directory using AWS Directory Service, establish a **two-way forest trust** to the on-premises AD, then create **IAM roles** with a trust policy for `ds.amazonaws.com` and assign on-premises AD users/groups to those roles.

This is the AWS-recommended pattern for federated console access from an on-premises AD. A two-way forest trust relationship from AWS Microsoft AD to your on-premises Active Directory is required, along with IAM roles with trust relationships configured to AWS Directory Service. A two-way trust is required for AWS Enterprise Apps such as the AWS Management Console.

The IAM role trust policy is straightforward:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Principal": { "Service": "ds.amazonaws.com" },
    "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
  }]
}
```

You then create an IAM role that grants access to the AWS Management Console for services your AD users need, ensure the IAM role has a trust relationship with AWS Directory Service, assign Active Directory users or groups to the IAM role, and verify that users can access the AWS Management Console.

This solution is fully managed by AWS — no custom code, no SAML IdP build-out, and the company keeps a single source of truth for identities (on-prem AD).

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

**B. LDAP directly to IAM** — IAM does **not** support direct LDAP integration. IAM is not an LDAP-aware identity store; you cannot map AD groups to IAM roles via LDAP without a federation layer (SAML 2.0, AWS Managed AD, or IAM Identity Center). This option describes a feature that doesn't exist.

**C. Custom identity broker with STS** — This is a valid pattern (described in the AWS docs as "Enabling SAML 2.0 federated users" alternative), but it requires building, hosting, securing, and maintaining a custom application that authenticates against AD and calls `sts:AssumeRole`/`GetFederationToken`. That is the **highest** operational overhead of all options, the opposite of what the question asks.

**D. Amazon Cognito federated to on-prem AD** — Cognito user pools are designed for **end-user authentication to customer-facing applications** (web/mobile), not for federating workforce identities into the AWS Management Console. Cognito identity pools issue temporary AWS credentials for app access to AWS APIs, not interactive console sign-in. Using it here would be architecturally incorrect and would still not provide native console SSO from AD.

## References

- [How to Access the AWS Management Console Using AWS Microsoft AD and Your On-Premises Credentials](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/how-to-access-the-aws-management-console-using-aws-microsoft-ad-and-your-on-premises-credentials/)
- [Creating a trust relationship between your AWS Managed Microsoft AD and self-managed AD](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/ms_ad_setup_trust.html)
- [Grant access to AWS Management Console for on-premises AD users](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/enable-active-directory-console-access)
- [Editing the trust relationship for an existing IAM role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/edit_trust.html)
- [Granting AWS Managed Microsoft AD users and groups access to AWS resources with IAM roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/ms_ad_manage_roles.html)

zh.question: 一家公司正在开发一款使用 Amazon EC2、Amazon S3 和 AWS Lambda 资源的新应用程序。该公司希望允许员工使用其存储在本地 Microsoft Active Directory 中的现有凭证访问 AWS 管理控制台。每位员工必须根据其角色拥有对 AWS 资源的特定访问权限级别。哪种解决方案能够以最小的运维开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 配置 AWS Directory Service，在 AWS Directory Service 中为 Microsoft Active Directory 创建 Active Directory。建立与本地 Active Directory 的信任关系。配置 IAM 角色和信任策略，以授予员工访问 AWS 资源的权限。
options.B: 使用 LDAP 将本地 Active Directory 与 AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) 直接集成。将 Active Directory 组映射到 IAM 角色，以控制对 AWS 资源的访问。
options.C: 实现自定义身份代理，用于对本地 Active Directory 用户进行身份验证。配置身份代理以使用 AWS 安全令牌服务 (AWS STS) 向授权用户授予基于 IAM 角色的 AWS 资源访问权限。
options.D: 配置 Amazon Cognito 将用户联合到本地 Active Directory。使用 Cognito 用户池来管理用户身份并管理用户对 AWS 资源的访问权限。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

公司希望员工使用已经存在于**本地 Microsoft Active Directory** 中的凭证登录到 **AWS Management Console**，并对 EC2、S3 和 Lambda 进行基于角色的访问。目标是**最小化运营开销**。

## 正确答案：A

使用 AWS Directory Service 创建 **AWS Managed Microsoft AD** 目录，建立与本地 AD 的**双向森林信任**，然后创建 **IAM 角色**，其信任策略指向 `ds.amazonaws.com`，并将本地 AD 用户/组分配给这些角色。

这是 AWS 推荐的从本地 AD 实现联合控制台访问的模式。需要从 AWS Microsoft AD 到本地 Active Directory 的双向森林信任关系，以及配置与 AWS Directory Service 信任关系的 IAM 角色。AWS Management Console 等 AWS 企业应用需要双向信任。

IAM 角色信任策略很直观：

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Principal": { "Service": "ds.amazonaws.com" },
    "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
  }]
}
```

随后，创建授予 AD 用户所需服务 AWS Management Console 访问权限的 IAM 角色，确保该 IAM 角色与 AWS Directory Service 建立信任关系，将 Active Directory 用户或组分配给该 IAM 角色，并验证用户可以访问 AWS Management Console。

此解决方案完全由 AWS 托管——无需自定义代码，无需构建 SAML IdP，公司为身份保留了单一信息源（本地 AD）。

## 其他选项为何错误

**B. LDAP 直接连接到 IAM** — IAM **不**支持直接 LDAP 集成。IAM 不是 LDAP 感知的身份存储；无法通过 LDAP 将 AD 组映射到 IAM 角色，除非使用联合层（SAML 2.0、AWS Managed AD 或 IAM Identity Center）。此选项描述的是不存在的功能。

**C. 具有 STS 的自定义身份代理** — 这是一种有效的模式（在 AWS 文档中描述为"启用 SAML 2.0 联合用户"的替代方案），但它需要构建、托管、保护和维护一个自定义应用程序，该应用程序对 AD 进行身份验证并调用 `sts:AssumeRole`/`GetFederationToken`。这在所有选项中产生的**运营开销最高**，与问题所要求的相反。

**D. 与本地 AD 联合的 Amazon Cognito** — Cognito 用户池设计用于**最终用户对面向客户的应用程序的身份验证**（Web/移动），而非将员工身份联合到 AWS Management Console。Cognito 身份池为应用程序发放临时 AWS 凭证以访问 AWS API，而非交互式控制台登录。在这里使用它在架构上不正确，也无法从 AD 提供本机控制台 SSO。

## 参考资源

- [如何使用 AWS Microsoft AD 和本地凭证访问 AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/how-to-access-the-aws-management-console-using-aws-microsoft-ad-and-your-on-premises-credentials/)
- [在 AWS Managed Microsoft AD 和自管理 AD 之间创建信任关系](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/ms_ad_setup_trust.html)
- [为本地 AD 用户授予 AWS Management Console 访问权限](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/enable-active-directory-console-access)
- [编辑现有 IAM 角色的信任关系](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/edit_trust.html)
- [使用 IAM 角色为 AWS Managed Microsoft AD 用户和组授予 AWS 资源访问权限](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/ms_ad_manage_roles.html)

en.question: A company has an Amazon DynamoDB table that contains records of users that have signed up for a trial of the company’s product. The company is using a spreadsheet to track data about the product trial. The company needs to ensure the spreadsheet is automatically updated with the latest information when individual trials begin, are updated, or finish. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster from the table. Set the view type to old image. Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the cluster data to update the spreadsheet. Subscribe the Lambda function to the cluster.
options.B: Create a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster from the table. Set the view type to new image. Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the cluster data to update the spreadsheet. Subscribe the Lambda function to the cluster.
options.C: Enable a DynamoDB stream for the table. Set the view type to new image. Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the stream data to update the spreadsheet. Subscribe the Lambda function to the stream.
options.D: Enable a DynamoDB stream for the table. Set the view type to old image. Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the stream data to update the spreadsheet. Subscribe the Lambda function to the stream.

en.explanation:
# DynamoDB Streams + Lambda to Update External Spreadsheet

## Scenario
A DynamoDB table tracks product trial signups. The company wants an external spreadsheet to be automatically synchronized whenever items are inserted, modified, or removed in the table. The solution must be event-driven so updates propagate without manual intervention.

## Correct Answer: C

**Enable a DynamoDB Stream on the table with view type `NEW_IMAGE`, and subscribe a Lambda function to the stream.**

DynamoDB Streams is the AWS-native change data capture (CDC) mechanism for DynamoDB. Whenever an application creates, updates, or deletes items in the table, DynamoDB Streams writes a stream record with the primary key attributes of the items that were modified. A stream record contains information about a data modification to a single item in a DynamoDB table. You can configure the stream so that the stream records capture additional information, such as the "before" and "after" images of modified items.

You can use an AWS Lambda function to process records in an Amazon DynamoDB stream. With DynamoDB Streams, you can trigger a Lambda function to perform additional work each time a DynamoDB table is updated. This perfectly matches the requirement: every time a trial begins, is updated, or finishes, the stream record will trigger the Lambda function, which writes the latest state to the spreadsheet.

### Why `NEW_IMAGE` view type?
The spreadsheet needs to reflect the **latest** state of each trial record. NEW_IMAGE — The entire item, as it appears after it was modified. This gives the Lambda function the full, current item to push to the spreadsheet without requiring an extra `GetItem` call.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A & B — DAX cluster:** DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is an **in-memory write-through/read-through cache** for DynamoDB designed to reduce read latency from milliseconds to microseconds. DAX **does not emit change events**, has **no concept of view types** (`NEW_IMAGE`/`OLD_IMAGE` are properties of DynamoDB Streams, not DAX), and Lambda **cannot subscribe to a DAX cluster**. DAX is the wrong service entirely for change-data-capture use cases.

- **D — Stream with `OLD_IMAGE`:** Although DynamoDB Streams + Lambda is the correct architecture, OLD_IMAGE — The entire item, as it appeared before it was modified. Using `OLD_IMAGE` would push *stale* (pre-change) data to the spreadsheet, the opposite of what's required. Also, on `INSERT` events there is no old image, so newly created trials would have no data to push.

## Reference Architecture
```
DynamoDB Table  ──(Stream, NEW_IMAGE)──▶  Lambda (event source mapping)  ──▶  Spreadsheet API
```

## Sources
- [Change data capture for DynamoDB Streams](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Streams.html)
- [Using AWS Lambda with Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-ddb.html)
- [StreamSpecification API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/APIReference/API_StreamSpecification.html)

zh.question: 一家公司拥有一个 Amazon DynamoDB 表，其中包含注册试用该公司产品的用户记录。该公司使用电子表格来跟踪产品试用数据。该公司需要确保在单个试用开始、更新或结束时，电子表格能够自动更新为最新信息。哪种解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 从该表创建 DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) 集群。将视图类型设置为“旧映像”。创建一个使用集群数据更新电子表格的 AWS Lambda 函数。将该 Lambda 函数订阅到该集群。
options.B: 从该表创建 DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) 集群。将视图类型设置为“新建映像”。创建一个使用集群数据更新电子表格的 AWS Lambda 函数。将该 Lambda 函数订阅到该集群。
options.C: 为该表启用 DynamoDB 流。将视图类型设置为“新建图像”。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数，使用该流数据更新电子表格。将该 Lambda 函数订阅到该流。
options.D: 为该表启用 DynamoDB 流。将视图类型设置为“旧图像”。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数，使用该流数据更新电子表格。将该 Lambda 函数订阅到该流。

zh.explanation:
# DynamoDB Streams + Lambda 更新外部电子表格

## 场景
DynamoDB 表跟踪产品试用注册。公司希望在表中插入、修改或删除项目时自动同步外部电子表格。该解决方案必须是事件驱动的，以便更新无需手动干预即可传播。

## 正确答案：C

**在表上启用 DynamoDB Stream，视图类型为 `NEW_IMAGE`，并将 Lambda 函数订阅到该流。**

DynamoDB Streams 是 AWS 原生的 DynamoDB 变更数据捕获 (CDC) 机制。每当应用程序在表中创建、更新或删除项目时，DynamoDB Streams 会写入一条流记录，包含被修改项目的主键属性。流记录包含有关 DynamoDB 表中单个项目的数据修改信息。您可以配置流，使流记录捕获额外信息，例如修改项目的"之前"和"之后"镜像。

您可以使用 AWS Lambda 函数处理 Amazon DynamoDB 流中的记录。使用 DynamoDB Streams，您可以在 DynamoDB 表每次更新时触发 Lambda 函数以执行额外工作。这完全符合需求：每当试用开始、更新或结束时，流记录都会触发 Lambda 函数，该函数将最新状态写入电子表格。

### 为什么选择 `NEW_IMAGE` 视图类型？
电子表格需要反映每条试用记录的**最新**状态。NEW_IMAGE — 修改后显示的整个项目。这为 Lambda 函数提供了完整的当前项目，可以推送到电子表格，而无需额外的 `GetItem` 调用。

## 为什么其他选项错误

- **A 和 B — DAX 集群：** DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) 是为 DynamoDB 设计的**内存写穿/读穿缓存**，用于将读延迟从毫秒级降低到微秒级。DAX **不会发出变更事件**，**没有视图类型的概念**（`NEW_IMAGE`/`OLD_IMAGE` 是 DynamoDB Streams 的属性，不是 DAX），Lambda **无法订阅 DAX 集群**。DAX 完全是错误的变更数据捕获服务。

- **D — 使用 `OLD_IMAGE` 的流：** 虽然 DynamoDB Streams + Lambda 是正确的架构，但 OLD_IMAGE — 修改前显示的整个项目。使用 `OLD_IMAGE` 会将*过期的*（变更前的）数据推送到电子表格，与需求相反。另外，对于 `INSERT` 事件，没有旧镜像，因此新创建的试用将没有数据可推送。

## 参考架构
```
DynamoDB 表  ──(Stream, NEW_IMAGE)──▶  Lambda (事件源映射)  ──▶  电子表格 API
```

## 参考资源
- [DynamoDB Streams 变更数据捕获](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Streams.html)
- [将 AWS Lambda 与 Amazon DynamoDB 配合使用](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-ddb.html)
- [StreamSpecification API 参考](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/APIReference/API_StreamSpecification.html)

en.question: A developer is launching a global application that delivers content to multiple countries. The developer needs to serve specific content based on the country of each user and each user’s primary language. The developer must ensure that content is served reliably and with low latency. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Amazon API Gateway REST API. Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator to resolve requests to the API. Configure endpoint groups on the accelerator. Attach listeners for each country and language.
options.B: Store the content in a centralized Amazon S3 bucket. Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket. Create an Amazon Route 53 hosted zone that includes the endpoint for the S3 bucket. Create records in Route 53 that use geoproximity and geolocation routing policies.
options.C: Create an Amazon API Gateway REST API. Connect the REST API to AWS WAF. Use geo match statements and regex match statements to allow or deny requests based on the labels returned from web request evaluations.
options.D: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses the application as an origin. Configure the distribution to forward the Accept-Language header and the CloudFront-Viewer-Country header to the origin.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A developer needs to deliver content to users globally, with content tailored to:
1. **The user's country** (geolocation)
2. **The user's primary language**

The solution must be **reliable** and have **low latency**.

## Correct Answer: D

**Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses the application as an origin. Configure the distribution to forward the `Accept-Language` header and the `CloudFront-Viewer-Country` header to the origin.**

CloudFront is AWS's global content delivery network, providing low latency through its edge locations worldwide. CloudFront can forward specific headers to the origin so the origin can return personalized content:

- **`CloudFront-Viewer-Country`** — Contains the two-letter country code for the viewer's country. CloudFront automatically determines this from the viewer's IP address.
- **`Accept-Language`** — A standard HTTP header sent by browsers indicating the user's preferred languages.

With these headers, your origin or your edge function can receive information about the viewer without the need for you to write your own code to determine this information. If your origin returns different responses based on the information in these headers, you can include them in the cache key so that CloudFront caches the responses separately. For example, your origin might respond with content in a specific language based on the country that the viewer is in.

The AWS documentation explicitly addresses this exact use case: If you want CloudFront to cache different versions of your objects based on the language specified in the request, configure CloudFront to forward the Accept-Language header to your origin, and you do the same with `CloudFront-Viewer-Country` for country-based variation. This allows you to serve different versions of your content based on the device the user is using, the location of the viewer, the language the viewer is using, and a variety of other criteria.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

### A. API Gateway REST API + Global Accelerator with listeners per country/language

- **AWS Global Accelerator does not have "listeners per country/language."** Global Accelerator listeners are defined by **port and protocol** (e.g., TCP/443), not by country or language. Endpoint groups are tied to AWS Regions, not to countries or languages.
- Global Accelerator improves network performance via the AWS global backbone but does **not** inspect HTTP headers like `Accept-Language` and cannot tailor content based on language preferences.
- This option misuses Global Accelerator's architecture.

### B. Centralized S3 bucket + S3 Transfer Acceleration + Route 53 geoproximity/geolocation

- **Route 53 routing policies route DNS queries**, not content. Geolocation routing returns different DNS answers, but here there is only one centralized S3 bucket — there's nothing different to route to.
- **S3 Transfer Acceleration** is designed for **uploading** large objects to S3 over long distances using CloudFront edge locations; it is not a CDN for content delivery to end users and isn't optimized for low-latency content reads.
- Route 53 cannot inspect the `Accept-Language` header, so language-based content selection is impossible at the DNS layer.

### C. API Gateway REST API + AWS WAF with geo match and regex match statements

- **AWS WAF is a security/firewall service** that allows or blocks requests; it does not serve different content versions. Geo match statements can block or allow by country, but they cannot deliver localized content.
- This option **does not address low latency** for global content delivery — API Gateway REST APIs are regional unless fronted by CloudFront, and WAF doesn't add a CDN layer.

## Reference Implementation Approach

In the CloudFront cache behavior, attach an **origin request policy** (or include in a **cache policy**) that forwards:
- `CloudFront-Viewer-Country`
- `Accept-Language`

The origin then inspects these headers and returns the appropriate localized content. CloudFront caches separate versions per (country, language) combination, providing low latency from edge locations worldwide.

## References

- [Add CloudFront request headers (CloudFront-Viewer-Country)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/adding-cloudfront-headers.html)
- [Cache content based on request headers (Accept-Language)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/header-caching.html)
- [Use managed origin request policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/using-managed-origin-request-policies.html)

zh.question: 一位开发者正在推出一款面向全球多个国家/地区的应用程序，该应用程序需要根据每个用户所在的国家/地区和主要语言提供特定的内容。开发者必须确保内容能够可靠且低延迟地提供。哪种解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建 Amazon API Gateway REST API。创建 AWS Global Accelerator 标准加速器来解析对 API 的请求。在加速器上配置端点组。为每个国家/地区和语言附加监听器。
options.B: 将内容存储在集中式 Amazon S3 存储桶中。在该存储桶上启用 S3 传输加速。创建一个包含 S3 存储桶终端节点的 Amazon Route 53 托管区域。在 Route 53 中创建使用地理位置和邻近性路由策略的记录。
options.C: 创建 Amazon API Gateway REST API。将 REST API 连接到 AWS WAF。使用地理位置匹配语句和正则表达式匹配语句，根据 Web 请求评估返回的标签来允许或拒绝请求。
options.D: 配置一个使用应用程序作为源的 Amazon CloudFront 分发。配置该分发，使其将 Accept-Language 标头和 CloudFront-Viewer-Country 标头转发到源。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

开发人员需要向全球用户提供内容，内容需要根据以下因素进行定制：
1. **用户所在的国家**（地理位置）
2. **用户的主要语言**

该解决方案必须**可靠**且**延迟低**。

## 正确答案：D

**配置一个 Amazon CloudFront 分发，以应用程序作为源。配置该分发以将 `Accept-Language` 标头和 `CloudFront-Viewer-Country` 标头转发到源。**

CloudFront 是 AWS 的全球内容交付网络，通过遍布全球的边缘节点提供低延迟。CloudFront 可以将特定标头转发到源，以便源返回个性化内容：

- **`CloudFront-Viewer-Country`** — 包含查看者所在国家的两字母国家代码。CloudFront 从查看者的 IP 地址自动确定此信息。
- **`Accept-Language`** — 浏览器发送的标准 HTTP 标头，指示用户首选的语言。

借助这些标头，您的源或边缘函数可以接收有关查看者的信息，而无需您编写自己的代码来确定此信息。如果您的源根据这些标头中的信息返回不同的响应，您可以将它们包含在缓存密钥中，以便 CloudFront 分别缓存这些响应。例如，您的源可能会根据查看者所在的国家返回特定语言的内容。

AWS 文档明确说明了这个确切的用例：如果您希望 CloudFront 根据请求中指定的语言缓存不同版本的对象，请配置 CloudFront 以将 Accept-Language 标头转发到您的源，对 `CloudFront-Viewer-Country` 执行相同操作以实现基于国家的变化。这允许您根据用户使用的设备、查看者的位置、查看者使用的语言以及各种其他条件来提供内容的不同版本。

## 为什么其他选项是错误的

### A. API Gateway REST API + Global Accelerator，每个国家/语言有监听器

- **AWS Global Accelerator 没有"每个国家/语言的监听器"。** Global Accelerator 监听器由**端口和协议**定义（例如 TCP/443），而不是由国家或语言定义。端点组与 AWS 区域相关联，而不是与国家或语言相关联。
- Global Accelerator 通过 AWS 全球骨干网改进网络性能，但**不会**检查 HTTP 标头（如 `Accept-Language`）且无法根据语言偏好定制内容。
- 此选项误用了 Global Accelerator 的架构。

### B. 集中式 S3 存储桶 + S3 传输加速 + Route 53 地理邻近/地理位置路由

- **Route 53 路由策略路由 DNS 查询**，而不是内容。地理位置路由返回不同的 DNS 答案，但这里只有一个集中式 S3 存储桶 — 没有不同的内容可以路由到。
- **S3 传输加速**旨在使用 CloudFront 边缘节点通过长距离将大型对象**上传**到 S3；它不是面向最终用户的内容交付 CDN，不适合低延迟内容读取的优化。
- Route 53 无法检查 `Accept-Language` 标头，所以在 DNS 层面无法进行基于语言的内容选择。

### C. API Gateway REST API + AWS WAF，使用地理匹配和正则表达式匹配语句

- **AWS WAF 是一项安全/防火墙服务**，它允许或阻止请求；它不提供不同的内容版本。地理匹配语句可以按国家允许或阻止，但它们不能提供本地化内容。
- 此选项**无法解决全球内容交付的低延迟问题** — API Gateway REST API 是区域性的，除非由 CloudFront 提供前缀，WAF 不会添加 CDN 层。

## 参考实现方法

在 CloudFront 缓存行为中，附加一个**源请求策略**（或包含在**缓存策略**中）以转发：
- `CloudFront-Viewer-Country`
- `Accept-Language`

源随后检查这些标头并返回相应的本地化内容。CloudFront 按 (国家, 语言) 组合分别缓存版本，从全球边缘节点提供低延迟。

## 参考资源

- [添加 CloudFront 请求标头 (CloudFront-Viewer-Country)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/adding-cloudfront-headers.html)
- [基于请求标头缓存内容 (Accept-Language)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/header-caching.html)
- [使用托管源请求策略](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/using-managed-origin-request-policies.html)

en.question: A company generates SSL certificates from a third-party provider. The company imports the certificates into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to use with public web applications. A developer must implement a solution to notify the company’s security team 90 days before an imported certificate expires. The company already has configured an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. The company also has configured an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic that has the security team’s email address as a subscriber. Which solution will provide the security team with the required notification about certificates?

options.A: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that specifies the ACM Certificate Approaching Expiration event type. Set the SNS topic as the EventBridge rule’s target.
options.B: Create an AWS Lambda function to search for all certificates that are expiring within 90 days. Program the Lambda function to send each identified certificate’s Amazon Resource Name (ARN) in a message to the SQS queue.
options.C: Create an AWS Step Functions workflow that is invoked by each certificate’s expiration notification from AWS CloudTrail. Create an AWS Lambda function to send each certificate's Amazon Resource Name (ARN) in a message to the SQS queue.
options.D: Configure AWS Config with the acm-certificate-expiration-check managed rule to run every 24 hours. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that includes an event pattern that specifies the Config Rules Compliance Change detail type and the configured rule. Set the SNS topic as the EventBridge rule’s target.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A company imports third-party SSL/TLS certificates into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) for use with public web applications. The developer must notify the security team **90 days before** an imported certificate expires, leveraging an existing SNS topic (with the security team's email subscribed) and a pre-existing SQS queue.

The decisive constraint is the **90-day lead time**, which makes most ACM-native expiration mechanisms infeasible.

## Correct Answer: D

> ⚠️ The originally listed answer **A** is incorrect because the native ACM "Certificate Approaching Expiration" EventBridge event **cannot be configured for more than 45 days** in advance. Only AWS Config's `acm-certificate-expiration-check` managed rule supports a 90-day window.

### Why D works

AWS Config's managed rule [`acm-certificate-expiration-check`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/acm-certificate-expiration-check.html) "checks if AWS Certificate Manager Certificates in your account are marked for expiration within the specified number of days." The rule accepts a `daysToExpiration` parameter (default 14) with no documented upper limit, so setting it to **90** causes any ACM certificate within 90 days of expiry to be marked **NON_COMPLIANT**.

When the compliance state changes, AWS Config emits a `Config Rules Compliance Change` event to Amazon EventBridge. An EventBridge rule matching that detail-type and the `acm-certificate-expiration-check` rule name can target the existing SNS topic, which delivers the email to the security team. This is exactly the pattern AWS documents in [Get notified when ACM imported certificates are near expiration](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/acm-certificate-expiration):

```json
{
  "source": ["aws.config"],
  "detail-type": ["Config Rules Compliance Change"],
  "detail": {
    "messageType": ["ComplianceChangeNotification"],
    "configRuleName": ["acm-certificate-expiration-check"],
    "resourceType": ["AWS::ACM::Certificate"],
    "newEvaluationResult": { "complianceType": ["NON_COMPLIANT"] }
  }
}
```

Running the rule every 24 hours ensures the security team is notified once a certificate crosses the 90-day threshold.

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

### A — ACM Certificate Approaching Expiration event (originally marked correct, but wrong)

The native [ACM EventBridge expiration event](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/supported-events.html) is published daily starting at most **45 days** before expiration for imported/private certificates (30 days for public ACM-issued certs). The configurable [`ExpiryEventsConfiguration.DaysBeforeExpiry`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/APIReference/API_ExpiryEventsConfiguration.html) parameter is constrained to a range of **1–45**. AWS re:Post explicitly states: *"By default, the ACM Certificate Approaching Expiration event sends notifications 45 days before an event's expiration. You can change the day, but you can't exceed 45 days."* AWS's own remediation guidance is: *"To set up notifications for more than 45 days before an event's expiration, use a custom EventBridge rule"* with AWS Config — i.e., option D. Therefore option A is technically incapable of satisfying the 90-day requirement.

### B — Lambda polling + SQS

Two problems: (1) SQS does not deliver emails to the security team — the team is subscribed to the **SNS topic**, not the queue; (2) building and maintaining a custom Lambda polling job is unnecessary operational overhead when AWS Config provides a managed rule for exactly this use case.

### C — Step Functions invoked by CloudTrail "expiration notifications"

CloudTrail does not emit certificate-expiration events. CloudTrail records **API activity** (management and data events), not certificate lifecycle/expiry events. There is no CloudTrail event that fires when a certificate is approaching expiration, so the Step Functions workflow could never be triggered. Additionally, like option B, this option routes notifications to SQS rather than the SNS topic the security team is subscribed to.

## Key Takeaway

For ACM expiration notifications:
- **≤ 45 days** in advance → use the native ACM EventBridge event (`ACM Certificate Approaching Expiration`).
- **> 45 days** in advance (e.g., 90 days) → use AWS Config's [`acm-certificate-expiration-check`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/acm-certificate-expiration-check.html) managed rule with `daysToExpiration` set appropriately, then route `Config Rules Compliance Change` events through EventBridge to SNS, as documented in the [AWS re:Post guidance](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/acm-certificate-expiration).

zh.question: 一家公司从第三方提供商处生成 SSL 证书。该公司将这些证书导入 AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)，以便在公共 Web 应用程序上使用。开发人员需要实现一个解决方案，以便在导入的证书过期前 90 天通知公司安全团队。该公司已配置了一个 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列。该公司还配置了一个 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题，并将安全团队的电子邮件地址添加为订阅者。哪种解决方案能够为安全团队提供所需的证书通知？

options.A: 创建一条 Amazon EventBridge 规则，指定 ACM 证书即将过期事件类型。将 SNS 主题设置为 EventBridge 规则的目标。
options.B: 创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数，用于搜索所有在 90 天内到期的证书。编写 Lambda 函数，将每个已识别证书的 Amazon 资源名称 (ARN) 以消息的形式发送到 SQS 队列。
options.C: 创建一个 AWS Step Functions 工作流，该工作流由来自 AWS CloudTrail 的每个证书到期通知触发。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数，将每个证书的 Amazon 资源名称 (ARN) 以消息的形式发送到 SQS 队列。
options.D: 配置 AWS Config，使其每 24 小时运行一次 acm-certificate-expiration-check 托管规则。创建一个 Amazon EventBridge 规则，其中包含一个事件模式，该模式指定 Config 规则合规性变更详细类型和已配置的规则。将 SNS 主题设置为 EventBridge 规则的目标。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

一家公司将第三方 SSL/TLS 证书导入 AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)，用于公有网络应用程序。开发人员必须在导入的证书到期前 **90 天**通知安全团队，利用现有的 SNS 主题（安全团队已订阅电子邮件）和预先存在的 SQS 队列。

关键约束是 **90 天的提前期**，这使得大多数 ACM 原生到期机制不可行。

## 正确答案：D

> ⚠️ 原始列出的答案 **A** 不正确，因为原生 ACM"Certificate Approaching Expiration"EventBridge 事件**最多只能提前 45 天**配置。只有 AWS Config 的 `acm-certificate-expiration-check` 托管规则支持 90 天窗口。

### 为什么 D 有效

AWS Config 的托管规则 [`acm-certificate-expiration-check`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/acm-certificate-expiration-check.html)"检查账户中的 AWS Certificate Manager 证书是否标记为在指定天数内到期。"该规则接受 `daysToExpiration` 参数（默认 14），没有文档化的上限，因此将其设置为 **90** 会导致任何在到期前 90 天内的 ACM 证书被标记为 **NON_COMPLIANT**。

当合规状态变化时，AWS Config 向 Amazon EventBridge 发出 `Config Rules Compliance Change` 事件。与该详情类型和 `acm-certificate-expiration-check` 规则名称匹配的 EventBridge 规则可以定向到现有的 SNS 主题，该主题会向安全团队发送电子邮件。这正是 AWS 在 [Get notified when ACM imported certificates are near expiration](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/acm-certificate-expiration) 中记录的模式：

```json
{
  "source": ["aws.config"],
  "detail-type": ["Config Rules Compliance Change"],
  "detail": {
    "messageType": ["ComplianceChangeNotification"],
    "configRuleName": ["acm-certificate-expiration-check"],
    "resourceType": ["AWS::ACM::Certificate"],
    "newEvaluationResult": { "complianceType": ["NON_COMPLIANT"] }
  }
}
```

每 24 小时运行一次该规则，确保安全团队在证书跨越 90 天阈值时收到通知。

## 为什么其他选项不正确

### A — ACM Certificate Approaching Expiration 事件（原标记为正确，但错误）

原生 [ACM EventBridge 到期事件](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/supported-events.html)从到期前最多 **45 天**开始每天发布（对于导入/私有证书；对于公有 ACM 颁发的证书为 30 天）。可配置的 [`ExpiryEventsConfiguration.DaysBeforeExpiry`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/APIReference/API_ExpiryEventsConfiguration.html) 参数被限制在 **1–45** 的范围内。AWS re:Post 明确指出：*"默认情况下，ACM Certificate Approaching Expiration 事件在事件到期前 45 天发送通知。您可以更改天数，但不能超过 45 天。"* AWS 自己的补救指南指出：*"要设置在事件到期前超过 45 天的通知，请使用带有 AWS Config 的自定义 EventBridge 规则"*——即选项 D。因此选项 A 在技术上无法满足 90 天的要求。

### B — Lambda 轮询 + SQS

两个问题：(1) SQS 不向安全团队发送电子邮件——该团队订阅的是 **SNS 主题**，而不是队列；(2) 构建和维护自定义 Lambda 轮询作业是不必要的操作开销，而当 AWS Config 为此用例提供托管规则时就不需要了。

### C — 由 CloudTrail"到期通知"调用的 Step Functions

CloudTrail 不发出证书过期事件。CloudTrail 记录的是 **API 活动**（管理和数据事件），而不是证书生命周期/到期事件。没有 CloudTrail 事件会在证书即将到期时触发，因此 Step Functions 工作流永远无法被触发。此外，与选项 B 一样，此选项将通知路由到 SQS，而不是安全团队订阅的 SNS 主题。

## 关键要点

对于 ACM 到期通知：
- **≤ 45 天**提前 → 使用原生 ACM EventBridge 事件（`ACM Certificate Approaching Expiration`）。
- **> 45 天**提前（例如 90 天）→ 使用 AWS Config 的 [`acm-certificate-expiration-check`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/acm-certificate-expiration-check.html) 托管规则，将 `daysToExpiration` 设置为适当的值，然后通过 EventBridge 将 `Config Rules Compliance Change` 事件路由到 SNS，如 [AWS re:Post 指南](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/acm-certificate-expiration)所述。

en.question: A developer has an AWS Lambda function that needs to access an Amazon DynamoDB table named DailyOrders. The Lambda function must be able to perform read operations on the table. The Lambda function must not be able to perform write operations on the table. The developer needs to create an IAM policy to associate with the Lambda function's execution role. Which IAM policy statement will meet these requirements?

options.A:
```json
{
    "Version": "2012-10-17",
    "Statement": [{
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Action": [
            "dynamodb:BatchGetItem",
            "dynamodb:GetItem",
            "dynamodb:Query",
            "dynamodb:Scan",
            "dynamodb:BatchWriteItem",
            "dynamodb:PutItem",
            "dynamodb:UpdateItem"
        ],
        "Resource": "arn:aws:dynamodb:eu-east-1:321456987012:table/DailyOrders"
    }]
}
```

en.explanation:
## Scenario

A Lambda function needs **read-only** access to the DynamoDB table `DailyOrders`. The execution-role IAM policy must allow read operations and explicitly **prevent** any write operations (PutItem, UpdateItem, DeleteItem, BatchWriteItem). Following the principle of least privilege, the policy should grant *only* the read actions and omit any write actions.

## Correct Answer: D

Option D allows exactly the DynamoDB read APIs — `BatchGetItem`, `GetItem`, `Query`, and `Scan` — scoped to the `DailyOrders` table ARN. This matches AWS's documented read-only pattern. Per the AWS DynamoDB Developer Guide, the read-only policy grants permissions for the GetItem, BatchGetItem, Scan, Query, and ConditionCheckItem DynamoDB actions only, and as a result, sets read-only access on the table. Because IAM uses an implicit deny, no write API can be invoked when only read actions are listed in an Allow statement.

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Action": [
      "dynamodb:BatchGetItem",
      "dynamodb:GetItem",
      "dynamodb:Query",
      "dynamodb:Scan"
    ],
    "Resource": "arn:aws:dynamodb:eu-east-1:321456987012:table/DailyOrders"
  }]
}
```

## Why the Other Options Are Wrong

- **A — Incorrect.** It grants read actions but also explicitly allows `dynamodb:BatchWriteItem`, `dynamodb:PutItem`, and `dynamodb:UpdateItem`. This violates the requirement that the function must **not** be able to perform write operations.

- **B — Incorrect.** Includes `dynamodb:PutItem`, which is a write action. Read and write access combines actions like GetItem, BatchGetItem, PutItem, UpdateItem, DeleteItem, Query, and Scan — so PutItem is a write operation that must not be granted.

- **C — Incorrect.** Uses `Effect: Deny` on `Query`, `Scan`, `PutItem`, and `UpdateItem`. This actively **blocks** read operations (Query and Scan), which the function legitimately needs. Additionally, an explicit Deny statement alone provides no Allow — without an accompanying Allow statement, all DynamoDB calls would be denied due to the implicit deny default. It also fails to deny `DeleteItem` and `BatchWriteItem`, leaving gaps even in the deny logic.

## References

- [IAM policy to grant read-only permissions on items in a DynamoDB table](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/read-only-permissions-on-table-items.html)
- [Amazon DynamoDB: Allows access to a specific table](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_examples_dynamodb_specific-table.html)

zh.question: 开发人员有一个 AWS Lambda 函数，需要访问名为 DailyOrders 的 Amazon DynamoDB 表。该 Lambda 函数必须能够对该表执行读取操作，但不能执行写入操作。开发人员需要创建一个 IAM 策略并将其与 Lambda 函数的执行角色关联。哪个 IAM 策略语句能够满足这些要求？

options.A:
```json
{
    "Version": "2012-10-17",
    "Statement": [{
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Action": [
            "dynamodb:BatchGetItem",
            "dynamodb:GetItem",
            "dynamodb:Query",
            "dynamodb:Scan",
            "dynamodb:BatchWriteItem",
            "dynamodb:PutItem",
            "dynamodb:UpdateItem"
        ],
        "Resource": "arn:aws:dynamodb:eu-east-1:321456987012:table/DailyOrders"
    }]
}
```

zh.explanation:
## 场景

Lambda 函数需要对 DynamoDB 表 `DailyOrders` 具有**只读**访问权限。执行角色 IAM 策略必须允许读取操作，并明确**禁止**任何写入操作（PutItem、UpdateItem、DeleteItem、BatchWriteItem）。遵循最小权限原则，策略应仅授予读取操作，不包含任何写入操作。

## 正确答案：D

选项 D 仅允许 DynamoDB 读取 API — `BatchGetItem`、`GetItem`、`Query` 和 `Scan` — 范围限制在 `DailyOrders` 表 ARN。这与 AWS 文档中的只读模式相符。根据 AWS DynamoDB 开发人员指南，只读策略仅授予 GetItem、BatchGetItem、Scan、Query 和 ConditionCheckItem DynamoDB 操作的权限，因此在表上设置只读访问。由于 IAM 使用隐式拒绝，当 Allow 语句中仅列出读取操作时，无法调用任何写入 API。

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Action": [
      "dynamodb:BatchGetItem",
      "dynamodb:GetItem",
      "dynamodb:Query",
      "dynamodb:Scan"
    ],
```
